Cardinals-Texans Trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. Brewed Quietly For Weeks
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Houston Texans' deal for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made waves through the NFL world over the weekend in one of the more surprising trades made in quite some time.
Harrison's departure from Arizona isn't at all surprising — things clearly weren't working with the former No. 4 overall pick and he had previously hired agents to help navigate a deal earlier in the week.
However, the timing threw practically everybody off. A big-name player such as Harrison was offloaded, at least in public eyes, quickly. The Cardinals made Harrison inactive on Saturday morning, and by time their Week 5 contest kicked off, Harrison was on the move to Houston.
SI.com's Albert Breer added the trade process began weeks ago.
"The Cardinals asked around for a second-round pick plus a sweetener. Houston, over the 24 hours leading into kickoff Sunday, wound up coming around on that, ending an interesting process that ended Harrison’s two-plus years in Arizona," he wrote.
"It actually began weeks ago, with the No. 4 pick from the 2024 draft deciding to hire an agent to handle his situation, bringing in veterans Todd France and Tory Dandy of Athletes First.
"Quietly, the groundwork was laid for Harrison’s exit, starting then. The writing had been on the wall with the team’s decision to extend another young receiver, Michael Wilson, to pair long-term with big-money tight end Trey McBride. It had to stay that way for Arizona to get the type of return that would motivate the team to move Harrison. And things heated up over the course of the weekend, with the Texans’ effort to reunite Harrison with Stroud, his teammate at Ohio State."
Harrison, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur and general manager Monti Ossenfort did a strong job of collectively downplaying the noise while the workings of the trade were happening. All three parties, to varying extents, shot down trade rumors through the last few weeks.
Even after the deal was complete, figures such as LaFleur and Ossenfort didn't dive deep into the reasons for a trade.
“Decisions like this are never easy,” said Ossenfort in a statement after terms became final.
“Ultimately, we have to do what is best for our football team and that will always be the driving factor. We are extremely grateful to Marvin for what he has contributed to our organization and wish him the very best as he moves forward in his career.”
LaFleur, speaking after the loss to the Lions, added, "I'm not going to totally get into that right now. I really like Marvin Harrison.  He's a good person. I wish him well. We did what we thought was in the best interest of the Cardinals. Any guy that does not play to the level that I feel like they're capable of, I'm always going to put that on me and  coaching in general."

title: Cardinals Eying Free Agent Help to Upgrade OL
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' offensive line needs help, and the team is looking to upgrade their trenches with a potential addition via free agency.
The Cardinals are hosting Jamaree Salyer for a visit, according to ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler. Salyer is healthy after recovering from a knee issue and has versatility to play either guard or tackle:
Free agent OL Jamaree Salyer is visiting the Arizona Cardinals today, per source. Salyer had his knee scoped in August and is healthy now, will likely sign in coming weeks. Salyer can play tackle or guard, has 40 career starts. pic.twitter.com/3wVu0OJMQP
The Cardinals recently lost Paris Johnson Jr. for the season and Isaiah Adams to injured reserve last week, missing two of Arizona's starting five offensive lineman. Second-round pick Chase Bisontis was also lost in preseason play.
The Cardinals rolled out seventh-round rookie Jayden Williams at left tackle and Jon Gaines at right guard in their Week 5 loss to the Detroit Lions. Mike LaFleur highlighted the Cardinals' inability to run the ball as their biggest area of concern.
“Not bad. Against a pretty good front. We were mixing and matching where 97 (Lions Edge Aidan Hutchinson) was trying to get some ribs and licks and trying to help those guys, but I thought for the most part they did a fairly good job. Obviously, we threw the ball way too much because of how that game got out of hand and trying to establish a run game. If you guys want me to be candid, that’s really where I want to see us improve more," he said.
"That was going to be a hard game running the football, but we’re better than that. There were more yards out there than what was had. Some of it was them swimming our blocks and our double teams, but other times there was some space and we just weren’t taking up that space. We have to put them in better positions, but there’s more to be had in the run game.”
LaFleur was also less than impressed with their pass protection, which required more running back help to chip as opposed to Jeremiyah Love running routes as a receiver.
“Just helping out with those edges and stuff like that. I mean they have a pretty premier player so even if we’re in a six-man protection with the back, if they’re not bringing a linebacker, we still work at what you’d call a shave technique on their edge guys where you’re helping those tackles," he added.
"That’s not just our tackles; that’s all the tackles I’ve ever been a part of. You don’t want to put those guys on islands anywhere I’ve ever been too often.”
Salyer was initially believed to be lost for the season after signing with the Miami Dolphins this summer, though he was released and now appears to be healthy.

title: Cardinals' Mike LaFleur Highlights Arizona's Biggest Problem
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a run game problem, and Mike LaFleur knows it.
Through five weeks, the Cardinals rank in the bottom ten of NFL teams in terms of rushing yards per game (91.6) while they're averaging under four yards per carry at 3.8.
That's created a massive imbalance in the Cardinals' offense, one that has LaFleur digging for answers after the team's Week 5 thrashing to the Detroit Lions.
“Obviously, we threw the ball way too much because of how that game got out of hand and trying to establish a run game. If you guys want me to be candid, that’s really where I want to see us improve more," said LaFleur.
"That was going to be a hard game running the football, but we’re better than that. There were more yards out there than what was had. Some of it was them swimming our blocks and our double teams, but other times there was some space and we just weren’t taking up that space. We have to put them in better positions, but there’s more to be had in the run game.”
The Cardinals now move forward into the foreseeable future with Paris Johnson Jr. out for the season and Isaiah Adams on injured reserve for at least the next three weeks. Arizona's down two of their starters along the offensive line — a unit that was already viewed as average before the season began.
Their running back corps also isn't finding success. Jeremiyah Love is nursing an ankle injury and is averaging 3.7 yards per carry while backfield mate Tyler Allgeier is at 3.4. Arizona runners are averaging just 1.0 yards before contact, which ranks in the bottom half of the league.
Trading away Marvin Harrison Jr. only makes life easier for defenses to prepare for Arizona's rushing attack. So does the stagnant play of Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, and the Cardinals' inability to stop opposing offenses only dwindles their opportunity to have a balanced offense.
Arizona's inability to run the ball at high levels isn't talked about in the likes of making changes at quarterback — or defensive coordinator — though it very much is one of the larger problems for LaFleur to solve after such a struggling start.
With injuries piled up in the desert, it's tough to imagine the Cardinals can really turn things around unless a massive shift in philosophy upfront occurs.

title: State of the Arizona Cardinals, Part 1: How We Got Here
full_text:
It has certainly been an eventful first quarter of the 2026 season for the Arizona Cardinals.
The team started with an electric upset in Week One over the Los Angeles Chargers on the road and have slowly been falling back to Earth ever since. Competitive first halves against division foes Seattle and San Francisco turned into fiascos and the past two weeks against the Giants and Lions have been nothing short of disastrous.
Unfortunately, it is a narrative all too common for the Cardinals fan. A glimmer of hope for the future quickly blotted out by the harsh realities of the NFL.
Things seems bad right now, that would be hard for anyone to deny. So let us take a minute today to review the past five weeks and see where the team really is. We will review the results, check in on the state of the roster, and try to see where the team might go from here.
So whether you have been following the team closely this season or are just tuning in to see what your team is up to in yet another "rebuilding year" hopefully this will provide something for you.
The Cardinals successfully surprised the majority of the NFL world with a convincing win on the road to open the 2026 season. Their 26-14 victory felt complete with a great effort from quarterback Jacoby Brissett and the offense paired with a strong showing from a defense that came into the season with several question marks.
Week Two brought Arizona back to down to reality. They were competitive in the first half against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks finishing the period tied 7-7, but the wheels came off in the second half on the way to a 31-7 loss.
The schedule did not get any easier the following week back on the road to Santa Clara to face off against another division foe, the San Francisco 49ers. The Cardinals had it within 2 points late in the fourth quarter, but the defense couldn't stop George Kittle from finding the end zone with under two minutes left and a failed onside kick gave the team its second loss of the year, 36-30.
Week Four against the New York Giants started with as good of an offensive performance as could be expected, the Cardinals scoring on their first two offensive drives. The quick start quickly fell apart with the offense stagnating and the defense struggled to get a stop, allowing the Giants to score 17 unanswered points and take the lead. Arizona had a chance to score with seconds left but Brissett ended the game with a 98-yard pick-six.
Most recently, the Cardinals faced the Detroit Lions and former offensive coordinator Drew Petzing at home in Week Five and were thoroughly trounced. Once again scoring on their first drive, Arizona rapidly lost control of this game. Jahmyr Gibbs had over 200 yards from scrimmage and the defense surrended a season high 45 points, the most since a similar beatdown in Week 14 of the 2025 season against the Los Angeles Rams.
Injuries are a well-known and accepted part of the NFL season and the Cardinals have certainly had their fair share of them already this season.
The team is tied for the 10th most injured in the league after five weeks of play. There are currently five players with injury designations that should return at some points this season, but in addition there are already ten players who have hit the Injured Reserve list that are done for the year.
The IR list includes some of the biggest pieces of this roster, including starting LT Paris Johnson, Jr. and CB1 Will Johnson. Starting RG Isaiah Adams was recently added to the list and two key pieces of the 2026 Draft class hit the list before the season even started, second round pick G Chase Bisontis and fourth rounder DL Kaleb Proctor.
The loss of Johnson and Adams means that the Cardinals offensive line is down to 3/5 of their original starters. The secondary has also been decimated. Will Johnson is the biggest loss but of the fifteen total players with some sort of injury designation at the moment, four of them are safeties, a position lacking a true pair with Budda Baker after the loss of Jalen Thompson to free agency this offseason.
One of the big narratives of this season from the first week centered around the production and value of the No. 4 overall selection of the 2024 draft, Marvin Harrison, Jr.
With the high draft selection and the Hall of Fame pedigree, Harrison, Jr. was considered by most at the time to be a can't miss, generational wide receiver prospect after a stellar collegiate outing at Ohio State.
His rookie season in 2024, was good but not spectacular and questions began to pop up surrounding Harrison. His sophomore season had a rocky start, concerns about his catching and lack of effort starting to be raised among some but the year was cut short due to injury.
Harrison's 2026 did not get off on a stellar note, either. There were a few highlight catches but he still was not a featured part of the Cardinals offense and questions from fans and the national media reached a fever pitch in the past few weeks.
This all leads to the news that broke last Friday that the Cardinals had negotiated a trade for Harrison, but the details were initially kept close to the vest. On Sunday, we received the official news that he and a 7th round pick would be traded to the Houston Texans for a 2027 2nd and 6th.
Harrison now becomes the first former Top 5 wide receiver selection since Ahmad Rashad to be traded within the first three years of his career. interestingly, it was also the Cardinals that traded Rashad in 1974 to the Buffalo Bills for quarterback Dennis Shaw.
Harrison's trade means one big thing for the Cardinals going forward this season. The role of Michael Wilson as WR1 is now undisputed and the team will have to search through their wide receiver room to find some additional production alongside him and Kendrick Bourne, who has been a decent addition so far.
Part Two of this piece will address what I think has gone wrong with the Cardinals so far and where the team can go from here.

title: Cardinals, Texans Changed One Detail of Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Houston Texans have slightly changed the trade that will see Marvin Harrison Jr. depart the desert.
Initial reports indicated the Cardinals were sending Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick to Houston in exchange for a 2027 second and sixth-round pick.
However, updated terms have been revealed, and it's actually the Cardinals getting a seventh and Houston gaining a sixth.
It's not a massive change in return by any means, though the Cardinals still get a tad less value from the deal with Houston.
The trade is still pending a physical from Harrison, who was made inactive this weekend by Arizona.
Final, updated trade terms between Arizona and Houston, pending physical: 🏈Texans receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr. 2027 6th-round pick 🏈Cardinals receive: 2027 2nd-round pick 2027 7th-round pick pic.twitter.com/kmPih56iFd
The trade is expected to be finalized soon after being officially announced by the team.
Harrison had just five receptions on the season before being dealt to Houston over the weekend in what was surely the strangest sequence of events in recent trade history.
News broke Saturday morning of Harrison's trade, though nobody knew where Harrison was going or for what compensation until more details emerged Sunday as Arizona kicked off action against Detroit.
“Decisions like this are never easy,” said Cardinals General Manager Monti Ossenfort in a statement .
“Ultimately, we have to do what is best for our football team and that will always be the driving factor. We are extremely grateful to Marvin for what he has contributed to our organization and wish him the very best as he moves forward in his career.”
When speaking with reporters Monday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur says the trade wasn't a distraction for his team.
"I said yesterday, I'll double down on it — I don't think it was a distraction on Sunday," LaFleur said.
"I know it wasn't. Now, with that being said, Marv's a good buddy of theirs. Marv's a good guy. You guys all know that, you know Marv. So anytime you're losing a teammate, a good guy for the locker room, that's never obviously going to be easy. Some guys can be harder than others because they're close to him. But that wasn't the reason we didn't play well yesterday. There was no distraction with that. I firmly believe that. You'd have to ask them, but I firmly believe that."
Both the Cardinals and Texans are 1-4 after five weeks of play. Harrison now reunites with college quarterback C.J. Stroud in Houston.

title: Cardinals Fans Wanting Major Changes Get Disappointing Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals aren't making any major changes after dropping to 1-4 on the season.
Head coach Mike LaFleur addressed reporters today and declined any significant shake-ups following the team's 45-21 drubbing courtesy of the Detroit Lions in Week 5.
"No," said LaFleur when directly asked if any roles or play-calling duties were changing.
That means polarizing figures such as defensive coordinator Nick Rallis and starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett will be in their respective roles for another week. Arizona travels to play the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6.
Why is LaFleur confident in the current process working with his team?
"Because I've seen it, I just haven't seen it consistently," said LaFleur before diving into both sides of the ball.
"And again, I know we can help them with that consistency by providing the clarity, calling the right plays, both offense, defense, special teams. It's a 60-minute game, but the first three drives, our defense looked great. And I get what people are going to say in the first week and what's going on with the Chargers, but they did some really good stuff. There were moments in the Giants game, we forced the three turnovers. We get the four sacks, but we just haven't consistently done it for 60 minutes. And we need to tackle that.
"There's going to be no changes with play-callers, but we're looking at how to improve this defense and make sure that we are better than what we're putting out there. Better with the points, better just in totality. Because I do believe we have the right guys on defense to play better, and I told them that today. But we got to help them with that, whether that's providing the clarity, whether it's making it easier, what have you. And we got to dive into that hard over these next two days. And same thing on offense. When it's going good, it's going good — or it's a three-and-out machine, and there's really nowhere in between right now for us."
Cardinals fans are calling for Carson Beck to start, as the third-round rookie sits behind Brissett and Gardner Minshew on Arizona's depth chart. Brissett's performance on Sunday again was uninspiring and as losses pile up, the pressure to make a quarterback change will only grow.
LaFleur says that's not coming. Yet.
"If we think that's what's best, but haven't had those discussions. We'll end up having that discussion tomorrow at about noon," LaFleur said when asked about making Beck active on game days.
Earlier today, we wrote about LaFleur having the power to make changes to turn the tide of Arizona's season. While he was adamant sweeping changes were coming, he did hint at some different possibilities coming on the defensive side of the ball.
"Obviously, my job is to see the issues and handle the issues and have the tough conversations. So, if I felt like changes were needed for us to help us win this week, then I'm going to do that. It's my responsibility," LaFleur said.
"But I don't think that gives us the best chance to win this week. title: Cardinals GM Breaks Silence on Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have officially agreed to terms with the Houston Texans in a trade that will send Marvin Harrison Jr. out of the desert.
Arizona is sending Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 second and seventh-round selection. The trade initially was completed over the weekend but needed to be finalized with Harrison passing his physical.
Harrison, the Cardinals' former fourth overall pick in 2024, hadn't met the large expectations placed upon him through the full two seasons played in Arizona. He had just five receptions to begin 2026, and now the two sides go their separate ways.
“Decisions like this are never easy,” said Cardinals General Manager Monti Ossenfort in a statement after terms became final.
“Ultimately, we have to do what is best for our football team and that will always be the driving factor. We are extremely grateful to Marvin for what he has contributed to our organization and wish him the very best as he moves forward in his career.”
The Cardinals dropped to 1-4 after a thrashing to the Detroit Lions in Week 5, just over 24 hours after the Harrison news broke.
Head coach Mike LaFleur insisted it wasn't a distraction for the team in their 45-21 loss at State Farm Stadium.
"I really like Marvin Harrison. He's a good person. I wish him well. We did what we thought was in the best interest of the Cardinals," LaFleur said post-game.
"Any guy that does not play to the level that I feel like they're capable of, I'm always going to put that on me and coaching in general."
Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett added, "It's tough. It's a person we all have a relationship with outside of football. As much as everybody says the business is the business, that doesn't make it easy. That makes it toughest because it is part of the business. It's somebody I know I'll miss and a lot of guys in that locker room will miss. I'm sure a lot of us are rooting for Marv."
Harrison is now reunited with his former Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud in Houston, who just found their first win of the 2026 season after dominating the Tennessee Titans.
The Cardinals now move forward without Harrison in the mix, though Trey McBride and Michael Wilson will still anchor their passing attack moving into the rest of their schedule.

title: Cardinals Know Massive Change is Needed — It's Up to Mike LaFleur to Make Them
full_text:
Mike LaFleur hit his breaking point on Sunday night.
The Arizona Cardinals head coach — even in spite of losses — typically has maintained a positive attitude in post-game press conferences. A 1-3 record entering Week 5' s contest against the Detroit Lions previously had LaFleur wanting to trust the process he's banking his early head coaching career on.
Yet after a 45-21 thrashing from the Lions at State Farm Stadium, LaFleur's demeanor at the podium was different. He wasn't upset, or disappointed, he was pissed . If an artist sketched LaFleur's eight minutes talking to reporters, he'd have steam coming out of his ears.
Rightfully so. LaFleur saw his Cardinals' defense begin the game with three straight three-and-outs before being dog-walked by former Arizona offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. LaFleur's own side of the ball mustered a garbage time touchdown to creep past 20 points after a day of struggles in practically every way possible.
"Yes, obviously not good enough. I know we're better than that, but that doesn't mean shit right now because that's not what we did today," LaFleur said post-game. "I have to be better for these guys."
Changes have to be made across the board. LaFleur's done his best to stiff-arm the mob of angry Cardinals fans to begin the season, but Arizona's season has quickly slipped away.
The first likely change comes in the form of stripping defensive coordinator Nick Rallis of his duties. Arizona's defense has allowed four consecutive 30-point performances, and Sunday's 45-point performance from Rallis' unit might have been the cherry on top.
"There's a lot to fix right now and I respect the question. I understand that and I get it comes with the territory," LaFleur said when asked about making defensive changes.
"Right now my focus is me fixing everything and talking to these players, talking to these coaches and figuring out how this never ever happens again as long as I'm here."
The reality is unless changes are made, that could very well happen again — soon. The Cardinals are set to face all of the Rams (twice), Broncos, Cowboys, Seahawks and Chiefs in their next slate of games. Sean McVay's offense needs no introduction while the Chiefs, Cowboys and Seahawks are all top ten in scoring offense.
Case in point: the sledding is only going to get tougher. Arizona has senior defensive coach Teryl Austin waiting in the wings, who offers years of experience coordinating a defense. Now just might be time to pull that lever.
Offensively, the Cardinals have been far from what many had expected out of LaFleur's system. After trading away Marvin Harrison Jr. , the team's attack was limited to few big plays and scoring opportunities alike.
Many believe it's time to move on from starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, a passer who simply isn't producing results for Arizona. However, LaFleur was again quick to defend Brissett when prompted on making a change with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck in the wings.
"I have way too many other things that I need to correct right now. (QB) Jacoby (Brissett) was not the problem. We were a problem as a team today and again, that starts with me," LaFleur said.
It's admirable for a coach to deflect blame and not pin problems on any of his players. Pointing fingers during press conferences is what bad organizations do, and for as bad as the Cardinals currently are, there's hope that can change with LaFleur.
Yet LaFleur's willingness to back underperforming figures in the desert comes at a cost. This is the same song and dance that arguably got former head coach Jonathan Gannon fired last season, and while LaFleur's job isn't up for debate, failing to make changes when necessary is how you fast-track yourself to those conversations.
LaFleur's a smart coach with plenty of promise and potential. There's a reason he was hired in the first place, and to his credit, he's surrounded himself with veteran coaches on both sides of the ball. It's still in the first year, and LaFleur's had little time to establish his identity and put his fingerprints on personnel decisions.
Yet each loss that mounts for the Cardinals will only put more pressure on the organization to make changes. LaFleur's first season in charge wasn't meant to be judged by wins and losses, but if he doesn't demonstrate the ability to identify problems and address them, that leaves the door open for bigger picture conversations.

State Farm Stadium has been anything but "home sweet home" for the Cardinals lately. Through two home games, they have been outscored 28-to-76 (-48 point differential).

Arizona has struggled mightily on defense this season. Things did not improve on Sunday, as the Cardinals allowed a season-high 45 points.

Per Next Gen Stats, Jared Goff's 3.37s time to throw was his second-longest in a game this season. All three of his passing touchdowns came on throws over 2.5 seconds.
Against the Cardinals, Jared Goff completed 6-of-12 downfield passes (10+ air yards) for 152 yards and three touchdowns. Per Next Gen Stats, his three downfield touchdowns in Week 5 were a season-high.
The Cardinals' offense came out of the locker room sharp. On their opening drive of the game, Arizona orchestrated a 14-play, 73-yard scoring drive to take an early 7-0 lead. But the offense fell flat once again, going three-and-out on the next five offensive drives.

title: Falcons See Surprising Movement in Power Rankings Despite OT Loss to Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons let the Baltimore Ravens claw back into Sunday’s primetime showdown, surrendering 15 unanswered points in an overtime loss. As a result, the Falcons dropped to 2-3 and face another tough test against the Chicago Bears in Atlanta.
Michael Penix Jr.’s health will be at the center of discussions again this week after the Falcons’ quarterback suffered another injury that puts his availability in question.
Elsewhere in the division, the Panthers sat out this week, the Buccaneers stunned the Cowboys Thursday night, and the Saints continued their downward trajectory with a third straight loss. Falcons OnSI pulled the results from those sites and put them all in one place for fans. See below where the Falcons land compared with their division rivals.
The Falcons continued climbing Conor Orr’s power rankings despite losing to the Ravens in overtime, moving into the top spot in the NFC South. He cited Michael Penix Jr.'s presence as the biggest boon to the team and sent good vibes into the universe that the rib injury isn't serious.

Nick Shook still believes in what the Falcons can do, keeping them at No. 15 in his rankings. He said they're becoming an “imposing offensive force” with a “sneaky-good” defense. The hope is that Penix stays in the mix, which is why he sees the Falcons’ ceiling.

title: Where Do Atlanta Falcons Stand in NFC South after 5 Games?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons suffered a tough 30-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football, ending their two-game winning streak. Despite entering the matchup as one of the hottest teams in the NFL, Atlanta could not capitalize on several opportunities to secure a victory.
The Falcons had chances to put Baltimore away but struggled to finish drives and allowed the Ravens to complete a fourth quarter comeback. The defeat leaves Atlanta searching for answers as it looks to regain momentum in the NFC South race.
With Week 5 in the books, here is where the Falcons stand in the division.
Atlanta currently holds second place in the NFC South with a 2-3 record, sitting half a game behind the Carolina Panthers, who are 2-2 after taking their bye week in Week 5.
Carolina's position at the top gives the Panthers an early advantage in the division, but the Falcons remain within striking distance. Atlanta has shown flashes of being a competitive team this season, and a strong performance in Week 6 could help the team close the gap.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New Orleans Saints are tied behind Atlanta, with both teams holding 1-4 records. Neither team has found consistent success early in the season, leaving Carolina and Atlanta currently occupying the top two spots in the division.
For the Falcons, Sunday's loss was a missed opportunity to improve their record and put pressure on the Panthers. Instead, Atlanta must regroup and focus on getting back into the win column.
The Falcons will face the Chicago Bears in Week 6, giving them an opportunity to respond after their disappointing loss to Baltimore.
Carolina will travel to Philadelphia to take on the Eagles, while the Saints head to MetLife Stadium to face the New York Giants. The Buccaneers will host the Pittsburgh Steelers.
These matchups could have a direct impact on the NFC South standings. If Atlanta takes care of business against Chicago while Carolina struggles against Philadelphia, the Falcons would move into a tie with the Panthers for the division lead, but the Panthers would hold the head-to-head tiebreaker.
The NFC South has often featured competitive division races in recent seasons, and the current standings suggest another battle could develop between Atlanta and Carolina.
Although the Falcons are coming off a frustrating loss, they remain just half a game behind the division leader. The Buccaneers and Saints also have time to improve their positions, but both teams need to start stringing together victories.
Atlanta's immediate focus is getting back on track against Chicago. With the division still tightly contested, the Falcons have an opportunity to regain momentum and challenge Carolina for the top spot as the season progresses.

title: Divine Deablo Takes Ownership of Falcons Run Defense Struggles vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons entered Sunday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens with the NFL's top-ranked run defense, but they struggled to contain Derrick Henry and Baltimore's rushing attack.
The Ravens finished with 208 rushing yards on 35 carries, including 102 yards on 24 attempts from Henry, exposing weaknesses in a defense that had allowed just 48.3 rushing yards per game entering the contest.
Following the loss, linebacker Divine Deablo took responsibility for the disappointing performance, acknowledging that Atlanta must improve both individually and collectively.
"Defensively, we just got to do better job of stopping the run. Clearly, they had 200. I'll put that on me for real. For real. We got to be better as a whole, but I definitely got to be better myself," Deablo said.
Deablo reflected on the frustration of a defense that had established itself as one of Atlanta's biggest strengths early in the season.
Deablo pointed to one area that needs improvement from him.
"Sometimes trying to make a play. Getting out of my gap. I got to stay in my gap, make sure I do my job plus one," Deablo said.
Against a physical rushing attack like Baltimore's, maintaining gap integrity is critical. When defenders leave their assigned areas, it can create openings for offensive linemen to exploit and give running backs additional room to operate.
Deablo also explained the challenges of Atlanta's defensive scheme, which requires players to remain disciplined when defensive linemen move across the formation.
"We got, you know, we do different things sometimes. Sometimes we have movement. So, I'm imagining this guy is going to be here, but he might not make it over there. So, I just got to make sure I secure that gap before I make the move I want to make," Deablo said. "You secure your gap first and then go make a play."
That responsibility becomes especially important when offensive linemen climb to the second level and attempt to block linebackers. With defensive linemen focused on their individual gaps, linebackers must react quickly while maintaining their own assignments.
"Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Somebody's definitely climbing. So we got to, you know, secure our gap off of that climb and then still try to get to the ball. So, a little more challenging," Deablo said.
Deablo also evaluated Atlanta's efforts to contain Derrick Henry.
"For the most part, we did a great job [forcing Derrick Henry back inside]. We had a few mishaps where he got to our corner. But overall pretty good," Deablo said.
Despite those challenges, Deablo emphasized that execution remains the most important factor.
"We had plenty of opportunities to make a play and we just didn't. So, at the end of the day, we just got to do our job," Deablo said.
Atlanta's performance against Baltimore was a significant setback for a defense that had been effective at limiting opposing rushing attacks. Moving forward, the Falcons must improve their gap discipline, execute their assignments and take advantage of opportunities to bring down ball carriers.
It won't take long to see if their corrections work, because they face the Chicago Bears and their No. 1-ranked rushing offense on Sunday .

title: Drake London has Massive Numbers with Michael Penix Jr. at QB, and He Doesn't Care
full_text:
This offseason, Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London signed a massive contract extension that made him the third-highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL on a per-year basis at $35.3 million.
Like the rest of the team, London had trouble getting out of first gear during the first two weeks of the season with Cooper Rush at quarterback. He had 6 catches for 70 yards in the two losses.
Michael Penix Jr. returned at quarterback for Week 3 against the Green Bay Packers, and London had 21 catches for 408 yards in the next three games, including 118 on Sunday night against the Ravens.
This isn't anything new for London and Penix. The Athletic's Josh Kendall asked London how aware he was that his numbers improved dramatically with Penix as his on-again, off-again quarterback the last three seasons.
"I mean, I'm a little bit aware that they go up, but nothing too crazy right now. I'm just worried about W's at the moment," London answered.
They don't just go up; they skyrocket. 15 starts for Penix, and London has 103 catches and 1,570 yards in those games, not all of which Penix finished. Extrapolated across 17 games, London would have 117 catches and 1,779 yards.
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2025 with 119 catches, 1,793 yards, and 10 touchdowns. London's production is almost identical.
Rams wide receiver Pika Nacua was second in receiving yards with 1,715. No one else had more than 1,429.
When asked if the numbers themselves surprised him, London remained humble.
"I mean a little bit," London answered.
"I just try to go out there and catch the ball if it comes my way," London said. "If I get opportunities and stuff, I try to make the best of them and do whatever is best for the team. The numbers, that's just like a cherry on top type of situation.
"Nothing really changes. We're going in there, and we're striving for greatness. We're striving to get better every day, every hour, and just come out there and be ready for Sunday's game against a very, very good Chicago team."
Penix is day-to-day this week after suffering a rib injury against the Ravens. Falcons fans and London fantasy football owners hope it's Penix behind center on Sunday against the Chicago Bears.
Lost in the numbers is London's blocking ability. Not only is he one of the most productive receivers in the NFL, he's one of the best blockers at his position.
Many around the league who ignore the playoff-less Falcons questioned the big contract extension to London, but few who watch him play every day had those concerns.

title: Chicago Bears Offense Could Provide Even Bigger Challenge to Falcons Than Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons entered their matchup against the Baltimore Ravens with the NFL’s No. 1 run defense, allowing just 48.3 rushing yards per game.
However, Baltimore exposed weaknesses in Atlanta’s defensive front, rushing for 208 yards on 35 carries and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt.
Derrick Henry led the way with 102 rushing yards and added a receiving touchdown on a screen pass, helping Baltimore control the line of scrimmage and win in Atlanta. For a Falcons defense that had been dominant against the run entering Sunday night, it was a significant step backward.
Atlanta’s struggles were particularly evident during Baltimore’s overtime drive. The Ravens ran for 45 yards on the ground during the possession, wearing down the Falcons’ defensive front as they moved down the field. After spending much of the game trying to contain Henry and Baltimore’s rushing attack, Atlanta struggled to get the necessary stops when it mattered most.
Falcons defensive lineman Gervon Dexter acknowledged that improving against the run is essential.
“We got to stop the run to get the pass rush, so we want to get more of those opportunities. We got to do a better job at stopping the run,” Dexter said.
Baltimore’s success on early downs made it hard for Atlanta to dictate the game's terms defensively. The Ravens consistently gained positive yardage, keeping the Falcons from focusing on pressuring the quarterback and adding strain to the defensive front as the game progressed.
Dexter also recognized the challenge of containing Henry, whose ability to finish runs can make him especially dangerous late in games.
“Obviously, he’s a good player. You got to stop his feet, get him behind the line of scrimmage, and make a play on him. He’s one of those players in a long time where he can, like you say, finish those games. So we knew we had to try to get him down there,” Dexter said.
The challenge does not get any easier for Atlanta over the next two weeks. The Falcons’ next two opponents, the Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers, both rank among the NFL’s top 10 rushing offenses.

The performance exposed an area that needs immediate attention, especially with two productive rushing offenses coming up on the schedule.
Atlanta has already shown it can be one of the league’s best run defenses. Now, after Henry and the Ravens wore them down, the Falcons must return to that standard before their upcoming opponents exploit the same weaknesses.

title: Michael Penix Jr. Injury Update: Adam Schefter Provides Latest on Falcons QB
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. had a rough start and finish to the team's 30-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football.
He started the game 0-5 and took until midway through the second quarter to complete his first pass. He finished with a towel over his head as he watched Tua Tagovailoa take the field in overtime after suffering a rib injury on a hit in the backfield.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday afternoon that the rib injury isn't considered to be a problem for Penix long-term, but that doesn't mean he'll be suiting up against the Chicago Bears on Sunday.
"Michael Penix’s rib injury is not considered serious, per sources. Penix might be able to return for Sunday’s game vs. the Bears, but the team wants to be cautious and see him practice this week before it knows whether he will be able to play in Week 6," Schefter reported on X .
Bookending the start and finish of the Ravens game was a fantastic performance from Penix. The Ravens had sold out to stop Bijan Robinson and the Falcons' rushing attack, and Penix made them pay.
On Atlanta's first offensive touchdown drive, Penix went 5 of 5 passing and finished it with a touchdown pass to Kyle Pitts Sr. He finished the game 19 of 32 passing for 240 yards and a touchdown.
Along the way, Penix showed off the howitzer of a left arm that made him the No. 8 overall pick in 2024. On four separate occasions, he converted third-and-10 or more yards with long passes, and Drake London was his favorite target.
London finished the game with seven catches for 118 yards, his third straight 100-yard game with Penix as the starting quarterback.
If there was a chink in his armor, other than another injury, Penix struggled on bootleg passes that required a touch pass over a defender. One such occasion cost the Falcons a touchdown, and while offensive tackle Jake Matthews will feel he probably should have made the catch, Penix would probably say he could have made it easier with better placement and touch.
Another occasion saw Bijan Robinson open in the backfield, but Penix left it short with a defender pressuring him. Robinson had a lot of green turf in front of him had the pass been on target.
That said, there's no question Penix put the team on his back for more than two quarters as Atlanta couldn't find a running game en route to a 23-15 lead. The Falcons hope he will be healthy enough to start on Sunday against the Chicago Bears.
If not, Tua Tagovailoa could get the start he was scheduled to make in Week 1 after injuring an oblique three days before the opener in Pittsburgh.

title: Why the Falcons’ OT Loss to Ravens Could Be Wake-Up Call They Need
full_text:
For two weeks, the Atlanta Falcons were riding high on back-to-back wins over the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints .
The team was playing some inspired football behind the Week 3 return of starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. , a reimagined offense after a disastrous first two weeks of the season, alongside a shutdown defense that earned high statistical marks across the NFL.
But the inevitable happened – the Falcons took a loss.
And it may be for the better.
“It’s heartbreaking to an extent,” said Atlanta cornerback Billy Bowman Jr.
“I know this team is going to bounce back, and the feeling in the building is getting back to work, focus on next week, and overcome this lesson.”
On Sunday Night Football, Atlanta (2-3) suffered a rare primetime game loss to the Baltimore Ravens (4-1). Baltimore visited Atlanta and left with a 30-23 Week 5 overtime win .
The Falcons led 17-9 midway through the third quarter, but were outscored 21-6 for the rest of the night. Backup quarterback Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley, replacing the injured Lamar Jackson , scored a one-yard sneak to take the overtime lead after nearly eight minutes of the 10-minute overtime period.
With Penix out of the game with a rib injury sustained from a hit by Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson as time expired in regulation, Tua Tagovailoa came in to take it home.
That he did, after a 20-yard gain to wide receiver Drake London . Then, Tagovailoa in fact did take it home by tossing a game-sealing interception to Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton.
“Obviously, we didn’t do enough to win that game. Really missed opportunities,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski recapped the loss. “When you’re playing a good football team, and these margins are razor-thin, we’ve got to come through on some of those plays. We can be better in those moments. Disappointing, frustrating,  but we will learn from it.”
A culprit in the Falcons’ loss was struggling to stop the Baltimore rushing attack, as running back Derrick Henry led with 102 rushing yards, contributing to a 208-yard effort on the ground. The Falcons entered the game with the NFL’s top run defense .
Falcons running back Bijan Robinson eclipsed 100 scrimmage yards but was fairly neutralized.
“It’s just one game. It doesn’t define us,” Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. said. “We’ll get back to the drawing board and get these details right for next week.”
A Sunday positive was Atlanta’s ability to lean on Penix without its fine-tuned run game. The quarterback went 19-for-32 for 240 yards and threw a touchdown pass. London and Pitts were heavily involved in the offense.
Defensively, the defense showed it can get on the scoreboard as safety Jesse Bates III returned a 30-yard fumble recovery after safety Sydney Brown punched the football out of the hands of Ravens tight end Mark Andrews.
“We’re going to be good. It’s one game,” Penix reacted to the Falcons’ loss to the Ravens. “Obviously, it’s a game we felt like we could’ve won – we should’ve won. Whenever you get a chance to close out a game with a good team like that, you’ve got to do it. But we’re good with where we’re at. The loss sucks, but we’ve got to be ready for next week.”
So, in the loss, Atlanta has some building blocks moving forward in the season.
And now the Falcons are humbled entering another home game against the Chicago Bears in the potential return of quarterback Caleb Williams, who’s been out since Week 1 with a grade two right hamstring strain.
And the best thing about it is that Atlanta is still in play for the NFC South, holding on to the No. 2 spot behind the Carolina Panthers and ahead of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Saints.

title: Falcons' Missed Opportunities Prove Costly in Overtime Loss to Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons had several opportunities to put away the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football, but missed chances on offense and costly mistakes on special teams ultimately contributed to a heartbreaking 30-23 overtime loss.
Atlanta held a late lead and appeared positioned to secure its third consecutive prime time victory. However, the Falcons struggled to turn favorable field position into touchdowns, missed multiple opportunities to score and allowed Baltimore to capitalize when the game was on the line.
For a team that had played well enough to put itself in position to win, the inability to finish drives proved costly.
One of Atlanta's biggest issues was its inability to capitalize on opportunities inside Baltimore territory. The Falcons repeatedly moved into scoring range but settled for Nick Folk field goals instead of touchdowns, keeping the Ravens within striking distance.
The missed opportunities were particularly frustrating because Atlanta had chances to create a two-possession advantage and put additional pressure on Baltimore. Instead, the Ravens remained in the game long enough to mount a late comeback.
One of the most memorable moments came in the third quarter when Atlanta attempted a red zone trick play. Matthews reported as an eligible receiver and became the intended target on a pass from Michael Penix Jr.
The play had the potential to catch Baltimore off guard and produce a critical touchdown. However, Penix's pass sailed over Matthews, resulting in an incompletion and another missed scoring opportunity.
Here is the pass to Matthews. Penix throws him open but ball goes through his hands. #Falcons pic.twitter.com/6FbtFJZvlM
Rather than adding seven points to its lead, Atlanta failed to execute a creative play that could have changed the complexion of the game.
The Falcons also committed three costly special teams penalties, disrupting field position and creating additional challenges for the offense. Against a Baltimore team capable of generating explosive plays, those mistakes made it even more difficult for Atlanta to establish control.
Falcons offensive lineman Chris Lindstrom acknowledged that Atlanta could put the game away but failed to take advantage.
“Just that when you have an opportunity to put a team away, you gotta do it. And we didn’t do that. And so we gave them an opportunity, and what great teams do is they take advantage of it,” Lindstrom said.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski shared a similar assessment of the team's performance.
“Credit to Baltimore,” Stefanski said. “Obviously we didn't do enough to win that game. We had missed opportunities, and when you're playing a good football team, the margins are razor thin like we knew they would be; we've got to come through on some of those plays.”
Despite Atlanta's missed opportunities, the Falcons still had a chance to secure the victory late in regulation. Baltimore instead drove 71 yards in six plays, with Tyler Huntley connecting with Devontez Walker for a touchdown with 40 seconds remaining. Derrick Henry then scored on a direct snap for the two-point conversion to tie the game at 23.
Atlanta's defense could not produce the stop needed to preserve the lead, sending the contest into overtime.
The Falcons also lost Penix to a rib injury late in regulation, forcing backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa to take over. Baltimore scored on its opening overtime possession when Huntley crossed the goal line on a one-yard quarterback sneak.
Tagovailoa then threw an interception to Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton, ending Atlanta's hopes of responding.
The loss was a reminder that winning against quality opponents requires more than simply creating opportunities. Atlanta had chances to extend its lead, finish scoring drives and deliver a decisive defensive stop, but failed to do enough in critical moments.
The Falcons will now prepare for the Chicago Bears, who rank first in the NFL in rushing yards per game. Atlanta must clean up its mistakes and become more efficient in the red zone if it hopes to rebound. Against Baltimore, the opportunities were there. The execution needed to finish the job was not.

title: Michael Penix Jr. Reveals Why He Couldn't Return for Falcons in Overtime
full_text:
ATLANTA – Michael Penix Jr. sat on the Atlanta Falcons sideline, towel draped over his head, as Tua Tagovailoa threw a game-clinching interception.
For the first time in 329 days, Penix had returned to the field where he tore his ACL. But as the Falcons tried to claw their way down the field with the fourth quarter ticking away, he found himself walking off it with yet another injury.
Penix, whose Falcons led the Ravens in prime time for nearly the entire game, took a big hit from Tavius Robinson. He left the field after the training staff tended to him, but returned for one play before the Falcons were forced to punt, sending the game into overtime.
Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed Penix suffered a rib injury, something the oft-injured quarterback struggled with in college, but he could not comment on its severity. The quarterback will get imaging to better assess the extent of his ailment on Monday, but Penix said it is too soon to know if there are any similarities between his issues in college and what he has now.
“It’s frustrating, but the biggest thing is I want to be out there, especially in a big moment in a game like that,” the quarterback said. “I felt like I needed to be out there.”
Penix said afterward he did not feel the injury would be a long-term issue for him and even believed there was a chance he could have returned in overtime. Had the Falcons started with the ball, he expected to lead the offense back onto the field.
Instead, he felt his body get “cold” during the Ravens’ 14-play touchdown drive that sucked 7:03 off the clock. He tried to fight through the pain, but he wasn’t where he needed to be health-wise to go back out onto the field.
“I did not feel like I was going to be able to give our team what we needed to be able to help us win that football game, because of the pain I was feeling,” Penix said. “As I was sitting there, what I was going through, it started getting worse and worse.”
Sunday was a frustrating development for a Falcons team that had felt it had turned a corner with Penix under center. For at least three quarters, it felt like they would keep rolling. Penix didn’t complete a pass until the Falcons’ fourth possession, but he took off after that point. He started 0-of-4, but completed 19 of his next 28 passes for 240 yards and a touchdown, with 13 of those 19 completions going for either a first down or a touchdown.
Penix was especially effective when the Falcons needed him most, finishing 9-of-15 for 163 yards and a touchdown on third down, the most completions and yards in a game in his career. He found wide receiver Drake London five times in those situations, and he connected with his favorite target for 86 of his 118 receiving yards on third down.
London was one of six Falcons to catch a pass, and with Penix as its conductor, the offense was humming. Atlanta held a lead for nearly the entire game and was building on their positive momentum from the two previous weeks.
By all appearances, Sunday was set to continue the Falcons' offensive success from their last two weeks, until it wasn’t, and that momentum came crashing down after a single hit to the ribs.
The Falcons had chances to put Baltimore away on Sunday night, and this loss goes beyond a fourth-quarter quarterback injury. The defense faltered late, allowing Derrick Henry and the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens to pile up 200 yards on the ground, while the offense missed far too many opportunities in key moments.
“There are plays that we can make; there are calls that we can give our guys to be better,” Stefanski said. “In a game like that, all those little plays add up to being a big play.”
But for Penix and this team, this is all the NFL world will be talking about. Just two games after returning from a torn ACL, the quarterback is back in the training room, with his immediate future in question.
“I just pray he's alright,” running back Bijan Robinson said. “I know the whole team does.”
Still, he remains confident that he will be out there for his team next Sunday when the Chicago Bears come to town.
“Knowing me, I’m going to be ready to go next week,” Penix said, “because I’ve sat out enough in my career.”

title: Falcons Winners & Losers After Blown Second-Half Lead Against Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons lose a tough overtime game to the Baltimore Ravens, 30-23, in a tightly contested matchup at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Atlanta showed flashes of its potential on both sides of the ball, with several players stepping up in key moments while others struggled to capitalize on opportunities. With impressive individual performances and areas for improvement, here are the winners and losers from the Falcons’ Week 5 game against the Ravens.
Jessie Bates III was one of Atlanta’s biggest defensive standouts, making his presence felt throughout the game. The veteran safety helped the Falcons' defense deliver a critical takeaway after Sydney Brown punched the ball out, and Bates recovered it and returned it for a touchdown.
It marked Bates’ fifth defensive touchdown, but all four of his previous touchdowns came on interception returns.
Bates also made a crucial play on Baltimore’s first second-half two-point attempt, breaking up Tyler Huntley’s pass after the Ravens scored on a screen to Derrick Henry. His ability to make game-changing plays in multiple phases of the defense was instrumental in Atlanta’s effort.
Whether creating turnovers or preventing points, Bates continues to demonstrate why he is one of the most important players on Atlanta’s defense.
Atlanta’s defensive front deserves recognition for its ability to pressure the quarterback and disrupt Baltimore’s offensive rhythm. The Falcons recorded four sacks, with Kendal Daniels, Samson Ebukam and Jared Ivey each contributing one. Zach Harrison and Cameron Thomas combined for another half sack.
The defensive front also generated 8 quarterback hits and consistent pressure, making life difficult for Huntley. Brandon Dorlus was particularly disruptive, applying pressure throughout the game.
Atlanta’s ability to generate pressure created opportunities for the secondary to make plays, including the defensive touchdown that helped Bates reach the end zone.
Although Baltimore found some success on the ground, the Falcons’ pass rush showed how disruptive this unit can be when it consistently wins at the line of scrimmage. The defensive front remains one of Atlanta’s biggest strengths moving forward.
Drake London and Kyle Pitts provided two of Atlanta's biggest offensive bright spots, giving the passing game much-needed production.
London led the Falcons with seven receptions for 116 yards, doing much of his damage on third down. His ability to move the chains and deliver in critical situations helped Atlanta sustain drives and create opportunities downfield. London remains a reliable target for quarterback Michael Penix Jr., particularly when the offense needs to convert in high-pressure situations.
Pitts also delivered an encouraging performance, finishing with five catches for 42 yards and a touchdown. His scoring reception appeared to involve a ball that went through tight end Austin Hooper's hands before Pitts secured it for the touchdown.
Pitts’ red-zone production was particularly valuable, while London’s third-down production highlighted his importance to Atlanta’s passing attack.
The Falcons need consistent contributions from their receiving corps to complement their rushing game. London’s production and Pitts’ touchdown were positive developments, giving Atlanta two players capable of making a significant impact through the air.
After an outstanding game from the Falcons’ quarterback, Ravens defender Tavius Robinson hit him and forced a fumble. Penix returned to the field one play later but did not return for overtime.
Instead, Tua Tagovailoa threw an interception that ended the game.
Atlanta's biggest concern was its inability to stop Baltimore from breaking off several significant gains on the ground. The Ravens finished with 208 rushing yards on 35 carries, averaging 5.9 yards per attempt.
Justice Hill delivered one of the game's most damaging plays when he broke loose for a 47-yard run in the second half that set up a TD. Derrick Henry also had a big day, totaling 102 yards on 24 carries.
While Atlanta made important stops, those explosive runs let Baltimore gain chunks of yardage without consistently sustaining long drives. The Ravens also used their passing game's versatility, with Henry scoring on a screen pass from Huntley in the second half.
The gut-punch came on the overtime possession, when the Ravens rumbled downfield for the go-ahead touchdown. A gassed Falcons defense couldn't slow Henry and that rushing attack, which accounted for nine carries on the 14-play drive.
The production is particularly concerning because Atlanta entered the matchup with the NFL’s No. 1 run defense. Allowing that many yards is a significant challenge for a unit that had established itself as one of the league’s best at stopping the run.
The Falcons did show flashes of strong run defense, but limiting explosive plays must become a priority. Better tackling, gap discipline, and execution will be necessary to keep opposing offenses from consistently creating big gains.
Zachariah Branch had a disappointing day in terms of his opportunities to impact the game. The rookie had not recorded a punt return, limiting his chances to change field position on special teams.
His offensive involvement also included a costly negative screen pass that resulted in an eight-yard loss. He later caught a 23-yard screen pass, the longest gain of his career.
Branch possesses the speed and explosiveness to become a difference maker, but Atlanta needs to find ways to maximize those abilities while avoiding negative plays
The Falcons will need to be more deliberate in their use of Branch moving forward, particularly when attempting to get the ball into his hands in space.
Jake Matthews experienced a difficult moment during his 200th career start. The veteran offensive tackle missed a touchdown opportunity, marking his first missed touchdown of the game, according to game observations.
Jake Matthews Dropped The Open Big Man Touchdown 😂 That’s A Miss. 😬 pic.twitter.com/HDCzVqdIYV
Matthews has been one of Atlanta’s most dependable offensive linemen, making the moment all the more notable. Reaching 200 starts is a significant milestone, but the missed opportunity overshadowed part of what should have been a memorable occasion.
One mistake does not diminish Matthews’ overall body of work or his importance to Atlanta’s offensive line. However, the Falcons need to capitalize on scoring opportunities, especially in a matchup where possessions and momentum can shift quickly.

title: Calais Campbell Made History And Honored Late Mother With Ravens In Week 5
full_text:
The last time Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell was in the state of Georgia before the team's Week 5 game against the Atlanta Falcons was in the wake of unspeakable tragedy for him and his family.
In late June, about a month before the six-time Pro Bowler was slated to report to his 19th and what he believes will have been the final training camp of his illustrious Hall of Fame-worthy career, his mother, Nateal Campbell, was found slain at her Buckhead townhouse in Atlanta during a welfare check.
To make matters even worse, his older brother, Ciarre Campbell, was arrested at the scene and charged with murder after police found him in possession of a knife.
Sunday would've been the former matriarch of the family's 72nd birthday. Instead of being celebrated on the same day her son was slated to pass NFL legend Jim Marshall for the record for most games ever played by a defensive lineman from a suite or somewhere in the stands at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, she was watching over him from further above. Yet, he still felt her presence as the battle-tested Ravens rallied to beat his former team 30-23 in overtime .
"I just wanted to play my heart out for my mom today." Calais Campbell talked about honoring his mother in last night's victory. 💜 pic.twitter.com/Z2yKgSKyPS
"It felt really good. I just wanted to play my heart out for my mom today [and] honor her," Campbell said. "I felt like I achieved that goal. I left it all on the field today."
Before the game, he wore a memorial shirt in her honor with pictures of her on it, and with his siblings in attendance.
Calais Campbell with a loving pregame tribute to his late mother, Nateal: “She would’ve been here, celebrating loud as can be. … I’m just grateful that I had a wonderful mother.” Calais will set the NFL record for games played by a DL tonight, breaking a tie with Jim Marshall… pic.twitter.com/REKLY1wIna
"She would've been here celebrating loud as can be, getting hype, telling me to go out there and make some plays," Campbell said in a video tribute on Instagram. "I'm just grateful that I had a wonderful mother for all the years I had her."
The 40-year-old expressed even greater gratitude after the game when his teammates came through on what was a very special yet still somber day for him and the whole Campbell family.
"I feel really good to honor my mom today and I am really happy that we got a win," Campbell said. "I know a lot of the guys were trying to get a win because they knew how much this meant to me, and I am very grateful."
It's one thing to hang in and bounce around the league for a decade plus, but to do what Campbell has been able to pull off in his late 30s and officially his 40s as of Sept. 1, is nothing short of spectacular.
Despite nearly two decades on the job, he continued to show he is still one of the best interior disruptors in the game in  Week 5 against the Falcons, the team he signed with after his first stint with the Ravens ended.
"I really did not make a whole lot of plays, but I felt like I was playing some of my best football of my career, in spurts," Campbell said.
Humility is another one of the honorable traits that the team captain and former Walter Payton Man Of The Year award recipient possesses. However, he sold himself short when recalling the plays and significant contributions he made to the best performance by the Ravens' revamped defense of the season in his 283rd career game.
Atop the record books. Calais Campbell has now played more games than any defensive lineman in NFL history. pic.twitter.com/JzO3AmaEwh
Campbell played 50% or more of the Ravens' total defensive snaps in a game for the third time this season and helped fellow multi-time Pro Bowler and his former mentee, Nnadmdi Madubuike lead the charge in stifling what had been a juggernaut of a Falcons' rushing attack the previous two weeks. He recorded a pair of total tackles, both of which were solos, including one that went for a loss. His overall grade of 85.1 was the highest given to a Ravens player on either side of the ball.
Calais Campbell is still a dawg in his 283rd career NFL game. pic.twitter.com/QwXOk1ZAAy
"It is hard to even explain just the work that [Campbell] puts in, how he goes about his business, the pro that he is, how he makes everybody around him better," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I know he was dealing with some, obviously, emotional thoughts and things, playing in Atlanta [on] his mom's birthday.
"I mean, [it is] pretty amazing. It was really cool to see the guys have his back, I would say, and know that that meant a lot to him without him having to say anything about it. [I] just feel very blessed to be around Calais and have him on our team, and him be the leader that he is and impacting our team the way that he is, both on the field, obviously, and in the locker room."

title: Ravens Head Coach's Words And Actions Indicate This About Lamar Jackson's Status
full_text:
The Ravens have one of the best records in the NFL while having to workshop around a multitude of personnel and injury issues and face a significant upgrade in level of competition starting in Week 7.
This week presents another unique challenge for rookie head coach Jesse Minter as he prepares for his first AFC North game, on the road at Cleveland, with his offensive line likely to be reshuffled for the sixth-straight week and with quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status in limbo with an ankle injury and his practice time almost surely to be compromised. Now is not the time to deviate from the overarching medical approach that has served Baltimore well during its 4-1 start, and backup Snoop Huntley was excellent in the clutch Sunday night.
There is a strong case to be made for taking no risks with Jackson unless he is able to practice fully at least by Thursday, and a multitude of sound reasons why erring on the side of caution at this point in the season – for a team in Super Bowl or bust mode – makes all the sense in the world. And Minter seems to understand as much. The Ravens have taken the longview with other star players and even in the way the coach spoke Monday about his two-time MVP quarterback it was clear to the discerning ear that he is going out of his way not to raise expectations to the level where his return is anything close to guaranteed.
“Definitely doing better,” Minter said of his superstar QB. “Wednesday, I am not sure about exactly how that practice will look, but again, to Lamar's credit, he is doing everything he can to get back out there. I thought he was awesome (on sidelines Sunday night). There are a lot of cool pictures and clips of him on the sideline in between series talking to Snoop' and hyping guys up.
“What a wonderful teammate and leader that he is, even when he was not playing. So, I am very, very proud of Lamar for handling himself like that, and again he is doing everything he can. I think we will know more definitely by the middle of the week.”
Here’s why we wouldn’t be surprised at all is Jackson came back Week 7 against the Bengals:
The fact Minter made Wednesday sound that murky tells me Jackson isn’t practicing fully to open the week and if Huntley looks good in practice and if Jackson is likely to be limited on Thursday, then should we just devote all the snaps to Snoop and let Lamar take over the following week? With all the offensive line shake-ups are we going to throw multiple QBs into the mix?
Minter leaving things that open ended, and the fact that Jackson was ruled out last Friday and there was no real emphasis put on his pre-game training and work, tends to point to a multi-week absence. This is a team that was very cautious with Zay Flowers early this season and waiting longer with Nnamdi Madubuike’s return from neck surgery than they might have to try to get him back to close to normal, every-snap form before activating him. They brought in a new sports science team headed by former New Zealand rugby trainer Dr. Nic Gill in the offseason to try to rethink their approach to some of this stuff.
Even the call to have newly-signed, $30M/year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson get a procedure on his finger that would take him out at least two weeks spoke to them taking a long-term view with potential lingering issues for key players in September/October given how this franchise’s success is measured in January.
The Ravens appear to be in quite the hurry to try someone else at center now – this will be center No. 4 since the start of the regular season – after paying a very steep price to land offensive lineman Cam Jurgens from the Eagles last week in a very risky acquisition . But he was in the concussion protocol when they landed him and was never going to practice last week or play in Week 5.
A player returning to play must go through a battery of sessions off the field and then full work off the side and then come through that okay and be cleared to eventually return to full practices. How will all of this sync up with Jackson also being able to practice anything close to full enough to actually get to practice with this new center before he can play? The idea that Jackson could do nothing all week and then get cleared after a glorified walk-thru and play a game Sunday with a center he has literally never worked with before is quite a stretch.
Remember it’s not like Jurgens has been here for practices and training camps and OTAs before. He just got here. Now, don’t get me wrong, I am more than fine with sticking with Vega Ioane at center – and I am far from convinced that Jurgens is some big immediate upgrade from how that rookie was performing brand new to the center position – but we know how it works and they got Jurgens to impact them right away (it wreaked of a level of desperation likely not warranted ).
But these timelines might not align with also making a late QB switch over the weekend.
Jackson in general needs to feel very good about his body and how fine tuned he is to play at the genius levels where he operates. And while the Browns have very good talent in key defensive spots, the Ravens play a top-five schedule from here on out in terms of quality of opponent defense.
From Week 7 on, the Ravens play six straight teams that went to the playoffs in 2025 ahead of their bye the first week of December. Their season is going to come down to the final four games, invaribly – all AFC North contests – and for all that Huntley brings, having to try to get into the playoffs with him in the dead of winter unable to push the ball downfield isn’t going to work … like it didn’t work last season.
It would make sense for Jackson to truly test himself in practice on mutliple occasionsl before I’d play him this week, and the Ravens are already sending signals that might not be how the work week plays out.

title: Three Ways Ravens Rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane Can Boost Ravens Offense
full_text:
The Ravens should be getting rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane back at the perfect time.
They could certainly use him.
The “Zay And Pray” offense remains very real for the Ravens , with top receiver Zay Flowers continuing to carry an extremely heavy load in the pass game and even being asked to chip in more now in the run game with backup Snoop Huntley in for Lamar Jackson last week and the offensive line constantly reshuffled due to injury and ineffectiveness.
Baltimore could badly use a new element to be folded into the passing attack no matter who the quarterback is Sunday at Cleveland, and there is reason to believe Lane could return soon enough as he is eligible to leave Injured Reserve with the four-week minimum absence now complete. The wrist surgery did not preclude him from getting in cardio and trying to keep his conditioning base, though it remains to be seen if he requires more than a week of practice to be cleared to play.
Lane played only one half of the Week 1 game at the Colts before suffering the injury, curbing the momentum he took into the season after a dominant summer in training camp and the preseason games. The Ravens released veteran receiver Chris Moore on Tuesday - he'll sign to the practice squad soon enough - creating a spot on the active roster for Lane.
“Ja'Kobi has done a really good job,” Minter said. “I would say sometimes, when you are going through an injury and you are on IR, how much can you do physically to be ready to play, to your point, that first week back?
“I think he is in a really good place from a conditioning standpoint, from what he has been able to do with the training room and the rehab standpoint. So, we will see how that shakes out on Wednesday.”
There are some immediate ways Lane can contribute.
Flowers has been an absolute beast in the slot, but the guy getting the second-most run there, tight end Mark Andrews, can’t move or separate and is looking each week more like a sunk cost . Flowers has 318 receiving yards in the slot and a gaudy 16 yards/catch. The rest of the team have combined for 248 yards in the slot on 12.4/catch.
Lane was doing a lot of his damage in the preseason in the slot , especially on crossers and working the middle of the field, where at 6-4 he is a great compliment to Flowers, who is smaller and shiftier. And having the big target in the slot who can separate and capitalize on a large catch radius is even more important as the field gets constricted in the …
This was a major area of concern a year ago, with Baltimore 27th in redzone passing. So far this season Jackson has been an expert in this part of the field and he and Huntley have found six different pass catchers on redzone TDs (all with one each(.
Lane’s body type is a natural to do damage and he is slithery and can leave his feet to make a play. Jackson had a lot of success throwing to former move tight Isaiah Likely in this areas the last few years and no doubt the Ravens had replacing some of that stuff when they took Lane in the third round.
There really isn’t anyone doing anything on this team in this regard except for Flowers. Lane and fellow rookie Matthew Hibner are their best chances to start changing that.
Flowers is first on the team with 182 yards after the catch; running back Derrick Henry is second at 97, astoundingly for a guy who rarely gets targeted. Flowers has done that in basically playing the equivalent of three games considering injury absences. Rashod Bateman is second on the team in YAC among receivers with a paltry 52 in five games.
Lane should be able to offset that wide divide even if his opportunities are fairly limited as he works back into the offense. Jackson loves big targets and has his highest passer rating throwing to tight end and Lane can certainly work a lot of areas on the field that Andrews did before he fell off.
