title: Unsung Heroes From The Ravens’ Week 5 Win Over Falcons
full_text:
In Week 5, the Baltimore Ravens came out on top in their first primetime game of the season with a 30-23 overtime victory over the previously surging Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football. While they were one of three AFC North teams to emerge victorious this past week, since the Cleveland Browns were the only ones who didn't, they now sit alone atop the division standings at 4-1.
In a game where they came in not favored to win with their star quarterback and pass rusher out , the Ravens never led at any point during regulation and mounted an impressive late rally to earn their third straight win.
The Ravens were able to secure the victory thanks to some underrated yet impactful performances from a handful of well-known starters and some of their less-heralded players making plays in all three phases of the game.
Going up against the top-ranked defense in the league in terms of applying pressure and stopping the run, this unit held up in pass protection when it mattered most and imposed its will when it came to run-blocking. The Falcons went from allowing 193 rushing yards in their first four games combined to letting the Ravens rack up a season-high 208 yards in one night, and the big boys in the trenches deserve just as much, if not even more, credit as the stars of the game such as backup quarterback Tyler Huntley and running back Derrick Henry.
Two players who deserve special recognition for their performance and grit are rookie interior lineman Olaivavega Ioane and third-year right tackle Roger Rosengarten. The first-round offensive guard was stellar in his second straight start at center, aside from a couple of off-target snaps, and Rosengarten showed some excellent situational awareness after briefly leaving the game when he wisely leapt out of his stance when a Falcons defensive player jumped into the neutral zone before the snap. In doing so, he drew five-yard penalties on two separate occasions, and while that might not sound like a big deal, when mounting a comeback while short-handed on the road, every inch and yard counts and can be the difference between being on the outskirts or just within comfortable field goal range.
On the other side of the ball, the Ravens faced another tall task with a second-ranked rushing attack through four weeks and one of the best pass-protecting offensive lines in the league. After a shaky start to the season, in which this unit was still getting healthy and gelling, it played its best game to date under a national spotlight. The collective effort it took to bottle up arguably the most explosive running back in the game, Bijan Robinson, to 86 yards on 17 carries began with how the Ravens played up front in the trenches along the interior.
The combination and rotation of Pro Bowlers Nnamdi Madubuike and Calais Campbell, with fellow starter Travis Jones and a handful of snaps from John Jenkins and Broderick Washington, not only led the charge to stuff the run but also applied some nice interior pressure as well. Madubuike was getting constant penetration into the backfield, registering a quarterback hit and nearly had a couple of sacks. Campbell had his best game of the season in his second stint with the team, recording a pair of tackles, both of which were solos, and one went for a loss as he received the highest overall grade of any player on either side of the ball from Pro Football Focus with an 85.1 .
Calais Campbell is still a dawg in his 283rd career NFL game. pic.twitter.com/QwXOk1ZAAy
While the third-year pro didn't see a single snap on offense for the fifth week in a row as Henry and fellow veteran Justice Hill split backfield duties, he still made his presence felt in a noticeable way as one of the Ravens' most active and impactful special teams players. Ali's 17 snaps in the third phase of the game tied veteran safety K'Von Wallace for the fourth-most on the team; he led all players in special teams tackles with both a season and career single-game high of three total, including a pair of solos.
After battling through a hamstring and calf injury that caused him to leave last week's game early and limited him during the week of preparation, the four-time Pro Bowler was not only one of three players who played 100% of the Ravens' defensive snaps, but he also made some key plays. While he was one of several defensive backs who got picked on at times and gave up some conversions in coverage, he was highly impactful when sent on well-timed blitzes.
Humphrey recorded a quarterback hit and applied quick pressure on a huge fourth-and-short stop in the third quarter that resulted in a completion to a diving tight end who was tackled short of the line to gain by rookie outside linebacker Zion Young. He finished with four total tackles, including two solos, and was the Ravens' fifth-highest-graded defender with an overall grade of 67.
The @Ravens defense gets the stop on 4th down! @BALvsATL on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0UrbWMHtd4
All Pro safety Kyle Hamilton was far from the only Georgia native on the team who had an impact and made their presence felt in this game. On a day in which long-snapping was under a microscope around the league after botched and high snaps led to disaster, the seventh-year veteran was on point all game for the Ravens, delivering accurate snaps to rookie punter Ryan Eckley to boot away and get in place for second-year kicker Tyler Loop to drill through the uprights. Moore's most notable play of the night was the physical solo tackle me made on the Ravens' second punt of the game in the second quarter for his second of the season in his first time playing in the 2018 SEC Championship as a senior at the University of Georgia.

title: Nnamdi Madubuike's Impact On Ravens Defense Can Already Be Felt In These 3 Ways
full_text:
Nnamdi Madubuike is getting better by the week.
Progress won’t always be linear, especially with the former All-Pro defensive tackle coming off neck surgery in the spring, and assignments vary from week to week based on the prowess of the opponent, but there is no doubt that this lineman is back to being a disruptive force, it’s hard to imagine the Ravens would have had nearly as much success neutralizing Atlanta’s vaunted rushing attack without him, and the best is still to come with just three games under his belt.
Especially with the Ravens having to play without $30M/year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson the last two weeks, Madubuike’s presence has been vital and he is making a major impact across the board already. His mere ability to log more playing time, and impactful playing time, has allowed everyone else in their defensive line rotation to perform on at a less-demanding rate (and 40-year-old Calais Campbell is coming in right at the pitch count talked about this summer) .
Here’s how Madubuike, 28, is already making everyone else better by being in the middle of this defense:
Madubuike has played 140 snaps over three games, which has settled everything else down. He is sixth on the team in reps in that span, but only middle linebacker Roquan Smith and the regulars in the secondary have played more. By comparison, Travis Jones – a Robin who has to be Batman when Madubuike is out – is second on the team in snaps on the defensive line over the last three weeks with just 107.
It’s like Madubuike has played one more game than the rest of this group since he’s come back. That’s a tall ask and the Ravens did quite well to take the approach they did with his return , not activating him until they believed he could take on a significant role rather than a very gradual ramp up.
Guess who leads the Ravens in pressures over the last three weeks?
Yup, Madubuike with 11. He’s playing a heavy load, as noted above, and still getting a 13% pressure rate and that’s despite there not being a proven disruptor off the edge and him facing some stout offensive lines in that span.
Madubuike is second on the team in QB hits since he came back and tied for first with six QB hurries. He’s seeing the double teams again and extra attention and also had to deal with a trip to Brazil for his first game back in over a year, so he’s only really getting into the flow of a normal schedule now.
It’s only a matter of time before the sacks start coming and getting the chance to play some games up from with Hendrickson should help in that regard. The Ravens need to get the edge pressure rates cranking.
If you recall, a Dallas team that can’t run on anyone ran all over the Ravens in Brazil. That was Madubuike’s first game back, it was essentially his preseason all in one afternoon and he was just getting back used to rotations and playing with this defensive line. And, uh, the run defense the last two weeks has been excellent
Tennessee’s Tony Pollard entered Week 4 on a tear for two weeks averaging round 5.5 yards per carry on under center runs; those went nowhere against the Ravens with Madubuike anchoring. Pollard ran 16 times for 48 yards (3.0/carry).
Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson came into Week 5 the best back in the NFL, averaging 7.4/carry on outside zone and with the Falcons rolling up 477 rushing yards in the past two games. Robinson ran 17 times with just three rushes of five yards or more against the Ravens; he had one carry for 38 yards and 16 for 48.
If this defense becomes the top five unit many believed it could be in Jesse Minter’s first season as head coach, Madubuike will have everything to do with it. So far, so very good.

title: 4 Reasons The Ravens Must Bench Mark Andrews Now
full_text:
The Ravens decision to extend Mark Andrews late last year as a lost season was spiraling away, to try to spite younger tight end Isaiah Likely, who wouldn’t take Baltimore’s offers that close to testing free agency, was always nonsense.
It was petty and sophomoric – it wreaked of the personal over the business which has been quite an issue for general manager Eric DeCosta – and it was decried around the league as such. It’s already created a major problem for Baltimore’s new offense. DeCosta couldn’t get anything of value for Andrews, 31, in trade after the 2024 season – which ended on another massive drop by the former Pro Bowler on a two-point conversion in the playoffs. Rather than accept the pass catcher was in decline he gave him $13M a year last December, ahead of free agency, and essentially guaranteed him a ridiculous $35M in cash through 2027 ( with $5M fully guaranteed for next season ) in what will go down as an utter failure in evaluation and negotiation.
DeCosta likes to play favorites . Likely (a much younger ascending player who is tearing it up for the Giants) ended up getting a deal very similar to the reward DeCosta gave Andrews (Andrews wouldn’t have sniffed that money in free agency with his freefalling metrics). Now rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle must try to find a way to clean up this mess. Andrews can’t run or jump, he does nothing downfield and hasn’t for years and won’t ever again; he also can’t really catch consistently anymore with drops not just a playoff problem, but a consistent one.
Andrews essentially accounted for a 16-point swing in Sunday night’s comeback, overtime win at Atlanta , dropping a sure touchdown early in the game, fumbling deep in his own territory for a scoop-and-score Falcons touchdown and failing to convert a two-point conversion late in the game. His 2026 campaign has picked right up with the downward spiral that began in the 2024 playoffs. DeCosta is the only one who somehow can’t see it , while others speak gingerly around the problem.
"He'd be the first to tell you there are things he'd like to have back," from Sunday night, coach Jesse Minter said of Andrews, while fawning over a few catches he made late in the game.
Because of that salary and what the GM thinks he can do, Andrews is always on the field, seeing the same target share as dominant receiver Zay Flowers and bogging down an offense predicated on explosive plays. Don’t get me wrong, good on Andrews for cashing in; he’ll go in their ring of honor and was a warrior but a team desperate for anyone other than Flowers to win consistently in the pass game can’t afford miscalculations this grave. With two-time MVP Lamar Jackson at his best throwing to tight ends, this kind of massive oversight can be the difference between going deep in the playoffs and not.
It’s time for Andrews to take a backseat to the rookie options in this offense. Here’s why:
Andrews hasn’t been a move guy for quite some time, and the fact he is the only pass catcher on the team besides Flowers making real starting NFL money to do so is a sham. Making him sixth-highest paid TE in the NFL at the time of his December extension was dumbfounding.
Andrews is averaging a microscopic 2.0 yards after the catch this season (NFL tight ends average 5.0). He averages a pathic 8 yards per catch, unfathomable by modern standards with TEs glorified slot and outside WRs schemed up for downfield impact. His EPA/Target (-0.15) is basically the worst by far of any NFL tight end who plays this much (and we’ll get to that) and he has one play over 15 yards all season. He is averaging 6.67 air yards per route run; that’s blocking TE territory but he ain’t paid to block.
It’s nothing new. Here’s Andrews’s ranks among all TEs with at least 25 catches since the start of last season:
Yards/Rec: 8.6 (44th)                            NFL Avg: 10.2
YAC/Rec: 2.1 (52nd of 52)                    NFL Avg: 4.9
EPA/Target: -0.05 (48th)                      NFL Avg: 0.24
Yds/Target : 5.99 (47th)                         NFL Avg: 7.46
Explosive /Target : 8% (43rd)              NFL Avg: 13.4%
Because of how much he makes, Doyle can’t just bench him. And because of how much Jackson and his teammates like him and what he’s done in the past and how much he meant to Jackson early in his career, he sees an egregious amount of the ball and the only way to curtail that is to leave him on the bench more.
Otherwise, well, that’s how you end up with 100 targets the past two seasons – for just 599 total yards! – and that’s how you end up with Andrews being targeted on 22.6% of all Ravens passes this season (dangerously close to Flowers at 23.3%) and only Rashod Bateman (16%) on the entire team is also above 5% target share.
Andrews is second in the team in routes run since the start of last season (458), behind only Flowers (570). He’s second on the team this season in routes run (114), second only to Bateman (135). What the heck are we doing here? You have to yank him to save the offense from him.
He has one game over 50 receiving yards since the start of last season. C’mon man.
Not only is he years removed from being ascending, there is no playoff profile to cling to. You want to keep him a main thing in the regular season because he is a playoff hero – maybe. But Likely did more in his first playoff game honestly than Andrews has kind of ever done in his career. He has zero postseason TDs and a handful of brutal drops, and a procession of miscues since that two-point drop and a fumble in Buffalo in the playoffs.
One area Andrews is among all NFL tight end leaders, however, is in drops. He’s tied for fifth in drops since the start of last season at his position group and I have him for five so far this season and they tend to come on key first-down opportunities early in games, or in the redzone or in the endzone.
His catch radius has become seriously limited by the inability to make anything happen off his feet. The drops are in his head now.
Yeah, they didn’t sign Darren Waller like we begged them to (working out great for young QB Bryce Young in Carolina) and losing “Joker” TE Durham Smythe for the season to an Achilles is a big loss. But they don’t have to be Andrews-dependent by a long shot.
Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner is a better blocker than anyone could have hoped for , he has excelled in reps out of the backfield as more of an H back or a fullback and he has real straight line speed and can be a YAC guy on quick hitters (which are the norm if backup Snoop Huntley has to play another week). He has taken well to more work and is unquestionably a better pass-catching option than Andrews now. Fellow rookie TE Josh Cuevas has also looked more comfortable each week.
Care to guess whe leads all NFL tight ends (with at least five receptions) in YAC/reception at 9.0? It's the same guy who leads all NFL tight ends with an EPA/target of + 1.55. Hibner.
And Doyle could also lean into more 11 personnel (three receivers) when third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane returns from his wrist surgery, which should be soon. He was already looked at as a big-bodied slot target, and the Ravens absolutely need to cut way down on Andrews’s usage and get more speed and twitch and athleticism on the field. Now.

title: Ravens Coach Jesse Minter Provides Injury Update On Lamar Jackson And Other Key Players
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter did not commit to a timetable for injured quarterback Lamar Jackson to return from his ankle injury that kept him out of Week 5, while he remains hopeful of edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane and new center Cam Jurgens returning this weekend.
Jackson is dealing with an ankle injury suffered in the win over Tennessee in Week 4 that kept him out of practice this week and seems likely to keep him out of at least part of practice this week. Minter ruled Jackson out on Friday – which was not a surprise given the fact he did nothing at practice all week – and the Ravens have been very judicious with injuries to vital players already in this young season.
Numerous NFL executives, from afar, suggested to me that Jackson could well miss multiple games given he could return to the game against the Titans and needed to wear a boot and get an MRI. The Ravens have faith in backup Snoop Huntley, who was superb in the fourth quarter and overtime of the comeback win over Atlanta Sunday night, and Jackson’s status will be evaluated closely through the week.
“He’s definitely doing a lot better,” Minter said of Jackson Monday adding that “I’m not sure about exactly how that practice will look,” in terms of returning to the practice field on Wednesday. “He’s doing everything he can,” Minter added. We wouldn’t be surprised if Jackson returns for Week 7 against the Bengals.
Minter again made it sound like Jurgens, acquired from the Eagles last week despite having major back surgery in 2025 and being in the concussion protocol at the time of the trade, continues to trend toward making his Ravens debut in Week 6.
Playing center on a new team, midseason, is no small task and Minter applauded the off-field work Jurgens is doing to master the offense but having him play in his first game without being able to rep with the quarterback and get settled between his new teammates would be quite odd., while the price the Ravens paid to land him shocked execs around the NFL.
“Cam is still kind of in the finishing stages with the protocol,” Minter said. “We'll know a lot more Wednesday, but we feel good about where he’s at.”
Hendrickson has a surgical procedure before Week 4 to repair a finger injury that was clearly bothering him. Minter said at the time that it would be a short-term absence and the Ravens could use the $30M/year edge rusher back as soon as possible.
Lane suffered a wrist injury in the first half of the Week 1 win over the Colts and was put on Injured Reserve, but is eligible to return now. He was a revelation in the preseason and the Ravens need more athletic targets to emerge downfield besides Zay Flowers, who is having an unreal start to the season . Lane could be a big slot option to help mitigate the lack of overall tight end production, and particularly with starter Mark Andrews no longer a viable downfield threat. Minter applauded Lane’s effort to stay as well conditioned and in game shape during his four-week absence.
“Both those guys have put themselves in a real good position,” Minter said of Hendrickson and Lane possible playing Sunday.

title: 13 Winners and 2 Losers From Ravens' Comeback Overtime Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens extended their win streak to three in a row in Week 5 of the 2026 regular season on Sunday night by rallying to beat the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in overtime on the road in primetime.
They came into this game as underdogs with franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson out due to an ankle injury, but proved all their doubters and detractors wrong by coming out on top. While it was far from perfect, they made enough key plays in all three phases of the game to emerge victorious and take sole possession of the top spot in the AFC North standings, with their first division game coming up next week.
Here are several Ravens players and coaches who stepped up and showed out, and others who made some costly mistakes from coaching and execution standpoints.
Playing back in his hometown for the first time since his days at Marist High School, the three-time All Pro made big plays throughout this game, with none bigger than the game-sealing interception in overtime. He flew around the field making clutch tackle after clutch tackle, both in space and at the line of scrimmage, from getting Falcons quarterback Michael Penix down short of the line to gain on scrambles or stonewalling star running back Bijan Robinson for no gain. All six of his tackles were solos, and he broke up a pass as well
KYLE HAMILTON CALLS GAME!!!!!!!!!!!! pic.twitter.com/gvQbG6hvzI
For the third time since returning for his second stint with the Ravens, the seventh-year veteran stepped in for a two-time league MVP and led the team to a huge victory over an NFC opponent, and second in primetime. Huntley went from looking a little unsettled in the pocket and under pressure early on in this game to surgically dissecting the vaunted Falcons defense down the stretch and in overtime (11/12 with a 122.7 rating and a rush TD and pss TD in fourth quarter and OT). He made huge plays with his arm, going 24-of-32 for 201 passing yards and two touchdowns with a passer rating of 111.6. While he didn't run for a lot of yards, he made several key plays with his legs on his six carries, including the game-winning touchdown on one of several successful quarterback sneaks in this game.
TOUCHDOWN RAVENS!!!! SNOOP SCORES ON THE SNEAK!!!! Tune in on NBC!!! pic.twitter.com/gXCy7TPNxS
The second-year pro was another Georgia native who made several impactful plays in this game, most of which occured either in space or behind the line of scrimmage. He led the team with 10 total tackles, including six solos and two very impressive solo takedowns of Robinson for losses, where they were one-on-one, and Starks didn't let himself get juked by the two-time Pro Bowler.
As is the case, no matter who is under center, but especially when Jackson is out, the Ravens leaned heavily on the future Hall of Famer, who has now scored at least once in every game this season. Henry ended his three-game skid of being held under 100 rushing yards by leading the team with 102 on 24 carries, and he added 18 more yards to his scrimmage total by picking up 18 yards and a touchdown on his lone reception, which came on a perfectly executed screen pass where he stiff-armed Falcons linebacker Jared Ivey on his way into the end zone. He also punched the ball across the goal line for the game-tying two-point conversion to force overtime.
22 FOR 2!!!!! TIE GAME!!! TUNE IN ON NBC. pic.twitter.com/y669SJJGPK
The fourth-year pro was a physical force for the Ravens all night on the edge, helping set it against the run to bottle up Robinson as well as coming off it as a pass rusher. He delivered a crushing blow to Penix at the end of regulation for a strip-sack that could've won the game for the Ravens had one of his teammates recovered it, and the big hit ended up putting the third-year quarterback out of commission for overtime. Robinson finished with six total tackles, including three solos and one for a loss, a pass breakup that nearly resulted in an interception. He got lucky that Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews dropped the perfectly lofted pass in the end zone, where he was the nearest player in coverage.
Tavius freaking Robinson 🇨🇦🇨🇦🇨🇦 pic.twitter.com/2aF6ykqEj6
The bounce-back campaign for the sixth-year veteran continued to pick up steam in this game as he not only led the team with 62 receiving yards, but he picked up several of the Ravens' most crucial conversions on his five catches, including three for 38 yards and three first downs on the game-tying drive at the end of the fourth quarter to force overtime.
. @_SNOOP1 ➡️ @R_bateman2 Tune in on @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/FNh6dRMLvQ
The fourth-year pro joined Robinson in having another strong overall performance around and behind the line of scrimmage. He finished third on the team in total tackles with seven, including five solos and one for a loss, to go along with his first sack of the season and a pressure on Penix where he came unblocked on a blitz up the middle
The eighth-year veteran went from struggling to find his footing in the first half to ripping off chunk gains in the second. He only carried the ball four times but finished second on the team with 73 rushing yards, the bulk of which came on a key third-and-short conversion where he exploded up the middle for a season-long 47-yard scamper. Hill also ran for 21 yards on another third-and-short on the Ravens' first drive of the game, moving the ball just outside the red zone.
JUSTICE HILL!!!!!!!!!! Tune in on @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/78PchVhbt3
The second-year pro kept adding to his rebirthed legacy in Baltimore by going 3-of-3 on field goals, including a pair of 51-yarders. He was responsible for all nine of the Ravens' first-half points and is now a perfect 5-of-5 on field goal attempts beyond 50 yards this season after converting only 1-of-4 as a rookie last year.
With four-time Pro Bowl veteran Trey Hendrickson out for the second week in a row as he recovers from finger surgery, the second-year pro rose to the occasion in more ways than one. Green was more than Matthews could handle off the left side for most of the night, recording multiple key and quick pressures, his second sack of the season and a quarterback hit. He was stout as a run defender as well, logging a pair of solo tackles, both of which were solos for a loss, including a play where he blew up a Robinson run five yards in the backfield by bulldozing Matthews into the backfield on an outside zone run.
Mike Green gets to the QB❗️ Tune in on @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/Sxs3RWYKQ5
The two-time Pro Bowler didn't have a monster game, finishing with less than 100 scrimmage yards for the first time this season, but he was still highly impactful by picking up several key first downs to extend drives. He led the team with nine targets and eight receptions for 53 receiving yards and picked up 13 rushing yards and a first down on the first play from scrimmage of the game. He would've finished as the team's leading receiver on a play where he picked up 26 yards, but since he drew a defensive pass interference three yards deeper downfield, the team accepted the penalty.
Tyler Huntley makes something happen with the big play to Zay Flowers!! Tune in on NBC. pic.twitter.com/8kEW1KsvOt
Head coach Jesse Minter and his staff were on point for most of the night, but were absolutely nails in crunchtime with the game on the line in the fourth quarter and in overtime, in how they both managed and called the game. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was in his bag all night and turned up even more for the game-tying and winning drives with how he sequenced and dialed up plays to exploit matchups and put his players in a position to succeed. Minter called some timely blitzes and pressures to come up with key stops in the fourth quarter, including holding the Falcons to a short field goal after an eight-plus-minute drive.

title: 4 Major Issues Ravens Must Still Fix On Defense
full_text:
The Ravens may have forged a new identity under rookie head coach Jesse Minter Sunday night, finding a way to comeback and beat the Falcons in Atlanta in primetime despite lacking their highest-paid player on offense and defense.
Baltimore was without two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson and without $30M/year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson and trailed throughout the game, and still came away with the win, 30-23, in overtime . Minter funneled more manpower to the line of scrimmage than ever before this young season to try to tamp down elite running back Bijan Robinson, and it worked expertly. And, yes, while doing that will leave you a little exposed on the back end , this secondary is also supposed to be the strength of the team, and a young quarterback just back from his third ACL surgery shouldn’t be able to repeatedly convert on third-and-10 or longer as Michael Penix did throughout the course of this game (Atlanta was 9/17 on third down in regulation despite being in long situations).
Tavius Robinson’s late sack, which effectively knocked Penix from the game and forced washed back-up Tua Tagovailoa into the contest, proved huge, but if this defense is going to be Super Bowl quality there remain significant areas that must be improved and cleaned up.
“Obviously, you kind of know when you play a lot for the run you may give up a few things in the passing game,” Minter said late Sunday night. “But again, I thought we could have played some third downs better, from both schematical (approach) and just playing the plays. But man, I am just really, really proud of our guys.”
Hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton, who put the game away by picking off Tagovailoa in overtime, kept it real as always: “I don't think we played well, for real. The third-down stuff was crazy … Third down, we have to do better. But it obviously feels a lot better fixing those mistakes with a win. I might be a little too cynical or critical, but we can be better."
Here’s what needs to improve:
Minter will always want to flood the field with defensive backs, and he played a 3-4 base throughout the first half t o mitigate Bijan Robinson and it worked expertly (17 carries and just three for five yards or more), but Penix converted seven first downs passing against Minter’s dime defense on 14 dropbacks and did so from these distances: 3 yards, 6, 10, 10, 10, 11 and 15.
Penix had a 101.7 rating throwing against dime Sunday, Baltimore has faced 95 dropbacks vs it (21 is NFL average; Rams are second with 71 and they play Monday). The Ravens rank 20th in opposing QB rating vs dime (89.5) and 20th in completion percentage (66%) and 21st in yards/attempt (8.3).
Baltimore’s dime coverage is even worse on third-and-fourth down, allowing a 94.4 rating and 9.5 yards/attempt. Minter needs to find the right mix back there or be willing to use more nickel. Overall the Ravens are just 14th in the NFL in opposer passer rating; outside of Dak Prescott have not faced a top QB.
The hope is that Hendrickson’s return will mean everything. That’s always been the hope.
After his finger surgery, the Ravens need him to look like his Week 1 version. The Ravens are just 20th in pressure rare through five gams and Minter continued to have to blitz on one of every three plays, which is not his comfort level or preference. His blitz rate was around 22% with the Chargers.
Ravens edge players had just two total QB hits in Sunday night’s game despite Penix not really trusting his repaired knee to take off and run nearly as much he did coming out of college as a first-round pick. Merely re-inserting Hendrickson needs to be a cheat code for Minter; if this becomes a scheme-reliant thing we’ve got problems. Former All-Pro defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike is back to being a menace on the inside following neck surgery and getting him and Hendrickson going at the same time will be vital.
Top receivers continue to take games over against this secondary. I strongly believe lack of pass rush in critical moments has a lot to do with that, but they also are going to need top corners Nate Wiggins (who has problems with Drake London Sunday) and Marlon Humphrey to make plays on the ball.
The Ravens have been thrown on 171 times – ninth-most in the NFL – and their cornerbacks do not have a single interception. They don’t have many pass breakups. They don’t get their hands on the ball much at all and haven’t for years.
Here’s what No. 1 receivers have done against them since Week 2 (Carnell Tate of the Titans hasn’t looked like a top wideout against any other team, but he’s as good as it gets for that suspect operation):
London (ATL): 7/11, 118 yards, 7 1st D
Tate (TEN): 9/12, 145 yds, 6 1st D
CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 7/8, 112 yds 5 1st D
George Pickens (DAL): 7/11, 82 yds, 4 1st D
Chris Olave (NO): 8/10, 86 yds, TD, 6 1st D
Minter has a lot more on his plate than ever before having to run a sideline and manage a game, which is brand new to him, and also call the defense. His early-game plans have generally been stout but as games go along this defense tends to wilt, the fourth-quarter collapse gene is still in there and the second half in general has not been good enough.
The Ravens are 26th in the NFL allowing 2.64 points/drive in the second half. QBs – again, not very good ones by and large – complete 69% of their passes (21st) with a 102.7 rating (21st). Baltimore allows 5.6 yards/play (20th) and 129 passing yards (26th) and they rank just 18th in third-down defense in the second half.
In the fourth quarter the Ravens are allowing 5.9 yards/play (26th) and 94 passing yards (31st) and 3.83 points/drive (tied for 31st) and a 42% TD rate (30th). Atlanta rolled up 126 yards in the fourth quarter Sunday and this remains a very real issue; the Ravens holding them to two field goals after marching down the field late was vital.
The Ravens have allowed 46 points in the fourth quarter, tied (with the Eagles) for second most in NFL (only Washington is worse).

title: Critical Takeaways From Wild Ravens Comeback, OT Win In Atlanta
full_text:
The Ravens overcame a bevvy of injuries, including two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson missing the game, rallied to force overtime with a two-minute drive, went ahead in overtime and sealed a huge win over the Falcons with Kyle Hamilton's interception.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter and novice offensive coordinator Declan Doyle managed the game expertly, knowing what they were up against with Atlanta boasting the best rushing attack in the NFL to go with the top rushing defenses and the best pass rush in terms of pressure rate. Backup quarterback Snoop Huntley is very limited in the downfield passing game but saved his best work for late in two TD drives and secure a 30-23 win at Mercedes-Benz Stadium to surge to 4-1.
Baltimore’s pass rush was tepid for most of the night, the secondary gave up repeated big plays on third downs (four of third-and-10 or longer), and went 9/19 on that down in regulation, but got key goal-to-go stops late again. Tight end Mark Andrews, who has been in major decline for years, had a rough game that took points off the board but caught a key pass in overtime.
The offense, which finally cut down on its penalty issues, mustered it's crispest drive of the night to tie the game at 23 in the dying seconds, with Huntley (24/32 for 201 yards with a rushing TD and two passing TDs) looking at ease and finally using the middle of the field, throwing a short TD pass to Devontez Walker, then Derrick Henry converted a Wild Cat two-point conversion that sent the game to overtime.
"Snoop is just one of the coolest dudes," Minter said after the game. "He doesn't get rattled."
Here are the key takeaways from Week 5:
The Falcons pass rush was a problem most of the night and the Ravens had trouble sustaining things, but the drive to tie the game was masterclass - going 71 yards in six plays in 1:51. The operation was smooth and in sync.
Minter opted to take the ball after winning the toss in overtime and the Ravens reconstructed offensive line continued to take the game over. They had a helluva second half and, facing a defense that came in allowing 2.7 yards/carry, the Ravens got Henry over 100 yards and they ran for 209 yards as a team.
The Ravens mustered a 14-play drive in overtime that erased over seven minutes from the clock to give them their first lead since 3-0. Atlanta backup QB Tua Tagovoalia had to replace Penix late in the game after he took a big hit and Hamilton read him perfectly to end the game with a pick after the Falcons had started to drive.
"It could be a launch point to really get us going," Minter said of the way his team finished the game.
The overpaid tight end was horrible a few hours after the best tight end on the Ravens roster the last two seasons, by far, Isaiah Likely, comminated Washington for the Giants as he has been doing all season. Andrews cannot separate anymore, he can’t run routes downfield, he is good for about eight yards a catch and he continues to drop easy passes early in games.
Andrews basically cost Baltimore 14 points in the first half of this game. And really 16 because he needed to make a better effort on a two-point conversion that came his way, too.
He dropped a touchdown pass early in the game, a play that simply has to be made, and then had a terrible fumble deep in Baltimore territory that was returned for a touchdown. General manager Eric DeCosta has a nasty habit of letting the wrong people walk, and giving Andrews $13M when he couldn’t land a fourth round pick for him back after his terrible drop in the 2024 playoffs to spite Likely will have major ramifications for this season as he runs low on anyone besides Zay Flowers to make plays downfield. Likely making about the same money as Andrews is even sillier.
The Ravens’s pressure peaked early in the game and they were unable to pressure jittery young QB Michael Penix Jr., coming off his third ACL surgery, as the game worse on, especially on obvious pass-rush situations. He had far too much time to operate in general on second-and-long and third-and-long and the Ravens need $30M edge rusher Trey Hendrickson back from his finger surgery ASAP.
Atlanta went up, 14-6, late in the first half when Penix picked up 13 yards to Kyle Pitts on second-and-16, the Drake London for 25 on third-and-three, and Jahan Dotson for 36 on third-and-six, and then Pitts for a touchdown on third-and-five.
In the fourth quarter, Penix had all day to hit London for 14 yards on third-and-two from the Atlanta 18 and then he hit London again for 19 yards on a third-and-15 in which no one could get anywhere close to making the QB concerned.
The Ravens vaunted secondary got picked apart. Minter doesn’t want to blitz but he had to Sunday night (43%) with very shaky results and Penix converted a third-and-10 inside of six minutes that was a backbreaker. There was not nearly enough winning going on up front and Baltimore’s fourth-quarter defense will remain among the worst in the NFL until some real closers emerge.
It would take a commitment from the offensive and defensive game plans to be synced to keep this game close given Baltimore’s injury issues, including, of course, no Jackson. It would take a willingness from young offensive coordinator Declan Doyle to keep it simple here and he did.
The best way to stop Falcons dominant running back Bijan Robinson is to keep him off the field and prevent him from getting a volume of plays on the ground to get going. That’s what we got. Jesse Minter played a loaded line of scrimmage, as was required, and Baltimore’s makeshift offensive line helped them sustain possession.
The Ravens ran 40 plays in the first half. They ran the ball 19 times. They were using over 41 second of wall clock time per play in the first half and that helped them keep the ball for 19:28 in that opening half. So even without scoring any touchdowns they were very much in the game at 14-9.
Atlanta held the ball for nearly as much time in the second half, however, with Baltimore’s defense wilting. But overall Minter applied heavy attention to the line, sticking with heavy fronts, and they bottled up Bijan Robinson (17 rushes for 86 yards) outside on one long blast on an outside zone play.
"Overall, I thought we played Bijan very well," Minter said.
Minter boasted about hunting explosives with Huntley this week but thankfully that was just talk. Well done.
You don’t want Huntley, with a 5.9 yards/attempt average for his career, trying to be something he’s not on the road against a defense that is getting a lot of pressure and with an offensive line that has never played together before. Minter cut down on the motion, the ball was designed to come out quickly and too the flats and with the offensive line so experimental in the interior, the Ravens attacked the perimeter of the field as they needed to .
He leaned into the screen game and horizontal passes, and the designed screens for Derrick Henry we told you were coming, one of which went for a touchdown. And the biggest offensive play of the game came in a “Pony Package” with Henry and running back Justice Hill on the field with Hill taking a draw 47 yards to set up Henry’s touchdown .
The Ravens got a defensive stop on the opening drive of the first half, to keep the deficit at 17-9 and not greater, continuing a recent trend of holding teams to three at critical times even after giving up some yards previously.
The Falcons got cute and called a pass to a tackle eligible rather than just hammer the ball on the ground. Safety Malaki Starks and corner Marlon Humphrey were excellent in run support in goal-to-go defense in general on the night and it was going to take defensive backs being very active in that regard to corral Atlanta’s rushing attack.
Humprey, who had a rough start to the season and missed most of practice with a calf injury, provided sound tackling and also had a great blitz on a fourth-and-short play to force a pressure and get Atlanta off field late in the third quarter.
Vega Ioane…

title: Joe Brady Puts James Cook on Notice as Bills RB's Fumbling Issues Continue
full_text:
Buffalo Bills running back James Cook has an issue with fumbles that once again reared its ugly head on Monday night.
During the Week 5 game against the Los Angeles Rams, Cook had a pair of fumbles and lost one of them . And that lost fumble came at a crucial time, as Cook coughed up the rock in the overtime period and nearly cost his team the game.
Thankfully for the Bills, Greg Rousseau blocked Harrison Mevis' field goal on the next drive, which saved Cook and the Bills and allowed Buffalo to drive down the field and win the game.
On Tuesday afternoon, head coach Joe Brady didn't mince words about Cook's fumbling issues and even said that Cook could lose carries if the problems persist.
"I have all the confidence in him, that's why I put him right back out there," he said of Cook . "But, obviously, at some point there has to be consequences to when we're putting negative stuff out there."
"That can't happen and at some point it's going to cost us football games, and it almost cost us one," Brady added. "And so, it's got to improve or the carries are going to decrease."
That's a bold statement from Brady, who is threatening to take carries away from last year's rushing champion.
That said, Cook's fumbling issues have gotten so bad that it's necessary to put him on notice in the hopes it will lead to the veteran running back fixing his major problem.
Cook has a whopping four fumbles in five games this season.
Of course, this is not a new issue for Cook, who has struggled to hold on to the football throughout his career. Cook had six fumbles last season, and he had four in 2023.
According to Pro Football Focus , Cook's 10 fumbles since last season are the most in the NFL among running backs. The next closest player is Atlanta Falcons superstar Bijan Robinson, who has seven in that span. So, that goes to show you Cook isn't the only elite running back to have this issue.
Considering the fact that we're just five contests into this season and he is already two shy of his career-high puts an extra bright spotlight on the problem that has plagued Cook for far too long.
The problem with lessening Cook's carries is that it will hurt the offense. Ty Johnson and Ray Davis are solid backs, but they do not have the game-changing ability Cook has.
However if Cook is hurting the team and costing it games, like he nearly did on Monday night, his advantage in ability over the other two doesn't mean as much.

title: Week 6 NFL Power Rankings: Bills Crash Top 5 Following OT Win Over Rams
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills entered Week 5 feeling the pressure . They were coming off a disappointing loss to the New England Patriots and were in danger of losing their AFC East lead .
Their opponent wasn’t going to make it easy on them either as the Bills were in Southern California to take on the Los Angeles Rams. As expected, it was a back-and-forth contest with plenty of fireworks.
Buffalo managed to make just enough plays as Greg Rousseau blocked a field goal in overtime, allowing the Bills to march down the field for a winning kick of their own.
As the dust settles on a wild Week 5, let’s see how the Bills stack up against every other team in our Week 6 NFL Power Rankings roundup.
Connor Orr kept the Bills at No. 4 and has a hard time forgetting the fumble issues that have plagued James Cook.
”We forgive James Cook but we don’t forget. I thought it was incredibly awesome of Joe Brady to give Cook the ball one more time after his second fumble to let him know he had his back. But those ball security issues will rear their head as the games matter more each week,” Orr wrote.
ESPN moved the Bills to the third spot after spending last week at No. 5. There are still some concerns according to Nick Suss, who believes their pass defense needs help.
”The Bills haven't had much issue pushing offenses backward on first down. But opponents have had far too much success extending drives in second-and-long and third-and-long situations. Plenty of this has to do with the Bills' dwindling cornerback depth, but that's hardly an excuse for how C.J. Stroud, Jared Goff, Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford completed 74.6% of their passes for 558 yards and five touchdowns (posting a 80.8 QBR) on second downs against the Bills,” Suss wrote.
Recently, Sean McDermott discussed their issues against the pass and expressed confidence that his former team will get things figured out as they become more comfortable under Jim Leonhard.
Chad Graff and Josh Kendall work together on The Athletic’s weekly power rankings and they had the Bills moving up one spot following their huge win.  They were impressed that Buffalo bounced back following a frustrating loss to the Patriots in Week 4.
”Buffalo rebounded well from a home loss in Week 4, kicking off a weeklong stay out West by somehow outlasting the Rams in a wild back-and-forth game on Monday night.”
They added that there was still plenty to clean up, mentioning penalties and James Cook’s fumble, but Buffalo is still one of the best in the business.
Like SI earlier, the Bleacher Report kept Buffalo at No. 4 despite the win. Brent Sobleski said he knew this week would be a heavyweight bout while noting that the outcome didn’t center around Josh Allen.
”The Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen and Los Angeles Rams' Matthew Stafford landed multiple haymakers. Ultimately, the former left the contest with a victory, though the outcome didn't center on Allen,” Sobleski wrote.
“Instead, James Cook coughed up the ball in overtime and allowed the Rams to take possession and attempt a game-winning field goal--which Greg Rousseau blocked.”
Nate Davis is still not buying the hype. At least not completely.
While No. 7 isn’t a bad ranking overall, he seems to be punishing them for previous failures in the postseason.
“QB Josh Allen has proven he can win in overtime. Does that mean he can win in overtime in January? Maybe even February? Monday night's rousing defeat of the Rams feels like one that could count for a lot more than just a mere Week 5 victory,” Davis wrote.
Fair or not, that’s a perception Joe Brady will have to battle all year as the head coach of the Bills.

title: Bills' Bradley Chubb Gets Last Laugh With NFL Suspending Rams' Alaric Jackson For Punch
full_text:
Los Angeles Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson is being punished by the NFL after an altercation with Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb following the Week 5 game that saw the Bills emerge victorious .
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson is expected to be suspended for two games for hitting Chubb with the punch on Monday night.
"Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson is expected to be suspended two games for punching Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb during Monday night’s postgame gathering, per sources. But the NFL has not yet notified the team nor the NFLPA," Schefter reported.
With the two-game ban, Jackson will now miss the Week 6 game versus the Arizona Cardinals and the Week 7 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, barring a successful appeal that is unlikely considering everything was caught on video.
The incident happened after Monday night's contest. Chubb and Jackson exchanged words on the field after the game and after Chubb walked away, Jackson followed him and the two players were face to face before Jackson threw the punch.
Thankfully, both players were separated before the situation could get worse.
Despite being the victim of the punch, Chubb would not say who hit him, although it was already crystal clear with all the cameras around.
"Somebody swung, but hey, that's not on me to tell who," Chubb said, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop . "There's cameras out there. I just know, you know what I'm saying, I'm just ready for next week."
At the end of the day, Chubb didn't make a big deal about it.
"It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game. It was a close game," Chubb said. "And, you know, they always catch the second guy. So, I let him swing. And then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled."
"Like I said, it was an emotional game. Tempers got flared," Chubb added. "But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week."
Not only was it an emotional game that saw some heated moments between players throughout, it was a wild one, also.
After both teams struggled over the first three quarters, each team's offense woke up in the fourth in what was an explosive quarter of play that resulted in the game going into overtime.
The Bills looked like they might find pay dirt on the opening drive of the extra period, but a James Cook fumble thwarted that.
Then, it looked like the Rams would win the game with a field goal, but Greg Rousseau came up huge with a block on the kick and allowed the Bills to fight on.
Thanks to a few big gains on the ground from Josh Allen, the Bills got themselves into field goal range and Tyler Bass did the rest.
With the win, the Bills now improve to 4-1 while the Rams fall to 2-3. And, making matters worse, the Rams also lost their starting left tackle for two games.

title: Josh Allen Recaps Odd Joe Brady Decision to Kick With So Much Time Left in Bills' Win
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' rookie head coach Joe Brady displayed tremendous confidence in kicker Tyler Bass , but it didn't come without substantial risk.
Passing up an opportunity to shorten the imminent attempt, Brady sent Bass out to try a 45-yard field goal on second down immediately following the two-minute warning in overtime on Monday Night Football against the Los Angeles Rams.
Fortunately for the Bills, Bass , who has been perfect on field goal attempts since returning from missing the entire 2025 season , calmly nailed the kick right down the middle to end the NFL's Week 5 finale in thrilling fashion.
"There was no panic. It was just conversations of how do we want to handle this. 45-yard kick, I felt like T. Bass was going to boot that and be good with it," said Brady.
For reference, NFL kickers have converted 45-yard field goals approximately 79 percent of the time over the past decade. Although the odds are good, it's far from a chip shot.
Arguably more important than shortening the field goal distance, however, the Bills declined to buy insurance against a potential Bass miss by not bleeding time off the game clock.
Rather than attempting the field goal on second down, the Bills could've called at least one more safe run play such as a quarterback sneak to take another 40-plus seconds off the clock. Therefore, if Bass missed, the Rams would have barely 1:00 remaining and no timeouts on the potential ensuing possession.
"We had some conversation on the sideline about, hey, what should we do?" said Brady. "Do we take two knees right there and go back and at least they don't have a chance at a rebuttal? … Do you run two kind of QB sneaks and just know you're not losing yards, but there's a lot of risk — bangs on the head or punching at the ball?"
Ultimately, Brady chose to go no further, immediately putting the outcome on Bass's shoulders.
Quarterback Josh Allen supported Brady's decision during his postgame comments , reiterating the unwanted risk that comes from running another play, or two, from scrimmage in that particular situation.
"Listen, they're gonna go Blitz Zero every play. You can hit your head into a wall and hopefully get yardage, but you're putting the ball at risk every time you do that. Even with good ball security, but potential penalties, potential turnovers," said Allen.
The fact that Bass was apparently comfortable with kicking from the spot at which the Bills stood likely made the decision easier.
"Felt very confident about the left hash, and T. Bass wanted it there. Felt like it was within his range, within his safety range. Joe made the decision to put the ball down and kick it, and T. Bass drilled one," said Allen.
Still, Buffalo could've remained on the left hash by executing two QB sneaks over left guard while also taking significant time off the game clock. Furthermore, Brady is seemingly overstating the risk, considering the Bills' unprecedented success on Allen's short yardage attempts .
Even though there may have been a better way, however, Bass eliminated any reason for critics to second guess the decision.

title: Rob Gronkowski Finally Apologizes for Dirty Hit That Concussed Bills' All-Pro in 2017
full_text:
Rob Gronkowski made one of the dirtiest plays on a Buffalo Bills player in team history. And nearly a decade later, he's trying to make amends for his actions.
During a Week 13 matchup with the defending Super Bowl champion New England Patriots in the 2017 NFL season, the Buffalo native earned a myriad of more haters for an uncalled-for hit on Bills' star rookie Tre'Davious White.
Not only did he drop an unnecessary elbow, White missed the rest of the game with a concussion.
Gronk now realizes that that action was a mistake. But he did so out of frustration with NFL officials, not necessarily White.
The apology might cancel itself out here, @gronk 😂 pic.twitter.com/oeNcZnkYaF
"I wish I went after the referee, verbally, instead of attacking Tre'Davious White," said Gronk to his colleagues on the NFL on FOX pregame show. "Defenders were dropping all over me throughout that season. And for that play right there, Tre'Davious White held me three times; there was no flag on the play, he caught the interception. And I was so frustrated with the referees that I elbow-dropped Tre'Davious White.
"So, I'm sorry, Tre'Davious White. I should've elbow-dropped the ref."
The apology would have felt more meaningful if Gronk had not also placed blame on White for his play that led up to it. He claims that White's third career INT had more to do with him interferring with the future Hall of Fame TE than him being able to cover him well.
You can review the tape yourself and make a decision on whether the rookie CB played it cleanly or if he was rewarded with an uncalled PI call. So, no, he was not mad at White to begin with. But he acknowledges that if he had gotten the PI call too, he would not have been upset with the refs and would not have taken it out on the LSU product.
But this all coincides with Gronk trying to reconnect with his hometown team.
This confession from Gronk comes two weeks after he became one with Bills Mafia during the pregame coverage of Buffalo hosting the Chargers in Week 3.
"They love me so much they're allowing me to be part of all the tailgating traditions," while shooting a segment with legendary Bills Mafia member Ken 'Pinto Ron' Johnson. "It's like time heals all wounds."
Gronk, who wore his high school jersey from his playing days in Western New York, lost a lot of fans after his unsportsmanlike play against White. But his recent apology may bring some back for the Buffalo native.
Live in Orchard Park, Gronk is living it up with Bills Mafia! @BuffaloBills | @RobGronkowski pic.twitter.com/wDN31dMopd

title: Bills' Postgame Injury Update: Starter Spencer Brown Left MNF Win After 16 Plays
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills pulled out an amazing road win over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football, but they lost their starting right tackle in the process.
The rock-solid Spencer Brown left the October 12 primetime game after 16 offensive snaps due to an apparent back flare-up in the second quarter.
Brown went down following a 1st-and-15 snap from the Bills' 37-yard line with 6:22 remaining in the first half. The play was a wide receiver screen to the right that Khalil Shakir took for a six-yard gain. Brown did not appear to suffer injury as a result of contact as he was trailing the action seemingly unimpeded before grabbing at his back.
Initially tabbed as questionable to return, Brown was shown walking into the locker room on the ESPN broadcast. The Bills eventually ruled him out midway through the second half.
"I don't have anything on Spence. Obviously, he couldn't finish the football game. We'll have to kind of evaluate what that kind of looks like," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady after the 37-34 overtime win.
The 28-year-old Brown, who is on a four-year contract reportedly worth $72 million, has a history of back issues that required surgery following the 2021 season.
In 2025, a flare-up caused Brown to begin training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list. Fortunately, back problems have not noticeably limited the right tackle's availability over the years. He's averaging 15 regular season appearances per year for his career.
Backup Tylan Grable filled in for Brown, playing the remaining 48 offensive snaps at right tackle. He committed two penalties, but seemed serviceable overall. Grable, a 2024 sixth-round pick, was initially ahead of Ryan Van Demark on the depth chart as a rookie before an injury set him back.
Starting cornerback Christian Benford was sidelined for five plays after appearing to reaggravate his toe injury.
Tightly covering Rams' wide receiver Puka Nacua on a 3rd-and-3 play with about 10:00 remaining in regulation, Benford's toe seemed to hit the ground hard as he tackled the pass-catcher after a four-yard gain. He was cleared to return later in the fourth quarter.
The toe issue initially popped up in Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers, forcing him out of the 24-16 victory. Benford missed the every practice the following week, and the Bills scratched him from the lineup for the October 4 game against the New England Patriots.
Starting safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson went down with what looked to be a potential knee injury with 00:55 remaining in the third quarter. Apparently, it was just a scare as he returned with 11:23 left in the fourth quarter.
The Bills were playing without wide receivers DJ Moore and Josh Palmer , who were scratched due to injury. Starting slot cornerback Dee Alford was also unavailable due to an ankle issue.
WIth a Week 6 road game against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, Buffalo is not traveling back home to Orchard Park and will remain out west for practice.

title: Hailee Steinfeld Goes Viral With NSFW Cheer For Josh Allen During Bills-Rams
full_text:
While Josh Allen was running the Buffalo Bills to a victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night in the 37-34 win for Buffalo, his wife, Hailee Steinfeld, was every Bills fan.
With the Bills and Rams knotted at 27 late in the fourth quarter and the Bills facing a second-and-17, Allen took off for a huge 21-yard run that set Buffalo up at the Rams' five-yard line, which led to a touchdown run from James Cook a few plays later.
After Allen's clutch play, the broadcast showed Steinfeld cheering her man on while he was taking off down the field and there is no doubt about how much she was into it.
"Go Josh! Let's go, Josh! Let's f****** go!" Steinfeld said in the viral clip, which you can check out below.
Hailee Steinfeld was HYPE for Josh Allen's run 🔥 pic.twitter.com/eVqOwaGY9m
Just like every Bills fan, Steinfeld is clearly living and dying on every play and we love to see it.
Unfortunately for the Bills, that touchdown was not enough to seal the win, as the Rams came back down the field on the very next series to tie the game, sending it into overtime.
The extra frame didn't disappoint, either.
Allen busted off a few more big runs on the game-winning drive that ended with a 45-yard field goal from Tyler Bass. The performance loudly dismissed the rumors that he was hiding a potential knee injury .
He first scrambled for 19 yards on second-and-7, and then ripped off a 13-yard run on the very next play to move the Bills up to Los Angeles' 27-yard line, where Tyler Bass kicked the game-winning field goal.
In all, Allen finished with a whopping 121 yards and one score on 10 carries while also adding 210 yards through the air and one touchdown to one interception.
“When it’s there, it’s there,” Allen said of his explosive runs. “I don’t want to make a living on that, I understand that, but I do know how much of a backbreaker that can be on a defense when you think you’re in pretty good coverage. I felt like there was some room to maneuver there and keep the chains moving.”
Bills fans hold their collective breath whenever Allen takes off with the football because it puts him at increased risk of injury, but his legs are such a weapon and he simply must take what the opposing defense gives him when he can.
On Monday night, Allen did just that and it made a huge difference in the Bills' win over the Rams.

title: Five Winners, Four Losers From Bills Exciting Win Over Rams in Week 5
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills just won a thriller in overtime against the Los Angeles Rams.
It was a low scoring first half, with Buffalo going into the break with a 13-7 lead. While both defenses were making plays during the first 30 minutes, that all changed in the second half. There was a stretch of six consecutive drives that ended in touchdowns as the two teams played to a 34-34 tie in regulation.
In overtime, there was more back-and-forth as the Rams ended the Bills' first drive by forcing a turnover. Buffalo responded by blocking a field goal attempt, setting themselves up for a game-winner of their own. Tyler Bass ended up knocking his attempt through the uprights, giving Buffalo a thrilling 37-34 win.
With that exciting game in the books, let's see which players stood out as both winners and losers for the Bills in Week 5.
Ray Davis got things off to a hot start for the Bills, taking the opening kickoff back 70 yards. He was eventually pushed out of bounds, but gave the offense the ball at the Los Angeles 26. The offense lost five yards on their first drive, but thanks to Davis, they took a 3-0 lead despite the three-and-out.
On the second offensive snap of the game, Josh Allen fired a bullet over the middle of the field and hit Dawson Knox in the end zone for what should have been a 23-yard touchdown. That wasn't the case, as Knox dropped the pass , forcing the Bills to settle for a field goal after Ray Davis gave them the ball at the 26-yard-line thanks to his 70-yard kick return.
After the Rams went up 7-6, the Bills needed something to click on offense. That happened as they went 69 yards on five plays to take the lead right back. James Cook ran in a 17-yard touchdown to cap off the drive, but it was Ty Johnson who made the big play on that drive.
On second-and-nine, Johnson took a screen pass from Allen and followed an excellent block from center Connor McGovern. Johnson turned the short pass into a 40-yard gain , finally being pushed out of bounds at the 17-yard line.
Cole Bishop has developed into a trusted starter, but he had a gaffe on Monday that helped set up the Rams for a touchdown. Bishop was beaten on a route by tight end Tyler Higbee and was guilty of pass interference. That gave the Rams the ball at the one-yard line, and Blake Corum ran in a touchdown on the following play, giving them a 14-13 lead.
Trailing 14-13, the Bills nearly gave the ball right back to the Rams. James Cook lost the ball when linebacker Nate Landman punched it out and the officials initially said Los Angeles recovered. After discussion, that was changed and Buffalo kept possession. On replay, it was clear that the Rams had a shot at the recovery, but right guard O'Cyrus Torrence wrestled it away. Buffalo ended up scoring a touchdown on a nine-play, 61-yard drive, which wouldn't have been possible without Torrence.
This wasn't a good day for C.J. Gardner-Johnson. He was flagged for unnecessary roughness on a second-and-16 play, which gave the Rams a fresh set of downs and 15 yards. He was beaten for a touchdown by Davante Adams. He also suffered a lower-body injury in the third quarter , but was able to get back into the game. Unfortunately, when he did, Gardner-Johnson promptly gave up an 18-yard pass to Tyler Higbee. On that play, he simply let the tight end go behind him without any help over the top.
Josh Allen had just four completions in the first half, but turned it on during the second. He still completed just 12-of-19 passes, which is uncharacteristic. Still, he made the plays when they mattered the most, oftentimes doing so with his legs. Allen finished with 121 yards and one touchdown, and had some fourth-quarter and overtime fireworks on the ground.
During their final drive, Allen had a 15-yard gain on third-and-five and then ran 21 yards on second-and-17, moving the ball to the Rams' five-yard line with 1:48 to play, setting James Cook up for the go-ahead touchdown.
In overtime, he had a 19-yard and a 13-yard run to help set up Tyler Bass for a 45-yard game-winning kick. He finished with the second-highest rushing yardage total of his career, and it was the highest since his rookie season in 2018.
James Cook was nearly the one to lose this game for Buffalo, fumbling it away in overtime. It was his second fumble of the game and while O'Cyrus Torrence recovered the first, Aaron Donald of the Rams got this one. Thankfully for Cook, he was bailed out by one of his teammates.
Greg Rousseau walked out of Week 5 as the biggest winner for the Bills. After the Cook fumble, the Rams moved the ball 50 yards and were set up for a game-winning field goal from 48 yards out. The attempt was blocked , however, by Rousseau, which gave the Bills the ball back. That was all they needed, as Allen used his legs to set up a game-winning field goal by Tyler Bass.

title: Alaric Jackson Punches Bradley Chubb in Postgame Altercation After Bills vs. Rams
full_text:
After the Buffalo Bills pulled off a wild win over the Los Angeles Rams in the Week 5 game on Monday night, there was an altercation between Alaric Jackson and Bradley Chubb.
The altercation occurred as players were talking on the field after the final whistle. Jackson was doing a jersey exchange with a Bills player when Chubb appeared to say something to the Rams offensive lineman.
Chubb then walked away, but Jackson followed him, got in his face and punched the Bills edge rusher before the two were separated.
Chubb attempted to get after Jackson once it was broken up, but he was held back by teammates while having more to say to Jackson. Check out the full exchange below.
Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe
Not a good look for Jackson, who is likely going to face a fine and a suspension from the NFL for his actions. We would expect the decision to come down in the next day or so.
We saw tempers flaring throughout the contest, as players on both teams got into some scuffles, but nothing escalated to anything close to the level we saw after the game, which amounted to a Monday Night Football classic.
There wasn't much excitement over three quarters, with Buffalo staking itself to a 19-14 lead going into the fourth.
However, the fireworks came from there, with the Rams and Bills exchanging touchdown drives throughout the final frame, which pushed the game to overtime.
Then, there was a wild sequence of events.
The Bills drove 51 yards to the Rams' 22-yard line before James Cook coughed up the football. The Rams then managed to drive 50 yards before Harrison Mevis' 48-yard field goal was blocked, with Greg Rousseau coming up with the rejection.
From there, the Bills drove 35 yards and Tyler Bass booted the game-winning field goal from 45 yards out to secure the 37-34 victory for Buffalo.
With the victory, the Bills are now sitting at 4-1 and keep the razor-thin distance between themselves and the New England Patriots, who moved to 3-2 after their Week 5 win, in the AFC East.
Meanwhile, the preseason Super Bowl champion Rams are now a disappointing 2-3 and in third place on the NFC West behind both the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers and 3-2 Seattle Seahawks.
The Bills will meet with the Las Vegas Raiders on a short week in Week 6 and the Rams draw the Arizona Cardinals, and will likely square off with their division rival without their left tackle.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Bills Resilient Week 5 Win Over Rams
full_text:
Two juggernauts met on Monday Night Football with the Buffalo Bills visiting the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5. The game got off to a hot start, with Ray Davis taking the opening kickoff back 70 yards to give Buffalo the ball at the Los Angeles 26.
Things slowed down from there, with both defenses playing well. That led to a low-scoring first half, with the Bills going into intermission with a 13-7 lead. In the second half, both teams found their rhythm, with multiple touchdowns each in the final quarter.
In overtime, both teams made huge plays. First, Nate Landman forced a fumble by James Cook, but Greg Rousseau blocked the game-winning field goal attempt . That gave the Bills one final chance, and Tyler Bass knocked in a 45-yard field goal to give them the win. Here are some big takeaways from the huge win.
Buffalo had a couple of chances to take a commanding lead in the first quarter, but couldn't capitalize. Ray Davis set them up near the red zone, taking the opening kickoff 70 yards to the Los Angeles 26. They had a chance at a touchdown, but Dawson Knox dropped a pass in the end zone. Josh Allen was sacked on the following play, leading to a field goal from Tyler Bass.
The Rams then missed a 50-yard field goal of their own, and the Bills responded with a strong drive. Leaning heavily on James Cook, they went 55 yards on 10 plays but stalled at the Los Angeles five, again settling for a field goal. Two golden opportunities for a touchdown were missed, meaning they went into the second quarter with a 6-0 lead instead of 14-0. That also allowed the Rams to take the 7-6 lead with their first score of the game, which happened right at the eight-minute mark in the second quarter.
We all expected fireworks in this one, but that wasn't the case in the first half. Instead, it was a defensive battle with the Bills going into the break with a 13-7 lead. What was more shocking than the score was the stat line. Josh Allen completed just 4-of-7 passing attempts for 60 yards and an interception, compared to 16-of-23 for 99 yards and a touchdown for Matthew Stafford. Buffalo moved the ball well on the ground, with James Cook rushing for 55 yards and Allen going for 21 in the first half, but seeing just four completions was shocking.
The Bills took the lead back in the second half when Keon Coleman caught a seven-yard pass to give them a 19-17 advantage. That play would have never happened if not for O'Cyrus Torrence.
Early on that nine-play, 61-yard drive, James Cook fumbled the ball and the Rams were there for the recovery. The officials even signalled that Los Angeles recovered it, but changed the ruling as it was revealed that Torrence was able to wrestle the ball away from everyone under the pile. His fight allowed Buffalo to keep some much-needed momentum and their offense looked completely different after his play.
Buffalo took a lead on a five-yard touchdown courtesy of James Cook, but there was enough time on the clock for the Rams to move down the field and tie the game. It was a disappointing drive as the secondary allowed completions of 14 yards, 16 yards, 15 yards, and nine yards before Kyren Williams ran it in from one-yard out to force overtime. That was the third consecutive touchdown drive for the Rams, all in the fourth quarter.
Buffalo was undisciplined all night, getting hit with 13 penalties for 112 yards. That was a problem for them, as it gave the Rams far too many free yards while also putting their offense in tough situations all night.
Fumbling has been an issue for James Cook throughout the past couple of years, and that's continued this season. He had two fumbles against the Rams, and while Torrence made a great play to get the ball back, the Bills weren't as lucky with his second.
Following a 57-yard reception from Khalil Shakir in overtime, Buffalo was in range to take the lead. That was until Nate Landman (who also forced the first fumble) punched the ball out. Aaron Donald made the recovery, allowing the Rams to get in range for a field goal that nearly won them the game.
As we saw with O'Cyrus Torrence, good things happen when you don't give up. All hope seemed lost following the overtime turnover and ensuing Los Angeles drive, but then Greg Rousseau came through with a huge blocked kick.
Of course it's Greg Rousseau with the FG BLOCK 👋🏈 pic.twitter.com/C7hzQEnvR6 https://t.co/xBcXpdzMQd
He has had a fantastic season and saved the game here for his team. Now, the Bills will turn their attention to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6.

title: The Panthers' Most Indispensable Player Isn't Who You Think
full_text:
Ask me who the Panthers' most indispensable player is, and Bryce Young is probably the answer I'm supposed to give. He's playing the best football of his career, this offense finally looks like it knows what it wants to be, and we've already seen what happens when Carolina doesn't have the quarterback position figured out.
And believe me, I don't want to see what this team looks like without Young right now.
Tetairoa McMillan would be right there for me, too. He already has 385 receiving yards through four games and just put up 14 catches, 192 yards, and two touchdowns against Detroit. I've gotten to the point pretty quickly where when Young throws one up to McMillan, I'm almost expecting him to come down with it.
Then there's Chuba Hubbard, who I think sometimes gets lost in these conversations because he isn't the shiny new toy. But watch what happens to this offense when Hubbard gets rolling. Young doesn't have to do everything, defenses can't just come after him, and Carolina can actually control a game a little bit.
So I get it if you pick any of those three. If somebody tells me Young is the answer, I'm not going to spend 20 minutes telling them they're wrong.
Before you tell me I've lost my mind, I'm not saying Lloyd is better than Young. I'm definitely not saying I'd rather build a football team around a linebacker than a quarterback. I'm looking at this Panthers team right now and asking myself which player I'd be most nervous about losing.
For me, it's Lloyd, and I think that probably says as much about this defense as it does about him.
I still don't know what to make of this defense. Carolina is giving up 387.2 yards per game, the pass rush hasn't consistently gotten home, and Jared Goff just threw for 412 yards against them. There have been drives where I've sat there wondering if they're ever going to get off the field.
Somehow, they keep finding a way.
The Panthers have eight takeaways through four games and five fourth-down stops. They held Atlanta to three points, Cleveland scored 21, and Detroit piled up 452 yards before Carolina finally made the stop it needed at the end. I'm not going to sit here and tell you it's always pretty because it definitely isn't.
That's where Lloyd comes into this for me. In the three games he's played, he has 31 tackles, two interceptions, and a sack. Against Atlanta, he had nine tackles, two interceptions, a sack, and took one of those interceptions back for a touchdown.
That wasn't just a good game. Dave Canales said afterward that he didn't know if he'd seen a better performance from a linebacker in 17 years of coaching in the NFL.
And yeah, I know Carolina already played without Lloyd once. He missed the Cleveland game with a calf injury, and the defense didn't completely fall apart. The Browns scored 21 points, and Bobby Okereke and Tyrel Dodson gave Carolina two experienced linebackers to lean on.
But I also watched Lloyd come back against Detroit, play every defensive snap, and finish with nine tackles. He even chased down Detroit's fourth-down hook-and-lateral to kill a scoring chance. That's the kind of stuff I'm talking about.
He's become one of those players I find myself watching when Carolina needs something. Maybe it's a third down, maybe the other team is driving, or maybe the defense just needs somebody to make a play before things start getting away from them. More and more, I expect Lloyd to be somewhere around it.
Maybe that's why I look at “best player” and “most indispensable player” a little differently. If you ask me who Carolina's best player has been through four games, I might say Young. McMillan would be right there, and I wouldn't argue much if somebody picked him.
But this isn't about who I'd take first in a draft. It's about the player I'd be most nervous about losing right now.
I didn't expect my answer to be a linebacker.
Devin Lloyd is just that good.
