title: Early Week 6 NFL Odds for Huge Panther-Eagles Matchup Revealed
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are heading on the road to face the Philadelphia Eagles again. They last did so in 2024, when Bryce Young was first starting to break out and the Eagles were on their way to a Super Bowl title.
A Xavier Legette drop stood between Carolina and a shocking upset. Now, the two teams are in very different states. The Panthers are well-rested after their bye. Meanwhile, the Eagles will be traveling back from London amid heartbreak after a stunning last-second collapse.
The two teams seem to be in very different situations than one another , and this week marks one of the biggest rest advantages any NFL team will have over its opponent. Will the Panthers win? The odds don't think so.
The Carolina Panthers open as road underdogs to the Philadelphia Eagles. They are -102 on the moneyline on DraftKings , with the Eagles sitting at -118, so it's not as if there's a huge gap between these two teams.
The spread is a minuscule 1.5 points. The Panthers are -115 to cover, while the Eagles are -105 to do the same. Vegas expects a very tight game between these two playoff hopefuls.
The over/under is set at 42.5 points. The over is -105, and the under is -115. Based on all this information, the final score is expected to be somewhere in the ballpark of 22-20 for the Eagles. Regardless, it is expected to be close.
This is somewhat surprising. It is always difficult to be road favorites against any NFL team, but the Panthers are coming off a huge upset victory and are as well-rested as you can be.
They're likely to get Jalen Coker, Monroe Freeling, and Jaelan Phillips back. They're still without Jonathon Brooks, Xavier Legette, Jaycee Horn, and Mike Jackson, but they're going to be healthier than when they beat a better team, the Detroit Lions.
The Eagles are also traveling a long way after losing a game in which they scored a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. It's as defeated as a team can possibly be, but the odds don't believe it will make that much of a difference.
Plus, the Eagles' offense isn't built to take advantage of Carolina's weaknesses like Detroit's was, and even then, the Panthers got numerous key stops. Home-field advantage appears to be doing a lot for the Eagles in this week's odds.

title: Will Jalen Coker Be Back in Week 6? Injury Update, Return Timeline for Panthers WR
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are emerging from their bye in Week 6 and the hope is that wide receiver Jalen Coker will make his return to action.
Coker suffered an injury in the second half of the Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns that forced his early exit from the contest and led to Coker missing the Week 4 game entirely.
With an extra week of rest, there is optimism that Coker will be able to suit up in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Here's what we know about Coker's injury and return timeline.
Coker is currently dealing with a quadriceps injury, which isn't his first rodeo with the injury during his career.
The day after suffering the issue, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said the injury was a "minor quad strain" and the expectation was he wouldn't miss much, if any, time.
Well, Coker did end up missing time despite logging a few limited practices in Week 4, but that was also a sign he wasn't far off from returning.
Head coach Dave Canales offered a positive update on Coker on Monday, as he told reporters that Coker is "on track" to play this week.
However, Canales also cautioned that the Panthers had to evaluate Coker throughout this week of practice before determining whether or not he will play.
"Dave Canales: WR Jalen Coker (quad) is 'on track' but has a couple of big days of practice ahead of him this week heading into Sunday's game at PHI," The Athletic's Joe Person reported.
All signs are pointing to Coker returning this week, but we will still be glued to the Panthers' injury report, with the first installment coming on Wednesday.
A limited practice would keep Coker on the right track, but a full practice would almost guarantee he'll be ready to go for Sunday.
Assuming he plays, Coker is definitely a starting option.
While the Eagles' secondary has a lot of talent on paper, that has not produced desired results against opposing passing attacks this season.
According to CBS Sports , the Eagles are tied for the fourth-most fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.
As far as Coker himself is concerned, he ranks as WR11 overall in terms of fantasy points per game, according to Fantasy Pros , which makes him a borderline WR2 play.
Until further notice, Coker is a starting option in all formats, regardless of matchup.

title: 3 Crucial Panthers Injuries to Monitor Ahead of Big Eagles Matchup
full_text:
The bye week has come and gone for the Carolina Panthers . Now it's time to build on the Sunday Night Football win and keep the first-place spot in the NFC South.
Carolina doesn't have it easy this week, though, as the Panthers head to Philadelphia , to face the 2-3 Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field.
The Eagles are coming off a disastrous loss in London, with the Jaguars winning on a game-winning field goal. Both teams already have plenty of reason to play with desperation, and the Eagles will undoubtedly bring that intensity against Carolina.
With that said, Carolina will need all the reinforcements it can get. The Panthers have been one of the NFL's most injury-prone teams in the NFL this season. Entering Week 6, here are 3 key injuries to monitor
Taylor Moton is one of many prominent Panthers to be ruled out during training camp. Dealing with a blood clot in his lung, Moton hasn't played a down of football this season, but is set to be the starting right tackle once healthy.
Moton's return is now in sight , as he's been taken off the PUP list and activated to the 21-day practice window. This doesn't mean he can return this week, but it means that the return is coming sooner than later.
Panthers' head coach Dave Canales spoke on Moton's return, saying that while he's cleared medically, he hasn't seen football this year.
Moton's timeline will be based on his appearance on the practice field and how quickly he can ramp up. That said, Moton hasn't been ruled out for this week yet, even if theres an outside chance.
During the Panthers' primetime win against the Detroit Lions, Freeling suffered a knee injury that ruled him out for the remainder of the game. Obviously, when a knee injury happens, it's easy to think the worst, but thats not the case here.
Speaking with reporters during the bye week, Canales said that he's "hopeful" Freeling can suit up in Philadelphia.
Canales added to that this week, "I mean it's timely certainly, and Monroe's doing everything he can to make himself available for this week."
Freeling's presence could be a huge factor, especially since theres no guarantee Taylor Moton will return this week.
If both are out, then sixth-year tackle Stone Forsythe will get the start, which is a tall task against a very talented Eagles defensive line.
Similar to Freeling, Phillips injury occurred during the SNF win, as Carolina's premier pass rusher left the game after hurting his hamstring.
Canales gave an update on Phillips on Monday, saying that he "has a chance" to play against the Eagles. Phillips could be an X-factor in this game, as Jalen Hurts is still one of the more mobile QBs in the NFL.
Phillips would also be making his return to Philadelphia, where he played roughly half of last season before leaving to join the Panthers in free agency.

title: Panthers Ridiculously Tumble in Power Rankings Despite Enjoying Week Off
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are coming off the bye week, and it couldn't have gone better. Their next opponent, the Philadelphia Eagles, traveled to London and lost a demoralizing heartbreaker. They also lost two offensive linemen prior to that.
Aside from the now 1-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the divisional threats to Carolina both lost, so the Panthers are still in first. It was a great bye week. We recently covered how it even led to a boost in their Super Bowl odds and their Power Ranking placement.
Elsewhere, though, the Panthers weren't as fortunate. CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco , who has notably not been kind to the Panthers all season (or historically), docked the Panthers in his rankings, even though they did nothing to deserve it.
Pete Prisco has picked the Panthers to lose every single week. Twice, he's been made to look foolish, especially on Sunday Night Football in Week 4, when Carolina upset the Detroit Lions thanks to a sterling offensive outing.
He has spent a lot of time in the last few years criticizing Bryce Young, and he's even been a little hesitant to give Young credit this year. He was always critical of Cam Newton, even when he was literally the NFL's best player.
So perhaps it's not all that surprising that the Panthers slipped down in his weekly NFL Power Rankings despite not doing anything to hurt their standing. Previously, the Panthers were 18th after their upset win over the Lions.
Now, they're 20th. "They come off their bye atop the NFC South standings. Their road game this week at Philadelphia isn't as daunting as it looked a few weeks ago," he wrote.
Sometimes, teams move up in the Power Rankings despite not playing. If a team is ranked 21st, and the teams ranked 17th-20th all lost in ugly fashion, then it stands to reason that the 21st team would move up despite not playing.
Now, the inverse can also be true, but it's less common. Still, that's what happened here, although in Prisco's rankings, the three teams immediately ahead of the Panthers also lost, and some of them lost ugly games.
The good news is that despite Prisco's seeming inability to credit the Panthers, he has them ranked as the best team in the NFC South, ousting the Atlanta Falcons after they lost to the Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens.

title: PFF's Early All-Pro Team Highlights a Major Panthers Injury Loss
full_text:
They are the only team in their division that currently does not own a losing record. When last we saw the Carolina Panthers, Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan were outdueling the Detroit Lions’ Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown. The result was a 32-26 prime time triumph over Dan Campbell’s club.
During the first three weeks of the season, Carolina’s starting offensive line was left tackle Rasheed Walker, left guard Damien Lewis, center Luke Fortner, right guard Robert Hunt, and rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling. During the team’s 21-18 loss in Week 3 at Cleveland, Lewis went down with an elbow injury. Last Sunday night, it was Corey Bullock who got the start.
Against the Lions, Carolina ran for 127 yards on 28 carries and two scores—most of that from Chuba Hubbard. Young connected on 29 of his 41 throws for 329 yards and two touchdowns—192 of those yards and both scores via McMillan. However, Young was sacked three times—the fourth time in as many games he’s been dropped on multiple occasions.
Last week, Gordon McGuinness of Pro Football Focus named his First-Quarter All-Pro Team. In terms of First Team selections, Lewis was his choice at left guard. The seven-year pro is currently PFF’s fourth-ranked player at the guard position—second in pass protection and sixth in run blocking.
Entering Week 5, the Panthers’ offensive front was ranked a disappointing 25th in the league by Pro Football Focus . And according to McGuinness, give credit to the 6’2”, 327-pound interior blocker.
“Down both starting tackles, the Panthers still ranking 25th here is a testament to the organization investing at the tackle position this offseason. The other reason for Carolina not ranking lower has been the dominance of left guard Damien Lewis. He has compiled PFF grades above 80.0 both in pass protection and as a run-blocker and has surrendered just one pressure from 123 pass-blocking snaps.”
That’s an excellent point. Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu and right sider Taylor Moton are currently sidelined, and yet the Panthers’ offense has been one of the best in the league. Credit to president of football operations/general manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales. You will recall that two of Morgan’s biggest moves in 2024 after being promoted from assistant general manager was the free-agent signings of Lewis and Hunt.
This Sunday at Philadelphia, that offensive line will be severely tested by the Eagles’ talented defensive front. Can the Panthers win two games in a row for the first time this season? More significantly, is there any chance that Lewis will be available for this showdown in the City of Brotherly Love?

title: Panthers Could Make Rare Trade With Eagles Before Playing Them
full_text:
NFL teams typically don't trade players to teams right before they play them, especially when the trade deadline is about a month away. There is no urgency for one team to give up a player who could immediately hurt them on the other side .
That said, the Carolina Panthers are desperate, and they could call up the Philadelphia Eagles this week and trade for cornerback Kelee Ringo, who has largely become a special teams player.
The Eagles would be taking a risk by giving up a player with intimate knowledge right before a huge NFC battle. But the Panthers need help as soon as possible, which could reflect an increase in the price.
Regardless, CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani pitched the Panthers as an ideal landing spot for Ringo, and he's spot on.
The Panthers lost Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson to injuries in Week 3. Neither is going to be back any time soon, though both are expected to return before the season is over. In the meantime, things are bad.
The Panthers may have beat the Detroit Lions in Week 4, but they were honestly lucky. Jared Goff tossed for over 400 yards, and Akayleb Evans was in coverage for about 200 of them. It was abuse at the highest level.
The Panthers won't face the Lions, arguably the NFL's best offense, again, but they can't afford to have a walking mismatch in coverage on every single snap. They need some sort of reinforcement. Enter, perhaps, Kelee Ringo.
Now, as mentioned, the Eagles might be very hesitant to do a deal now, but the fit makes too much sense to ignore.
"Kelee Ringo needs a change of scenery and is in the final year of his rookie deal. The former fourth-round pick out of Georgia has the physical makeup you want at 6-foot-2, 207 pounds," Jordan Dajani wrote.
That makes him the ideal short-term replacement while Carolina navigates who should be its CB2 opposite Horn in 2027 and beyond. Plus, physically, Ringo is similar to Horn. They're both big, strong corners.
Dajani continued, "He's started in just eight of 55 career games played with the Eagles, and he has played only on special teams this season. However, there are multiple teams out there that need cornerbacks right now to come in and contribute immediately."
The Panthers are one of those teams. In fact, they might be the team most in need. The Panthers had arguably the best cornerback duo in the NFL, and both of them are out. It's an unfathomable situation, but the Eagles just might hold the answer.

title: Panthers K Ryan Fitzgerald Hasn't Missed a Field Goal — So Explain This
full_text:
I don't think I've ever been this confused by a kicker.
Ryan Fitzgerald hasn't missed a field goal all season. He can line up from 53 yards, and honestly, I feel pretty good about it. Then Carolina scores a touchdown, Fitzgerald comes out for the extra point and I'm sitting there wondering what's about to happen.
Through four games, Fitzgerald is 9-for-9 on field goals . He's 3-for-3 from 40 to 49 yards, made his only attempt from 50-plus and has a long of 53. If I stopped right there, we'd be talking about how reliable Carolina's kicker has been.
But I can't stop there because he's 10-for-13 on extra points. Fitzgerald missed one against Chicago and then missed two against Detroit. Somehow, the kick that's supposed to be easier has been the one making me nervous.
The Cleveland game is where this really started standing out to me. Carolina couldn't get into the end zone for most of the afternoon, so Fitzgerald basically became the offense. He went 4-for-4 on field goals , including a 53-yarder, and scored Carolina's first 12 points.
And here's the weird part: I wasn't really worried when he came out there to kick them. Even when Fitzgerald lined up from 53, I felt pretty good about his chances. That's probably not how I'm supposed to feel about a 53-yard field goal, but he's given me a reason to trust him.
Then we get to Detroit. Fitzgerald made both of his field-goal attempts but missed two extra points. Carolina still won 32-26, so those points didn't end up deciding the game, but I definitely don't want to keep finding out how many missed extra points the Panthers can get away with.
I'm not saying Carolina has a kicker problem, either. How can I say that when the guy hasn't missed a field goal? Fitzgerald also showed as a rookie that pressure doesn't seem to bother him much, going 4-for-4 on game-winning field-goal attempts last season.
That's why I'm having such a hard time figuring this out. If Fitzgerald were missing everything, this would be an easy conversation. He's not. He's perfect on the kicks that are supposed to make me nervous and 10-for-13 on the ones I barely used to think about.
Maybe the extra points get cleaned up after the bye, and we never talk about this again. I hope that's what happens because Fitzgerald has been too good on field goals for three missed extra points to become the story of his season. But Carolina is going to play close games, and eventually one point could be the difference.
For now, I guess this is where I'm at with Fitzgerald.
Fifty-three yards? I'm good.
Extra point? I'm watching.

title: Jalen Coker, Taylor Moton Among Positive Monday Injury Updates From Panthers
full_text:
The arrow is pointing up when it comes to Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker returning from injury in Week 6.
Coker suffered a quadriceps injury during the Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and was ruled out for the Week 4 contest against the Detroit Lions.
The Panthers had a bye in Week 5 , so Coker had some extra time to get right without having to miss another game. And, based on an injury update from head coach Dave Canales, it looks like the time off did him a lot of good.
On Monday, head coach Dave Canales revealed that Coker is now "on track" to play in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, but he cautioned that Carolina needs to see how he gets through a week of practice first.
"Dave Canales: WR Jalen Coker (quad) is 'on track' but has a couple of big days of practice ahead of him this week heading into Sunday's game at PHI," The Athletic's Joe Person relayed.
The Panthers will release their first injury report of the week on Wednesday afternoon, so we'll know more about Coker then.
If the veteran wideout can turn in even a limited practice, that will be a good sign for his chances of playing. A full practice would almost guarantee he'll return in Week 6.
While he has posted one great game and one good game in 2026, Coker has also dealt with injury issues. On top of his quad issue, Coker also battled an ankle injury before that.
Coker wasn't the only positive injury news for the Panthers on Monday, as Canales revealed that both offensive tackle Taylor Moton and defensive lineman Turk Wharton had their practice windows opened .
Moton was placed on the non-football illness list before the start of the season after it was discovered he had a blood clot in his lung. Wharton had an offseason procedure on his neck that resulted in him landing on the PUP list.
Canales said that the return of Moton is "certainly timely," as his replacement, Monroe Freeling, is dealing with a knee injury. The Panthers coach called Wharton's impending return a "breath of fresh air."
While both players are close, there is no guarantee they will make their returns this week. Both will likely need some time to ramp up, so it could be even more than one more week until they get back into the lineup. That said, for a team that has gotten nothing but terrible injury news this year, it's just nice to hear they're close.
The Panthers have time, too, as they're in first place in the NFC South going into Week 6 despite a 2-2 record. Carolina grabbed that spot during its bye week.
"It's playing out really nicely. It has nothing to do with how we perform," Canales said of the Panthers taking over the lead in the division during the bye.
One of the worst divisions in the NFL, every team in the NFC South has been on the struggle bus this season, but Carolina has looked like the best of the group through five weeks.

title: 5 Hail Mary Cornerback Moves Panthers Just Have to Consider Now
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers badly need a cornerback. With Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both out, special teamer Akayleb Evans got picked on badly by the Detroit Lions last time out. These moves would be desperate, but after seeing what happened to Evans, we may be well past desperate.
The Packers may have earned a win in Week 5, but they're still facing an uphill battle to relevance this year. It might be wise to move a fringe player who is heading to free agency next season, and the Panthers would probably be happy to bring in Keisean Nixon.
The Panthers need anyone at cornerback so Akayleb Evans can go back to special teams, and Nixon has starting experience. Carolina can work with that while they wait for Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson to come back.
There's a reason Marshon Lattimore is still available even now, and that should concern the Panthers. However, at this stage, anyone is better than Akayleb Evans for another game at cornerback. Even Lattimore.
Plus, he knows how to defend NFC South wide receivers, and maybe after some time off, he will have a little left in the tank. The Panthers have done well dumpster diving already (Darren Waller, Bobby Okereke), so why not try again?
The Panthers and Buccaneers don't do business very often, especially in a season where both are fighting for the NFC South crown. Now, the Buccaneers are hanging on by a thread, so it might be wise to go ahead and trade someone like Zyon McCollum.
"McCollum enjoyed a tremendous start to the 2024 season, but since then, his production has certainly waned. Over the first four games of 2026, McCollum sports just a 58.3 PFF coverage grade, although his passer rating against (80.4) and forced incompletion rate (13.3%) are both in at least the 60th percentile," PFF's Bradley Locker explained.
The New York Jets made Nahshon Wright a healthy scratch, so he's an obvious trade candidate. The Panthers should be all over that. Wright had eight takeaways last year and 11 passes broken up, so he'd be an outstanding replacement for Horn and/or Jackson.
The Eagles are decidedly not out of the NFC East race, and they face the Panthers this week, but Carolina should be calling about Kelee Ringo. According to CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani , he "needs a change of scenery and is in the final year of his rookie deal."
Dajani noted that Ringo has the ideal physical makeup for an NFL cornerback, which makes him a decent Jaycee Horn replacement. Horn is of similar stature and very physical, so Ringo could step up in his absence.

title: Bears Add Montez Sweat Replacement to Active Roster After Suspension
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have a reinforcement coming at edge rusher this week, which is especially important after Montez Sweat's unexpected suspension.
On Tuesday, the Bears announced they have activated defensive lineman Shemar Turner off the physically unable to perform list. The corresponding move was the addition of Sweat to the reserve/suspended list.
Turner suffered a torn ACL last season , limiting him to just five games during his rookie campaign. The 2025 second-round pick had his 21-day practice window opened weeks ago and was coming up on the deadline before his activation on Tuesday.
The move comes on the same day Sweat was served a two-game suspension by the NFL for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances.
Sweat will be out for the Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons and the Week 7 contest versus the New England Patriots, barring a successful appeal.
Sweat had posted two sacks and 13 pressures so far this season, ranking third and second on the team, respectively, according to Pro Football Focus .
To be quite frank, we have no clue.
Turner had a disappointing rookie season before his injury after he didn't post a single sack or pressure over 74 snaps.
Upon his return on Sunday, Turner, who hasn't played in a game in nearly a full calendar year, isn't likely to play a full complement of snaps, so Chicago is going to need contributions from others.
Along with Turner, the Bears also have Austin Booker and Dayo Odeyingbo as their starters, and James Lynch, Daniel Hardy and Jamree Kromah as backups.
However, there's a chance the Bears won't have Odeyingbo , which would only make matters worse in the wake of Sweat's ban.
Odeyingbo is not even certain to play this week after he left the brutal loss to the Green Bay Packers early with a quad injury . Odeyingbo started off questionable to return before he was doubtful and ultimately did not return to the game.
We do not have a concrete update on Odeyingbo's status for the Week 6 game against the Falcons yet.
It's bad enough that Sweat is going to miss to games, but losing Odeyingbo would be even worse because he has been arguably the team's best edge rushers this season, which has been a pleasant surprise after he entered this season with low expectations.
Odeyingbo ranks second in sacks with three behind Austin Booker, but he owns the team lead in pressures with 14.
We'll know more about Odeyingbo's situation on Wednesday, when the Bears drop their first injury report of the week.

title: Montez Sweat's Suspension Isn't Only Problem Bears Have in Edge Rusher's Room
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were blindsided on Tuesday afternoon after it was revealed that edge rusher Montez Sweat has been suspended.
The NFL announced that Sweat has been suspended for two games for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances.
That means, barring a successful appeal, Sweat will not be on the field for Chicago in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons or in Week 7 against the New England Patriots.
"Montez Sweat of the Chicago Bears is suspended for the club’s next two games without pay for violating the NFL’s Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy," The Athletic's Dan Wiederer said.
It goes without saying how brutal of a blow this is to the Bears' defense, as Sweat is the team's best edge rusher, although he doesn't lead the team in sacks or pressures going into Week 6.
Sweat's suspension isn't the only problem the Bears have at the position currently, so his ban puts the defense in an even more precarious spot.
During the Week 5 contest against the Green Bay Packers, fellow edge rusher Dayo Odeyingbo exited early with a quad injury .
Odeyingbo has tallied three sacks and 14 presures through five games, marks that rank second and first on the team, so it goes without saying how important he is, especially in the wake of Sweat's injury.
Now, we don't have an update on Odeyingbo yet, so it isn't clear how much time he will miss, if any, but if Odeyingbo is on the shelf for any period of time, the Bears are going to be in rough shape.
Chicago does have Austin Booker, who has been on a heater of late with three sacks in two games, and he leads the team with four sacks, which is just a half shy of his career-high of 4.5.
But Booker, who recently expressed frustration with his role , can't do it all on his own and the Bears are extremely thin in the depth department behind him.
The other available edge rushers on the Bears' 53-man roster include Daniel Hardy, Jamree Kromah and James Lynch, but none of those guys inspire confidence. Hardy has zero career sacks, Lynch has 3.5 in 75 career games and Kromah has never even played a regular season snap in the NFL.
The Bears will be getting Shemar Turner back from the PUP list this week, but he only has five career games under his belt and has never posted a sack.
It would be nice to still have Marcus Davenport on the practice squad, but the veteran edge rusher abruptly retired recently .
Safe to say, the Bears are in a really difficult spot at edge rusher right now and they can only hope Odeyingbo will be able to go on Sunday or else sacks and pressures might be extremely tough to come by.

title: Bears' Montez Sweat Suspended for Next Two Games for Violating NFL Policy
full_text:
The NFL announced on Tuesday that it will be suspending Chicago Bears defensive end and one-time Pro Bowler Montez Sweat without pay for the Bears' next two games, according to Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic . Sweat was found to be in violation of the NFL's Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy, the NFL alleges.
This unfortunate development leaves Chicago's defense in dire straits ahead of a pivotal Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. The Bears are coming off arguably their worst performance of the season in a disastrous loss to the Green Bay Packers and badly need a win to get some momentum back on their side. Now, however, they'll have to find a way to do it without one of their defensive leaders.
Sweat started the season strong for the Bears, getting two sacks in the first three weeks. But he hasn't earned a sack since then, and his 73.1 impact grade from Pro Football Network falls below the league average of 75.0. Nevertheless, he remained an impactful defender for Chicago and his absence will be sorely felt on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons and next Thursday against the New England Patriots.
As a silver lining, third year defensive end Austin Booker appears to be coming into his own as a capable pass rusher. According to Bears reporter Herb Howard, Booker had expressed frustration with his limited role on the team through the first four weeks of the season. In Week 5, however, Booker saw an increased role and racked up two sacks, his first multi-sack game in his NFL career.
However, that's a small consolation for the Bears who badly need a strong defensive showing. The Falcons have made mincemeat of opposing defenses this year, thanks specifically to an electric season from running back Bijan Robinson. The Bears would have a hard enough time stopping him as it is. Without Sweat, however, a difficult task becomes monumentally hard.
There's no way to sugar-coat this loss for the Bears. They've just lost a captain and leader of their defense at a time when their entire season appears to be hanging in the balance. Their only hope is that Caleb Williams can return from injury for Week 6 and lead a high-octane offense that puts up points in bunches. They'll also be hoping that Booker can have another career game.
If Booker continues his upward trend, he may even push the Bears into making a hard decision regarding Sweat's future with the team. Sweat signed a four-year extension with the Bears shortly after they acquired him from the Washington Commanders in a deal at the 2023 trade deadline, and the 2027 season will be the final year of that deal. If the Bears feel that Booker has supplanted Sweat's role, they could save $21 million worth of cap space by releasing him.

title: Bears Considered Possible Suitor For Pair of Jets Trade Candidates
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' defense was riding high for three weeks, but the unit came crashing back down to Earth in a 31-7 Week 5 loss against the Green Bay Packers.
A loss like that is bad in and of itself, but it's even worse when it is against a division rival. Chicago's cornerbacks got absolutely torched, and a key edge rusher, Dayo Odeyingbo, got hurt .
The cornerback position has been a concern all season long, and especially because of No. 1 cornerback, Jaylon Johnson, who has been terrible. The team's other outside cornerback, Tyrique Stevenson, hasn't been any good, either.
As for edge rusher, things have been better than expected with Odeyingbo, Austin Booker and Montez Sweat, but Odeyingbo's injury is a stark reminder of how important it is to have depth at one of the most important positions on the football field.
Knowing all of that, general manager Ryan Poles should continue to look out for help at both positions.
Pro Football Focus' Bradley Locker identified 15 possible trade candidates recently and New York Jets cornerback Brandon Stephens and edge rusher Will McDonald were two of them.
And, he deemed the Bears as a possible fit for both players.
"Given that Stephens is a 2028 free agent and the team drafted D’Angelo Ponds in the second round, a trade may not be that implausible," Locker stated. "Pittsburgh and Detroit could have interest given their needs, while Stephens’ 88.7 man coverage grade would be enticing to Chicago and Cincinnati.
"The Jets seemed to make future investments in the edge rusher position with David Bailey and Joseph Ossai this offseason, while Kingsley Enagbare has also played more than McDonald," Locker said. "The 27-year-old on a one-year deal should draw eyes for teams looking to better pursue the quarterback."
With the struggles of Stevenson and Johnson , and with rookie Malik Muhammad still being unproven, the Bears should most definitely consider making an addition at cornerback.
Adding to that, there is no such thing as too much edge rusher help, so the same goes for that position. Chicago's need will be dire if Odeyingbo is forced to miss extended time, although we don't know if that will be the case with his quad injury yet.
Stephens has no doubt seen struggles over what has been an inconsistent career, but he has been solid over five games this season. Stephens has allowed completions on 41.9% of the passes thrown his way and a passer rating of just 72.1. His coverage grade of 68.1 ranks 23rd among 104 qualified cornerbacks, according to Pro Football Focus .
Those numbers are far and away better than Johnson's (83.3%, 118.7) and Stevenson's (60%, 143.7), so Stephens could be viewed as an upgrade.
McDonald has posted two sacks and 12 pressures so far this season, marks that would rank tied for third and third among Chicago edge rushers.
In the two previous seasons, the Jets EDGE showed he's capable of impressive production with 10.5 sacks in 2024 and eight in 2025.
Adding one or both of these players would make for a crowded situation at cornerback and/or edge rusher, but the Bears should hedge their bet in order to make sure they aren't lacking at either spot during a season in which they have Super Bowl aspirations.

title: Embarrassing Loss Exposed Bears' Real Need Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
Bears defensive flaws became obvious in Sunday's loss at Green Bay, as they suddenly looked like a team with two rookies in their secondary.
Their inexperience issue had only been exposed briefly in the opener, but when you win by 22 points no one seems to mind much. When you get blown out in Lambeau Field, it's not difficult to detect.
The five pass completions of 30 yards-plus by Jordan Love was an NFL record and spoke more to their secondary breakdowns than their pass rush's problems. They had two Austin Booker sacks and, according to Pro Football Focus, they graded out nicely at coming after Love for a team that just lost by 24 points to their biggest rivals. The only defensive linemen who failed to achieve what PFF's scale calls good numbers coming for the QB were Jordan van den Berg, Kentavius Street and James Lynch. Combined, those three had only 28 pass rushes. That was a very small number compared to others and made their situations less significant.
The coverage was the real problem, not the rush. This week the defense is going to need to devote all resources to stopping running back Bijan Robinson, meaning many of their defensive backs will be locked up in one-on-one coverage with Falcons tight ends or wide receivers. The potential for more big plays allowed exists.
For months, Bears fans and NFL analysts have spent their time pining for a trade to acquire Maxx Crosby, Khalil Mack, insert edge rusher here. The can't connect the Bears to any trade idea fast enough for an edge. Yet, the Bears have three defensive ends with two sacks or more on the year and their pass rush pressure hasn't been bad at all. ESPN's pass rush win rate has the Bears 14th in this metric as a team, after they were among the league's worst at it all last season.
What the Bears really need on defense immediately simply to survive on a weekly basis in the NFL is someone at a different position. They lost their biggest move of free agency when safety Coby Bryant went out for what could be the season with a knee and leg injury. Their replacements are not performing at an adequate level and definitely didn't on Sunday.
🚨THIS IS AWFUL🚨 This video of #Bears DB Cam Lewis suddenly collapsing in the middle of a play has gone viral. Lewis appeared to go down without making contact with another player. You rarely ever see anything like this happen on a football field. 🙏 pic.twitter.com/y69HoFEo9o
The Bears need a real NFL safety playing in back with rookie Dillon Thieneman, who gave up a  big play  Sunday but generally has played well for his lack of experience.
Safety Xavier Woods graded out with the worst overall Bears overall pass coverage grade against the Packers, and looked like he was in slow motion on one TD pass allowed. Safety Cam Lewis was sub-par. Lewis did have a decent start to the year for two games, but both of his last two efforts were poor by PFF grading and now he has a hip injury.
Xavier Woods just got BAKED. pic.twitter.com/uWRSfkVkwD
The Bears never did adequately address their safety problem after losing Bryant by trading for a starting caliber player. They went scrounging through the unwanted free agent pile. Usually there is a reason if a player is unsigned by the start of training camps.
Instead of looking at their defensive line, the Bears should have been trying to trade for someone to play safety through the bulk of the regular season, someone who could help get Thieneman some direction in back when he needs it. A quality safety might even be able to help Jaylon Johnson keep from being embarrassed the way he was Sunday.
It's not too late. There are players who are potential solutions before the November trade deadline.
Here are names of players who could be available based on contract, their playing time status with their current team, or their team's likely willingness to move someone before the deadline.
This is the defensive rookie of the year huh? Dillon Thieneman is actually buns 😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/Q9YKTjHyoB
He's being paid like a top safety but not performing that way with a 1-4 team in the early stages of rebuilding. A veteran player, he wasn't with the Saints when Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen was there so there is no scheme knowledge. He played for the Chiefs and Texans prior to being in New Orleans.
Just watch Justin Reid (#21) on this play pic.twitter.com/SRef70T6Qt
Of course, they wouldn't be making this trade this week since they play the Falcons but Bates is out of contract after this year and has a lousy 130 passer rating against when targeted this year. Falcons GM Ian Cunningham--or is it football president Matt Ryan--probably could be talked into coughing up this veteran for a draft pick. Much speculation has been he'll wind up in Detroit, but the Bears would be a good place for him as well.
FUMBLE! JESSIE BATES PICKS IT UP AND RUNS IT IN FOR SIX! @BALvsATL on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QNUGByteeh
People are always speculating the Cardinals' seven-time Pro Bowl safety is available, but his high salary could prevent the Bears from looking his way. He's not off to a great start, having allowed two TD passes per Pro Football Reference numbers. He also has a 109.4 passer rating against when targeted and allows 12.5 yards per completion when targeted. Still, the Bears could use a 30-year-old safety to help guide Thieneman and Baker has been a good one. The Cardinals are going nowhere in the NFC West and should be trying to build their stockpile of draft picks. Cost is an issue, though.
Budda Baker is a potential trade candidate from the Cardinals. Arizona seems close to going into full-blown sell mode, and Baker could net a Day 2 pick this year. Baker is under contract through 2027, so a contender would get two playoff runs with an elite safety. pic.twitter.com/F91QGLQQAu
This would be a shrewd acquisition because the 49ers had him starting in his first two seasons and he has been bumped to backup duty now, but still plays effectively.  He has been on the field for only 112 pass plays this year. In 2024 as a rookie, he allowed only a 44.4 passer rating against and 35% completions (7 of 20) when targeted.
Malik Mustapha with FORCE 😳 @49ers 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/aawaRQPSqH
An undrafted 25-year-old who is out of contract after this season, he became the starter last year and was strong in coverage but isn't nearly as effective this season with a new coaching staff. Cleveland's surprising 3-2 start might keep them from trading him, although it must be remembered they are still in a rebuilding mode and would listen to offers.

The three-year, $36 million contract extension he signed probably makes him less likely to be moved. He has been an effective defender and is in his prime.

A backup for the Raiders who started in 2024 and 2025. This would be a more risky addition since he has allowed 11 TD passes the past three seasons. The Bears probably have better ways to address their problems by using Lewis.

title: Bears NFL Power Rankings Week 6: Experts Dock Chicago After QB, Defensive Debacles
full_text:
As we turn the page to Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, it's time to see how the Chicago Bears stack up in the NFL power rankings of experts.
What we can confidently say is that the Bears aren't going to be moving up in anyone's power rankings after getting absolutely shelled by the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.
While the Bears should get a bit of a pass because they didn't have Caleb Williams under center, that is not an excuse for how badly the defense played, which was especially frustrating to watch because the unit had played better the previous three games.
Ranking: 13 | Last week: 7
The Bears take a terrible tumble in Orr's power rankings this week, and we can't say we blame him. Chicago's loss was a total failure on both sides of the ball .
That said, Orr isn't concerned about the Bears.
"Chicago is going to be fine, and I’d urge everyone not to ruin the Ben Johnson-Matt LaFleur rivalry. It’s too awesome," Orr said.
Ranking: 10 | Last week: 10
No change for the Bears in Davis' rankings, which means he isn't holding the loss against Chicago, and for good reason: the Bears didn't have their starting quarterback .
"Just throw out Sunday's Lambeau sleep. Injured QB Caleb Williams appears on the verge of returning for a team that generally held up well without him," Davis writes.
Hopefully Williams is going to be back in Week 6, and it appears that's a real possibility . Otherwise, the Bears have a decision to make between Tyson Bagent and Casee Keenum (spoiler: they should choose Keenum).
Ranking: 13 | Last week: 8
ESPN's Courtney Cronin was asked to answer what the biggest issue on the Bears' defense is and she rightly pointed to the play of cornerbacks Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson.
"The Bears' preseason belief that their secondary would be the strength of the defense has gone out the window. That unit allowed Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love to complete six passes for 25-plus yards and has been trending down since a shootout with the Panthers in Week 1," Cronin said.
"Rookie defensive backs Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad II will understandably experience growing pains, but the play of veteran cornerbacks Jaylon Johnson (77.3% of targets thrown into his coverage have been caught) and Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (allowing a 140.7 passer rating when targeted) is a major cause for concern ," she added.
We're not really surprised by the play of Stevenson, who could be irrelevant once Kyler Gordon returns and takes over in the slot, which should push Muhammad into Stevenson's role on the boundary.
Johnson is the far more alarming situation. He has been getting cooked all season long, and that was the case again in Week 5 , when he allowed a pair of long completions, including one to Christian Watson that went for a touchdown.
Before that play, Johnson nearly allowed a touchdown on a long pass but it was negated because of penalty.
Johnson struggled last season, also, but we believed that was a result of him playing hurt. But Johnson is fully healthy this year and is still not playing anywhere near the level we expect.
That's a major problem for Chicago, and Johnson is firmly on track to getting cut in 2027.
Ranking: 15 | Last week: 8
We've saved the worst for last, as Prisco docking the Bears seven spots in his rankings amounts to the biggest drop Chicago has seen in this round-up.
"The run game struggled against the Packers, and because of that the backup quarterbacks did as well. But the worst part: The defense was awful," Prisco said.
The absence of Kyle Monangai was quite apparent, as Roschon Johnson could get anything going through the air. D'Andre Swift had a pretty good game, but he didn't have many opportunities because of game script.
The Bears are hoping Monangai will be back in Week 6, but with him being labeled as "week-to-week," the second-year running back could end up missing another contest.

title: Ben Johnson's Answer on Bears' Week 6 Starting QB if Caleb Williams Can't Play is Telling
full_text:
Unlike last week, Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson was not quick to name the Week 6 starter on Monday if Caleb Williams can't play against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.
After starting Case Keenum in Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles, Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson kept the Week 4 decision for who would start between Keenum and Tyson Bagent close to the vest and did not announce it publicly before starting Bagent ( well, unofficially, at least ).
Then, ahead of the Week 5 game against the Green Bay Packers, Johnson made the announcement early in the week , revealing Bagent would get the nod for a second straight game
Things are different this week, though. Johnson was asked who would be the starter in Week 6 if Williams can't play again, but he was not quick to name anyone. Instead, Johnson said the team plans on "assessing" the situation during the week.
"No determination has been made in terms of what direction we’re going," Johnson said of the starting decision, according to ESPN's Courtney Cronin . "There are a lot of things that we’re assessing right now."
When asked specifically if Bagent is still the No. 2 quarterback, Johnson dodged the question.
"We have three guys that can win games in this league," Johnson said.
Seeing the difference in Johnson's willingness to name one of his backup quarterbacks the starter for this week is telling. We take this as a sign that Bagent's QB2 status is in real trouble, at best, and it could mean Chicago is moving off him entirely.
And, quite frankly, they should be. Bagent was terrible against the Packers and the Bears should be turning to Keenum if Williams isn't able to make it back after a three-week absence from his hamstring injury.
Bagent just looked lost on Sunday. He wasn't as accurate as he was in Week 4, and he tossed a pair of bad interceptions, which ultimately led to him getting benched for Keenum.
"We felt like we just wanted a little spark there," Johnson said of benching Bagent on Sunday. "Tyson just could never feel like he got in a rhythm here today, and so we'll look at why that was the case. The second interception happened, and we just felt like let's give Case a chance out there and see if we get different results."
Keenum came into the game and didn't fare much better, with the 38-year-old signal-caller throwing an interception and losing a fumble in what was a continuation of the poor play the Bears received from their quarterbacks in the divisional loss.
But, to be fair to Keenum, he came into an impossible situation down 31-7, so he deserves the benefit of the doubt.
As of right now, if Williams can't go, we predict it'll be Keenum, not Bagent, against the Falcons.
Thankfully, it appears the Bears may not have to decide between their two backup quarterbacks, as the chances of Williams returning in Week 6 are looking at least pretty good.
Williams showed progress on Friday by logging a limited practice , which was his first practice participation since his Grade 2 hamstring strain.
Then, on Sunday, Williams got some work in pregame and looked to be moving well before he was ruled inactive for the contest.
NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported that Williams is "pushing to play" and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noted that "all signs point to" Williams making his return against Atlanta.
If we had to guess, we'd say Williams will be under center when the Bears take the field on Sunday. We might have a clearer picture on Wednesday, when the Bears drop their first injury report.

title: The Bears Aren't Afforded the Luxury of Slow-Playing Kyler Gordon's Return
full_text:
Kyler Gordon is one of the Chicago Bears' most polarizing players. There's no denying his impact when he's on the field. The star nickelback is one of their best defenders.i
However, concerns over his health have persisted throughout his career. He's never been able to stay healthy, and those issues became especially glaring last season. Unfortunately, they've also bled into the 2026 campaign.
Bears head coach Ben Johnson has been notably mum when asked about Gordon (and he's been asked about him a lot).
Ben Johnson's full answer when asked about Kyler Gordon. Very interesting. You can tell he is a bit annoyed. pic.twitter.com/iRjIfCXxXN
Understandably, he expected Gordon to be fully healed from the hamstring injury that plagued him last season. Nevertheless, that somehow wasn't the case, as Gordon was placed on the Physically Unable to Perform list at the start of training camp.
Some even began questioning whether the 26-year-old played his last snap for Chicago. The best ability is availability, and that also happens to be the only one Gordon doesn't possess.
With that said, the team opened up his 21-day practice window on October 1. He will officially have until next Thursday to be added to the active roster, or he'd be forced to miss the entire season. With him consistently practicing in full since returning to the (practice) field, there's little doubt whether he'll see the field for Chicago this season.
However, Johnson and Co. have emphasized the importance of trust with Gordon. That has led many to question what his role will be when he does finally return to the lineup.
Their hands are officially tied, though. Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson's play has given them no choice.
The Bears' defense has had a few Jekyll and Hyde performances thus far. They haven't had any mid-tier performances. They've either been horrible (as they were against Green Bay and Carolina) or great (as they were in the other three contests).
However, Stevenson and Johnson have unfortunately been consistently bad . They've strung together multiple poor performances to begin the season, and some have even questioned whether the latter should be benched. The two-time Pro Bowler has looked a step slow in coverage all season and has allowed 83.3% of passes thrown his way to be completed this season.
While Gordon's presence might not be enough to outright bench Johnson, it would give them some stability on the back end. The Bears have struggled mightily at defending hyper-athletic pass-catchers this season. While Gordon might not have elite top-end speed, his short-area quickness is unmatched in Chicago's cornerback room.
Kyler Gordon back in action. Full participant today. pic.twitter.com/2qfdmdvjl9
It's still unclear whether Chicago will activate Gordon ahead of their Week 6 matchup against Atlanta. If Michael Penix Jr. doesn't play, they conceivably might wait until their Week 7 game against New England. However, he'll surely play a big role as soon as he's ready to go.
The Bears desperately need a spark in the secondary, and, if he stays healthy, the star nickelback is the perfect man to provide it. He has a chance to reclaim his status as one of the league's premier slot cover men if he can make the most of the opportunity.

title: What Bears Miss Most About Caleb Williams Can Rapidly Reverse Their Fortunes
full_text:
One loss to the Green Bay Packers and the world has ended for Bears fans.
Take a look at social media over the last day and Ben Johnson's great turnaround of the franchise might as well have never happened. His play calling, game plan and failure to get the team up emotionally so they could win one for the late Mike Ditka are all among reasons Johnson is being lambasted.
Cornerback Jaylon Johnson was probably cut on social media about 739,000 times on Monday for his coverage breakdowns.
Dillon Thieneman? A bust. Malik Muhammad? A bust.
Ryan Poles should be fired for the Montez Sweat trade in 2023. Ryan Poles should be fired, period.
I know one god damn thing.. We better be seeking a poor man’s Caleb Williams in the draft as a backup QB moving forward..
These are all out there floating around simply from one loss.
It all sounds like something Packer fans would say about the Bears, and ironically Packers fans were all saying something similar about their own team just a few weeks ago after their blowout loss to Atlanta.
I knew Tyson Bagent played really poorly yesterday, but after the dust settled, I can say that I didn’t realize he played one of the worst games I had ever seen from a Bears quarterback. And that’s saying something.
This is life in the NFL, where fans think the season depends on one game only to realize, "oh yeah, there's a game this week."
Tyson Bagent probably gets the most criticism just one week after a win.
People forget Ben Johnson is 2-1 vs Green Bay with Caleb pic.twitter.com/Tn1keWmlAl
There's nothing really wrong with the Bears that can't be fixed, especially by one simple thing about their play. Of course, this is Caleb Williams' return. With as much productivity as Johnson squeezed out of Case Keenum against the Eagles in his start, there's nothing like having your starter and especially one thing about Williams.
Bears fans saw it if they were watching Josh Allen send the Rams to their third loss in five games. Remember, this was the team everyone said was a lock to win it all. And they're 2-3. How does that make Bears fans feel about their team?  It's early and no one should be too caught up in a 3-2 record is the message.
Rome Odunze's falloff needs to be studied. pic.twitter.com/QI73kV5clg
What the Bear saw from Allen is something they have when they get Williams back, provided he really is healthy. It's that ability to take it upfield if everyone is covered. It's the great deodorizer for Johnson if the play call doesn't work or is sniffed out by the defense.
The Bears have had 15 runs for 107 yards from Williams in less than two games of action. He had a 29-yard long, ran for seven first downs and two touchdowns. He might have even scored a third against Minnesota when he went down with the hamstring injury. His 29-yard run five weeks into the season is still top 20 for fastest runs in the NFL (16th, 20.78 mph).
This is the defensive rookie of the year huh? Dillon Thieneman is actually buns 😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/Q9YKTjHyoB
He moved the sticks, put points on the board with his legs and his arm.
Meanwhile, without him for three starts and the end of the Vikings game the Bears have had three less rushing attempts from their backup QBs combined. Bagent has seven scrambles for 18 yards, Keenum five for 10 yards. Both ran 7 yards for a long. They have only one first down and had one touchdown from the two on the ground combined. Bagent has no rushing first downs and Keenum one. Bagent averages. 2.3 rushes per game and Keenum 1.7. Williams averages 7.5 rushes a game. This is a major factor for a team that loves the concept of ball control, or wants that added dimension to complement the pass, or just wants the running ability to set up passes off platform.
Jaylon Johnson's completion percentage allowed by year. 2020: 56.4% 2021: 59.7% 2022: 58.8% 2023: 55.2% 2024: 66.1% 2025: 72.7% 2026: 83.3%* He's been trending down for quite some time but this is as bad as it gets.
Josh Allen beat the Rams this way. Williams does it to Bears opponents.
It's about passing but if you can complement it with the run the passer's skillset is all the more dangerous.
Who deserves the most blame today? Jaylon Johnson Tyson Bagent Dennis Allen Ben Johnson Montez Sweat Rome Odunze Everybody?
Williams even can help the defense by letting them play with a lead or with the ball because of his ability to run.  Williams is the answer to what ails them in so many ways.
Before succumbing and getting in step with the group throwing in the towel on this season, simply remember what the team looked like in Week 1 on offense and can again once Williams returns and is throwing to his wide receivers and tight ends, throwing it farther downfield than Bagent, or running it like a running back at times.
Blame pie for Chicago Bears today goes like this: 🍕- Ben Johnson - 50% The team was unprepared for this rivalry, and he was out coached 🍕- Tyson Bagent - 15% 🍕 - Jaylon Johnson - 15% 🍕- Roschon Johnson - 5% 🍕- Dennis Allen - 5% 🍕- Rome Odunze - 5% pic.twitter.com/6jwu4CjDTE

title: Austin Booker Expressed Frustration Over Role With Bears Before Week 4 Game vs. Jets
full_text:
Chicago Bears defensive end Austin Booker is apparently not happy with his role over five games of the 2026 season.
A few days before the Week 4 game against the New York Jets, Booker spoke to Bears beat writer, The Score's Herb Howard , and expressed frustration with his role.
Booker told Howard that he wanted more snaps on defense.
"Two days before the Jets game, Bears DE Austin Booker expressed to me that he wasn’t happy with his role on the team," Howard wrote. "He wanted more playing time. In the two games since then Booker has 3 sacks and 4 (tackles for loss)."
Howard said he asked Booker on Monday if he had changed his approach prior to the past two games, when Booker has notched three sacks and four tackles for loss, and Booker responded:
“No. When the snap count goes up, the production goes up," Booker said.
Well, Booker's desire for more snaps was met on Sunday, as the third-year edge rusher played a season-high 44.  In the game against the Jets, he only played 20, although that did equate to 62.5% of the defensive snaps in the game.
It isn't clear if the increase in snaps was Booker getting the "squeaky wheel gets the grease" treatment or a result of the injury to Dayo Odeyingbo , who left after 23 snaps with a quad injury.
Booker played 40 (58.8%) in Week 1, but then saw his playing time dip to 19 snaps (36.5%) the next week, and then he played 30 (60%) and 20 snaps, respectively, over the next two games. The 44 snaps in Week 5 amounted to 72.1% of the total plays on defense for Chicago.
Booker was an absolute menace against Green Bay. Along with his two sacks and three tackles for loss, Booker also added four run stops and his 85.3 overall grade was third-best among the Bears defensive players, per Pro Football Focus .
It was the second time in his career Booker has tallied two sacks in a game. The other time came in Week 15 of last season, when he had two sacks and two tackles for loss in the win over the Cleveland Browns.
With those two sacks, Booker is now up to four on the season and is just 0.5 shy of his career-high, which he achieved in eight games last season. He ultimately played in nine but did not tally a sack in the Bears' regular season finale. He did, however, post another sack in the playoff win over the Green Bay Packers.
It isn't clear if Odeyingbo is going to miss any time with his injury, but if he does, Booker will almost certainly be locked into more snaps until the veteran returns.
Even if Odeyingbo plays, it's clear after Sunday that the Bears need to figure out a way to get Booker more involved.

title: Bengals' Offense Has Finally Found Strength in One Major Weakness
full_text:
The worst week of the NFL season is the bye week. That's where the Cincinnati Bengals find themselves in Week 6.
After a sloppy 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, the Bengals will have a week to recover and prepare for a major matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
Everyone can agree this team has a lot to work on if they want to avoid a 0-2 start in the AFC North. But there are a lot of positives to take away from the first five weeks of the season. One of the biggest positives has actually been the play of the offensive line.
Since Joe Burrow took his first steps on the field as a member of the Bengals, the team has struggled to protect their star quarterback.
Every season, the conversation turns to how the Bengals cannot protect Burrow, and every fan feels that is one of the biggest hurdles holding back this team. Well, that hasn't been the case in 2026.
According to Pro Football Focus , the Bengals have a pressure allowed rate of 20.6%, which is fourth best in the league. Only the Atlanta Falcons, Kansas City Chiefs, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers have posted a better percentage.
Protecting Burrow is the most important goal for this team every time they step on the field. The Bengals' offensive line has allowed just nine sacks this season. That ties them with the Indianapolis Colts for seventh-best in sacks allowed.
After Sunday's game in Miami, it's clear that the offense is clicking. The Bengals were dominant in the red zone, and Burrow connected with four different targets on touchdown passes in the win. If everyone stays healthy, this offense could reach heights that would even surprise the likes of Burrow and his explosive collection of offensive talent.
However, the defense is another story. For now, just celebrate the wins, and this offensive line is giving the fans something to be proud of. After years of discussion around protecting Burrow, the offensive line is in position to keep the franchise signal-caller upright.
Burrow has thrown for 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. He has a 71.4% completion percentage, 104.4 QB rating and a 75.3 QBR. He also received a major compliment for his recent play from national NFL analyst Mark Schlereth.

title: Joe Burrow Gets 'Brady-esque' Praise After Bengals' Week 5 Win
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals entered their early bye week on a high note with a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday.
Sure, there's plenty to pick at from the Bengals' performance, but earning a win in the NFL should never be overlooked. With all the talk about what needs to be fixed before the team takes the field in two weeks, there's one area that's doing just fine.
That area is the offense, and the guy who leads that unit. Quarterback Joe Burrow was in elite form on Sunday. Fox analyst Mark Schlereth, who called the game, sees a lot of one legendary quarterback in Burrow's game.
During a conversation about Burrow on The OG Football Show, Schlereth had nothing but praise for the Bengals superstar.
"I spent about three hours watching Joe Burrow type and I walked out and thought to myself, I can see why they never run it," Schlereth said. "He's so Brady-esque in that he's the best scrambler in football that never leaves the pocket. He never escapes out of the back of the pocket. He's always working toward the line of scrimmage, even if it means he's going to take one in the teeth."
Any time a player is compared to Tom Brady, ears are going to perk up. Brady is arguably the greatest ever to play the game. When someone who has the accolades at the highest level, like Schlereth, says Burrow has the attributes of Brady, it's coming from a strong source.
A lot of the talking coming into the game against the Dolphins was about the Bengals relying too much on their pass game. After throwing 54 passes in Week 4, Burrow had 32 pass attempts in Week 5. The workload was reduced, but the success rate was still high as Burrow completed 23 of those 32 passes and tossed for touchdowns with a QBR of 126.3.
Having a strong run game to back up Burrow is obviously vital. However, this team goes as far as nine can lead them. Seems like a good idea to give him as many opportunities to make a play as the coaching staff can.
Burrow has thrown for 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. He has a 71.4% completion percentage, 104.4 QB rating and a 75.3 QBR. Check out the full clip below:

title: Bengals Star Ja'Marr Chase Gets 'People's Elbow' Fines Wiped Out on NFL Appeal
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase got a win in his celebration battle with the NFL. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport posted on X Wednesday afternoon that Chase won his appeals for fines the NFL handed down to him and Tee Higgins for their "people's elbow" celebrations during the Week 2 win against the Texans.
There is no word on whether Higgins had all of his fines rescinded. Each fine was $14,926. The NFL fined Higgins four times and Chase twice from that one game. The two players were fined $89,556 for the arm signage.
"Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase won appeals of fines for his 'people’s elbow' celebration, as two fines of $14,926 were rescinded from the #Texans game," Rapoport posted on X. "From the appeals office letter, 'On appeal, Mr. Chase … further contended that even if he committed the violation, his fine should be reduced because he received no warning that this was not allowed. He added that this is a new celebration with his teammate and that it is not offensive. Mr. Chase finally stated that the NFL is assuming the worst of him and his teammate without discussing with the NFLPA.'"
A bunch of these fines from an oddly-heavy Week 2 got rescinded this week, and Chase is the latest to get his money back.
He revealed the fines to the media when they came down and implored the NFLPA to help its stars.
"I don't know. I'm trying to figure out because that's not what it is," Chase told the media about getting the league's perspective on what they think the gesture is. "This is literally like a wrestling move. You know what I'm saying? So I don't know. Maybe I should stop. I don't know. Maybe I could do it like this (he did a tweaked version of the move at the podium). Keep doing it. I don't know, man. I don't know. It was something different for us, something we try to be unique with. Just stopping the fun. So it is what it is."
The league clearly changed its tune on what the "people's elbows" meant, and Chase at least got his bread back.

title: 'That's Just The Media' - Jordan Battle Backs Up Comments Against Miami With One of Best Bengals Outings
full_text:
Jordan Battle talked the talk and walked the walk on Sunday.
The Bengals safety became the first player with multiple interceptions in the same game for Cincinnati since Logan Wilson in 2023. He revealed the ball-patting tell for Miami passer Malik Willis, and that bold callout paid off.
Now, Battle addressed the performance after the game and did admit he couldn't see Willis's eyes on either of the interceptions, but he had the script all the same.
Battle finished with seven tackles, two picks and a 79.2 Pro Football Focus grade (third-best on Bengals defense).
"That's just the media. You know, everybody's looking for the next story, and obviously it went big, went viral, and that's just part of football," Battle said about the patting comments.
Battle got the first pick off a deflection and the second one off a great read in the open field. It was a strong performance on the ball, but he can still clean up the tackling more.
The safety was the only Bengal to miss multiple tackles on PFF's grading following the game. He missed two of the Bengals' six missed tackles.
"Yeah, pretty much like I feel like everybody's saying it, just finish," Battle said about what the team needs to do next. "Games like that got to be able to close them out. I feel like even better than we did. Give up the late touchdown and the offense obviously getting the ball back as well. So it's got to be better. But closing out, doing a better team effort late in games."
Something the whole team feels . There is no clear top team in the NFL right now, and the Bengals can be that, but they can't keep committing untimely mistakes as they have in the first third of the season.
"We got to be smarter. We got to be smarter. Two fumbles in the red zone. A couple of personal fouls that hurt us, hurt our field position, and gave them points on the board. We got to be smarter," Joe Burrow said after the win.
Cincinnati has a few days off before getting back together and working on the Ravens matchup in Week 7.

title: Bengals Pass Catcher Expected to Miss Rest of 2026 NFL Season With Major Injury
full_text:
The Bengals lost a key depth piece for the season on Tuesday. WLWT's Charlie Clifford posted on X that backup Bengals tight end Tanner Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle in Sunday's 31-24 win over Miami and is done for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
Hudson had just been signed to the active roster for the rest of the season, but his time gets cut short in 2026. He finishes the season with seven catches for 33 yards and a score against the Dolphins.
" Bengals tight end Tanner Hudson suffered a torn pectoral and is expected to miss the remainder of the season, his agent tells WLWT," Clifford posted . "Brutal news for a reliable pass-catching option in Cincinnati."
Zac Taylor noted the injury in Monday's press conference but didn't indicate it would be this serious. Cincinnati also saw depth linebacker Swayze Bozeman break his forearm and go on in-season injured reserve.
The team signed former Notre Dame linebacker Jack Kiser to replace him and could add another piece to replace Hudson on the roster or practice squad ranks during these bye week days.
Cincinnati is trying to put together a winning streak after the days off and take advantage of the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL by most metrics.
They have to clean up the self-inflicted wounds to fully maximize it.
"Trust me, I'm not going to sit here - we got to win games in this league, and we've all sat in this room and seen some get away from us," Taylor said on Sunday. "We won the game, and I'm excited about that. Then, our defense created a turnover there at the very end that gave us three extra points that made it a 7-point game that made it feel a little bit different. We did some good things. There are some positive things we did, but there are also some things that we don't turn the ball over in the red zone like that: the kickoff, the PAT, the field goal. Those are things that we're better than that, and we got to clean that up."
Cincinnati takes on the Ravens next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Barrett Carter Doesn't Believe Bengals Defense Played to Standard in Week 5 Win
full_text:
Winning the NFL is hard to do. The Cincinnati Bengals know that quite well. Coming into their Week 5 meeting with the Miami Dolphins, the Bengals had lost two straight.
The losing skid ended in Miami as the Bengals earned a 31-24 win over the winless Dolphins. Getting a win before the bye week makes this an easier week to get through for fans, but the players understand their performance on Sunday wasn't enough.
Linebacker Barrett Carter spoke with the media about the defense's performance and let everyone know that the unit did not meet the expectations the players and coaches know they can reach.
"I'm not going to take away the value of winning, that's something we don't take for granted, but just watching the tape and finishing the game up yesterday, we all know that game was not up to our standard," Barrett told Cole McIntire of FOX19 . "We know that's nowhere near our standard and nowhere near what we need to do to play long-term football."
If you only saw the final score you would have thought this was a back-and-forth contest. However, it was a game the Bengals always had in hand, they just couldn't figure out a way to close the door.
The Bengals allowed the Dolphins to rush for 217 yards on Sunday. Prior to the game between the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night, the Bengals allowed the 10th most rushing yards per game at 123.
It wasn't just the run defense that was a concern on Sunday. The Bengals entered the fourth quarter with a 10-point lead against one of the more disappointing teams in the league and allowed Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis to almost pull off the unthinkable. Willis scored a rushing touchdown and had a passing touchdown in the final quarter.
Every game is vital in this league. When the Bengals resume play they will have one of their most hated rivals, the Baltimore Ravens, waiting for them. If Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is back by then, this defense needs to look levels better the next time they take the field.

title: Bengals Announce Linebacker Addition During 2026 Bye Week
full_text:
The Bengals announced a roster addition amidst Swayze Bozeman's move to injured reserve. Cincinnati is signing former Jaguars linebacker Jack Kiser off of waivers to help fill the special teams void.
The 2025 fourth-round pick played in 14 games for Jacksonville, totaling 10 defensive tackles and four special teams tackles last season. He spent one game on the Jaguars' practice squad and was inactive for three games earlier this season, before being waived over the weekend.
He played for Al Golden at Notre Dame and should be able to slide in quickly on that front. Bozeman broke his arm but is expected back this season.
"Swayze (Bozeman) broke his forearm, so he'll go to IR," Taylor said about the latest injury updates earlier today. "Tanner Hudson has a pec issue that we're gathering more information on. Kyle Dugger (quad) is still week to week. Those are really the main three right now in terms of guys that would be affected coming out of the bye."
Cincinnati won a grimy 31-24 game on Sunday, but the Bozeman arm injury is the only major issue that popped up from the Miami heat. Now, the whole team gets to reset for a few days and focus on Baltimore next week.
"We had a tremendous opportunity coming out of the bye with the divisional game to put ourselves to the top there, and so right in front of us. So opportunity to get healthy, get your legs back under us," Taylor said today. "I do think the heat really hits well after Miami. I mean, I've never coached there for four years, never really thought about that. But the heat really does drain you, to the point where I'm sure it affects you the next week.
"So I'm happy that it hit for guys to be able to recover and get that, and then get your legs out under us and start getting ready for some colder weather, which we're very familiar with, as the season gets going here."
Kiser figures to work into the special teams unit soon after Bozeman played 64 snaps on the kicking units this season. The new Bengals LB played 193 played snaps last season on ST and none this campaign in Jacksonville.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Bengals Injury Situation Entering 2026 Bye Week
full_text:
Zac Taylor and the Bengals are back from Florida, with no major injuries added to the ledger after a rough week on that front. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins got through the game without any setbacks, and Zac Taylor discussed the team's overall health before entering the official bye week window.
Cincinnati is 3-2 on the season for the first time since making the Super Bowl during Chase's rookie year in 2021. The Bengals beat Miami 31-24 and didn't have any huge issues pop up after the game.
"Swayze (Bozeman) broke his forearm, so he'll go to IR," Taylor said about the latest updates. "Tanner Hudson has a pec issue that we're gathering more information on. Kyle Dugger (quad) still week to week. Those are really the main three right now in terms of guys that would be affected coming out of the bye."
The Bozeman blow stings, he has played 63 snaps for the Bengals on special teams this season.
The Bengals kept up with the rest of the AFC contenders this week and didn't lose any ground in the division. A group that could get really shaken up after Cincinnati's second division game of the season on Oct. 25 against Baltimore.
Cincinnati has two AFC wins so far and needs to amass as many as possible.
"Glad we won. Hard to win in this league. We've certainly been in those games before where we let them slip away and didn't get the win," Taylor said on Sunday. "Credit to Miami. They fought us tooth and nail till the very end. I thought Jeff Hafley is doing a great job with these guys, man. He's got them believing. They fought us like they fought a lot of other teams. They gave themselves a chance. There are a lot of frustrating things on our end. We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the four-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown, gave them four points, and gave up over 200 yards rushing. Plenty to clean up.
"The bye hits us at a great time. I know these guys are worn out. We've had some down-to-the-wire games the last three weeks. I know how hot this one was today. The bye week comes at a great time for us to be 3-2. These guys will regroup. We know who we are. Today, there are a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks."
The Bengals lick their injury wounds this week before preparing for Baltimore.
