title: Jordan Battle, Dalton Risner And More Pop With Strong Pro Football Focus Grades Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Pro Football Focus grades are in for the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon. Cincinnati leaders like Joe Burrow and Zac Taylor weren't too thrilled with how the team played, and the grades reflect that.
Cincinnati had its third-lowest team grade of the season (72.7) and only had 11 players grade out at 70-plus or higher. Starting on offense, Tight end Tanner Hudson made the most of his call-up with a team-high 89.9 PFF grade on 19 snaps.
The rest of the top five went in this order: Guard Dalton Risner (84.6), Joe Burrow (76.3), WR Ja'Marr Chase (75), and RB Samaje Perine (70.7).
Risner is posting his best year of grading since entering the league in 2019. He has a career-high 81.7 offensive grade and a career-best 80.7 pass-blocking grade powering that mark. He's currently the sixth-highest graded NFL guard with at least 190 snaps.
At the bottom, A few skill position players rounded out the low offensive grades, including Drew Sample (46.1), Chase Brown (47.3), Mike Gesicki (55.3), Tee Higgins (56.5), and Mitch Tinsley (58.8).
Brown and Perine were pretty close in snap count, at 38 for Brown to Perine's 33, something to monitor in the final two-thirds of the season.
Moving to the defense, defensive end Boye Mafe had arguably the best performance of any Bengal and continues to prove the team right for pivoting to him instead of sticking with the Trey Hendrickson train this offseason.
Mafe notched a defense-high 88 grade on 49 snaps. Five other Bengals defenders logged 70-plus grades: LB Demetrius Knight Jr. (79.2), safety Jordan Battle (79.2), DE Shemar Stewart (71 on only eight snaps), DT B.J. Hill (70.9), and CB DJ Turner II (70.3).
Linebacker Oren Burks also just missed out on that group with one of his best games as a Bengal. He had a 69.5 grade on nine fill-in snaps.
At the bottom of the defense, defensive end Cashius Howell (45.4) checked in with the lowest grade, followed by safety Bryan Cook (45.9), defensive end Cedric Johnson (47.5), linebacker Barrett Carter (52.4), and cornerback DJ Ivey (54.1). Cook had one of the Bengals' six missed tackles in the game.

title: Joe Burrow Reflects on Dominant Play in One Area During Bengals Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' backs were up against the wall coming into Week 5. After back-to-back losses, it felt that a loss to the winless Miami Dolphins would have sparked even more uncomfortable conversations around the team.
It wasn't the cleanest performance, but the Bengals got back in the win column with a 31-24 victory over the Dolphins. There are certainly some things that need to be cleaned up, however, quarterback Joe Burrow was on his A-game.
After his impressive performance on Sunday, Burrow spoke with the media and was asked specifically about his effectiveness in the red zone.
"Our receivers did a good job of finding space. We didn't get a ton of man coverage, but when we did, we made them pay," Burrow explained. "We had good field position most of the day, and I think for the most part we took advantage of it. But we had some dumb mistakes, and we got to get those fixed if we want to be a great team."
Three of Burrow's four touchdowns on Sunday were in the red zone. Like Burrow stated, if a team is going to give this offense good field position for the majority of the game, the unit has to make them pay. That's exactly what Burrow did.
Along with their red zone success, the Bengals converted 69.2% of their third down conversions. Extending drives is the name of the game, and this offense will bruise any defense if they can stay on the field.
This offense can be the most dynamic unit in the league. They proved that on Sunday. But there is still a lot to clean up before they take the field again in two weeks.
In particular, running back Chase Brown had some struggles hanging on to the football. The Bengals running back had two fumbles on the day.
Waiting for the Bengals out of the bye week is the Baltimore Ravens, who picked up a dramatic win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football. With the Bengals already suffering a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, the game against the Ravens will be pivotal for the AFC North race.
Early bye weeks are brutal, but a reset at this point in the season may not be such a bad thing for a team that has already seen injuries to key players.

title: 3 QB's Browns Could Target in 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
Even though the Browns are 3-2 and quarterback Deshaun Watson has looked better than ever in his five seasons with the team, Cleveland will likely draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.
Here are three prospects to watch out for:
The dream of drafting Manning seemed to end after the Browns won their third game in Week 4, as the most likely path to selecting the Texas quarterback would require the No. 1 pick.
However, that doesn't seem to be the case anymore.
Manning has faced his fair share of struggles this season, and they came to a head in Saturday's loss to Oklahoma. Manning threw two critical fourth-quarter interceptions: one pick-six and another that set up the Sooners to win.
Manning will likely declare for the 2027 draft, but he might not even be the first or second quarterback taken. If the Browns finish in the middle of the pack and draft around No. 15, Manning could slide to them.
Coming into the season, the talk was all about Manning as the No. 1 quarterback prospect for 2027, with Moore ranking No. 2. But even Moore has struggled this season.
The Oregon quarterback has played in only three games, and a concussion he suffered against USC in Week 4 kept him out of Saturday's game against Nebraska.
Moore could return this season, but it's unclear how he will perform.
Moore has thrown for 926 yards and nine touchdowns, with no interceptions, this season.
Simmons might not have been on anyone's radar as a first-round pick heading into the season, but he's played well at Missouri. Most people remember Simmons starting a few games for Ole Miss last season, but he got injured, which led to Trinidad Chambliss taking his job, and he never got it back.
Now, Simmons is playing well in his first season with the Tigers, throwing for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns and one interception in six games.
Simmons is already getting love to join the Browns, as Pro Football Focus's Gordon McGuinness mocked him to Cleveland in a mock draft on Tuesday.
"Simmons appears to be one of the biggest in-season draft risers, with Yahoo Sports' Nate Tice placing him in the top 10 of a recent mock draft." McGuinnes wrote. "Given how the Browns retooled their offensive line and wide receiver corps heading into the 2026 season, I think now is a great time for them to find a quarterback to build around. Simmons has earned an 87.5 PFF passing grade and produced a 17.6% positively graded play rate so far this season."
The Browns could end up sticking with what they have, but if they do consider making moves this offseason and bringing in new faces, these are the best options so far.

title: Where the Browns Rank in the NFL Standings and Team Statistics Through First 5 Weeks
full_text:
Through the first five weeks of the NFL Season, the Cleveland Browns are a very middle-of-the-pack team.
In some cases, they fall on the lower side of the spectrum. Ultimately, the Browns are not playing like a top team statistically anywhere.
In the official week six NFL power rankings, the Browns fell four spots from 17 to 21.
However, 21 is way better than 32, which is where the team was ranked after that ugly week one loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
While the rankings themselves mean virtually nothing, Cleveland is being looked at by experts as a near bottom ten team in the league.
But what do the actual stats say?
The major stat that stands out for Cleveland is the number of sacks allowed. So far in 2026, the Browns have allowed Deshaun Watson to be sacked 19 times. This leads the entire NFL.
Additionally, the Browns are failing to score touchdowns. They are tied for third-worst with only nine touchdowns this year.
On a positive note, the Browns have only thrown two interceptions this season (T-6th), but also have four rushing fumbles, which ties them for fourth most.
The final offensive stat that shows a major issue the Browns have is the average yards per carry. With only 3.7, the Browns find themselves tied for eighth-worst.
Defensively, the Browns look a lot better on the field than the stats give them credit for.
Cleveland has a total of six forced fumbles (T-9th) and four interceptions (T-8th). On top of that, they have a total of 16 sacks (6th) and 324 tackles (T-10th).
As for what needs to be cleaned up, the Browns are allowing 11.5 yards per reception (T-23rd). This number, accompanied by the 10 receiving touchdowns they have given up (T-25th), shows that secondary depth truly is another issue the Browns could invest some assets into bulking up.
Looking at some other numbers, the Browns are among 10 teams that have made every field goal attempted this year. Their total of 10 made field goals ties them for sixth most.

Arguably, the best Browns player statistically this season has been their punter, Corey Bojorquez.
Bojorquez not only has the longest punt in the NFL through five weeks (81 yards), but he averages 51.8 yards per attempt, which ranks second best in the league.
Unfortunately, Bojorquez has been able to play so well due to the number of reps he as received. Cleveland is tied for seventh in total punts with 24.
Clearly, the numbers show that the Browns have some major problems with the offensive line, secondary depth, and running game situation.
If they want a chance to win some more games and not be exploited by other teams, they should attack the upcoming NFL trade deadline, which is less than a month away.

title: What Raheim Sanders Landing on IR Means for Browns' Current Running Back Room
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to lose another one of their running backs due to injury.
In Sunday’s disappointing 17-12 loss to the New York Jets , the Browns ended the game down two of their running backs, both their lead option in Quinshon Judkins, as well as their back up Raheim Sanders.
Now, Sanders will miss at least the next four weeks after being placed on the injured reserve. This forced Cleveland’s hand in finding a running back to fill in during Sanders’ absence with Judkins presumed to miss time as well.
#Browns have signed RB Audric Estime and placed RB Raheim Sanders on IR for at least four games. Big loss.
In response to Sanders injured reserve designation, the Browns signed Audric Estime to the 53-man roster. He will likely take on a large amount of the work as Cleveland’s top running back if Judkins isn’t cleared.
Here are the running backs that can step up in the meantime for the Browns moving forward:
It was just announced yesterday that the Browns were signing Estime off of the Minnesota Vikings practice squad , but with the injured reserve move for Sanders, it’s now official.
Estime spent his first NFL season with the Denver Broncos, where he saw playing time in 13 games as a depth piece. Then, he spent his next season with the New Orleans Saints, appearing in seven games. His career totals include 122 carries for 508 yards and three touchdowns.
While Estime is only 23-years old, he has the type of skill set the Browns are looking for in their offense, as he can be a pass catcher out of the backfield as well. His combination of size and speed makes for an interesting pairing in an offense that’s desperate for run game help.
He’ll spend the next week getting up to speed on Cleveland’s playbook and should see playing time this Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens.
McLaughlin is the veteran option in the running back room for the Browns, as he spent his first three years of his career with the Denver Broncos before being signed by Cleveland.
If Cleveland feels they want more experience out of the backfield, then McLaughlin would be the smarter option to feature more in their offense. McLaughlin’s career totals include 228 carries for 1,124 yards and four touchdowns.
In McLaughlin’s Browns debut, he scored a 28-yard rushing touchdown on one carry against the Pittsburgh Steelers . That was promising to see him breakthrough in his first appearance, which could be a case to use him more in an offense in need of a spark.
The only way Patterson will see any playing time on the Browns main roster is if another injury occurs to one of their running backs. For now, Patterson remains on their practice squad waiting for his next opportunity.
In Patterson’s career, his stats include 126 carries for 503 yards and three touchdowns split between the Washington Commanders and the Los Angeles Chargers.
He’s another player with more experience, but not enough for Cleveland to view him as one of their top options. If another injury comes up, Patterson would hear his name called to likely back up whichever healthy running back remains.

title: Browns’ Tight End Concerns Could Set Up an Ohio Homecoming Trade
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have had immense difficulty in the run game through five games of the 2026 season.
Lack of depth at tight end may be the biggest contributor.
And in order to reach the team's full potential, adding a new body to the mix might be the best option.
The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 offseason program with multiple tight ends on their roster. The room thinned after Cleveland released Jack Stoll from injured reserve and placed rookie Joe Royer on the reserve/non-football illness list due to an off-the-field issue.
This left Blake Whiteheart, a fringe practice squad veteran, and Carsen Ryan, a seventh-round pick who has also worked at fullback, as the depth behind standout Harold Fannin Jr. Because of this limited tight end depth, the Browns may be restricted in terms of flexibility with heavier personnel.
Sets featuring multiple tight ends, such as 12, 13, and 22 personnel, can provide additional blocking options by adding more tight ends into the fray. Because the Browns have limited proven depth behind Fannin, their ability to use these personnel groupings is limited, making the offense much more one-dimensional.
Pair this with the fact that Cleveland’s tight end unit ranked last in the NFL with a 45.0 PFF run-blocking grade entering Week 5, according to Jets X-Factor, and the need for another quality tight end on the Browns roster is clear.
Because of the Browns’ lack of depth at tight end, it may be time for Browns GM Andrew Berry to go shopping ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10th. One potential fit for the Browns’ TE2 role is former Ohio State Buckeye standout tight end Cade Stover, as first suggested by Brandon Little of A to Z Sports:
With the Joe Royer mystery and lack of tight end depth, the Browns should call the Texans to see if they can get Cade Stover back to Ohio. Wouldn’t take much to get it done. pic.twitter.com/juBB5R7Jr8
Stover makes sense, as he is currently playing a limited role with the Houston Texans. Stover only has two receptions for 18 yards for the Texans this season.
Stover was drafted by the Texans in the 4th round of the 2024 NFL Draft and earned a 60.7 PFF run-blocking grade that season, the highest among Houston’s tight ends, checking another box for the Browns.
Stover is still on a rookie deal and was only drafted two seasons ago, meaning his price may not be low despite his limited role.
However, if Andrew Berry can get Stover at a price he deems acceptable- say, a day 3 pick, a return to Ohio could benefit both Stover and the Browns.

title: How Adding Notre Dame Standout Audric Estime Gives the Browns RB Room A Boost
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are adding a bit of insurance to the running back room.
On Monday, Oct. 12, it was announced that former Notre Dame standout and early NFL journeyman Audric Estime would be signing with the Browns . The front office, amid countless injuries to the running back room, is hoping that Estime can provide the depth with some much-needed depth.
He joins the team from the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad.
Sources: The #Browns are signing RB Audric Estime off the #Vikings practice squad to their 53-man roster. The 23-year-old Estime brings 508 career rushing yards, 130 receiving yards and 3 TDs to Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/cN57eboBz3
After losing RB2 Dylan Sampson earlier in the season, the team was dealt a bad blow on Sunday following a loss to the New York Jets. Starting back Quinshon Judkins was banged up, eventually leaving the stadium in a walking boot.
Just hours before the signing of Estime was announced, Browns head coach Todd Monken confirmed that Judkins and Sampson were still injured , but didn't give any insight into whether or not the two would be ready to suit up this weekend against the Baltimore Ravens.
Instead, he opted to say that every injured Brown wouldn't be fully ruled out yet.
But the signing of Estime does show that the Browns are at least somewhat planning for a future where another back is needed.
The 23-year-old was drafted in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft, playing for both the Denver Broncos and the New Orleans Saints since then.
He has rushed for a total of 508 yards, three touchdowns and roughly 4.2 yards per carry across the last two seasons, tacking on 130 receiving yards along the way.
With a heavier workload, or just a decent increase in general opportunities in both the passing and rushing attack, Estime could become a legitimate threat in the Browns' offense. After all, he showed just how impactful he could be while in college.
Just to also add, Estime is 5-11, 227 lbs, and is a physical north/south runner. He did run a 4.58 40 time at the combine, so he’s not a burner, but this reads to me like a Jud replacement while they sit him down for his health. Also, an Audric Estime & Jaleel McLaughlin… https://t.co/fEkZjtEoEL
In his 2024 junior season, he was one of college football's best running backs.
He took off for 1,341 yards and 18 touchdowns on a whopping 210 carries. He averaged 6.4 yards per attempt and rushed for over 110 yards per game.
While he was never really a big-time receiver in South Bend, he did haul in 26 catches for 277 yards across his sophomore and junior campaigns.
With Estime finding so much success while being a member of the Fighting Irish, there is a strong thought that with the right scenario, he can unlock that talent once again.
At the end of the day, a signing like Estime doesn't hurt the team at all.
He is not going to immediately come in and change the depth chart, but he does give the team another young option out of the backfield. While he will certainly have to prove himself, the strugglesome start to the season from Judkins and the rest of the room will give him a better path to reestablishing himself in the league.
If Judkins and Sampson end up missing Sunday's contest against the Ravens, the Browns will likely turn to Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin to take over most of the workload.
Well it took a couple years, but the Browns finally got Audric Estimé. The Browns are signing Estimé to their active roster off the Vikings practice squad. Coming out of Notre Dame, Estimé (5-11, 230) was drafted in the 5th round by the Broncos in 2024. The bruising back has… pic.twitter.com/A9vJJ6GIIP
However, all it takes is a few good practices, a solid first impression or an injury to someone else to immediately thrust him up the ladder and onto the gridiron.
For now, though, Estime will make his way to Cleveland and begin preparing for the Ravens this weekend. The two sides will clash at Huntington Bank Field at 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Oct. 18.

title: Browns Sign Running Back in Wake of Struggling Run Game and Injuries
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are looking for any way possible to give their run game a boost moving forward.
After suffering a tough 17-12 loss to the New York Jets this past Sunday, and Cleveland’s run game being virtually non-existent, the Browns had to make a move.
On Monday, the Browns went out and signed another extremely young option to hopefully boost their running back room moving forward.
Sources: The #Browns are signing RB Audric Estime off the #Vikings practice squad to their 53-man roster. The 23-year-old Estime brings 508 career rushing yards, 130 receiving yards and 3 TDs to Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/cN57eboBz3
Estime last played for the New Orleans Saints before being cut from the injured reserve just a few weeks ago. He was their preseason rushing leader, and has totaled 508 yards rushing on 122 carries in the 20 NFL games he’s appeared in.
He was picked up by the Vikings and put on their practice squad a little over a week ago but was picked up by the Browns on Monday to join their 53-man roster. This move was made in response to Quinshon Judkins’ injury sustained on Sunday.
Here’s why the signing of Estime makes sense for the Browns:
Aside from the recent injury to Judkins, the Browns are already without their backup running back Dylan Sampson, who was put on the injured reserve after his opening week knee injury.
Cleveland does still have Raheim Sanders in the backfield, as well as Jaleel McLaughlin, but outside of McLaughlin’s touchdown against the Steelers, both have been uninspiring options to lead the Browns’ backfield.
It’s not a good sign when the second leading rusher on the team is a 31-year-old Deshaun Watson at quarterback, and he only trails Judkins as their lead rusher by 54 yards.
In steps Estime, who brings two years of NFL experience to the Browns running back room. After starting his career with the Denver Broncos for 13 games, Estime played in seven games with the Saints.
It won’t be a permanent solution to Cleveland’s struggling run game by any means , but it’s worth a shot giving Estime playing time as he’s shown he can be serviceable. If the Browns want to develop their run game at all, they’ll need production out of Estime.
It isn’t expected that Judkins will miss an extended period of time , but after his significant injury suffered last season limited his availability during the offseason, the Browns might take it slow getting him back on the field.
The Browns have time to prepare for the Baltimore Ravens this Sunday, which is a great time for Estime to get up to speed with Cleveland’s playbook to ensure he’s ready to go moving forward.

title: If Deshaun Watson Keeps Losing, It's Time To Make a Change
full_text:
The rain was pouring down, and the offense was sloppy in the Cleveland Browns' loss to the New York Jets. The offense had a difficult time running the ball and protecting Deshaun Watson en route to scoring only 12 points.
The loss dropped their record to 3-2 and the Jets improved to 2-3.
Watson did not have a good game as he held onto the ball too long, leading to eight sacks. His decision-making was slow, and he did not even get a throw off on the last play of the game. The Browns even surprised themselves with a 3-1 start, and the odds of them making the playoffs increase exponentially at 4-1. However, they lost and the season may have a different outlook.
They fell to second place and will have to play the 4-1 Baltimore Ravens next week to try to keep pace in the division. The Jets game was considered very winnable, and the Browns should have come out victorious to make the playoffs more possible.
If the Browns’ offense continues to play poorly and losses start to mount, then they need to make a change at quarterback. Outside of a miracle, the Browns can finally move on from him after the season. They have to decide the future of the most important position in all of sports.
Should losses start to stack up, then the Browns may be in a position to draft a top quarterback from college. They also have backup Shedeur Sanders on the roster and he has not had a chance to show what he can do in Todd Monken’s offense so far this season. If the playoffs are not in the fold for the season, they have to see what Sanders can bring to the offense.
NFL purgatory is being “in the hunt” without making the playoffs. As the playoff contention window gets closer to shutting, then the move has to be made to evaluate Sanders.
The Browns also have two more games before having to make a decision on activating Dillon Gabriel from the injured list or shutting him down for the season with the injury designation. In the next two games, the Browns play the Ravens and the Tennessee Titans.
If the Browns lose both games, their record would drop to 3-4, with losses to the one-win Jets and zero-win Titans. Being under .500 pummels the odds of making the playoffs, and they would have lost to two bad teams. Watson should then be benched, and the Browns would still have time to play Sanders; if he shows he cannot play, then they can also see what they have in Gabriel.
Although Watson has led three game-winning drives so far this season, he has still not been overly impressive. There have been long stretches in each game where the offense goes stagnant. The game against the Jets was not all his fault, as the offensive line was bad, the receivers dropped good passes, and there was no running game, but he did not do enough to win.
They are still over .500 and one game should not alter the season, but winning will get more difficult if the offense continues to look like it did on Sunday. Todd Monken claimed that Watson gives the team the best chance to win, which he did for the first quarter of the season. If he cannot continue to win, then the Browns have to move on.

title: Todd Monken Shares Positive Update on Browns Running Back Injuries
full_text:
Well, the Cleveland Browns learned they still have more to work on.
Losing 17-12 in a Sunday duel with the New York Jets , the Browns moved to 3-2 on the season. While a loss is always going to be difficult to swallow, especially when it ends a three-game winning streak, what followed made the entire road forward even bumpier.
#Browns HC Todd Monken said Quinshon Judkins "had a little tweak" in his ankle from yesterday's game, which is why he left in a medical boot. Monken described Judkins as "day-to-day."
Already without running back Dylan Sampson due to an injury occurring in the season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Browns found out starting back Quinshon Judkins was newly banged up as well.
After the loss to the Jets, Judkins was seen in a walking boot, casting doubt on his health.
On Monday, Oct. 12, head coach Todd Monken confirmed that Judkins was dealing with an ankle injury. However, he did say that he wouldn't rule out any of the team's injured players for the Browns' Week 6 clash with the Baltimore Ravens, which includes Judkins.
He is considered day-to-day, though.
Along with Judkins, Sampson's timetable to return to the gridiron is unknown. The team is considering opening up his practice window this week, but the possibility remains up in the air as he continues to recover from his early-season knee injury.
Browns coach Todd Monken said there is a “possibility” the team opens RB Dylan Sampson’s practice window this week. He’s missed the last 4 games with a knee injury.
For a team that was looking at potentially being without an RB1 and RB2, hearing that both are not officially counted out for Sunday's game against Baltimore is a positive sign.
With both Judkins and Sampson still not fully healthy, the Browns may have to turn to a backfield that features just Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin as of now. And while both have shown little spurts of promise this season, there has not been a clear path ahead for anyone in the room.
As a team, the Browns have just 471 rushing yards on 126 attempts , finding the end zone twice along the way.
Through five games, that is less than 100 rushing yards an outing, a far cry from where the franchise has been in the past.
It's hard to blame one player in particular, especially considering the offensive line is still brand new and the whole unit is attempting to find its identity with starting quarterback Deshaun Watson leading the charge, but Judkins averaging just 3.0 yards per carry and Sanders and McLaughlin only receiving 11 combined handoffs to start the year, the Browns are going to be facing an uphill climb moving forward.
Both Sanders and McLaughlin, at least right now, don't feel like stomachable options out of the backfield for the next few weeks, especially as the Browns still look to establish a dynamic offense.
It wouldn't be shocking to see the front office go out and add a third option to the backfield if Judkins and Sampson both aren't ready to return by the weekend.
As the week continues on, Monken will certainly continue to provide updates on the two.
The Browns and Ravens clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland for an in-division clash on Sunday, Oct. 18.

title: 24 Hours Later: My Thoughts on Lackluster Browns Performance in Week 5 vs. Jets
full_text:
In a few months, we may be looking back on this game as the reason the Cleveland Browns missed the playoffs.
24 hours later, here are my thoughts on the Browns week five loss to the Jets
. @TheOGPAW and @HammerNation19 are wondering how much blame should be put on Quinshon Judkins on the Browns lack of run game. pic.twitter.com/iBaG4EslnE
The Browns had countless chances to score on offense. I understand the rain made things a lot harder, but there's always a way to get things done.
The Jets came into the game with the NFL's 25th-ranked run defense . Despite this, the Browns failed to establish a run game. They finished the game with 96 rushing yards, with 40 of them coming from Deshaun Watson.
Outside of the ground game, the worst moment of the contest by far came with just 4:13 to play.
Cleveland had just scored a touchdown. On the next defensive drive, Carson Schwesinger strip-sacked Jets quarterback Geno Smith. This gave the ball back to the Browns with the lead, 4:13 left to go, and in Jets territory.
You would think Todd Monken and the Browns offense would simply want to burn as much clock as possible right?
Instead, Quinshon Judkins ran the ball out of bounds, and after back-to-back incompletions, the Browns only took 21 seconds off the clock. Of course, this led to the fumbled punt, which set up the Jets for the win.
Outside of the special teams error, this drive is what lost the Browns the game. The inability to take either time off the clock or timeouts away from the Jets was incredible. Instead, Monken got too cute with the football, trying to put an end to the game.
This season, when the opponent figures out how to stop the Browns offense , that has been it. The best example of this was the week four game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Cleveland scored 21 of their 27 points in the second quarter. After halftime, the Browns had a scoreless third quarter followed by a squeaked out win in the fourth after leading by 14 earlier in the game.
Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson need to find a way to reset the offense during bad times throughout games. When things go wrong, they need a formation or set of plays they can confidently run despite the circumstances.
Outside of some great film on situational failure to review, the Browns need to move on from this game.
This loss cannot take away from the incredible start the team had with three straight game-winning drives. Looking at the schedule, the Browns have some very winnable games coming up.
This week, they play the Baltimore Ravens at home. Lamar Jackson's status is unclear at the moment, but it should still be close, with the defense. After that game, the Browns play the 0-5 Tennessee Titans, the Steelers once again, and then the 1-4 New Orleans Saints.

title: 2 Glaring Holes in the Browns Offense that Need Addressed Now
full_text:
So far this season, we have seen the Cleveland Browns on display five different times. Clearly, there are two big things that need to be fixed on Offense
With the NFL Trade deadline less than a month away, these positions are two the Browns should aim for in potential trades.
Ever since Quinshon Judkins was injured against the Bills last season, we have yet to see him return to that rookie-year form.
It doesn't help that Dylan Sampson went down with an injury in week one, but the Browns still should be getting it done with the former Buckeye.
If Cleveland decides it wants to improve the running back room, I do not expect them to fully get rid of Judkins. Instead, I see a trade to either bring in help alongside Judkins or to block for him.
That brings us to the main position group that needs to be reworked.
This is such a complicated group because all five starters are brand new to the team this season.
Is it a lack of experience? Two of the five big men are rookies who are only five games in to their professional careers.
Is it a lack of playing time together as a unit? The line has had all offseason to mesh, so you would hope that would be enough time to learn assignments and how to work together.
Regardless, the unit ranks dead last in sacks allowed with 19 this season. At this rate, the Browns are on pace to allow 65 sacks this year.
In the run game, the Browns are averaging just over 94 yards per game. Most of the time, 20-30 of those yards are coming from Deshaun Watson on scrambles.
Would you trade Jerry Jeudy to the Titans for Tony Pollard? Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay proposed the two teams swap players to help bolster areas of weakness on each roster. "No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed… pic.twitter.com/aXaVm1VTie
The Tony Pollard, Jerry Jeudy swap has been thrown around for the past few weeks. If the trade is legitimate, it is something the Browns should absolutely consider with Tennessee.
Pollard could bring another aspect to the Browns' run game as a dynamic runner, while Jeudy could go in as a much-needed pass-catching option for Cam Ward.
As for the Offensive line, the name doesn't matter nearly as much as the experience. The Browns need to go after a strong run blocker who has had reps with a winning line in the past.
Overall, changes need to be made to the Cleveland offense if they truly want to go all in for a playoff push this season.

title: Cowboys Legend Emmitt Smith Makes Epic Dancing With The Stars Super Bowl Night Cameo

The Dallas Cowboys haven't been in action since last Thursday, which was an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home, and the team won't return to the field until Sunday night against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field .

Dancing With The Stars was holding its first-ever Super Bowl Night , so they called on the show's champions with NFL experience, which included Smith and legendary wide receiver Donald Driver, who, funny enough, starred for the Green Bay Packers.
Before Tuesday night's competition got underway, Smith and Driver made a cameo on stage to take part in the show's opening number. Emmitt and Driver danced to "Humble" by Kendrick Lamar.
THEY ATE DOWN #dwts https://t.co/wadKbQRHVj pic.twitter.com/P0vdG82qw1
Smith won the third season of Dancing With The Stars in the fall of 2006, with professional dancer Cheryl Burke. Of course, during his time in Dallas, Smith was a three-time Super Bowl champ, Super Bowl MVP, NFL MVP, five-time All-Pro, 8-time Pro Bowler, and a four-time NFL rushing yards leader.
Smith still holds the NFL records for most career rushing yards, most career rushing touchdowns, and most career rushing attempts. It looks like he's still got those quick feet.

title: Dallas Cowboys First-Round Bust Continues To Struggle Finding NFL Home
full_text:
Former Dallas Cowboys starter Mazi Smith has struggled to live up to his lofty draft status, and was released by the Miami Dolphins on Tuesday. Smith, who was a first-round pick for Dallas out of Michigan in 2023 was part of the Miami practice squad and appeared in just one game for the Dolphins.
Smith spent two and a half years in Dallas before being traded to the New York Jets last season as part of the deal for Quinnen Williams. Smith played three games for the Jets, but never recorded a tackle. He was released ahead of the 2026 season before signing with Miami, where he also failed to record a tackle.
That means since leaving Dallas, Smith has appeared in just four games with 69 total snaps and not a single tackle. It's an incredible fall from grace for a player who entered the NFL as a serious threat to be a force as a nose tackle with a promising mix of speed and strength.
When the Cowboys selected Smith at No. 26 overall in 2023, he was supposed to solve their ongoing issues with run defense. Dallas had several flashy players at the time, including Micah Parsons and Osa Odighizzuwa, who were able to generate pressure on the quarterback.
What they didn't have was someone who could do the dirty work and shut down the run. That's what the 6-foot-3, 337-pound Smith was supposed to do. Unfortunately, he never found a steady role with the team.
Under Dan Quinn, Smith was asked to play a penetrating 3-tech role, with Quinn attempting to take advantage of his speed and athleticism. When Quinn left and Mike Zimmer took over, Smith was moved back to the 1-tech and fans were thrilled about the change. It seemed as though Zimmer was going to allow Smith to focus more on run defense, but he didn't find success there either. Instead, fans saw why Quinn tried to focus on his speed as Smith struggled to win with power and was often pushed off the line of scrimmage.
Now, Smith will be looking for his fourth NFL team. As for the Cowboys, they're still trying to figure out how to stop the run, even with Williams, Kenny Clark, and Otito Ogbonnia as their top defensive tackles.

title: Dallas Cowboys Hype Still Going Strong For Prominent NFL Insider Despite Slow Start
full_text:
It has been an ugly five weeks to start the season for the Dallas Cowboys , but the team will be entering Week 6 with 10 days of rest and an opportunity to make a statement with a big bounce-back win on the road.
Dallas wants to erase the memory of last week's embarrassing letdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and they'll attempt to do that against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football .
While the Cowboys have failed to live up to the preseason expectations, there are still many people who are believing in the team.
After all, Dallas entered the year with a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker and a completely revamped roster, so there will be some growing pains.
One person who still believes in the Cowboys is NFL insider Ian Rapoport, who voiced his support for Dallas entering a new week.
Rapoport shared his thoughts on Dallas' defense during an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show , and made it clear that he is still buying in on the Cowboys and believes they can be "really good" once the turnaround is complete.
“Maybe I’m crazy. … I still think the cowboys can be really good.” @RapSheet shares his thoughts on the Cowboys on the @RichEisenShow 👀 pic.twitter.com/eDv2wo7SUs
"They hired Mike Pettine. And this reminded me of when the Ravens had a young defensive coordinator named Zach Orr, who they really liked, and they kept bringing in Dean Pease to help," Rapoport recalled. "This, to me, has the same vibes. Like, I think the defensive coordinator is good. I think he's talented. I think he's going to be a good coach. Sometimes experience helps. Sometimes having someone come in and go, great thought, but it actually has to be this way. Sometimes that helps. And I think it was a good move.
"People talk about the Cowboys all the time. They do what they believe is necessary to win all the time, and they try to keep improving. The Joey Porter Jr. trade is going to be a really good one. He didn't play last week. That makes it hard to evaluate the defense. Bringing in Mike Pettine on the fly. Good move. Maybe I'm crazy. It's possible I'm crazy. But I still think the Cowboys are going to be really good . You can clip this off in like January."
Dallas has yet to field a fully health defense this season, so it's going to be exciting to see how the team responds when all of its projected starters are back on the field.
And after all of the years of dealing with putrid defenses, Cowboys Nation can battle through a few more weeks with the hope of seeing a turnaround. The words of encouragement from someone as dialed in as Rapoport certainly help.

title: Dallas Cowboys Announce Another Major Change to Help Christian Parker Fix Defense
full_text:
It's no secret that the Dallas Cowboys have arguably the worst defense in the NFL after five weeks of action.
Things were supposed to improve in the first year under new defensive coordinator Chrisitian Parker, but instead it appears they've only gotten worse. Sure, injuries have likely played a part in this, but that's hardly an excuse for some of the embarrassing miscues that have surfaced amid Dallas' 2-3 start to the season.
As a result of these shortcomings, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones announced Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan that Parker is moving from the sideline to the coaching booth in order to give him a better view of the defense during the game.
The changes for Parker keep coming, as this news from Jones comes less than 24 hours after Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer made his own announcement about a new addition to the coaching staff directed at helping Parker handle the defense.
Schottenheimer announced Monday that the Cowboys have hired former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive analyst. While Pettine was the defensive coordinator for the Green Bay Packers in 2019, he brought Parker on staff as a defensive quality control coach.
Jones said that the hiring of Pettine could have been done earlier, something Cowboys fans might feel is his attempt to cover up the team's clear initiative to aid Parker's ailing defense.
"This is something we would have done (earlier) had Mike been available," Jones said of Pettine, per Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com. "It fits so well because of the knowledge of the scheme, and the time he's had with Schottenheimer, the time he's had with Parker. Frankly, he's coached directly three of our players."
While the Cowboys have certainly failed the eye test on defense, the numbers don't do them any favors either.
Through five games, the Cowboys lead the NFL in most rushing yards allowed per game (168.4) and are second in total yard allowed per game (395.4).
At least Dallas doesn't have the worst pass defense in the league -- 12th-worst at 227.0 yards per contest -- but the scoring numbers are among the worst in the NFL at 27.2 points per game, eighth-worst through the first five weeks of the season.
Dallas' next chance to show things are trending in the right direction comes in another primetime spot, as the Cowboys will visit the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on Sunday Night Football in Week 6.

title: Cowboys Reuniting With Running Back After Cutting Ties With Veteran Offensive Lineman
full_text:
Just one day after the Dallas Cowboys cut a veteran offensive lineman, they have filled his spot on the 53-man roster.
On Monday, the Cowboys waived veteran offensive lineman Nick Leverett, who played in all five games with the team as a special teams contributor.
Then, on Tuesday, ESPN's Todd Archer is reporting that Dallas is signing running back Emari Demarcado to the 53-man roster, reuniting with the former Arizona Cardinals back. Leverett, meanwhile, is being re-signed to the practice squad.
Demercado was initially added by the Cowboys after cutdown day, when the Kansas City Chiefs waived him.
Dallas claimed the veteran running back one day after surprisingly waiving 2025 fifth-round pick Jaydon Blue , who everyone thought was at least going to make the Cowboys' 53-man roster.
When the Cowboys claimed Demercado, he was slated to serve as the team's RB3 behind Javonte Williams and Malik Davis. However, that quickly changed, as Davis suffered a season-ending hip injury just days before Week 1, which pushed Demercado into Dallas' RB2 spot.
Demercado didn't do much over two games, tallying five carries for 15 yards in that span. Then, Dallas decided to cut Demercado last week when guard Tyler Smith as activated off injured reserve. Dallas decided to keep Tyler Goodson, who was signed off the Atlanta Falcons' practice squad last month, over Demercado.
Over his three games with the Cowboys, Goodson has posted 34 yards on nine carries (3.8 yards per carry) and one catch for -5 yards. Now, he has some competition for the RB2 job.
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday that changes are coming to the roster , although we'd venture to guess swapping an offensive lineman for a running back isn't what he was talking about.
Instead, most of those changes are likely to come on defense, where the Cowboys have struggled badly.
"I’m not going to get to a bunch of them. Obviously, there’s a competitive advantage. But there’ll be some roster adjustments you guys will see. Some will be more noticeable than others, and some will be subtle as you look at it," Schottenheimer said, according to Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com .
We saw Dallas take the first step to trying to improve the defense by hiring former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant to help struggling defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
"Had a chance to work with Pettine for a number of years, along with the Jets, and he's gonna be here in a role to support everything that [Christian Parker] is leading and guiding, and we are really, really excited," Schottenheimer said.
The hire of Pettine is a very good step in the right direction, as the rookie play-caller, Parker, could use an experienced coach to help guide him through the troubled waters he's currently navigating.
Now, it'll be interesting to see what personnel changes Dallas is going to make on defense, and how effective they end up being. We may not know what those changes are until Sunday.

But while the team looks to regroup after last week's embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the NFL experts are dropping their latest batch of power rankings to show how teams around the league stack up against each other.
For the Cowboys, it's a rollercoaster, with rankings ranging from top 15 to the mid-20s. Much like the first five weeks of their season, inconsistency is the theme.
Let's take a look at what the experts from around the league are saying as we prepare for another primetime appearance for the Cowboys in Week 6.
This week's ranking : 23 Last week's ranking : 11
"I was listening to former Bengals coach Marvin Lewis the other day speak about Christian Parker’s staff in Dallas and his point was an interesting one: this is a very young staff around a first-time defensive coordinator. Multiple first-year coaches. My initial thought was that if Jerry Jones is truly a dangerous old man with money, he should pour some cash into a few analysts to help right the ship. Mike Pettine is a pretty good start." - Conor Orr
Orr acknowledges the Cowboys' immediate action this week to hire Pettine as an analyst. He brings some familiarity with Parker, thanks to their time together in Green Bay. There is mutual respect between the two, and it will be great for Parker to have someone he is comfortable with to bounce ideas off of.
While the Cowboys may have plummeted in the SI rankings, there is some reason for hope moving forward.
This week's ranking : 15 Last week's ranking : 12
"How do you pick just one issue when it comes to the Cowboys? They are giving up 27.2 points per game, which ranks 26th in the NFL. They are giving up 168.4 rushing yards per game, which is last in the league. They have recorded only five sacks and do not have an interception this season. Opposing quarterbacks are completing 72.3% of their passes. Through five games, new coordinator Christian Parker's defense might not be worse than it was under Matt Eberflus last season. But it is at least the same and a big reason why Dallas is 2-3." -- Todd Archer
You sense the theme here, right? The defense has been miserable, there is no other way to put it. And facing off against a Packers offense that just put 30 points on the board last weekend isn't the most exciting matchup for Christian Parker and company, but it will show just how much the unit is able to regroup after an embarrassing setback.

The defense is going to continue to be the talking point until things change, and Dallas took some positive steps this week. By bringing in Mike Pettine as a senior analyst, let's hope that the Cowboys can finally start moving forward and Parker can start to find his footing as a defensive coordinator.

title: Jerry Jones Defends Dak Prescott Heckler After 'Embarrassing' Tunnel Confrontation
full_text:
Last week, the Dallas Cowboys were embarrassed at home by the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers in primetime. The entire NFL world was watching, and the Cowboys found themselves as the laughingstock and punching bag around the league.
But the team didn't even need to wait until the morning sports talk shows to face the criticism and jokes, because it was right there at AT&T Stadium.
As Dak Prescott was making his way back to the locker room, a third-party contract worker, who was reportedly a valet driver, called out Prescott and the Cowboys for their "embarrassing" performance .
Prescott turned around to confront the man, but there was no further incident. On Tuesday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was asked about the incident and offered up an unexpected response during his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan.
Here’s our angle of a worker — either stadium employee or valet car driver — calling out Dak Prescott and the Cowboys performance, with Dak’s reaction which he said was prompted by the man looking away after saying the criticisms. #dallascowboys #nfl pic.twitter.com/ffznCyahvv
“The driver in question was not an employee, but fans can express themselves, and should express themselves,” Jones said during his appearance. “Whether he was our employee or not, he was a fan, it sounds like. So I'm for our fans expressing themselves .”
Who knew Jerry Jones would be the voice of reason?
To Prescott's credit, he had a similar response to the confrontation during his post-game press conference. He acknowledged the fan's right to criticize his performance and the team, but no one should be surprised if a player claps back.
Prescott said, "When he said it, I just happened to look at him at that point and he looked away, and then I turned my head back, and he said something else. That’s the part, just as a man of a person, feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don’t cower away from the reaction you’re going to get .”
Hopefully the team can use the incident as motivation to regroup and put together a better performance next weekend when they face off against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field .
Once again, the game will be under the bright lights, with kickoff set for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Surprisingly, the Cowboys are entering the game as slight 1.5-point favorites on the road, so let's see if they can get the job done.

title: Dallas Cowboys' 3 Biggest Concerns Entering Week 6 vs. Packers
full_text:
Thanks to several miscues by every team in the NFC East , the Dallas Cowboys have a golden opportunity to get back into the divisional race with a win in Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers .
Of course, the real question is whether Dallas can capitalize on the opportunity in front of them. They couldn't do so in Week 5, as they were thoroughly outmatched by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , who were starting an undrafted free agent at quarterback, Jalon Daniels.
Understanding they need help, head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced on Monday that Dallas added former Packers defensive coordinator and Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive consultant . He joins a coaching staff that has a lot of concerns entering Week 6, with the following three being the most pressing.
During the first four games of the season, CeeDee Lamb was unstoppable. He had at least five catches in each of those games, and went off in Week 4 against the Houston Texans with 17 receptions for 189 yards and a touchdown.
While he was taking off, the Cowboys weren't seeing the explosion from George Pickens they were used to. He had just three receptions in Week 4 and went into the Week 5 game without a touchdown. That changed against the Bucs as Pickens went for 130 yards and a touchdown. Unfortunately, Lamb had just two catches for nine yards.
Against the Packers, the Cowboys need to see both of their high-powered wideouts put up big numbers. That's the only way they will be able to keep up with the Packers, who should have an advantage against a banged-up secondary.
Despite struggles running the ball, Jordan Love and the Green Bay offensive have been able to rack up yardage through the air this year. Through five games, they have 1,355 yards passing, which is eighth best in the league.
Christian Watson has been especially problematic for opposing defenses, recording 474 yards and six touchdowns on 26 receptions. Second-year wideout Matthew Golden has also been playing well, with 24 catches for 397 yards and two touchdowns.
Either player is capable of racking up yardage in a hurry, and the Cowboys have a terrible pass defense that is dealing with multiple injuries . That could be a recipe for disaster.
Through five games, Dallas has just five sacks and no player has more than one. They knew when they went into the season they were unlikely to have anyone threatening for the league-lead in sacks, but the Cowboys also felt they had enough talent to get after the quarterback with a committee approach.
The issues in the secondary haven't helped, but it's clear that won't change. That's why the Cowboys need their pass rush to show up in this one to slow down the Green Bay offense. Whether they can rely on that remains their greatest concern.

title: Courtland Sutton Offers Strong Opinion on His Career-Low Start to the Season
full_text:
Courtland Sutton is off to a career-low start to his ninth NFL season. Bo Nix's slump hasn't helped matters, especially given that Sutton plays a quarterback-dependent position, but throwing out his 2020 campaign, which was mostly lost to an ACL tear, this is the slowest start to a season he's ever had.
Throw in the first-year learning curve of offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling the offensive plays the first four games, only to have Sean Payton take the play sheet back for Week 5, and the Broncos' juggling of how to fit in new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and it's been a struggle for Sutton this season.
The two-time Pro Bowler is on pace for a forgettable season statistically, but the 3-2 Broncos continue to win more games than they lose. Sutton's impact on this offense has been forgettable through five games, but he's striving to cultivate the right mindset and not allow his dip in production to affect his approach as a pro.
On Tuesday, the Broncos practiced for the first time this week in preparation for Thursday night's home tilt against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks . When asked after practice how he's handling not getting the ball as much this season, Sutton said, "Day by day, bro. Day by day."
Then the Broncos team captain let the fan base and media in on how he maintains his resilient mindset.
"Come to work every day, smile on my face, ready to work. You never know when the ball's going to find you," Sutton said on Tuesday. "I feel like the moment that you decide to take a step down, take a step away from it because things aren't going the way you want them to go in that specific moment, that's when you start to see failure creep in and doubt and all of these other negative emotions."
Sutton has just 11 catches for 104 yards thus far, but he was able to find the end zone for the first time this season last week in L.A. That used to be a solid single-game stat line for him.
Sutton has only been targeted 25 times, and the fact that they've only translated to 11 receptions illustrates how out of sync his chemistry with Nix currently is. That's a low target-to-reception ratio, but Sutton plans to keep his head down, do his thing, and not let these individual setbacks affect his attitude or mindset.
"Just staying prepared, staying ready, not allowing the circumstance to dictate my attitude, my effort, the way that I come to work, and the way that I attack my days," Sutton said. "So just staying prepared so that when my number is called, I'm ready."
As for Sutton's take on Nix, the veteran wideout has his guy's back completely, understanding that, as the quarterback, he carries "a lot of weight on his shoulders." If you polled anyone in the Broncos' locker room, Sutton believes you'd get the same response from each of Nix's teammates.
"It's not even just myself; I think if you ask all the guys in that locker room, the offensive guys, defensive guys, special teams, everyone has his back. We all know that for us to have success, we need 10 to be able to have that success," Sutton said of Nix. "We're going to always have his back no matter what, good, bad, or indifferent, because it would be the same way vice versa."
Sutton says that he and Nix have a lot in common as competitors who want everything to be perfect. So when it's not perfect, and frustration begins to settle in, they do a good job of reminding each other to "wipe it" and move on to the next play.
"When things aren't perfect, we get frustrated. So he sees me when something may happen in practice, and he comes over, and he's like, 'Wipe it. Let it go. On to the next one,'" Sutton said of Nix. "For us to be able to have that relationship, to both be able to go back and forth and say, 'Hey, look, wipe it, let it go. I got your back. You got my back. Let's go to the next play,'
"I think, like I said, you ask any of the guys in the locker room, everyone has that same mentality of wanting to have each other's back. And especially when it comes to 10, I think we all have that mentality of wanting to make sure that he feels comfortable, confident to be able to go out there and play fast."
Sutton may not be putting up Pro Bowl numbers right now, but he's fulfilling his role as a locker room leader. He's helping to keep his quarterback confident and rallying support in the locker room.
The Broncos continue to rally around Nix, and if the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, odds are, things will finally click for the third-year quarterback, and he'll be off and running. It doesn't help that the Broncos have faced the NFL's toughest schedule based on opposing offenses and the second-toughest based on opposing defenses.
I think some fans and folks in the media are losing sight of that because Nix hasn't taken those obvious steps forward that everyone expected him to in Year 3. But the level of competition Nix has faced to start this season — honestly, I've never seen anything like it, and that includes the Peyton Manning and John Elway eras. This Broncos team drew the shortest of short straws.
And yet, the Broncos are 3-2. From what I know about Sutton, Nix, and this Sean Payton-led team, all this early-season resistance training will eventually pay dividends for the Broncos, and they'll reach critical mass.
In the NFL, it's more about how you finish than how you start. Amid the rocky road of this early-season gauntlet, it hasn't been pretty, but the Broncos are still finding ways to win.
When they finally pull away from the first eight-week portion of this schedule, watch out. This team is developing a big, durable callus. And when everything finally clicks, nobody is going to want to see the Broncos on the schedule.
They've just got to keep their heads above water until this eight-week gauntlet is behind them. With selfless leaders like Sutton and others, I feel more than a little confident that the best is yet to come this season.

title: Kelberman's Korner: The Biggest Issues Currently Plaguing Broncos QB Bo Nix
full_text:
Let me start off by saying that Bo Nix isn't playing particularly good football at the moment. Certainly nothing like the Denver Broncos quarterback we all watched lead the club to what should have been a Super Bowl appearance just nine months ago.
Regarding the Broncos' slumping offense , which has surprised given this year's expectations, Nix is certainly worthy of fault. His efforts are more timid, apprehensive, and unconfident than the gunslinger of 2024 and 2025. He's supposed to be the franchise cornerstone, and has looked the farthest thing from it entering Week 6 .
Speculation points back to Nix's January ankle injury and subsequent surgeries as the primary suspects, with the masses theorizing he's become physically or mentally bothered by it. But that cannot be confirmed nor denied at this juncture.
What can be confirmed is that the proverbial blame pie has many slices to go around — and many individuals deserving. The argument to revive Denver's offense does not simply start and end with Nix.
Here are some of the other things that must be fixed sooner rather than later:
While veteran starter J.K. Dobbins upped his game a bit in last week's victory over the Chargers, the truth remains that Denver's offense ranks 25th in the NFL in rushing yards per game, and Dobbins himself is averaging under four yards per carry.
The Broncos are getting negligible ground contributions from RJ Harvey — their best pass-catching RB — and Tyler Badie, who's only seeing snaps due to rookie Jonah Coleman landing on injured reserve.
Coleman appeared to be the club's best true runner when he was healthy, so perhaps his potential return in Week 7 will alleviate some of the pressure from Nix, and rewire a pass-run ratio that got completely out of wack under now-former play-caller Davis Webb.
So much for Denver's supposedly "elite" front-five. With the exception of left tackle Garett Bolles and right guard Quinn Meinerz, the starting offensive line has struggled to generate push at the line of scrimmage — particularly for the ground game.
Left guard Ben Powers and right tackle Mike McGlinchey are playing at replacement-level standards, and the Broncos may soon want to think about a long-term future without those aging vets. Center Luke Wattenberg is financially protected by his 2025 extension, but he's made several errant snaps and is arguably the weakest link among the OL.
The pressure is mounting on Broncos offensive line coach Chris Morgan because, as the cliché goes, successful football starts up front. And they're the antithesis of that at the moment.
If you searched hard enough, you could probably find Courtland Sutton's face on a milk carton somewhere. Yes, he scored (on a wide-open pass) against the Chargers, but it's evident the now-31-year-old receiver isn't quite separating downfield like he used to.
Beyond that, the Broncos have utterly failed to incorporate their big offseason acquisition, Jaylen Waddle, who currently has more drops (5) than games with at least 20 receiving yards (2). Twenty . Most No. 1 WRs eclipse that on a single drive. But not Denver's.
Perhaps Nix's most reliable pass-catcher, second-year man Pat Bryant, is shelved on injured reserve for another three weeks, eligible to return in Week 11 following the Broncos' bye.
Reserve WRs Marvin Mims — who's disappointed amid a contract year — and Troy Franklin have been non-factors through the air as Denver ranks 26th in yards per play and points per game, and 25th in passing yards per game.

title: Broncos Have Two Major Matchup Problems to Solve vs. Seahawks
full_text:
On a short week, the Denver Broncos have a lot to improve, coming off their second-worst offensive showing of the season. You could call it the worst, given the caliber of defense Denver played in Week 5.
If the Broncos want to do better on Thursday Night Football against a much tougher team in the Seattle Seahawks, they have to win their key matchups. Let's break down the top two matchups to watch in this game.
The first part of this matchup deals with Nix vs. himself. He isn't playing up to his standard, and while his surgically repaired ankle could be an explanation, Nix hasn't used it as an excuse, claiming he's 100% healthy.
Some of Nix's recent remarks paint a picture of a gunshy quarterback hesitant to push the ball downfield after a few early-season interceptions. His timing is off in the pocket; he seems afraid of getting hit, and he is bailing on clean pockets at a higher rate than ever.
Yes, the Broncos' pass protection has allowed more pressure this year, but Nix is bailing clean pockets early, even when it's blocked up according to plan, leading to a higher self-pressure rate (meaning some of the pressures he is bringing on himself) and a higher clean pocket bail rate (meaning bailing the pocket without pressure).
Before Nix can truly reckon with his matchup against Macdonald, he has to first reckon with why he's so antsy and unsettled in the pocket. If it's not the ankle causing Nix's slump, then it's a between-the-ears issue.
The second aspect of this matchup is Seattle's coverage schemes. While Nix is efficient against Macdonald's top two coverages, the Broncos' offense isn't explosive and barely has a positive EPA.
Nix's success rate is below the league average and ranked in the bottom 12 since the start of the 2024 season. So he not only has to work through his own internal struggles, but he also has to figure out how to improve against a Seahawks defense ranked second in yards per game, first in yards per play, second against the pass, and first in takeaways.
Almost every area of Macdonald's defense is ranked in the top 10 five weeks in. The only exceptions are the Seahawks' rushing defense (No. 11) and red-zone efficiency (27th). There are some chinks in Macdonald's armor, but they're very fine and few and far between.
Seattle has a capable group of receivers that would challenge a healthy Broncos secondary. Alas, Denver's defensive backfield is not healthy and could be down three starters in this game. The Broncos are likely to be without No. 1 cornerback Patrick Surtain II, his boundary partner Riley Moss, and All-Pro safety Talanoa Hufanga.
If Moss and Hufanga are able to play, it's unclear how many snaps they'll see with a rib and ankle injury, respectively. Moss was listed as limited on the Broncos' 'estimated' practice report on Monday, after not participating in any sessions last week, so he could be progressing.
If Hufanga can't go, Denver will have to make sure safety Devon Key is ready to start. He may be an All-Pro special teams ace, but as a safety, Key's play has been uninspiring outside a small sample size in 2025.
Cornerbacks Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine did well in relief of Surtain and Moss last week, but the Los Angeles Chargers were down all but two of their top six receivers, basically. Meanwhile, the Seahawks are healthy, talented, and deep at the position.
Denver will need its defensive front to step up and pressure Sam Darnold to make life easier on the secondary.

title: Broncos-Seahawks Weather Forecast Hints at Potential TNF Wrinkle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are about to play their third primetime game inside of the first six weeks of the 2026 season.
The Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday Night Football throwdown. This is a juicy matchup, given how everyone knows this was what last year's Super Bowl should have been had Bo Nix not suffered his ankle injury in the divisional round.
That's all water under the bridge and the truth is, we'll never know what would have happened if Nix doesn't get hurt (though I'm exceedingly confident Denver would have gotten past New England at home). The Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions, making short work of the Patriots in the big game.
Beyond the 'Super Bowl That Never Was,' there's the Sean Payton vs. Mike Macdonald storyline that makes this Broncos-Seahawks matchup all the juicier. Macdonald was caught on a hot mic a few weeks back saying some untoward things about Payton and revealing that a " cold war " existed between the Broncos and Seahawks.
Although the Seahawks' head coach called to apologize and squash it, you have to wonder if Denver's head coach was as willing to forgive and forget as he claimed publicly.
The weather could be a factor in this one. Let's take a look at how it's shaping up for Thursday night, courtesy of NFL Weather .
The temperatures aren't bad, but the possibility of precipitation and the wind could factor in. It especially worries me when it comes to Broncos kicker Wil Lutz. He's missed three field goals in just five games this season.
Being in the thin air of Mile High is always helpful for a kicker who doesn't have the biggest leg, but without that power, if the wind starts a-blowin' and the rain falls, it could make Lutz even more unreliable than he's been thus far.
Other than that, any rainfall could inhibit the passing game for both teams. Nix is working to break out of the slump he's been in for most of this season, but this might be a game for Payton to really double down on pounding the rock and even use Nix as a rushing weapon.
J.K. Dobbins is coming off his best game of the season , and RJ Harvey should be fresh, considering he only touched the ball three times in L.A. last week. Against this tough Seahawks defense, if Payton doesn't stay committed to the ground game, it could be a long night for Nix.
Then again, Nix typically turns it on for primetime games. That's not an absolute, as Week 1 in Kansas City was about as ugly a performance as it gets for Nix in primetime, but it was an outlier, historically speaking.
Nix is 7-2 in primetime games as a pro, counting Christmas Day games. But there's no question he's in uncharted waters right now, relative to his slump, so perhaps all bets are off as it applies to forecasting how he'll play on Thursday night.

title: Broncos' Rookie Class Gets Harsh Reality Check in Latest NFL Rankings
full_text:
The Denver Broncos only played one rookie in their 23-17 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. In fact, practice-squad cornerback Brent Austin was the only Broncos rookie to dress in Week 5, and he wasn't even drafted.
With the stage set thusly, it should come as no surprise that NFL Draft On SI 's Justin Melo ranked the Broncos' 2026 draft class at No. 30 overall coming out of Week 5 and gave the overall group a D grade.
"The Denver Broncos didn't make a pick until 66th overall and Tyler Onyedim has been a weekly inactive. Jonah Coleman is unfortunately on IR . The rookie running back looked impactful when healthy and could still capture a big role this season. Fifth-round TE Justin Joly was outright released," Melo wrote .
Of the seven draft picks the Broncos made this past spring, only four made the team. It was always going to be a tough roster to crack, but the Broncos made some curious decisions at the end of August.
Two of the three draft picks the Broncos waived at the final roster cutdowns re-signed to the practice squad, with Joly being claimed off waivers by the Miami Dolphins . The Broncos did plan on bringing Joly back to the practice squad, but they lost him to Miami; that was the risk they ran by waiving him.
The four who made the 53-man roster out of camp were Coleman, Onyedim, fourth-round offensive lineman Kage Casey, and seventh-round tight end Dallen Bentley. All but Coleman have been a healthy scratch in every single game this season.
However, Coleman looked great in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, but he suffered an ankle injury that landed him on IR. He's eligible to return in Week 7, assuming he's healthy.
Coleman will be back, and the Broncos will use him in their rushing attack as they work to insulate Bo Nix amid his ongoing slump. Barring injury, we're not going to see Casey or Bentley in 2026.
However, Onyedim should be on the field. He was Denver's highest draft pick this year, and was one the best run-defending defensive tackles in the 2026 draft class.
Onyedim had a strong training camp, but Sean Payton, as a rule, with few exceptions, strongly prefers to play veterans. There are certain positions that Payton and his staff are even more reluctant to play as rookies: the offensive and defensive trenches.
Sai'vion Jones went through the same thing that Onyedim is last year, hardly seeing the field as a regular healthy scratch. But after a year of development in the system, the Broncos feel more confident in playing him, although he's the fifth guy in the team's five-man D-line rotation on game day.
One big difference between Jones and Onyedim, though, was that the former showed next to nothing in camp as a rookie while the latter made his presence felt on the regular. The Broncos continue to dress Jones and veteran Jordan Jackson on game days, with Onyedim walking the sideline in street clothes.
It's curious, but the Broncos have a deep defensive line, and they can afford to give Onyedim a year to assimilate. Barring an injury ahead of him on the depth chart, he's unlikely to see the field this year.
That means Coleman will literally carry the Broncos' 2026 draft class. It's hard to grade or rank a draft class when the team in question doesn't dress any rookies unless it absolutely has to.
Coleman, like RJ Harvey last year and Nix the season prior, was viewed as NFL-ready by Payton and the team. The early returns on Coleman back that up.
It's unfortunate he got hurt so early in the season, but Coleman will be back. And unless the Broncos are decimated by injuries at offensive line, defensive line, or tight end, Coleman will have to suffice when it comes to Melo and others ranking this team's draft class.
Coleman's shoulders are broad enough to carry that load, though.
