title: Sean Payton's Best Decision vs. Chargers Could Have Lasting Impact
full_text:
Sean Payton's first game back as the Denver Broncos' play-caller didn't result in an offensive resurgence . In fact, one could argue that the passing offense looked even worse in Week 5, and the Broncos' inability to convert on third down was shocking (1-of-12).
The Broncos did win the game, though, defeating the Los Angeles Chargers 23-17 . It wasn't pretty offensively, but Payton did get at least one decision right in his first game back on the headset.
In this game, the Broncos finished with 29 planned runs and 28 passes. Bo Nix had another maddeningly inconsistent day, going 16-of-27 for 123 yards and a touchdown, while losing a fumble.
However, if Payton hadn't stayed committed to the ground attack — even in the face of frustrating early-game inefficiency — the Broncos wouldn't have scored 13 fourth-quarter points.
J.K. Dobbins's performance for most of the game was lackluster, but in the fourth quarter, as that stingy Chargers defensive front began to wilt, the veteran running back was able to break off some big gains that not only kept the chains moving but also led to those much-needed points after Justin Herbert got the lead back.
Dobbins finished with 20 touches: 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, with two catches for six yards. It was his most productive game of the season, and Denver's win was no coincidence.
If Payton can continue to unlock Dobbins, and figure out how to get this offensive line run-blocking the way it's capable of, it would take an emormous amount of pressure off Nix. This is by design. Payton knows that a quarterback without a viable running game is vulnerable.
That's especially true for a slumping quarterback. On one hand, Nix has this team at 3-2 entering Week 6's tilt with the Seattle Seahawks; on the other, he's going through one of his worst periods as a pro.
"Obviously, the hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball," Payton said from the post-game podium on Sunday.
So long as Dobbins can stay healthy, Payton will keep feeding him in hopes that he and this offensive line can heat up. Against the Seahawks, the Broncos are going to need a ground game.
Amid Dobbins's Week 5 rise, Harvey disappeared. He was seemingly excised from the game plan, finishing with just three touches after leading the Broncos with 10 receptions the week prior.
With Dobbins going against his former team, maybe Payton had a hunch that he'd play well, but Harvey is an impact player, and while his vision as a rusher isn't on Dobbins's level, his explosiveness makes him one of the Broncos' few weapons opponents actually fear.
The problem has been usage. When 90% of Harvey's touches are swing passes or check-downs, teams see it coming from a mile away and swarm to the ball. Then his presence on the field becomes a tell.
Nix's inability to work the middle of the field as a passer has allowed opponents to shade coverage toward the boundary with linebackers, cornerbacks, and safeties, and it has limited what Harvey can do with those check-downs. He's not getting one-on-one opportunities to make a guy miss; he's getting swarmed by three or four guys, which leads to short gains.
There are other ways to utilize Harvey's receiving skill set, including as an over-the-middle target, or even a guy who can run a shallow drag across the field and beat man coverage. But it takes a quarterback who can see that to find him and capitalize on Harvey's skill set, and right now, Nix isn't trusting his eyes.
Payton's message to Nix after Sunday's win at SoFi Stadium was to " let it rip ." Nix interpreted that to mean "trust what you're seeing."
Hopefully, he does start trusting his eyes because the Broncos have talent on offense. But it's been sacrificed at the altar of Nix's slump thus far. The hope is that the young quarterback will soon snap out of it.
It was great to see Payton lean on Dobbins this week, but it shouldn't ever come at the expense of a healthy Harvey not touching the ball.
One of the downfalls of Davis Webb's four-game audition as the Broncos' play-caller was a lack of run-pass balance. In one game back, Payton fixed that, and it made a difference in a tough divisional road matchup.
Against the Seahawks on Thursday night, Payton will need to stay patient with the run again, even if Darnold is able to put some early points on the board. If the Broncos' offense is rendered one-dimensional against a defense of this caliber, Nix is in for a long night.
Staying balanced offensively kept the Broncos in the game against L.A. If Nix was even just a little more effective as a passer, the were some big plays to be had. Alas, his penchant for bailing clean pockets way early led to Payton's best-laid plans going up in smoke, as the Broncos' passing offense devolved into a slapdash brand of backyard football.
Meanwhile, the Broncos have highly-paid pass-catchers, like Courtland Sutton, Jaylen Waddle, and Evan Engram, just dying for Nix to competently run the offense and execute Payton's passing plays. The opportunities were there in L.A., but as has been the case all season, minus two fourth quarters, Nix was almost blind to them.
He's not seeing the field because he's not trusting his eyes, his offensive line, or his receivers. And so, Payton has to continue to batten down the hatches and nurse Nix's confidence and presence of mind back to full bloom.
Why Nix seems so hestitant and unconfident is anyone's guess. But the best tonic for any struggling quarterback is a viable run game.
So, utilize Dobbins and Harvey and get through one more tough opponent because help is on the way. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman is eligible to return from injured reserve in Week 7, and the Broncos will have three extra days to prepare for the Arizona Cardinals after Thursday night's game against Seattle.
If Nix bounces back this week, and the Broncos manage to defeat a defending Super Bowl champion for the third straight year, the storylines will shift away from quarterback doomsday and the Bo pile-on we've seen over the past 48 hours.

title: Why Broncos Are Likely Preparing for Talanoa Hufanga to Miss Week 6
full_text:
Things are going from bad to worse for the beat-up Denver Broncos secondary, which was without starting cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) for Sunday's victory over the Los Angeles Chargers.
Now, with a quick turnaround for Thursday Night Football against the visiting Seattle Seahawks, the Broncos could also be missing standout safety Talanoa Hufanga, who suffered an ankle injury versus Los Angeles and did not return.
Hufanga was listed as a "DNP" (Did Not Practice) on the team's initial Week 6 injury report. The report is an estimation as Denver didn't officially practice on Monday.
Surtain was also considered a "DNP," with his ankle expected to keep him out of action for at least another week. Moss was marked as a limited participant; he could have a chance to return this week.
Safety Brandon Jones (foot) and guard Ben Powers (biceps) were full goes in Monday's "practice."
Monday's #SEAvsDEN injury report: 📰 » https://t.co/l7MDqy4t8X pic.twitter.com/NXKLd2GiGm
One of the early stars of the young season, Hufanga recorded two solo tackles and a tackle-for-loss prior to going down in Week 5. He was replaced in the lineup by primary special-teamer Devon Key, who also made a pair of solo stops across 26 defensive snaps .
“I would say this, it’s time. There are two things, time and then the second thing is proper recovery from the last game," head coach Sean Payton said Monday when asked about the challenges of preparing on a short week. "For each player, getting their body ready for a short work week, so that the time and the recovery—those are the two things that hit me right away with that question.”
The entire Broncos defense — Hufanga included — deserved a game ball for their efforts against the Chargers, whom they held to just 237 total yards and turned over three times, as well as registering three sacks on slumping quarterback Justin Herbert.
However, their opponent this coming Thursday is on an entirely different level than the decimated Chargers. In addition to sporting the NFL's eighth-best scoring offense, the Seahawks feature arguably the sport's top wide receiver, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who leads the league in both receptions and touchdowns and is fresh off an eight-catch, 102-yard, one-TD performance in Week 5.
Smith-Njigba sustained an ankle injury during Sunday's loss to the 49ers, but he was listed as limited on Seattle's practice report and is anticipated to play on Thursday without any major restrictions.
Assuming he's on the field and Hufanga and Surtain aren't, the Broncos defense might have its collective hands full containing QB Sam Darnold's favorite target.
It's worth noting that Denver has three safeties currently on the practice squad — Taylor Rapp, Miles Scott, and Ugo Amadi — and may choose to promote one if Hufanga is ruled out.

title: Film Room: What's Really Behind Broncos' Alarming 3-and-Out Problem
full_text:
Sean Payton may have taken the play-calling away from Davis Webb this week, but the Denver Broncos still have many problems to solve on offense.
Forget the final score on Sunday. Denver beat the Los Angeles Chargers 23-17 , but that does not mean the offense played well, and it wasn’t called very differently to begin with.
For many reasons, Denver barely got any traction on Sunday. The Broncos' offensive line couldn’t execute in the running game.
To boot, the Broncos got little production out of the passing offense. They went 1-for-12 on third down and produced four three-and-outs in five possessions through the middle of the game. Denver had a fourth possession that only featured four plays thanks to a long defensive pass interference penalty.
When the Broncos were finally able to “generate” some scoring in the fourth quarter, every possession started in Chargers territory, with three of four possessions starting inside the 40-yard line.
Scoring 13 points on three consecutive fourth-quarter drives is awesome, but they all came on the heels of Denver's defensive takeaways and a turnover on downs. Those 13 points were achieved with just 79 yards of offense on 15 total plays, which is rather pathetic.
Denver's offensive inefficiency allowed the Chargers to stay in the game.
I dove into the Broncos' three-and-outs for this week’s film room to highlight issues in play-calling, personnel usage, and execution. It’s on everybody this week.
The first three and out of the game for the offense. Sean Payton in his bag with a pair of screens and a toss sweep to a WR. Great play calling.... pic.twitter.com/JgmX5JhH3Z
The first three-and-out possession featured some incredibly frustrating play-calling, combined with execution mishaps and infuriating personnel usage.
Payton tries to get running back Tyler Badie involved on the drive, opening up with a screen pass to get things started. Right tackle Mike McGlinchey whiffs on his block on defensive lineman Jamari Caldwell, who blows the play up in the backfield for a five-yard loss.
Caldwell uses a great swim move in open space to make the play, but McGlinchey needs to do a better job of walling this off and allowing Badie to make a play with the ball in his hands. If this play pops, Badie has blockers in front to open up a nice gain on first down.
On second down, Payton tries to get cute with a toss sweep to wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. This is an atrocious use of personnel and a horrible play call in this situation.
Mims manages to grind out three yards on the play, but there’s no reason to call this play in this situation. Denver paid $8 million to running back. J.K. Dobbins in the offseason. Let him run the football.
Following a McGlinchey false start, Payton has to dial up another screen play, this time to Mims on a receiver tunnel screen. Finding a quality play call for 3rd-and-17 while pinned deep in your own territory is an impossible task.
Getting quality execution is another thing. Tight end Nate Adkins and wideout Troy Franklin try to block the same defender on this play, but it wouldn’t matter anyways. This is folding your hand and trying to gain positive yards to help out the punting unit.
Bad execution on the next 3 and out. LAC was keyed into the run on 1st down, Bo vacates to the right and misses Trautman up the seam, then Badie runs into Powers and misses the cutback lane. I saw the safety crash down. Badie has to try to make a guy miss in the hole. pic.twitter.com/EnSES75bnh
Our next drive starts after Nik Bonitto sacked Justin Herbert to force a punt, and the Broncos' offense is pinned deep in their own territory again.
The Broncos try to get the running game going on first down with a pin-and-pull look to Dobbins. Adkins motions across the formation to kick out defensive end Ahkeem Mesidor, with left guard Ben Powers following behind him as a lead blocker.
McGlinchey doesn’t get any movement up front on the 3-technique defensive lineman, and the Chargers are keyed in on the run game, with the safety filling down from the second level when Adkins goes in motion. This is poor execution up front, and Dobbins has nowhere to go.
On 2nd-and-9, Payton calls a play-action pass with tight end Adam Trautman running a bender up the seam. The Chargers bring pressure from the left side, and Bo Nix panics in a fairly clean pocket, evading to his right rather than stepping up to find Trautman running wide open up the middle of the field. Nix has to start taking some chances with the football, especially when things aren’t as muddy as they seem.
With the Broncos now in another 3rd-and-long scenario, Payton calls up a draw to Badie to give the punt unit some breathing room. The offensive line does a great job opening up a large running lane to the right side, but Badie sees the safety crashing down to fill the gap from the third level of the defense and runs directly into the backside of Powers.
I understand trying to follow your blockers on this, but I would like to see Badie press this hole to the cutback and try to make a defender miss in the hole. You can’t block this play any better. Go make a play.
Nice drive starter to Engram. Dobbins doesn't have the speed on wide zone to get to the outside, and they can't execute Mesh on 3rd down due to pressure and WR timing. Another 3-and-out with bad execution. pic.twitter.com/HhWTRPYRsh
Following a long Chargers touchdown drive to open the third quarter, Denver goes three-and-out with some poor execution on second and third down.
They open the possession with a bootleg look and dump the ball down to tight end Evan Engram for a four-yard gain. This is a drive starter designed to get positive yards and set up a 2nd-and-manageable situation. Nice work.
On 2nd-and-6, Payton calls a toss sweep into wide zone with Dobbins carrying the ball, and Chargers linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips reads the play the whole way. It’s not always about the Xs and Os. Sometimes you need your Jimmies and Joes to make a play, and Phillips strings this out to the boundary.
This play highlights Dobbins's lack of explosiveness this season. He doesn’t look right as a runner, and he is too slow to bounce this outside.
Dobbins tries to cut back inside of wide receiver Lil’Jordan Humphrey at the point of attack, but it’s already too late. I’d like to see running back RJ Harvey tote the rock on this play, because his speed could have made a huge difference.
With 3rd-and-long upcoming, Payton draws a three-receiver set with the formation to the boundary, trying to open the middle of the field with a mesh concept. The timing of this play is messed up from the jump, with Mims and wideout Courtland Sutton bumping into eachother in their release package.
Nix gets instant pressure from a twist up front, and left tackle Garett Bolles gets called for holding while getting abused by Khalil Mack coming off the edge. The execution fails the offense, once again.
Run, Run, Pass. Solid work on 1st down. Powers gets beat by the swim on 2nd down. Bo and Sutton can't connect on the fade. This was after the Vidal TD. You HAVE TO have a better drive to stop the bleeding. pic.twitter.com/FEpxr1grAB
Denver only had the ball for one play on their next possession because Nix fumbled on first down, which led to a 42-yard Kimani Vidal touchdown run on the very next play. Down 17-10 and desperately needing an answer to stop the bleeding, the Broncos call a pair of runs to open the drive.
First down sees Dobbins pick up three yards on an outside zone. Dobbins reads this well, cutting back inside center Luke Wattenburg at the second level. Trautman does a nice job of walling off Mesidor at the point of attack, and the offense gets decent yardage to start the drive.
On second down, Wattenburg and Powers have a double team on inside zone, and Powers gets beat to the inside by a spectacular swim move as Wattenburg climbs to the second level. If Powers can sustain this block, Harvey has a great cutback lane to rip off a solid gain…

title: Broncos' Snap Counts Reveal Some Surprises in Chargers Victory
full_text:
It wasn't pretty offensively, but the Denver Broncos finally won at SoFi Stadium, defeating the Los Angeles Chargers 23-17 .
The win puts the Broncos at 3-2, tied with the Las Vegas Raiders for second place in the AFC West. The 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs were on bye this week, but they still lead the division.
The injury bug and Sean Payton's decision to take back the play-calling had a huge impact on the Broncos' Week 5 snap counts, with a few surprises. Let's examine how the Broncos relied in different players.
Keep in mind, on offense, Bo Nix and the Broncos' offensive line played 100% of snaps, with 62. Alex Palczewski garnered a season-high eight snaps in this one, too, as the Broncos deployed an extra O-lineman in some heavy looks.
After taking a back seat to Harvey last week, Dobbins led all Broncos running backs in snap share and  touches, finishing with 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, while catching two passes for six yards. Harvey was a relative non-factor in Payton's first game back as the play-caller, carrying just three times for seven yards and garnering just one target, which he did not catch.
Badie carried once for six yards and caught one pass for minus five yards. Prentice received his first touch of the season, diving three yards to move the chains for Denver's offense.
Sutton again led the way in snap share, but only finished with two catches on three targets for 18 yards. But at least the Pro Bowler notched his first touchdown of the season.
Waddle posted his third game of the season with two catches or fewer, despite leading the Broncos with five targets. He dropped one that would have been a sizable gain.
Franklin continues to keep his head down and do the dirty work as a blocker, and when Nix looks his way, he answers the bell, finishing with two catches on two targets for 16 yards. Humphrey out-earned Mims in snap share, and caught his only target for eight yards; it was the Broncos' first first-down conversion on an opening drive of the season.
Still wondering what the heck is going on with Mims? Me too. He caught both targets for six yards and carried once for three yards.
Engram was one of the Broncos' few impact players on offense , leading the team with four receptions for 55 yards. He's staying on the field to block way more than last year.
Trautman is a blocker, and so is Adkins. Neither garnered a target in Nix's 27 attempts.
Allen once again had a monster game, finishing with several pressures and his fourth sack of the season. Roach was a force, too, notching three tackles and disrupting the Chargers' beleaguered offensive line.
Nose tackle D.J. Jones turned in one of the best performances of his career as a Bronco , while Sai'vion Jones saw a season-high snap share. The main rotation is a four-man show, though, with Uwazurike as the fourth leg.
Bonitto was a force, sacking Herbert twice. Robinson was disruptive, and Tillman led the group in pressures. Elliss is still looking a little... slow.
Denver might want to consider replacing Elliss with Robinson in the starting lineup until Jonathon Cooper returns.
This was one of the Broncos' linebacker duo's best games of the season. Both played well, with Strnad leading the team in tackles (eight), followed by Singleton's seven.
No other inside linebacker saw the field on defense this week.
A tip of the cap to Barron and Abrams-Draine for holding down the fort while Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss are injured. The two young corners played well, although it's worth mentioning that L.A. was without Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey.
McMillian was his usual solid self in the nickel.
Jones had a great game, notching an interception and a fumble recovery, but Hufanga exited with an ankle injury in the second half. That foisted Key onto the field, and he was... okay. Not great, but okay.
Amid the shock of losing Hufanga, Skinner and Anderson each garnered one snap. It was the first defensive snap of the season for Anderson, and only the second game of the campaign where Skinner saw time beyond special teams.

title: Broncos Player Grades: Bo Nix's Slump Continues in Ugly Chargers Win
full_text:
The Denver Broncos decided to make a big change on offense, with Sean Payton taking the play-calling duties back from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb ahead of Week 5's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
That was an indication that Payton felt the play-calling, and not the execution, was the biggest issue, though his feelings may have changed after the Broncos turned in their worst offensive showing of the season against the Chargers, when you factor in the quality of defense they are playing.
Denver won 23-17 , but it was ugly at times.
The Broncos scored four times off the takeaways their defense generated, including a turnover on downs, which is a credit to Vance Joseph's unit. The Broncos' defense put together a solid game, though they weren't without their faults, putting the win on their shoulders to move to 3-2 on the season.
This week's player grades reflect Denver's horrendous offensive showing and strong defensive display, minus a few miscues. Let’s get into the grades.
Tillman earned Defensive MVP after having the biggest impact on his snaps. He picked up three pressures on only 10 pass-rush snaps, and leading the team.
Several other Broncos tied with two pressures, all with nearly twice as many pass-rush snaps as Tillman. His run defense was stout as well, which helped him earn Defensive MVP in this one.
The Broncos' offensive line has had issues, but not Meinerz. Even against the Chargers, the offensive line struggled in both phases , but not the All-Pro right guard. A guard can only do so much to carry an offense, but that doesn't stop Meinerz from trying every week.
Sean Payton’s post-game comments were telling . Something is wrong with Nix mentally. Somehow, someway, he needs to get out of his own head; otherwise, it could be a long season.
This is Year 3, but Nix isn't playing like a quarterback with 39 regular-season starts under his belt. He looks like he's massively regressed.
D.J. Jones | DL | Grade: 79.4
This was one of the better games from Jones in his Broncos career, and it highlights when and how he can be a great run defender. The Broncos' run defense had issues, but not because of Jones in the middle, where he was stout and closed multiple running lanes.
Brandon Jones | S | Grade: 77.2
This was a 2024-level performance by Jones, back when he looked like an elite safety. Alas, this was his first game like that since 2024. He flew around the field, both in coverage and against the run, without getting caught out of position.
Garett Bolles | LT | Grade: 70.1
Bolles has been solid to good all season long, and against the Chargers, he put on an outstanding showing. Yes, the Chargers are beat up defensively, but Bolles looked great and held the fort down, minus one holding penalty.
Mike McGlinchey | RT | Grade: 67.9
McGlinchey was my matchup to watch against the Chargers' pass rush , and he answered the call. He stepped up and put on a good game for the first time this season. With no pressures allowed and a good run-blocking game, McGlinchey showed his value; now he just has to sustain that level of play.
RJ Harvey | RB | Grade: 31.7
If the Broncos want Harvey to improve, he has to do so as a pass protector first and foremost. The run game is lacking with him, too, but he can be a passing weapon. But if his pass protection doesn’t improve and it's as bad as it was against the Chargers, he will become too much of a tell for opposing defenses, if he isn’t already.
Devon Key | S | Grade: 34.8
When you play a position that isn’t rotated and have to come in for an injury, it can be difficult to come in and play well. Key has done that before, but this time, stepping in for an injured Talanoa Hufanga, he didn’t play well. Hopefully, Key can be ready for Thursday Night Football if Hufanga misses time.
J.K. Dobbins | RB | Grade: 37.6
It looks like the injuries have finally caught up with Dobbins. Even with a few solid runs, he averaged just 3.8 yards per carry and spent most of the game under a 3.0 average. He doesn’t look bursty or explosive, and that's been paired with some terrible vision of late.
Jonah Elliss | OLB | Grade: 39.7
Elliss is a technical player, but he isn’t overly explosive or athletic for an edge rusher. Denver should look to play Que Robinson over Elliss, and after this season, consider moving Elliss to an inside linebacker and defensive play-caller role, as his brothers do with their respective NFL teams.

title: Release of Lions Veteran Safety Jalen Mills Signals Major Return
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a decision on veteran defensive back Jalen Mills.
According to the team, Mills was released from the practice squad, after being elevated on three occasions this season.
Safety Brian Branch has returned to practice, and if the front office feels that Mills has fulfilled his obligations, it would pave the way for the former second-round pick to return to game action after rehabbing from an Achilles injury.
With the hamstring injury to Rock Ya-Sin potentially being long-term, there is a pathway for Mills to return, should the front office decide to place him on the injured reserve list.
The team will practice all next week, and should provide the medical staff ample opportunity to evaluate if Branch can suit up and how much he can play against the Green Bay Packers .
Lions rookie Keith Abney had not played the safety position since middle, but he was called upon to man the back end along with Chuck Clark against the Arizona Cardinals.
“Thought he was solid. I thought he was solid," said Campbell. "The things that popped up for him were the, 'Hey, I haven't done this before,' which is what you want for a rookie. He's learning as he goes, but we feel very confident that he will learn from those and he won't make those mistakes again. So, I thought he played a good game. First start, first NFL start at safety, never played safety. He's banked some reps for us. We've been cross-training him. But, just man, there's meat on the bone there and he's got room to grow and we feel like he can continue to grow and get better.
"So, that was good. The other thing I want to mention before I got started, I should have said this, man, our fans were outstanding, man. They traveled well to Carolina," Campbell added. "We just didn't give them anything to cheer about. But, I mean, they took over that stadium and you could hear them. And by the end of it, it was good stuff, man. So man, we hear them. We hear you and we love it. We love it.”
The former NFL tight end indicated Abney has a feel for the safety position, which could bode well for his chances of earing increased playing time the rest of the season.
"I think that's a lot of it is, man, what is my responsibility? Some of this, we talk about quarter key. Depending on formation, three by one, two by two, am I getting too vertical to me? Well, if it does, then I stay engaged," Campbell explained, when asked what the coaching staff emphasized to the young defender. "If not and everything starts to go away, I quarter key, read the quarterback's eyes, then feel the pattern match or feel what's coming to me. So, it's different than corner because now you're seeing the whole big picture. And sometimes those guys, when you see the whole big picture , it's too much.
"But, he's kind of got a feel. He's got a feel for it. He's kind of crafty that way. And he's a little bit of jack of all trades and just a young growing player. And that was a step in the right direction yesterday. That was good to see. I mean, he's worth continuing to work with at safety.”

title: Lions First Quarter Rookie Report: Early Evaluations on 2026 Draft Class
full_text:
The first five weeks of the NFL season have offered the Detroit Lions a look at their crop of rookies.
It has been a bit of a mixed bag for Detroit's batch of newcomers, as they've had some who have already emerged into big roles while others are still finding their footing.
Here's a look at how each of the Lions' draft picks, as well as the undrafted free agent who made the active roster, have performed through the first five weeks of the NFL season.
Miller has made four starts already at right tackle, with an injury keeping him out of the Week 2 matchup against Buffalo. It's not hard to see why the team went with him as the starter, as Larry Borom really struggled in his only start in Miller's absence.
In the run game, Miller has been very encouraging to start his career. He has routinely handled his assignments, and has been serviceable in the passing game as well. Miller ranks first among rookie offensive tackles with a pass-blocking grade of 79.3.
Miller does rank fourth in pressures allowed with nine, but has performed better in that category than Spencer Fano, who was drafted eight picks ahead of him in the top-10.
Overall, Miller still has some strides to make but has made an encouraging first impression in his debut season.
Moore had an encouraging debut in the preseason, recording a sack in his only appearance during the exhibition slate. However, it has been less than a smooth transition for the Michigan product in the regular season.
He has appeared in all five games, but just notched his first two tackles of the season on Sunday. Moore has notched four pressures but zero sacks up to this point, and has played double-digit snaps in just one of the last three games.
Part of Moore's smaller role has been the emergence of D.J. Wonnum , who currently leads the defense with five sacks. Moving forward, Moore will need to produce more or risk falling down the depth chart.
Rolder was inactive each of Detroit's first two games and has played on defense in just one game up to this point. Detroit's defense is full of veteran linebackers, although they have just lost one as Devin White suffered a forearm injury that is expected to require surgery.
The Michigan product does have a tackle for loss to his name from the Carolina game, and could have a bigger role awaiting him because of White's injury.
Abney has logged defensive snaps in two games up to this point, those being the season-opener and the Week 5 win over Arizona. They have been two different roles, as he spent the opener logging snaps at nickel and played safety against the Cardinals.
In between those two games, he was inactive Week 2 and used exclusively on special teams in weeks 3 and 4. However, with some injuries in the secondary, the coaching staff elected to give him an opportunity at the safety position against Arizona and he delivered a solid showing.
He notched his first-career interception on a Hail Mary at the end of the first half, and notched six tackles. It was encouraging, and he may be worthy of a longer look even with Brian Branch returning potentially after the bye.
Law suffered a season-ending torn ACL in offseason workouts and remains with the organization on injured reserve.
Gill-Howard has been one of the surprises of the draft class up to this point, as he's earned a legitimate role already. He flashed serious pass-rush ability throughout the preseason, and that momentum has carried over into the regular season.
Gill-Howard has played at least 24 snaps in every game , and has eight tackles and one sack to his name already. He ranks 16th amongst all interior defenders in pressures with 13, and that number is first amongst rookie interior defenders.
While it hasn't always been flashy, it appears as though Gill-Howard has already carved out a niche and has high expectations moving forward after a strong start.
West, the team's seventh-round pick, was waived on cut day but returned to Detroit on the team's practice squad. However, he was released from the practice squad on September 11 as the team brought back Levi Onwuzurike after cutting him from the active roster.
A month later, West remains a free agent.
O'Neill has found a role on special teams for Detroit, as he has been active in every game. Though he has logged just eight total defensive snaps, he has seven total tackles across his various reps on special teams.
While he's buried on the defensive end depth chart at this point, O'Neill has become a staple on special teams coverage units and seems to be around the football every time it's kicked or punted.

title: Detroit Lions WR Jameson Williams Wins Fine Appeal
full_text:
Detroit Lions star wide receiver Jameson Williams earned a victory away from the field this week.
According to NFL media, "Lions WR Jameson Willaims won both his appeals of fines of celebrations against the #Bills, as amounts of $14,926 and $11,941 were rescinded. On one, Williams denied his "brief gesture" was offensive and argued "that marijuana is legal in some states if that was the gesture he was making."
The appeals officer, Derrick Brooks, shared with the former first-round draft pick, “Although I rescinded this fine, please make every effort to celebrate with your teammates in the best professional manner possible.”
The league has been cracking down on celebrations deemed inappropriate through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
#Lions WR Jameson Williams won both his appeals of fines of celebrations against the #Bills , as amounts of $14,926 and $11,941 were rescinded. On one, Williams denied his “brief gesture” was offensive and argued “that marijuana is legal in some states if that was the gesture he… pic.twitter.com/tQ3wu2KNZf
Recently, the NFLPA and the league released a joint statement that clarified the expectations for players celebrating postive results out on the football field.
“Football is the greatest game in the world. NFL players are admired by millions of fans, including young people competing at every level of the sport. The passion, emotion, and personality players bring to the field are a big part of what makes the game special and connects them with fans worldwide. Good sportsmanship is equally important.
To clarify the line between player expression and conduct that may result in discipline, players were reminded this week that the following are prohibited and may result in a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, a fine, or both:
1.) Gestures that depict violence, including the use of guns or other weapons, or gang-related signs. 2.) Gestures that depict smoking or drug use. 3.) Gestures that are sexual in nature.
“Conversely, recent celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will not be considered violations or result in discipline. The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules. When conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline. The player will be advised that continued use of the identified celebration may result in future fines.
“Individual and team celebrations are part of the game and help players connect with fans. Providing clear, consistent guidance allows players to express themselves while upholding the principles of sportsmanship that have long been a hallmark of NFL football.”

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly of Lions 45-21 Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions traveled into Arizona on a mission. The Lions were determined to rebound from an unexpected and embarrassing loss to Carolina. They faced a shorthanded Arizona team, missing multiple linemen and corners.
The Lions started slow, but left no doubt in the end, scoring on seven straight drives to win 45-21. There was good, bad, and ugly in the contest.
The stars of the Detroit offense came out to play. Sam LaPorta, Jahmyr Gibbs, Jared Goff, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Jameson Williams all had spectacular games . LaPorta was the initial sparkplug for the offense, getting the initial first down and finished as the leading receiver with 88 yards.
Williams caught his first two touchdowns of the season, showcasing his speed. Goff had four total touchdowns, with three passing and a sneak. St. Brown came alive late, and his two fumbles did not impact the game with both being recovered.
Gibbs’s play was at an elite level, with over 200 total yards on the day, including 151 rushing yards, and added two touchdowns. The Lions put up seven straight scoring drives, with their stars carrying the load to put up 45 points.
The pass rush finished with five sacks on the day. D.J. Wonnum recorded a two-sack game, including a high motor second effort sack. Derrick Barnes recorded a solo sack, and Alim McNeill, Aidan Hutchinson, Skylar Gill-Howard, and Malcolm Rodriguez split the remaining two sacks.
The Lions put Jacoby Brissett under pressure constantly and were also strong in stuffing the run. The top two backs for Arizona, Jeremiah Love and Tyler Allgeier, combined for 15 carries for 29 yards.
It was a stifling effort until late in the contest, when the game was out of hand.
It was a rough week in the secondary for Detroit, as they allowed Brissett to put up nearly 300 yards through the air. The secondary was routinely burnt , with Roger McCreary being the first guy targeted, before D.J. Reed, Chuck Clark, and Ennis Rakestraw each had times being beat.
McCreary recovered from a slower start to the game to record a mind-boggling six pass breakups. It was easily the best game in the Honolulu Blue for McCreary, although the last two scoring drives saw his man get free a few times.
Keith Abney II also added his first career interception on the day. With Brissett needing nearly 50 attempts and a phenomenal effort from McCreary, this category is merely ‘bad’ this week.
There were uncharacteristic lulls of sloppiness from the Lions on Sunday. This ranged from blown assignments leading to sacks on each of the first two drop backs to untimely discipline penalties, such as unnecessary roughness and false starts.
It was not the most polished effort in Arizona, and Chuck Clark throwing his hands in the air on two blown assignments in the second half was a rough look. Add in the usual surehanded Amon-Ra St. Brown recording 2 fumbles, one on a punt return, and it was not a clean effort.
That said, when a team scores on seven straight drives and finishes the final three quarters on a 45-14 run, it was obviously not the sloppiest effort.
The only ugly from Sunday’s match was a slow start in the first quarter. The Lions came out dysfunctional, getting sacked on third-and-five after winning their first coin toss of the year.
The Lions then allowed an Arizona score to begin the game, with the defensive back being their own worst enemies, flipping their hips incorrectly at points and allowing too much yardage.
The next two drives also led to punts, and one of those came after a 22-yard return by Tom Kennedy to set up the dangerous offense at midfield. At the end of the first quarter, it was rough for the Lions. They had -14 yards through the air and -5 yards in total in the opening frame.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 First Quarter Grades: Defense
full_text:
The NFL regular season is over a quarter of the way done.
With five weeks in the books, the Detroit Lions have accomplished a 3-2 record entering their bye week. While there have been some struggles on defense, there have also been some encouraging moments that suggest signs of progress.
Ultimately, though the team has plenty of weapons on offense, it will likely be the performance of coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's defense that determines the team's ceiling. There are clear concerns, and using the bye week to find some answers will be pivotal for the team.
Here are grades for each defensive position group following the first five games of the 2026 season.
Getting some extra production in the pass-rush was a big point of emphasis across the fan base, as finding a reliable second option to work with Aidan Hutchinson is something fans have longed for. Ultimately, the Lions seem to have found that in veteran D.J. Wonnum.
Through five games, Wonnum leads the team with five sacks and is rapidly approaching his career high of eight in a season, which he has notched twice. He has sacked the opposing quarterback in each of the last two games, and has had two games with two sacks in that span.
Hutchinson, to his own credit, has been solid with four while Alim McNeill has posted three. Hutchinson is tied-for-first in pressures with 32, and has a league-best 91.1 pass-rush grade from Pro Football Focus.
Meanwhile, McNeill leads all interior defensive linemen with 23 pressures. This gives Detroit two of the top-performing defensive linemen.
The Lions have also been encouraged with the performance of a pair of young players in Tyleik Williams and Skyler Gill-Howard. The two players have worked as a tandem, with Williams serving as the run-stuffer while Gill-Howard offers athleticism in pass-rush situations.
Gill-Howard ranks first amongst rookie interior defensive linemen with 13 pressures, and is 16th in the entire league in that metric after five games.
Detroit's defense currently leads the league in sacks, and while there have been struggles as a unit against the run, this performance in pass-rush has given them a big boost at times where they've needed it most.
Signed to a contract extension after an All-Pro season last year, Jack Campbell has had an up-and-down start to the season. He was tasked in stepping up both on the field and as a leader with the departure of Alex Anzalone, and to this point hasn't quite been able to reach that level.
That said, there have been some encouraging moments for him. He had the game-winning strip sack against the Jets late in the fourth-quarter, and has improved in recent weeks.
Derrick Barnes has also played a big role, and shined in the team's season-opening win over the New Orleans Saints. Malcolm Rodriguez and Devin White have split duties as the third linebacker, though White is expected to miss some time after suffering a forearm injury Sunday.
White's injury could open up more opportunities for Jimmy Rolder, who has shown some flashes in a small role. His biggest moment to this point has been a tackle for loss against the Carolina Panthers in Week 4.
Trevor Nowaske has also flashed some ability, as his presence makes the unit faster. He has earned more opportunities, and is another candidate to fill the void left by White's injury.
The group that has faced the most scrutiny to this point for Detroit has been their secondary, with many questioning Brad Holmes' lack of activity amidst the Terrion Arnold saga that ended with the former first-round pick being released.
At cornerback, the Lions have leaned on D.J. Reed as the top corner, but the veteran has yet to show that he can be a shutdown corner in their man-coverage oriented offense. He has allowed an opposing passer rating of 124.2, which is the worst amongst Detroit's cornerbacks.
Opposite him, Rock Ya-Sin began the year as the starter but has been replaced by Roger McCreary. While McCreary has taken his lumps, he recorded six passes defensed in the win over Arizona which suggests that he could be an answer.
The safety position has also taken some lumps, with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph both sidelined. Avonte Maddox, who began the year as a starter next to Chuck Clark, suffered a season-ending injury in Week 2.
That injury has forced Christian Izien into a bigger role, and the free agent acquisition has been serviceable. However, he did not log any defensive snaps Sunday as Keith Abney got a look at safety against Arizona, and that could be something the team explores as the season progresses.
Ultimately, the group is set to get a boost as soon as out of the bye with Brian Branch returning to practice next week. When he returns, he could be a much-needed spark for Sheppard's group.

title: 6 Lions Candidates Who Could Replace Tom Kennedy, Return Punts
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will be without wide receiver Tom Kennedy for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season.
Head coach Dan Campbell confirmed the news that the special teams ace and longest tenured member of the roster would need surgery to repair a significant MCL injury.
According to NFL media, "HC Dan Campbellw as hopeful Kennedy's absence would be shorter but further testing revealed the extent of the damage."
Speaking with local reporters, the former NFL tight end indicated he did not want wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown to return punts on a full-time basis, but would be in the mix on occasion.
The front office is currently looking across the league for potential replacements, but since the team is on a bye week, there is no real urgency this week.
Detroit next takes the field following their Week 6 bye next Sunday against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field.
Here are six Lions candidates who could fill in, while general manager Brad Holmes surveys the landscape to potentially add a new member to the roster.
While Saylors is not an elite touchdown threat, he has served admirably as the kick returner since last season.
According to the team, he ranked seventh in the NFL last season (27.2 yards/return).
He led the Lions and ranked ninth in the NFL with 897 kickoff return yards in 2025. He joined the Lions as an undrafted free agent after signing with the Bengals, following the 2023 NFL Draft.
The speedy wideout is always a threat to return a punt to the end zone due to his speed and elusiveness.
Similar to St. Brown, Detroit may not be comfortable with an offensive weapon serving in this role.
Campbell indicated Lovett was in the mix and could be an ideal first choice to replace the injured wideout. Lovett is currently on the practice squad.
In 12 games last season, he recorded one kickoff return for 22 yards.
Vaki has seen his role expanded in Detroit's offense as this season has progressed. He is considered among the top special teams players in the league.
"Ultimately in order to do well, you need good players," said special teams coach Dave Fipp. "And so we've been fortunate here since I've been here. We've had a lot of really good special teams players and a lot of guys embrace that role. And that really starts with (General manager Brad (Holmes) and those guys drafting good players and making sure that the bottom of the roster are guys that can help and contribute.
"Obviously (Lions Head Coach) Dan (Campbell) doing the same thing. So yeah, I mean we’ve still got our hands full and we got a long season to go, but yeah, a lot of the success starts at the very top and it really is the players.”
St. Brown did put the football on the ground a couple of time against the Cardinals. While he excels in many categories, it would be wise to only use the former first-round pick in spot duty to return punts.
Detroit can ill afford to lose St. Brown or any other key weapon for an extended period of time.
While lacking in return experience, he did serve as the kick returner after Kennedy departed the game in Week 5.
Dorsey has been a staple on special teams for the past few seasons. He could be used as the backup option, should the primary choice also go down with injury.

title: Detroit Lions Must Take Serious Look at Defense, Make Tough Decisions
full_text:
Dan Campbell and the Detroit Lions bounced back in a huge way Sunday, defeating the Arizona Cardinals, 45-21.
The Lions, which had lost two of their previous three games, seemingly heard the critics loud and clear. They played with an extra source of motivation and left no stone unturned in the Week 5 contest, notably scoring on seven straight drives from the second quarter on.
Detroit do-it-all back Jahmyr Gibbs spearheaded the dominant offensive effort, delivering a sensational performance. He notched big run after big run, evading defenders left and right on his way to 151 yards and two touchdowns on 25 carries.
Gibbs flashed big-play ability all afternoon, reminding Lions fans on multiple occasions of legendary back Barry Sanders. Gibbs finished the intraconference affair with a season-high 207 all-purpose yards .
With each passing week, Gibbs draws more and more comparisons to Sanders. And those won't stop anytime soon, especially now that the fourth-year back has surpassed the Lions all-time great for the most touchdowns in NFL history before the age of 25 (58).
Gibbs wasn't the only offensive standout for the Lions Sunday, either.
Detroit signal-caller Jared Goff produced yet another efficient performance to open up the 2026 campaign. The veteran quarterback played mistake-free ball, throwing for three touchdowns and zero interceptions in the blowout victory.
And through five weeks, Goff has compiled an impressive 1,485 passing yards and 12 passing touchdowns without tossing a single interception.
He's playing the definition of winning football, and is now just one of two quarterbacks in NFL history to throw for that many touchdowns without an interception through a season‘s first five games. The other QB: Russell Wilson.
"Goff is just Goff. He’s as good as they come,” Campbell said after the Week 5 win. “I’ve been so impressed with the way he’s played. He’s just gotten better every year, and here we are five in, he’s even better than last year. He’s the real deal.”
Goff is “the real deal” and has been all season long. And on Sunday, his teammates came through with their best collective performance of the 2026 campaign.
Yet, it doesn't mean the Lions have nothing to worry about headed into their bye week.
The Lions are still very much a flawed team, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. And while getting Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch will provide a much-needed boost, it won't cure all the team's defensive woes.
The Lions will notably remain thin at the cornerback position, a weakness which will likely continue to be the team's Achilles’ heel. Additionally, it's a sizable enough deficiency to where it could impede Detroit's efforts to win games in future weeks, just as it already has multiple times this season.
Along with that, Campbell & Co. need to take a critical look at defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's performance this season.
More often than not in 2026, Sheppard has been unable to put the defense in position to succeed. He's become known not only for devising faulty gameplans but also for failing to make the necessary in-game adjustments to get his unit off the field.
So, just because the Lions held the Cardinals to 21 points Sunday, it doesn't mean the second-year coordinator is off the hot seat all of a sudden. In fact, his fate is still very much in question, and I'm not yet convinced he's the right man to lead the defense moving forward.
Campbell & Co. could very well feel the same way. Subsequently, if they decide to keep him in charge of the defense, it doesn't mean he's guaranteed a job the remainder of the season. I think he deserves to be assessed on a weekly basis, and if his job performance regresses, there should be serious consideration for stripping him of his duties.
Sheppard still has much to prove in the weeks ahead, and so do the Lions.
Through the first five games of 2026, Campbell's squad has hardly looked the part of a Super Bowl contender. And beating the Cardinals doesn't move the needle for me (and it shouldn't for you, either).
Remember, Arizona was reeling coming into Sunday, and with the Week 5 loss, has now dropped four consecutive games. Consequently, you can't use the matchup with the Cardinals as a true measuring stick for where the Lions stand as a team.
The offense was undeniably explosive against Arizona, and has been the highest-scoring unit in the league so far this year.
However, it won't mean a thing if the defense reverts to its bad habits against Green Bay in Week 7. Sheppard, for his sake and the sake of Detroit's playoff hopes , can ill-afford for that to happen.
Without question, the Lions’ success the remainder of 2026 hinges upon Sheppard's ability to get the most out of the team's defensive personnel.

title: Everything Jared Goff Said After Detroit Lions Defeated Cardinals
full_text:
Here is everything Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff said, after the team earned their third victory of the 2026 NFL season by defeating the Arizona Cardinals 45-21.
The veteran signal-caller and Russell Wilson are now the only quarterbacks in NFL history to toss for 12 or more touchdowns and no interceptions, through the first five games of any season.
Against the Cardinals, Goff threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns. He added a rushing touchdown as well in the blowout victory.
On the aggressive approach to the game on both sides of the ball
“I think that’s kind of a part of our identity . It certainly has been in the success that we’ve had over the years. When we’re able to lean on teams and make them uncomfortable in situations that we’re comfortable with in some of these fourth downs and some of the stuff they’re doing defensively on third downs, it is the way we want to play. It is the way we want to be dominant and in control.”
Whether he felt the aggressive approach was necessary today
“I'm sure Dan (Campbell) may have, I think it worked so I would say I’m glad we did a lot of it. I don’t think it had anything to do with them. I think it's just we wanted to kind of get back to who we are and early on there, certainly we were sputtering. You've got to give kudos to our defense for holding us down there those first three drives and keeping us in it and not allowing that game to get out of hand. Then I think we scored seven drives in a row. We had a good day.”
Significance of the fourth-down conversion by TE Sam LaPorta
“I thought Sam was the catalyst today for everything. He really was. He had the fourth-down conversion on the in-cut which wasn’t a great throw and he made a great catch . Then he had the fourth down, fourth-and-one touchdown. Then he had a number of other catches — the third down and long that I checked down to him that he went and I think he got us into fourth and one, which we then scored on. Those three plays alone changed the entire landscape of the game and he's a hell of a player and I'm happy he's on our side. ”
On the play of running back Jahmyr Gibbs
“There are a lot of comparisons there, but he’s unbelievable. He really is. We did a good job in the run game, and still probably didn’t do as well as we could and he made a lot of guys miss in the backfield. and got a lot after the first touch. Obviously, he caught the ball well in the backfield. I think he had what, 50 or 60 yards through the air. Gosh, he’s electric. I think you saw the full scope of what we’re capable of.”
The importance of taking care of the ball after having five turnovers for gain so far this season
“I mean, some of them bounced our way. I think I had a sack-fumble today that we landed on, but I’ve been very conscious of that and through the last handful of years of my career tried to really focus on that. I have been doing a good job of that up to this point. Again, a lot of this stuff is the way the ball bounces, but I’m proud of that right now and want to keep that going.”
What the performance can do for the team going into the bye week?
“You almost wish you could play tomorrow after a game like today, but it’s good. It really is. It is better than the alternative and to win in the way we did — I think the way we were feeding off each other today and the energy the defense was giving us — that’s the way the game goes. It is a complementary football game and you could certainly feel it. I felt all day of (the fact that) they were playing with energy and swagger and then we were feeding off that, getting short field, scoring and then they would multiply that. It feels good to win in that way for sure.”
On the seven straight scoring drives
“It felt like (Offensive coordinator) Drew (Petzing) could call whatever he wanted and we were going to make it work. I think today was a good example of, like I've said, where we can go and what we are capable of. I think I said it earlier last week (but) we’ve been good, right? Today we were great ,and there are still some things to be better at certainly, but today we were like ‘OK, that’s what we were capable of.” It’s good to know that’s our standard now and we can hold guys accountable to what we just did today.”
On whether the win was meaningful for offensive coordinator Drew Petzing:
“I think it’s cool. I really think it is not as meaningful as it may seem outside to us, but yeah I think it’s cool anytime that happens against your former team. It's cool.”

title: Packers Broke the Bank for These 12 Players; Six of Them Are Broken
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The hits just keep coming for the Green Bay Packers.
The Packers are one of the most injured teams in the NFL , with many of the ailments being significant injuries to key players.
Including defensive tackle Javon Hargrave’s torn Achilles in the waning moments of Sunday’s game against the Bears, six of Green Bay’s 12 players with average salaries of at least $10 million are out of the lineup. They total $128 million in average annual salary.
In terms of cap dollars, they are consuming $72.08 million. That’s almost 24 percent of the cap not contributing to the lineup.
Here they are, with the dollar figures being their average annual salaries.
The Packers hoped Micah Parsons would be back for this week’s game against the Dallas Cowboys. Parsons no doubt wanted to be back to face his former team, as well. Instead, he hasn’t even started practicing.
His brother said the “best bet” would be Parsons returning in Week 10 against the Vikings or Week 12 against the Rams, the games bridging this year’s bye.
“First of all, you’ve got to get him back on the practice field,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “There’s a lot of testing that goes on before he gets medically cleared to get out there, and then I’m sure we’re going to want to give him some time to get back to playing football. As you see with most guys that are coming off a major injury, it takes a little bit of time.”
When healthy, Bako-Bewele is one of the best right tackles in the NFL. The Packers gave him a huge contract extension at the start of training camp in 2023, only for him to completely tear the patellar ligament that he partially tore last year. He’ll wind up playing 676 of about 2,100 snaps in 2025 and 2026.
Fortunately for the Packers, Anthony Belton is playing better. He has allowed zero pressures the last two games, according to PFF.
“He’s done a nice job,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday. “He’s firmed the pocket up. I think that was the biggest thing the first couple weeks was just the push that we were feeling in the pocket.
“I think him and Laken (Tomlinson at left guard) have done a really nice job just firming that up, allowing Jordan (Love) to see and not have that pocket pushed in his face. There were a couple reps in the game that, obviously, we got to clean up with him but, for the most part, he’s out there competing and doing a nice job.”
We might be able to erase Aaron Banks from this ledger at some point. Banks was inactive in Week 1 with a knee injury and started Week 2 but suffered a toe injury that held him out of the second half and then each of the last three games.
Banks has played 22 snaps this season. He returned to practice on Friday, though, so a decision will have to be made at some point whether Banks or Laken Tomlinson will start at left guard.
“One thing we have to keep in mind too is where do we fit those guys into the best five,” Adam Stenavich said. “We’ll evaluate that but, yeah, that’s going to be an interesting thing as we go through the next few weeks, for sure.”
After an injury-plagued 2025 season, the Packers gave Jayden Reed a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension in April. However, he wound up suffering a season-neck injury that required surgery. It ended his season after 41 snaps.
The Packers believed Skyy Moore could pick up the slack but he suffered an ankle injury early against Chicago and could miss a little time.
“Losing Skyy for however long he’s going to be out, that’s going to be interesting,” Adam Stenavich said. “We’ll see where Savion (Williams) is at this week. But J-Mike (J. Michael Sturdivant) is definitely going to have a bigger role, for sure.”
Josh Jacobs’ NFL future remains in limbo. Green Bay’s running game without him is averaging 60.4 yards per game – almost 20 yards worse than any other team – and ranks 31st with 3.05 yards per carry.
Javon Hargrave was averaging 30 snaps per game as a valuable role player on the defensive line. Even while missing the Week 2 game, he led Green Bay’s defensive tackles in pressures and pass-rush win rate.
The Packers are down to five defensive tackles: Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks are the starters, Jonathan Ford is the nose tackle, Chris McClellan is a rookie and Anthony Campbell is a first-year player who made his NFL debut in Week 2 but suffered an ankle injury and hasn’t played since.
“We see who we have, we see who they have and see if we can put the pieces together,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said on Tuesday. “But whoever’s up on gameday, I truly believe this, they have to play in some role for your team or why are you up on gameday? So, if they’re up, they’re going to be up and playing.”
The Packers have 28 players with average salaries of more than $2.0 million per season. They’re not big-ticket items, but cornerback Benjamin St-Juste ($4.9 million), receiver Skyy Moore ($2.5 million), running back Chris Brooks ($2.43 million), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper ($2.15 million) and tight end Luke Musgrave ($2.12 million) add another $14.1 million of average salary to the ledger.
Combined with the six expensive players listed above, those 11 players on the sideline have average salaries totaling $142.1 million. That’s 37.4 percent of the team total.
Not counting Hargrave, who remains on the 53-man roster, the Packers have almost $99 million of average salary on injury lists (injured reserve, physically unable to perform or non-football injury), according to OverTheCap.com . That’s $11 million more than the next team, Carolina, which the Packers will host in a few weeks. Their next two opponents are Dallas and Detroit, which have a combined $66.4 million on the shelf.
A formula at OverTheCap.com shows the Packers have the lowest contract utilization in the NFL, a byproduct of so many high-priced players being out of action.
“It truly is a next-man-up mentality and guys got to get ready to play,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Monday. “That’s just the nature of the beast and I think that’s one of the luxuries of having a 70-man roster. And we tell our players this all the time: Whether you’re on the active or you’re on the P-squad, you got to get ready to play.”

title: Packers Don’t Sign Short Cornerbacks, But They Just Did to Practice Squad
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have definite height requirements that they haven’t veered from in decades.
However, they did make a noteworthy exception to the rule by signing cornerback Elijah Culp to the practice squad following a Monday workout, a source confirmed what originally was reported by Easton Butler .
The Packers made it official on Tuesday afternoon and released guard Josh Gesky.
Culp ended his college career at James Madison. At pro day, he measured only 5-foot-9 3/4. That’s just fractionally taller than Ahmad Carroll, the Packers’ first-round pick in 2004. He was 5-foot-9 5/8. Carroll was a bust and the Packers haven’t taken another corner shorter than 5-foot-10 since.
What Culp lacks in height, he makes up for in speed with a 4.39-second time in the 40-yard dash and other physical attributes.
“I knew I had to run fast, man,” Culp said after pro day .
Short corners usually find a home as a nickel, and that is how Green Bay views him.
Culp is well-traveled. He opened his college career at Austin Peay in 2020 before transferring to Troy for 2021 and 2022. He transferred to Charlotte, where he redshirted in 2023 and started nine games in 2024.
At James Madison in 2025, he was third-team all-Sun Belt Conference with one interception and eight pass breakups in 13 starts. The interception came against Oregon in the College Football Playoffs.
PFF charged him with a 44.4 percent completion rate and only 9.9 yards per catch in 2025. That includes 1-of-2 for just 5 yards against Oregon and 1-of-5 for 7 yards in the opener against Louisville.
“I really like, honestly, his growth off the field at this point in time, even better than his growth on,” Dukes coach Bob Chesney said last season . “We knew what he could do on the field, but what he's doing off the field now and how he's growing into it, just a really good young man that's going to make a lot of people proud later in life when football is done.”
Culp, who was the No. 44 cornerback prospect in this year’s draft, according to The Athletic’s Dane Brugler, went undrafted and signed with the Cardinals, where he competed for a job in training camp. He recently served a stint on the Colts’ practice squad.
“My whole career I’ve been the underdog,” he told The Touchdown before the draft . “Even at high school, some of my coaches didn’t think I could make it – I was 5’7” back then, and so getting on the field was tough. But when I did get on, I brought that dog mentality, and they couldn’t take me off.
“So, really, I only started playing varsity in the 11th grade. And then by my junior year, I started to see the hard work pay off. It took some time to get there, but I reached the top. As a senior, I had 26 pass breakups. You just don’t see that. But my body grew as my game got better.”
That underdog mentality powered him through the draft process.
“That's my number one motivation,” Culp said at pro day . “Two is just like God gave me this blessing. I don't want to let him down. I'm grateful and I'm blessed for the opportunity. So that's why I wake up every day, even the days I don't want to.”
On the active roster, the Packers have starters Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse along with Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden. St-Juste dropped out of Sunday’s game against Chicago with a hamstring injury, meaning the team could be a man down at corner for this week’s game at Dallas. The only player on the practice squad is Domani Jackson, a sixth-round pick this year.
The Packers had a full practice squad so had to make another move. With the additions on the offensive line and with guards Jacob Monk and Aaron Banks returning to practice late last week, the team opted to release Josh Gesky, who signed with the Packers after going undrafted.
“Man, it would mean a lot,” to make it in the NFL, Culp told The Touchdown. “My family has been very supportive of me, helped me chase my dreams through four different schools. And reaching the NFL would change a lot of people’s lives, and it would definitely change ours.
“So I feel like everybody – me, my mom, pops, brothers – would all be very emotional when that call comes. They obviously know how much I’ve invested in this and I know what they’ve put in too. It would be a dream come true.”

title: Consensus NFL Power Rankings: After Stunning Fall, Stunning Rise for Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – How low could they go? And now, how high did they rise?
After a blowout loss to the Falcons and a lackluster win over the Buccaneers, the Green Bay Packers were 24th in l ast week’s Packers On SI Consensus NFL Power Rankings . However, their dominating win over the Bears on Sunday certainly changed the narrative.
First, what are the Consensus Power Rankings? We take eight of the best national power rankings and turn them into one better-than-the-best power ranking. Following a 31-7 win over Chicago, the Packers zoomed up all the way to 14th. That’s a 10-spot improvement based on one victory that seemed more in line with the preseason expectations.
Here are this week’s rankings, with more extensive analysis available by following the links.
Nobody moved the Packers up further than Mike Florio , who shot them up 12 spots from No. 23.
He liked Green Bay’s approach to the rivalry win: “When your adversary keeps talking, stay quiet and wait for your opportunity.”
The Packers rocketed up 10 spots from No. 22 in Conor Orr’s rankings.
“I get that I cannot, one week, punish the Steelers for what I considered a fluke victory over the Bengals (at the time) because Aaron Rodgers had too much time in the pocket, then vastly pump up the Packers for a deep aerial assault of the Bears, without drawing some ire,” he wrote. “The difference here is that Matt LaFleur has figured out how to run play action without a running game. And it’s leading to massive chunk plays.”
The Packers were the biggest movers in Pete Prisco’s rankings , leaping up 10 spots from No. 24.
“They were able to unleash Jordan Love against the Bears,” he wrote. “It needs to stay that way going forward. The deep passing game is their best option.”
The Packers zoomed up nine spots from No. 23 in the rankings selected by Josh Kendall and Chad Graff.
This week’s theme is who have they beaten. For Green Bay, it’s the woeful Jets, the Buccaneers with a backup quarterback and the Bears with a backup quarterback.
“The win over the Bears looks more impressive than it probably was considering the quarterback play Chicago got, but there’s no sense in apologizing for a win over a bitter rival that’s talking a lot of smack,” they wrote. “Jordan Love was exceptional Sunday, and Christian Watson looks like a true No. 1 wide receiver.”
The Packers shot up nine spots from 23rd in the rankings voted on by ESPN’s team beat writers.
This week’s theme is the biggest issue on defense. Rob Demovsky focused on the serious injuries to key players.
“In back-to-back weeks, the Packers lost linebacker Edgerrin Cooper and defensive tackle Javon Hargrave to season-ending Achilles injuries,” he wrote as part of a larger analysis. “Cooper was their best linebacker; Hargrave their most experienced defensive lineman. And who knows when edge rusher Micah Parsons will play?”
The Packers took the express lane up 11 spots in Nick Shook’s rankings, with the offense reaching Shook’s expectations.
As part of a longer writeup, Shook said: “Love delivered a fantastic performance, throwing for 367 yards and two majestic touchdowns to Christian Watson, demolishing a Bears team that couldn’t stop giving the ball to Green Bay’s suddenly feisty defense. Adding Micah Parsons into this equation soon makes the Packers one of the teams we must pay close attention to going forward.”
The Packers moved up six spots from No. 24 in Frank Schwab’s rankings.
“Through all the (justifiable) angst over the Packers' start, they're 3-2 coming off a blowout win over the Bears, who were the favorite to win the division,” Schwab wrote as part of a longer analysis.
“The Packers looked mostly poor during the first four weeks, but they find themselves in a good place now. There are things to clean up, but the trio of Jordan Love, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson might keep Green Bay in the playoff race.”
Ralph Vacchiano was the one writer who took a conservative approach. He inched the Packers up only three spots from No. 25 .
“The Packers' blowout win over the Bears was certainly out of nowhere, and probably some sweet revenge for Matt LaFleur’s team,” he wrote as part of a longer analysis. “The Packers still can’t really run the ball, and that’s going to hold them back. But Love and an improving defense have been enough to get them to 3-2. It doesn’t look pretty, but they have a chance to stay on their offensive roll with the Cowboys, Lions and Panthers up next.
The Cowboys are 20th in our rankings following an upset loss to the Buccaneers last week. They ranged from 15th to 23rd, including No. 21 at Fox Sports, where Ralph Vacchiano has them one spot behind Green Bay.
“I’m sure there have been worse losses in recent Cowboys' history than their Thursday night debacle at home against the winless Buccaneers, but I can’t think of any right now,” he wrote. “It’s pretty clear by now that Jerry Jones’ weird rebuilding of his defense created something worse. But where has the offense gone?”
Sportsbook odds aren’t part of our rankings, but they do provide another perspective. In Packers-related odds at FanDuel Sportsbook :
The Packers were +2000 to win the Super Bowl before Week 1 but have been in retreat. They fell to +3000 before facing the Jets and +3300 before hosting the Falcons but crashed to +6000 after losing to the Falcons. They stayed at +6000 after winning at Tampa Bay and briefly moved to +5000 after beating the Bears but are back at +6000.
In NFC North Super Bowl odds, the Bears are +1700, the Lions are +2200 and the Vikings are +2200. The Bears’ odds actually improved after losing to Green Bay; they had been +2000.
Green Bay opened the season ranked seventh in the NFC playoff odds (-112), fell to as low as 12th at +250 after the win at Tampa Bay, and are now 11th at +184. Among the division teams, the Vikings are -370, the Lions are -178 and the Bears are -146.
Quarterback Jordan Love opened at +2200 to win NFL MVP and remained there entering the Atlanta game. He plunged to +10000 but rebounded to +7500 after his powerhouse showing against Chicago.
At DraftKings, the NFC North championship odds still have the Vikings at the front and the Packers at the rear. The Vikings are a strong favorite at +100, followed by the Lions at +300, the Bears at +360 and the Packers at +730. Green Bay was +990 at this time last week. By implied probability, the Packers went from a 9.2 percent chance of winning the North to 12.1 percent.
