title: Chargers Work Out Multiple Big-Name Veterans Amid Injury Bug Onslaught
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are coming off another loss, this time to the hands of the Denver Broncos. The team is 0-5 and is currently tied for the worst record in the entire NFL with the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins. On top of losing five games straight to begin the NFL season, they are also dealing with a massive injury bug, causing the team to be short-handed for the upcoming weeks.
This injury bug saw 18 names on the Chargers injury report before the Broncos game, with guys like Tre Harris and Bud Dupree also getting hurt in the loss. We have yet to see the injury report for the Bolts' matchup in Week 6, but expecting it to be much better would be a poor idea. That said, the team is working out a plethora of names, hoping to add some roster depth during this injury-riddled stretch.
full game status for week 5 vs DEN pic.twitter.com/Ph53lJP3zb
Armour-Davis was a Baltimore Ravens fourth-round draft selection in 2022, giving the team three starts in three years, and played the 2025 season with the Titans, where he had 10 starts and recorded 34 tackles. During the season, he suffered a season-ending injury, likely giving a reason why he has not signed with any team. Amour-Davis' finds himself with a workout opportunity likely due to his connection with Joe Hortiz, who was a part of the Ravens scouting staff when he was draft.
Bell was a seventh-round selection of the San Francisco 49ers in the 2023 draft, playing for the team for two seasons, recording eight catches for 90 yards and three touchdowns. He spent 2025 with the New Orleans Saints, where he recorded two catches for 23 yards and a touchdown. Bell spent his college years with Michigan, having a connection with Chargers' head coach Jim Harbaugh yielding the likely reasoning for his workout beyond the need for another receiver.
Luke Grimm spent the 2025 and 2026 pre-seasons with the Chargers, becoming a reliable slot receiver who also had a special teams return touchdown, giving some validity to his ability to be on an NFL roster. He worked out with the team, being one of two names on this list to sign with the practice squad.
Hilton Jr. was an undrafted free agent after the 2026 NFL Draft ended, signing with the Washington Commanders. After being released in early August, he found his way to the Green Bay Packers, where he had no receiving stats other than a drop during the preseason. He was released shortly after. Hilton Jr. played at LSU, having 4.4 speed and five years of minimal production, giving the Bolt fans the reality of the current situation the team is in at the receiver position.
Tejhuan Palmer was an Arizona Cardinals sixth-round selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, becoming one of very few UAB players to be drafted into the NFL. Palmer spent time on the Cardinals' practice squad for both the 2024 and 2025 seasons, being elevated in one game in 2025. He played with the New England Patriots in the 2026 preseason, recording three catches for 33 yards.
Smith-Schuster is the headlining name of all the players who were worked out by the Chargers. He is a former 1400-yard wide receiver who has been in the NFL since 2017. Smith-Schuster never hit his 2018 season high of 1400 yards ever again, but has carved out a nice career as a role-playing wide receiver across three different teams. Smith-Schuster spent the off-season with the other Harbaugh brother, John, in New York. He did not make the team, but his 345-yard season in 2025 gives him more production than all of the other names combined on the list.
Jake Browning was an undrafted free agent pickup by the Minnesota Vikings in 2019, after being a strong QB at the University of Washington. Browning spent 2019-2020 with the Vikings, eventually moving on to the Cincinnati Bengals, where he would make a name for himself. He spent multiple seasons with the team, headlined by his 2023 run, where he filled in for Joe Burrow for seven starts, recording a league-leading 70.4% completion rate followed by 1936 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions.
In 2025, when asked to start once again, Browning did not play as well, recording three starts, earning 771 yards, six touchdowns and eight interceptions. After this season, he moved on to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, losing the QB2 job to UDFA Jalon Daniels. Browning was signed to the Chargers roster after impressing the staff in his workout. This is likely due to Trey Lance finding himself on injured reserve due to a random practice injury he suffered.
The final name that was worked out was Trask, who was likely the competition for Browning. Trask was once a second-round pick in 2021, where he was supposed to replace Tom Brady after he retired once and for all. That obviously did not happen, as Trask could never break into any sort of real playing time. He is viewed widely as a bust, but his 6'5 frame and strong production at Florida still gives him opportunities. His 2026 preseason with the Panthers was not bad, recording 252 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and two interceptions.

title: Chargers’ Disappointing Ladd McConkey, Joe Alt Injury Updates Just Make Things Worse
full_text:
An 0-6 record at the bye week looms for the Los Angeles Chargers if they can’t get healthy and on track in time for an encounter with the Kansas City Chiefs on the road.
But based on the injury updates and what the Chargers put on film over the first five weeks of losses, the outlook isn’t so hot.
That's especially the case when Jim Harbaugh-era franchise cornerstones like wideout Ladd McConkey and offensive tackle Joe Alt simply can't stay healthy.
Before practice even started this week, Harbaugh and the Chargers offered some bad-sounding updates, too.
During the loss to Denver last weekend, Ladd McConkey was surprisingly active. But as it turns out, that was just in an "emergency" situation because he wound up playing zilch.
Big problem, no doubt, and one made worse by Harbaugh saying early this week that it is only “possible” McConkey gets back to practice ahead of Week 6, according to The Athletic’s Noah Furtado .
As for Alt, ESPN’s Anthony Gharib reports that the star offensive tackle is still undergoing testing for his neck injury to determine the length of his absence.
Keep in mind that the Chargers were forced to essentially roll with four rookies on the offensive line in front of Justin Herbert to disastrous results. That doesn't sound like it will be changing much against the Chiefs with names like Kayode Awosika still rehabbing injuries.
Herbert’s wideout room doesn’t figure to get much better, either. Tre Harris, a possible No. 1 option, is now also “week-to-week” status with a new hamstring injury. Fellow wideout Quentin Johnston is going to be limited with his chest injury, too.
At this point, the injury list makes it pretty clear how things might turn out against the Chiefs before the bye. After the bye, maybe the team will get healthier with some rest and look a little more competitive.
Silver lining? All these injuries, at least, give younger guys a chance to make an impact in live reps. It will give the organization some good film to better make offseason decisions too. Though, whether or not that’s Harbaugh and his staff making those decisions, very much remains to be seen.

title: Chargers Week 5 Power Rankings: Akheem Mesidor Quickly Becoming a Monster
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are heading down a historically bad season, and things seem to get worse and worse.
On the bright side, some younger guys are showing signs of the future. Meaning they are putting on performances that emphasize better things to come.
Here are the rankings for the rookie and sophmores after Sundays disaster versus the Denver Broncos.
Mesidor has officially earned his way to the top of these rankings after making the kind of impact that can change a game in an instant. His ability to get after the quarterback and make life difficult for opposing offenses is exactly what the Chargers need from their young defensive players.
He is beginning to show why the organization invested in him, and his performance against Denver gives him a strong case for being the best rookie or sophomore on this team right now.
Meisdor is starting to rev up, and it’s happening at a fast rate. Every game he is making more plays compared to the previous matchups early in the season.
Playing center in the NFL is no easy task, especially for a rookie who is still adjusting to the speed and physicality of the game. He has plenty to learn, but getting meaningful experience this early in his career is something that could pay off down the road.
The biggest thing for Slaughter right now is consistency. He doesn’t need to become one of the league’s best centers overnight, but he does need to keep improving his communication at the position.
With four rookies starting for the offensive line, they were able to hold their own against a brutal defense. Slaughter was at the helm of that, and the performance was better than expected.
There is a difference between having the talent to make plays and consistently having the right situation to make them happen. The lack of carries should put him lower on the list, however he still has a lot of potential and has shown it all year so far.
His ability to contribute to the running game gives him a valuable role, and the Chargers need to continue finding ways to get him involved. As the offensive line develops and the offense looks for more consistency, Hampton has a chance to show why he remains one of the team’s most intriguing young players.
Harris had a unique opportunity on Sunday, as most of the receivers were injured making him the top target. He had a nice connection with Herbert early on. However the day was cut short for Harris, as he left the game with an apparent injury.
One thing worth remembering is that developing into a consistent NFL receiver takes time. Harris still has an opportunity to earn a larger role, and the Chargers could benefit from having another young pass catcher they can trust in important situations. If he can stay healthy and build on the positive parts of his game, he should be a great weapon for the Bolts in the future.
Travis Burke might be a surprising name to see on here. The Tackle had the highest grade according to PFF's numbers. With all of the injuries going on with that position, it was good to see some bright spots.
While his pass protection could get better, his run game is on a whole different level. This is another player I am excited to see in the future.
Logan Taylor deserves some recognition for the way he’s been thrown into the fire early in his rookie season. The Chargers have dealt with plenty of instability along the offensive line, and Taylor has already been asked to adjust to different positions on the fly. Week 5 wasn’t a perfect performance, but his ability to step in and handle a bigger responsibility makes him worth keeping an eye on as the season progresses. I really respect these rookies and how they are dealing with the circumstances.
Gadsden remains at number 7 after a quiet outing against Denver. The tight end did not have much of an opportunity to make an impact in the passing game, and that makes it difficult to justify moving him higher this week.
There is not too much to dissect since we all know what he is capable of, and with a Broncos defense that is pretty elite. He should have a rebound game soon.
Smith takes the biggest fall in this week’s rankings. His performance against Denver raised concerns, and he now has to respond with a stronger showing in the weeks ahead. Being a young safety means learning from mistakes quickly, especially when those mistakes can lead to big plays for the opposing offense. He has had to step up more than usual this season, so that should help him develop better.
Even with the drop, I wouldn’t write Smith off based on one difficult game. There was a reason he previously ranked at the top of the list. The challenge now is showing that he can bounce back, make better decisions and become a more consistent presence in the secondary.
Young defensive backs often face a difficult learning curve because they have to process what is happening in front of them while reacting to receivers and quarterbacks in real time. That makes consistency especially important, and Mickens has an opportunity to keep developing as he gains more experience.
Playing on the interior of an NFL defensive line requires a lot more than simply getting into the backfield. Defensive tackles have to handle double teams, hold their ground against the run and help create opportunities for the players around them. Those responsibilities can make it difficult for younger players to stand out immediately.
There is still room for Barrett to improve, and that is part of what makes his development worth watching. The Bolts need young players who can give them depth and eventually become reliable contributors in the trenches.

title: 8 Surprise Performances from Chargers Loss to the Broncos: Players Brought the Fight
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers dropped to 0-5 on the season for the first time since the 2003 after their week five loss to the visiting Denver Broncos. The Chargers were in this game. They entered the game with a third of their active roster on the injury report and were forced to start three rookies on the offensive line and were down to just two healthy wide receivers from the original 53-man roster.
The odds were stacked against them and their backs were against the wall but the Chargers did not flinch. Obviously, the results did not fall in their favor, but there was a lot of good on the field that bodes well for the future. Three of the Chargers starting offensive linemen were getting their first NFL starts as rookies.
Right tackle Alex Harkey was active on game day for the first time on Sunday. Harkey's first taste of walking onto an NFL field in a regular season game came starting across from the Denver Broncos defense, and he went to battle.
There were several players who gave everything to try to help win that game and their performances should be recognized. Let's dive in to some of the standout performances against the Broncos.
The Chargers started Travis Burke at left tackle, Logan Taylor at left guard and Alex Harkey at right tackle. These young guns did not flinch and brought the fight to the Broncos. I predicted the Chargers would try to attack the smaller Broncos edge rushers with their inexperienced offensive line paired with the return of Charlie Kolar and Scott Matlock and they absolutely attacked.
Burke was mauling Broncos in the run game, Taylor was creating lanes and generating movement and Harkey was tracking down second-level defenders on the move. Their performances in the run game was incredible given the circumstances. They fought and battled in pass protection as well. The Chargers being down to nearly no wide receivers did not help matters.
The Chargers front office missed opportunities to add depth to the offensive line in the past two drafts. It may be later than anyone hoped but these young players offer hope for the future.
Theo Wease Jr. was just signed to the active roster from the practice squad following a rash of injuries to the wide receiver room. Los Angeles entered week five down their wide receivers one, two, four, and five. Wease had a run with the Miami Dolphins and Mike McDaniel last season as a rookie and was recently signed to the practice squad.
He ended up playing 43 snaps against the Broncos just days after being signed to the active roster. Was it perfect, of course not, but he flashed full throttle effort. On Kimani Vidal's massive touchdown run, Wease flies downfield and throws a critical block to help keep that run alive.
He only got one target but he fought for a first down like his football life depended on it. With the way injuries have hit the wide receiver room, Wease came in and played as hard as he could and it could lead to him sticking around.
I did not expect Scott Matlock's return to mean so much to the offense but he blocked well against the Broncos. On Vidal's touchdown run, Matlock was leading the charge near the goal line and helped clear a path. The Chargers run game looked better than expected on Sunday and it's something to build off of. Matlock can be a big part of that attack.
Expectations are usually high for first round picks but Mesidor showed why those expectations exist. He put on a great performance against the Broncos both as a pass rusher and run defender. His speed and effort are infectious.
Daiyan Henley has played somewhat up and and down this season but seems to be settling in. He was all over the field against the Broncos and was flying around at full speed. When he is playing fast and physical, the Chargers defense hits a new level.
Tuli Tuipulotu has ascended to edge number one. He is an absolute game wrecker on the edge and he seems to be getting stronger. The Chargers better be prepared to make him a bigger contract offer if he keeps playing this way.

title: What Week 5 Loss Changed About Chargers' Trade Deadline Plans: Mack Deserves Better
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers dropped to 0-5 on the 2026 season following a Week 5 loss filled with inexcusable errors from head coach Jim Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert. The Chargers were already facing a near-existential crisis when they dropped to 0-4, now with injury reports featuring more than a third of the active 53-man roster, it seems that hope for a turnaround is all but mathematically gone.
The loss directly alters the mid-season plans for the Chargers front office. Had the Chargers reached their bye and been relatively competitive with any sort of chance at making the playoffs, the Chargers would not have considered selling off any of their assets . Now, heading into week six, Los Angeles has just one more week before their bye week in week seven arrives and they very well could be 0-6 at that point.
The Chargers defense continues to play winning football. The past two seasons have been punctuated in the playoffs by elite defensive play keeping the team in the game but the offense failing to deliver. That exact result has played out of this 0-5 stretch and to be frank, veteran Khalil Mack deserves better.
Mack chose to come back to the Chargers this offseason as his Hall of Fame-worthy career begins to wind down. He trusted the Chargers and the people in the building to get the offense going in the right direction, now with the failures at hand, the Chargers need to do right by him and trade him to a contender of his choosing.
Trading a veteran and leader like Mack would have been unthinkable six weeks ago. Now, after dropping to 0-5, the Chargers should have a sense of urgency to get him off the ship before it sinks.
The week five loss also opens the door for more phone calls and potential deals. The Chargers coaching staff and front office are unable to claim that they still believe they are going to be competitive down the stretch and every team in the NFL knows this.
The Chargers do have several position groups with younger depth who could benefit from extra snaps to finish out the season and give the team a better gauge of potential impact players for next season. Los Angeles has a pair of starting edge rushers outside of Mack and a deep rotation of off-ball linebackers.
The NFL trade deadline has been relatively quiet in recent years compared to expectations, but trades have begun to increase in frequency. The Chargers should take advantage when teams come knocking.
The 2026 season is all but over. Dropping to 0-5 should shift the team's focus from trying to save their season to trying to build and develop for the future. A veteran like Khalil Mack would be a welcome addition to any contender and the Chargers have to consider giving their younger players larger roles.

title: Chargers Are Cheap and It Could Cost Them Jim Harbaugh and Justin Herbert
full_text:
Nothing says more about the Los Angeles Chargers right now than Jim Harbaugh finally being speechless after the latest loss.
The Chargers sit at 0-5 and it’s easy to throw out blame. Sure, blame Harbaugh for some bad in-game decisions. Blame Justin Herbert for the sandwich-themed turnovers. Blame Mike McDaniel. Blame Joe Hortiz for the state of the roster.
But Harbaugh didn’t forget how to coach. Herbert knows how to quarterback. McDaniels is trying to run an offense with players who wouldn’t crack a 53 for other teams. And Hortiz probably has his hands tied by Chargers ownership.
Because it starts at the top: The Chargers are cheap.
The Chargers bought the expensive car but won’t put the nice fuel in it. They paid for Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel.
But they’re also 31st in cash spending . The Chargers’ cap-to-cash ratio (0.9711, no other team is below 1) is dead last.
Onlookers can argue until they’re blue in the face that this doesn't matter. But there’s a fine line between being “smart” with money and just being “cheap.”
Being “cheap” is what creates a five-man competition at left guard all summer in front of the franchise quarterback. Cheap is signing the bargain free-agent center before the market opens to get a deal. Cheap is still rocking with Quentin Johnston because it’s a deal. Or trading for Odafe Oweh, seeing his production in the defense, then not paying to keep him. Cheap is pretending to overvalue the comp pick process in the name of strong depth, when it’s really about budget.
And cheap is still sitting on $26 million in cap space while this all unfolds.
There's perplexing stuff to the cheap factor too. Best example is drafting a first-round running back instead of a premium position, when running back is the one position where "cheap" can be a really good, productive idea. Kimani Vidal says hello.
Not that Chargers fans expected anything different from this ownership group. But it’s going to cost them Harbaugh, and it might just cost them Herbert, who appears to be in a funk only a change of scenery will solve.
And if the time to move on from Herbert comes, Chargers ownership hasn’t exactly instilled confidence that it will use the bounty of assets gained in a way that does anything other than carefully balancing the checkbook before anything else.

title: 3 Winners and 3 Losers After Chargers Drop Yet Another Heartbreaking Game
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers had an opportunity to finally get their season moving in the right direction Sunday, but another late collapse left them searching for answers.
The loss dropped the Chargers to 0-5, making the start to the 2026 season increasingly difficult to ignore. Although several players delivered encouraging performances, costly mistakes ultimately overshadowed the positives.
Here are three winners and three losers from the Chargers’ latest defeat.
Vidal provided one of the game’s most exciting moments. The running back finished with 57 rushing yards on eight carries, including a spectacular 42-yard touchdown that gave the Chargers their first lead of the afternoon. His scoring run demonstrated the explosiveness and determination the offense desperately needed. Vidal broke multiple tackles and found a way into the end zone when the Chargers needed a spark.
Although his performance wasn’t enough to secure a victory, Vidal gave the coaching staff another reason to get him involved moving forward.
The Chargers’ defense needed a game changing play, and Tuipulotu delivered one late in the third quarter.
With Denver threatening to regain the lead, the defensive lineman forced a fumble from quarterback Bo Nix and recovered the ball himself. The turnover immediately put Los Angeles in excellent field position, setting up Vidal’s go-ahead touchdown on the following play.
While the defense couldn’t finish the job, his ability to create a takeaway was one of the afternoon’s biggest positives.
Rucci made his first NFL touchdown catch count. The tight end hauled in a seven-yard scoring pass from Justin Herbert in the third quarter.
The touchdown capped a productive drive that showed what the Chargers’ offense could accomplish when it sustained possession and converted important third downs. Rucci wasn’t the biggest name on the field, but his contribution mattered in a game where offensive production was difficult to find. His performance offered a small bright spot in an otherwise frustrating afternoon.
Herbert’s fourth-quarter mistakes proved decisive. The Chargers quarterback finished 14-of-24 for 121 passing yards and a touchdown, but his late-game struggles overshadowed the earlier scoring drive.
Herbert has previously demonstrated the ability to carry an offense through difficult situations. However, the Chargers need better execution from their franchise quarterback when games reach their most important moments.
Kolar’s early fumble helped put the Chargers in a difficult position from the opening quarter. The turnover gave Denver possession in favorable territory, allowing the Broncos to capitalize with a short touchdown run.
In a game decided by six points, surrendering possession so close to the end zone was an expensive mistake.
Herbert was sacked five times, and the offense struggled to maintain momentum throughout the afternoon.
The failed fourth-and-one attempt early in the fourth quarter was particularly damaging, preventing the Chargers from extending their lead and giving Denver a chance to tie the game.
With the offense already dealing with significant personnel challenges, the offensive line must find ways to provide Herbert with more time and create dependable running lanes.

title: Chargers Could Be Buyers and Sellers in the Coming Weeks
full_text:
The head coach was Marty Schottenheimer and the team finished 4-12 and in last place in the AFC West. The year was 2003, and the then-San Diego Chargers lost their first five games that season. Thanks to Sunday’s 23-17 setback to the visiting Denver Broncos, the Chargers are in that same boat in 2026.
Now keep in mind that that Schottenheimer and company righted that ship a year later, winning the AFC West with a 12-4 record. Is that in the cards for Jim Harbaugh and company?
In any case, it’s that time of the year when teams that find themselves in dire straits may be willing to part ways with some proven performers. At the same time, they may also be looking for some help on an area of the team that is not performing well for any number of reasons.
Last Wednesday, Bradley Locker of Pro Football Focus assembled a list of 15 players that could be dealt for. The deadline is Tuesday, November 10 at 4:00 pm ET. The first name listed is wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and this weekend, the Arizona Cardinals sent the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft to the Houston Texans.
1st and 10 · Denver Broncos Bo Nix ( @BoNix10 ) runs up the middle for 1 yard to DEN 41, fumbles, recovered by Tuli Tuipulotu ( @TuipulotuTuli ) at DEN 42 https://t.co/B3495YSvR2 pic.twitter.com/7zdiKxkD6F
Also listed by Locker are Chargers’ pass-rusher Tuli Tuipulotu and wide receiver Quentin Johnston. The former is in the final year of his rookie contract, and he and the team didn’t agree to an extension this offseason. Johnston is also in the last season of his original deal after the franchise picked up the fifth-year option on the 6’2”, 208-pound wideout.
Tuipulotu has been a player on the rise, and a year ago he not only led the team with 13.0 sacks, the former USC standout was named to his first Pro Bowl. He’s been a bright spot on a club that hasn’t had much to cheer about. He’s tied for third on Chris O’Leary’s defense with 22 tackles, third on the team with a pair of sacks, and leads the Chargers with eight quarterback hits. He also had a pair of takeaways, and two forced fumbles.
Meanwhile, there may not be a big market for Johnston. He’s played in all four games, been targeted 19 times and caught just seven passes for 108 yards and no touchdowns. In his first three NFL seasons, Johnston totaled 144 receptions for 1,877 yards and 18 scores. But his 59.5 catch percentage over that span also left a lot to be desired.
On the other hand, a Chargers’ offensive line that may be in worse shape than last year’s unit needs help at tackle once again with Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt ailing. Locker suggested that Pittsburgh Steelers’ right tackle Dylan Cook may be a player available now that he’s lost his starting job to 2026 first-round pick Max Iheanachor.
Next up for Harbaugh’s team are the first-place Kansas City Chiefs, who were off last week. The same could be said for the 2026 Chargers in terms of every game this season to date.

title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers, Harbaugh Make Dumb Mistakes, Season Slips Away
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers welcomed the Denver Broncos to SoFi Stadium in Week 5 crushed by injuries. Los Angeles started four rookie offensive linemen and were down nearly every wide receiver on the roster. Despite the terrible circumstances , the Chargers had a chance to win this game and boneheaded mishaps handed the Broncos the keys to victory.
At 0-5, the Chargers season is over. Mathematically they have not been eliminated yet but the writing is on the wall. The Chargers must now face tough questions and the demons that haunt organization. How did the team, with Super Bowl aspirations essentially fall off a cliff and forget how to play football on the way down.
The front office will be heavily criticized for how the team has performed and rightfully so. The franchise faces organizational questions that must be answered moving forward.
The game actually went almost exactly as I expected and key matchups proved to be just that. The Chargers defense owned the line of scrimmage for the majority of the game. The Chargers young and inexperienced offensive line attacked the Broncos smaller edge rushers in the run game and opened up the play-action game.
The biggest mistakes were made by Jim Harbaugh and Justin Herbert. Harbaugh made a complete error in judgement when using his first challenge to challenge the spot of a Bo Nix quarterback sneak. The odds of that being overturned are minimal and is was a waste of a timeout and challenge.
That wasted challenge came back to haunt the Chargers as they lost their second challenge later and faced a situation late in the game where that challenge would have helped them win. With just over ten minutes remaining and the Chargers up 17-10, Justin Herbert scrambled for what appeared to be a critical first down. The referees had an awful time with spotting the ball in this game and did not give Herbert the spot. If the Chargers could have challenged it, they would have won.
Harbaugh then made the fatal mistake. He irrationally sent out the Chargers offense to try to secure the first down via quarterback sneak and failed. To that point, the Broncos offense had only managed to score three points on their own, they scored a touchdown only on a short field prior to that. Instead of punting the ball and letting the defense continue on the warpath, Justin Herbert was stuffed and pushed back.
The field position and momentum that immediately went to the Broncos was a killer. Justin Hebert, sensing the lack of offense with nearly no receivers left, became reckless in this game as well and after that momentum swing, he started pressing and trying to do too much leading to turnovers. Herbert's fumbles and interception were squarely on him but so was the entire offense.
The Spanos family and Chargers ownership must be scratching their heads with how this season has gone. The investment in facilities, coaching staff and the big play to bring in Mike McDaniel were never considered risky, they were all considered home run moves.
Are coaching changes on deck? Mike McDaniel called a relatively good game and had a good game plan to attack Denver, especially with the lack of available players. Jim Harbaugh clearly is lost and does not understand how the team is here. Joe Hortiz has been a good drafting general manager but a catastrophic failure on the free agent market and with the offensive line.
My attention as it will be for many Chargers fans will pivot to 2027 draft preparation. But will the Chargers make a move with any of the coaches or the front office. Much of the data and analytics staff left the Chargers shortly after Jim Harbaugh's arrival , he could have used some extra advanced data against the Broncos and at the very least the organization may have to look to reinforce the department.

title: Rams Week 5 Snap Counts Reveal Major Shift in Wide Receiver Rotation
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5, 37-34 in overtime. Throughout the season, the Rams have been adjusting their wide receiver rotation, which has seemingly changed on a weekly basis. Against the Philadelphia Eagles, Tutu Atwell got more snaps in the offense and that carried into Monday. Let’s take a deeper look at the Week 5 snap counts.
Last week, Tutu Atwell played just four snaps fewer than Konata Mumpfield . That changed drastically on Monday night as Atwell out-snapped Mumpfield 32 to six on offense. Mumpfield barely saw any time, while Atwell was used in motion and even had one catch for four yards that resulted in a first down.
It will be interesting to see whether this continues or if it was simply matchup-based. Jordan Whittington also outsnapped Mumpfield 11 to six. Mumpfield played almost 70 percent of the offensive snaps in Weeks 2 and 3 and was down to 7.3 percent on Monday night.
What makes the Atwell situation odd is that he seemed to fall out of favor in the offense last season. Atwell’s role was diminished so much that the team didn’t make an effort to re-sign him in free agency. However, they traded for him before the season. It's possible that with Xavier Smith gone, Atwell's role has opened back up, but it's certainly notable.
Over the past two seasons, Jaylen McCollough has been the dime linebacker for the Rams on defense. Last week, he played just three snaps. On Monday against the Bills, that was down to just one. This season, McCollough has arguably been the Rams’ best tackling safety, and his absence was noticeable against the Bills as the Rams struggled to tackle in the secondary.
Most of McCollough’s snaps over the last few weeks have come on special teams.It’s worth wondering if the Rams are sacrificing McCollough's role on defense so he can contribute more on the coverage units. However, McCollough had just a 32.5 special teams grade via PFF against the Bills.
Last week, the Rams had to abandon 12 and 13 personnel because of the injury to Colby Parksinon. With Parkinson back in the lineup on Monday, the Rams were able to return to what they do best .
With only three tight ends active against the Bills, Allen, Colby Parkinson, and Tyler Higbee were all very active. All three played at least 50 percent of the offensive snaps as they rotated in 12 and 13 personnel.
Davis Allen played 41 snaps, his highest total of the season. While Allen played a higher percentage of the offensive snaps in Week 2, Monday marked a season-high in total snaps. Allen finished with two catches for 24 yards.

title: Alaric Jackson's Suspension Puts Rams in Difficult Position on Offensive Line
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without starting left tackle Alaric Jackson for the next two games. Following Monday night’s game with the Buffalo Bills, Jackson was caught on camera throwing a punch at Bradley Chubb . ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Tuesday that Jackson has been suspended for two games by the NFL.
Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson is expected to be  suspended two games for punching Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb during Monday night’s postgame gathering, per sources. But the NFL has not yet notified the team nor the NFLPA. pic.twitter.com/ZR54be9z1n
There is the possibility that Jackson appeals the suspension and it gets dropped to one game. However, given Jackson's history, that may be unlikely.  Any appeal will be heard by either Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera, or James Thrash, the hearing officers jointly appointed and compensated by the NFL and NFLPA to decide appeals of on-field player discipline.
Through the first five games, the Rams have remained healthy on the offensive line. Outside of three snaps, the Rams have had the same offensive line all season. Due to a poor decision from Jackson after the game on Monday night in which he let his emotions get the best of him, the Rams will have to make a change at left tackle.
When the incident was brought up on Monday night after the game, a suspension was to be expected. This isn’t Jackson’s first incident with the NFL. Back in 2024, Jackson was suspended for recording a sexual interaction with a woman without consent. This past summer, Jackson was arrested on a felony domestic violence charge, and that is still a pending legal situation.
According to the NFL's release, Jackson will be eligible to return to the Rams’ active roster on Monday, October 26, following the team’s October 18 game against the Arizona Cardinals and October 25 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. If Jackson is set to miss the next two games, that would put him back in the lineup for Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers.
With Jackson potentially out for the next two games, the Rams will need to work on how to replace him. The most likely scenario is that the Rams would play David Quessenberry at left tackle for the next two weeks. Quessenberry is the more experienced option and is listed as Jackson’s backup on the depth chart.
However, it also wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams were to activate Keagen Trost off of injured reserve . The Rams drafted Trost in the third round, but he was placed on injured reserve before the season after injuring his hamstring.
Following Week 4, Trost was eligible to come off of injured reserve. McVay was asked last week if the team had discussed elevating Trost or Justin Dedich. “We could open that up, but that's not a conversation that we've had at this point,” said McVay.
Trost may not start, but he would provide good tackle depth behind Quessenberry and give the Rams another option if needed. Trost brings the versatility to play on both the left and right sides of the offensive line. While Trost is more comfortable on the right side, he does have the ability to play left tackle. In a worst-case scenario, the Rams could also move Warren McClendon to left tackle and play Trost on the right side.
As the Rams look ahead to their game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, the most likely immediate solution will be Quessenberry at that spot. Even against the Cardinals, the loss of Jackson will be a significant one. Last season without Jackson, the Rams lost to the Atlanta Falcons. When Jackson was suspended in 2024, the Rams lost to the Cardinals, 41-10, while Dennis Gardeck had three sacks.
With the offensive line being one of the few areas where the Rams have had stability, Jackson's absence creates an unnecessary challenge. The Rams will now have to rely on their depth at one of the most important positions on offense because of a situation that could have been avoided.

title: Rams' Special Teams Problems Persist and Sean McVay Is Running Out of Answers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams used to be renowned for how good they were on special teams. While Jeff Fisher didn’t do a lot well, the Rams’ special teams with John Fassel were always among the best in the NFL.
In Fisher’s last season, the Rams ranked third in special teams DVOA. It was one of the few things that looked good as the Rams finished that season 4-12. Sean McVay kept Fassel when he took over and the Rams ranked second in special teams DVOA in 2017.
When Stedman Bailey scored on the fake punt return vs the Seahawks #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/fRQrvfkMf5
From there, things began to spiral. In 2018, the Rams were 17th and ranked 30th by 2020 when McVay moved on from Fassel. Despite having the seventh-ranked special teams unit in 2021, the Rams were last in 2023.
Things hit a tipping point last year when the Rams lost multiple games with special teams playing a major role in those losses. After Week 16, McVay made his first in-season coordinator change , firing Chase Blackburn.
Heading into this season, there was some optimism around the Rams’ special teams unit. McVay moved special teams periods toward the start of practice in an attempt to prioritize that phase of the game. He hired a respected special teams coordinatora in Bubba Ventrone. The Rams also signed Joe Cardona and Grant Stuard. They’ve added special teams players such as Maximus Pulley during the season.
“If you were at their camp, you’d heard about all of this, and the optimism that this would all be fixed—with a new commitment to getting it right,” wrote Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer . “Having Ventrone, Cardona and Stuard helped, but more than just that, they were symbolic of a renewed commitment.”
However, here we are after Week 5, and the Rams are in an all-too-familiar situation . The problems started in Week 1. In Australia, the Rams allowed a 45-yard kickoff return to Deebo Samuel to start the second half. Against the Giants in Week 2, Mevis missed a 43-yard field goal and the Rams took a 15-yard penalty that resulted in points.
In Week 3, the Rams had issues on both the punt and punt return units, sparking a change as the team cut Xavier Smith. Against the Eagles, the Rams allowed a 41-yard punt return that turned into a touchdown. On Monday night, Harrison Mevis missed from 50 yards and had a potential game-winning kick blocked in overtime . McVay was asked after the game if he expected changes on special teams.
“Yeah, I'm going to evaluate everything,” said McVay.
It’s been a weekly theme despite it being something that the Rams and McVay have tried to fix. An argument can be made that they should have done more. Following last season, it was always odd that the Rams didn’t bring in replacements or competition for Harrison Mevis, Xavier Smith, or Ethan Evans.
It made sense why McVay was so upset after the game on Monday night. A great performance from Matthew Stafford and the offense and a timely turnover from the defense were put to waste because of special teams.
“We did some really good stuff and in the kicking game, especially with our PAT field goal, not even close to good enough,” McVay said. “It cost us the game tonight.”
This is about as upset as I’ve seen Sean McVay after a game. He blames himself for the conservative third and five call in OT and kicking the long field goal. There will likely be special teams changes this week. pic.twitter.com/Y06H3vLON1
As McVay has done so often since taking over as head coach, it was as if he expected to simply hire an experienced coordinator and let them figure it out. Again, few changes were made to the core personnel outside of Cardona and Stuard – two Ventrone guys.
Following Monday night’s loss, it was clear that changes needed to be made. However, the changes don’t seem simple at this point. It’s hard to pinpoint exactly what fixes the Rams’ current special teams situation. What exactly is the solution?
Since the Rams moved on from Fassel at the end of the 2019 season, they’ve gone through four different special teams coordinators, including interim Ben Kotwica last year. They hired John Bonamego, who lasted one season. Joe DeCamillis was better, but lasted just two seasons. McVay hired a young, up-and-coming coach in Blackburn. Blackburn arguably lasted longer than he should have at 2.5 seasons before he was fired. This offseason, McVay hired a well-respected special teams coordinator in Bubba Ventrone.
In eight years, the Rams have had five different special teams coordinators. While the Rams could fire Ventrone after five weeks, that would seemingly only continue the coaching carousel that they’ve had at that spot.
Back in 2023, the Rams opted not to bring back Matt Gay. The Rams signed Tanner Brown as an undrafted free agent before cutting him in the preseason and eventually adding Brett Maher ahead of Week 1. Maher was inconsistent and the Rams signed Lucas Havrisik. Havrisik didn’t make it to the end of the year and Maher was brought back.
In 2024, the Rams drafted Joshua Karty, who finished 29-for-34 as a rookie before being cut halfway through his second season. Karty was one of the best kickers in the NCAA at Stanford and was a finalist for the Lou Groza award in 2022, given to the best kicker in the country. The Rams then moved on to sign Mevis to finish out the year. They are now onto Blake Grupe after cutting Mevis on Tuesday.
Grupe is the sixth kicker that the Rams have signed since 2023. They’ve averaged almost two kickers per season.
Multiple things can be true here. The Rams needed to make a change at kicker. However, it’s also fair to say that Grupe may not be the answer. The Rams have done this kicking carousel for the last four years. Why is this time any different?
At this point, the Rams have done this same dance over and over. They’ve pulled the plug at kicker only to be back at square one. They’ve added a respected coordinator and are still one of the worst special teams units in the NFL.
In 2023, the Rams had the seventh-worst special teams unit in DVOA history through five games. This year, the Rams top the list. Over the last four seasons, the Rams have had two of the seven worst special teams units. Only the 2023 Rams and 1977 Vikings made it to the playoffs.
If something doesn't change, this year’s Rams might be making some unfortunate history 😬 pic.twitter.com/zwlLkVR8PB
It’s easy to say that the Rams should just fire the special teams coordinator or make a change at kicker. A lot can be said about how much McVay prioritizes special teams. However, the Rams have fired the special teams coordinator and made changes at kicker for the past five years. It continues to be the same story. This offseason, McVay acknowledged that special teams needed to be better and he did prioritize it, yet the results haven’t reflected that.
We’re at a point where you ask, “where do the Rams even go from here?” It almost seems hopeless. While the names and processes have changed, the problems have persisted.
McVay has gotten so much right as the head coach of the Rams. However, special teams have remained his biggest blind spot. Despite all the changes he's made, none have produced sustained results.
The Rams have a roster capable of competing for a Super Bowl, but their special teams are actively holding them back. Until McVay finds a solution that lasts longer than a few weeks, it's hard to see how this story ends any differently.

title: Rams Signing Kicker Blake Grupe Is a Necessary Change That Was Long Overdue
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have made a change at kicker following their Monday night loss to the Buffalo Bills . On Tuesday morning, the Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe off of the New York Jets’ practice squad to hopefully bring some stability to the kicking operation.
Through the first five weeks of the season, the Rams have had problems on special teams, primarily with the kicking operation. Heading into Monday’s game, Mevis was still just 5-for-7 and had a miss from 48 yards last week against the Eagles. In Monday night’s loss, Mevis missed from 50 yards and also had a potential game-winning kick blocked in overtime.
While Mevis brought some stability to the kicking operation last season, there were always questions about his range. Mevis had been perfect with extra points and 19-for-20 inside of 45 yards. However, beyond 45 yards is where Mevis lacked consistency , and in today’s NFL, teams need a kicker who can hit from range when called upon.
Mevis had some strong moments, including hitting the game-winner last year against the Chicago Bears in difficult conditions in overtime. However, he was too inconsistent to start 2026 and the Rams were forced to make a change.
Grupe will now replace Mevis in Los Angeles. An undrafted free agent in 2023, Grupe spent three seasons with the New Orleans Saints. He had missed eight field goal attempts in 2025 and was eventually cut.
However, Grupe does have proven range. After being cut by the Saints, Grupe made a 60-yard field goal with the Indianapolis Colts. While he was brought back in the offseason, he lost the competition to Spencer Shrader in training camp. According to ColtsWire , Grupe was steady in training camp but struggled in the preseason games. During the preseason, Grupe was 2-for-4 with one miss inside of 40 yards and another miss beyond 50.
BLAKE GRUPE NAILS A CAREER-LONG 60-YARD FIELD GOAL FOR THE LEAD 😱 The Colts take a 1-point lead with 47 seconds left 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Ys9EJcPXar
Grupe has a career field-goal percentage of 81.9 percent. He’s 86-for-105 in his career and 19-for-27 beyond 50 yards with a long of 60.
While the Rams signed Grupe, it shouldn’t be the only move that they make. The Rams should also consider signing another kicker, such as Tanner Brown or Joshua Karty, to their practice squad in case they need to make another change or simply want to hold an active competition.
Adding Grupe is a step in the right direction, but an argument can be made that this should have been done a long time ago. The Rams should have made these special teams changes in the offseason, but instead stuck with the status quo. After sticking with Xavier Smith, he was cut after Week 3. The Rams stuck with Mevis and didn’t bring in any competition, only to cut him after their Week 5 loss.
The Rams have now made changes at both punt returner and kicker in the span of two weeks, but it remains to be seen whether those moves will be enough to fix a special teams unit that has consistently cost them games. Grupe may not be the long-term answer at kicker, but the Rams can't afford to continue learning lessons on special teams the hard way.

title: Rams Position Grades: Matthew Stafford Shines, Special Teams Falter in Loss to Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills in disappointing fashion on Monday Night Football, falling 37-34 in overtime. Let’s get to this week’s player and position grades.
For the fourth time in the last two seasons, the Rams lost a game in which Matthew Stafford threw for at least 370 yards and three touchdowns. Stafford played well enough for the Rams to win , which included leading a game-tying drive at the end of regulation. He completed a career-high 40 passes on Monday night. It’s a shame that the Rams couldn’t reward his performance in what was his best game of the year. PFF Grade: 67.9
The Rams struggled to get much going on the ground. Kyren Williams averaged just 3.1 yards per carry and Blake Corum had five carries for 19 yards. At the same time, both running backs found the end zone and made an impact in the passing game. Corum had a career-long 34-yard reception and Williams set the Rams up to score in the final seconds of the game.
Puka Nacua carried this group with 17 receptions on 24 targets. His 17 receptions marked a career-high and his 24 targets were the most for a wide receiver since Brandon Marshall in 2009. Davante Adams added two touchdowns of his own. The Rams didn’t get much production outside of those two, but Nacua and Adams played well.
Tyler Higbee has looked like his former self this season and remains a reliable option in the passing game. Without Terrance Ferguson, Higbee proved that he can still deliver in big spots, finishing with five receptions for 83 yards. Davis Allen got involved in the passing game as well. Had the Rams made the game-winning field goal, we would likely be talking about Allen’s 21-yard reception in overtime. Colby Parkinson made his impact felt in the run game as a blocker.
The offensive line was fine, but didn’t protect well in some moments. Stafford may have had a few opportunities to go down the field in the first half, but the Bills had a great game plan defending the Rams’ play-action bootlegs. Warren McClendon allowed five pressures at right tackle.
Defensively, the Rams got pressure on Josh Allen, but Josaiah Stewart was the only player to finish with a sack. They weren’t disciplined in their rush lanes and consistently allowed Allen to escape. The defensive line also struggled defending the run and limiting James Cook. As a group, they missed five tackles.
A lot of the Rams’ struggles in the run game came at the second and third levels. Nate Landman had two forced fumbles and created the turnover in overtime. However, Allen consistently made him look silly in the open field. Omar Speights got washed out in the run game too often. The Bills took advantage of the Rams’ lighter defensive fronts.
From a coverage standpoint, the Rams were actually very good. The Bills were not able to attack the Rams down the field very often in the passing game. However, this group, especially the safeties, struggled in space. This was by far Quentin Lake’s worst performance. AAs a group, they missed seven tackles, with Kam Curl being credited with three. A better tackling effort from the secondary and the Rams may have won this game convincingly.
There were plenty of negatives with this group on Monday night, but there were also some positives. Ethan Evans had a nice punt in this game. Following the 70-yard kickoff return, the coverage unit looked good after that. Additionally, Jordan Whittington had a few nice kickoff returns. With that said, all of that is overshadowed because of the missed field goal from 50 yards and the blocked kick that lost the game.
Sean McVay undoubtedly played a big role in this loss . His play call on 3rd-and-5 in overtime and his management of that entire sequence weren’t good enough. He made the right decision to go for two and made some great second-half adjustments. With that said, as much as the kicking unit deserves blame for the block, McVay deserves just as much criticism for how he managed the situation.

title: Week 6 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: Rams' Dream Team Reputation Starting to Fade
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams dropped to 2-3 after their 37-34 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. At some point, the Rams have to start getting results , and that’s not something they’ve done so far this year. The Rams have two wins, one against a New York Giants team with Jameis Winston, and their second against a hurt Philadelphia Eagles team.
It seems as if every week at this point, we’re talking about how the Rams are getting hurt by their special teams mistakes. On Monday night, it cost them again as Harrison Mevis’ game-winning field goal was blocked.
The Rams are starting to resemble the 2010 Chargers, who had a great offense and defense but ranked 32nd in special teams. They are also following a similar path to the 2011 Eagles, who were labeled a "dream team."
Even the Rams understand that they have to start getting results. “I feel like we're a good football team. We have to go out there and get some results,” said quarterback Matthew Stafford.
There comes a point when the dream team label and the perception that the Rams are talented on paper will begin to wear off. The Rams arguably played their best game of the season against the Bills, but that wasn’t good enough. In this week’s consensus power rankings, the Rams rank just inside the top-10. They are the only team with a losing record inside the top 10.
The Rams have three losses, all to teams ranked ahead of them. However, one more loss before their bye week could send them tumbling down the rankings. The belief in this team from the media will only last so long. Here are this week’s consensus power rankings.
In this week’s power rankings, the Rams dropped one spot from No. 7 to No. 8 . Over the next few weeks, the Rams should start to get healthy as Myles Garrett gets set to return. Still, the injury excuse can only carry so much weight. The Rams need to find some consistency.
It almost benefits the Rams in this week’s power rankings that they lost to another media darling in the Buffalo Bills. They also put up a good fight, losing in overtime despite having every chance to win. While the Rams dropped one spot in ESPN’s power rankings, they remained at number six in Connor Orr’s rankings .
It was wild seeing Matthew Stafford so vehemently trying to quiet down a crowd inside his own home stadium before he probably realized that it’s 70% Bills fans. There’s not much you can do there. At least the people who paid to be there weren’t disappointed.
Last week, the Rams sat at No. 5 in The Athletic’s power rankings, but dropped five spots to No. 10 after their loss to the Bills. The ‘dream team’ label is starting to fade in The Athletic’s rankings. For the third time this season, the Rams have dropped below .500 and remain unable to string wins together. That’s reflected here.
“The star-studded Rams haven’t had a winning record all season, and that’s partly because Harrison Mevis’ 48-yard, game-winning field goal attempt in overtime Monday night was blocked,” wrote The Athletic.
Nick Shook remains the only analyst to rank the Rams out of the top 10 . With that said, the Rams actually did move up in his rankings this week, improving one spot to No. 12. While Shook continues to rank the Rams lower than anyone else this season, it’s hard to argue with his logic. The Rams have a losing record and simply have not shown the consistency that a team inside the top 10 should.
“We learned that the Rams have rediscovered their offensive stride,” wrote Shook. “We also know they have problems stopping the run, and the back end of their defense cannot stop committing poorly timed penalties. Most of all, we learned that Sean McVay still hasn’t learned from his squad’s past special teams issues.”
The Rams barely remain inside Mike Florio’s top 10 , but that could change very quickly. It’s true that the Rams’ schedule gets easier over the next few weeks, but they have to prove they can be consistent. One loss over the next five weeks will certainly drop them outside of the top-10.
“They have five winnable games before the bye; if they lose any of them, things could get interesting down the stretch,” wrote Florio.
Now that the Rams are out of the grueling part of their schedule, the pressure is on for them to start winning games. Again, if the Rams don’t turn it around fast, the ‘dream team’ reputation will start to wear off. They’ve had a difficult start to their season, but an argument can be made that they should be 4-1 or, at the very least, 3-2. Instead, they sit at 2-3.
“The Rams really drew the short straw on their schedule this season, and it’s starting to take its toll,” wrote Ralph Vacchiano . “Their three losses this season are to the 49ers, Broncos and Bills — three legitimate Super Bowl contenders. But at some point, they’re going to have to beat teams like that if they want to realize their Super Bowl dream.”
Pete Prisco has the Rams just making the top 10 in his latest power rankings, and his confidence in them is starting to dissipate.
“Who saw this team at 2-3 after five games? Dream team? Maybe we all rushed to judgement,” wrote Prisco.
A get-right game against the Cardinals might be exactly what the doctor ordered after a disappointing loss to the Bills. The Cardinals just traded away one of their most talented offensive players in Marvin Harrison Jr. and have lost four straight.
Still, this is a feisty team and the Rams will have to be ready. They may rank 29th in the consensus power rankings, but they took the 49ers to the wire in Week 2. They also led the Giants early before losing, 36-24.
After five weeks, the cream is starting to rise to the top. At 5-0, the 49ers look to be one of the best teams in the NFL, if not the best. They beat a Seattle Seahawks team on the road, which is no easy task.
The bottom-half of the top-10 is where it gets more difficult. It’s hard to place an undefeated Vikings team that also ranks 30th in offensive DVOA. The Jaguars have looked like contenders at times, but they have a loss to the Broncos and arguably should have lost to the Eagles on Sunday. The next few weeks should provide more answers.

title: 10 Takeaways From Rams' Overtime Loss to Bills: Special Teams Disaster, McVay's Big Mistake, and More
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams fell to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in overtime, 37-34. It was another game that the Rams should have won , but special teams continue to be a thorn in the Rams’ side on a weekly basis. Coming out of that one, it’s understandable that the Rams would have a sour taste in their mouths.
“I’m really proud of our group. I thought offensively and defensively we battled,” said head coach Sean McVay.  “We did some really good stuff and in the kicking game, especially with our PAT field goal, not even close to good enough. It cost us the game tonight.”
The Rams are now 2-3 after five weeks and their last two losses have been difficult to swallow. Here are 10 takeaways from Monday night’s loss to the Bills.
With Colby Parkinson back in the mix, the Rams got back to their multi-tight end sets on Monday night against the Bills. While Max Klare was inactive, the Rams operated out of 12 personnel at a 24.4 percent rate. Going into Monday’s game, they were at around 4.5 percent. After using 13 personnel at a 1.3 percent rate last week, it was back up to 30.8 percent on Monday night.
Tyler Higbee had a vintage performance with five receptions for 83 yards. He has three games with 60 or more yards for the third time in his career. He is the only Rams tight end to have a three-game streak of 60 or more yards in the Super Bowl era.
This goes beyond the blocked field goal as we’ll get to that later. The Rams had a promising opening drive lasting 14 plays and over half of the first quarter. Despite working hard to go down the field, the Rams came up empty as Harrison Mevis missed from 50 yards.
While Mevis is reliable from inside 45 yards, t hat’s simply not good enough in today's NFL or a world that the Rams can live in consistently. In a league where kickers are consistently making field goals from 50-plus yards, the Rams are having to manage games completely differently because of their kicker. Mevis has four misses this year, three of which have come between the 45-50 range. It’s simply not sustainable.
While it’s true that penalties are up this year, there are situational and pre-snap penalties happening that are very uncharacteristic of a Sean McVay-coached team. On the opening drive, Kyren Williams had a 9-yard run that picked up a first down, but it was called back because of a holding penalty. The Rams had to settle for a 50-yard field goal that was missed. At the end of the half, the Rams took over at the 43-yard line. A false start on Warren McClendon pushed them back five yards.
The situational penalties have been killers. In the first half, the Rams defense had a 1st-and-20 that was wiped away due to a penalty on Quentin Lake. Later on the same drive, they got a stop on 3rd-and-goal, but a hold on Josh Wallace gave the Bills a first down. Allen would throw a touchdown pass three plays later. Between 2021 and 2025, the Rams had two games total with 10 or more penalties. The Rams have picked up 10 or more penalties in two of the last three games.
The Bills gained 16.3 yards after the catch per reception against the Rams. It was the highest average by any offense in a game since the start of the Next Gen Stats era, which began in 2016. The Bills' running backs alone had 125 yards after the catch and 57 yards after the catch over expected. Due to the injuries at wide receiver, the Bills didn’t have much of a downfield passing game.
In the second half, the Bills had a touchdown drive go 80 yards in just five plays. The only pass beyond the line of scrimmage on that drive was the two-point conversion. Josh Allen had over 100 yards rushing.The Rams struggled in space and in the open field on Monday night as players at the second and third levels consistently missed tackles and took bad angles. Defensively, the Rams are at their best when they can stop the run and get pressure on the quarterback. Much like in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, the Rams couldn’t stop it.
Puka Nacua’s stat line is almost insane to look at. The Rams targeted Nacua 24 times on Monday night. Yes, they targeted him 24 times. That’s the most targets for a Rams wide receiver in a single game in franchise history. It’s only the third time it’s happened in NFL history. The last player to do it was Brandon Marshall back in 2009 with the Denver Broncos.
“He can access all areas of the field,” said Matthew Stafford. “I think that's one of the major things for him. He’s fantastic in the screen game, underneath, middle of the field. Made some plays out on the perimeter as well today.”
In a sense, it would be nice for other players to get involved. That type of workload, given Nacua’s injury history, isn’t sustainable. However, when Nacua is playing as well as he did on Monday night and is part of what makes the offense go, how do you not keep giving him the ball? Nacua finished with 17 catches for 138 yards. In both games since his return, Nacua has over 100 yards receiving.
While the yards weren’t there for Stafford in the first half, he remained efficient. While he had a couple of misses, he generally looked more comfortable than he had in previous weeks . In the second half, Stafford went off, completing 21 of 26 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns. He finished with a career-high 40 completions for 383 yards and three touchdowns.
With that said, the Rams need to do a better job supporting Stafford. These are games that Stafford consistently lost in Detroit because he didn’t have the support. Over the last two seasons, the Rams have lost four games in which Stafford has thrown for at least 370 yards and three touchdowns. That can’t happen. As a team, the Rams need to be better.
Given how the offense was moving in the second half, an argument can be made that if the Rams had kept operating the offense as usual, they would have ended up in the end zone. However, after Stafford found Nacua for 21 yards to put the Rams at the 35-yard line, McVay got conservative.
On the first play, McVay called a quick pass from under center that fell incomplete. The next play was a screen pass to Nacua to set up 3rd-and-5. Instead of going for the first down, McVay called a run that picked up zero yards.
“I wish I would have had a better play call and gone forward, got it a lot tighter. I'm sick right now with myself,” said McVay. “I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go forward on third down and go to fourth or whatever it was. That's on me.”
Despite the problems with the field goal unit, McVay seemed content with settling for a 48-yard field goal. That sequence is one that will haunt McVay for a while. For as much as the blocked kick is on the field goal unit, it’s just as much on McVay for settling in that situation.
It’s easy to say that the Rams need to make changes on special teams, but what does that even mean at this point? The Rams could fire Bubba Ventrone, but they’ve gone through three special teams coordinators over the last two years. They could move on from Mevis, but this is a team that’s gone through kickers such as Joshua Karty, Brett Maher, and Lucas Havrisik over the last few years. There doesn’t appear to be a clear answer to fix a glaring issue.
With that said, something needs to change. McVay acknowledged that after the game, saying, “Yeah, I'm going to evaluate everything.” The Rams can’t stick with this as the status quo and call it good. The kickoff coverage bounced back, but allowed a 70-yard return on the opening kickoff. In a game where points are at a premium, the field goal unit left six points on the board. The Rams can’t keep losing games because of special teams.
This is at least the fourth game in the last two years that the Rams have lost that can be directly tied to a special teams mistake. At some point, that starts to have an impact mentally on the team as a whole. McVay himself sounded defeated in his post-game press conference.

title: Rams Winners and Losers: Special Teams, Sean McVay Come Up Short in Overtime Loss to Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in overtime , 37-34. Matthew Stafford is now the only quarterback to lose after throwing for at least 370 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions over the last two years, and it’s happened four times. The Rams had enough good individual performances to win the game, but they were once again doomed by special teams. Here are the winners and losers from Monday’s game.
At some point , the Rams are going to have to make a change at kicker , and it wouldn’t be surprising to see that happen this week. Mevis has missed two field goals, one of which was blocked, in the last two games. On Monday night, Mevis missed one wide left from 50 yards and then had the game-winning kick blocked in overtime. He’s now 4-for-8 in his career from 45 yards or longer. It’s simply not a world that the Rams can live in. Mevis is good from inside 45 yards, but that’s not good enough in the modern NFL in which kickers are regularly making kicks from that distance.
For the most part, Sean McVay was coaching a great game. After the offense scored just seven points in the first half, his adjustments seemed to pay off. The Rams’ offense scored a touchdown on all but one drive in the second half. Where McVay falls into the loser category is with his late-game management. Given how well the offense was playing, an argument can be made that they should have gone for two at the end of the game. In overtime, McVay got conservative and seemed to be content with a 48-yard field goal.
there is no reason to get conservative with Mevis as your kicker and the way the Rams offense is dominating
After some inconsistency in the first four games of the season, the Rams could not have asked for a better performance from Matthew Stafford. Stafford completed 40 passes for 383 yards and threw three touchdowns. He led the offense down the field to tie the game at the end of regulation to force overtime. This was a winning effort from Stafford, and it’s a shame that the Rams couldn’t reward that performance with a win.
It’s true that the Bills’ offense and Josh Allen are very good. At the same time, the Bills punted once the entire game. The secondary took away any downfield passing game, but Josh Allen and James Cook combined for 232 yards rushing. The Bills had a touchdown drive that went for 80 yards in five plays. On that drive, the only pass that Allen threw beyond the line of scrimmage was on the two-point conversion. For most of the night, the defense didn’t tackle well in space and didn’t stop the run. When they got pressure on Allen, they didn’t finish. If the defense plays better, the Rams win comfortably.
Puka Nacua was the entire Rams’ offense on Monday night against the Bills. He had a career-high 17 receptions on 24 targets. Davante Adams had some moments, but it’s surprising he wasn’t more involved. Additionally, Konata Mumpfield played just one offensive snap the entire game and has fallen behind Tutu Atwell. Atwell also had just one catch. Nacua is a great player, but that type of workload isn’t sustainable.
Speaking of Nacua, he’s a clear winner from this game. Coming into Monday night, Nacua was 86th in the NFL in receptions. He’s now seventh. Nacua’s 17 receptions are a career-high. In both games since his return, he’s had over 100 yards receiving and been a major part of the offense. Nacua looks to be healthy and playing like himself, which is a good thing. At the same time, the Rams can’t continue using him at this pace without risking injury .
