title: Miami Dolphins 2026 Week 5 Snap Counts Stories: Injuries Cause Shuffling
full_text:
What stood out regarding play counts in the Miami Dolphins' 31-24 loss against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday:
We'll start with the list of inactives, which was highlighted by four players missing the game with injuries, including wide receiver Caleb Douglas out for a third consecutive game with an ankle injury.
The only Dolphins player who was active but did not play was backup quarterback Kyle McCord.
Since we've been keeping track every game, the starting lineup was back to six rookies Will Kacmarek at tight end, Chris Bell at wide receiver, guard Kadyn Proctor, linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, cornerback Chris Johnson and safety Michael Taaffe.
-- The Dolphins opened with two tight ends and two wide receivers, which was why rookie fullback DJ Herman didn't get a start.
-- After the Dolphins had only 39 offensive snaps against Minnesota, that number jumped to a lot more respectable 66 against the Bengals.
-- After playing fewer snaps than Kacmarek against Minnesota, Greg Dulcich got a very heavy work load in Week 5 with 49 offensive snaps. That was his second-highest total of the season behind the 51 he played against the Kansas City Chiefs in the Week 3 home opener.
-- Besides QB Malik Wilis and the offensive linemen, the player with the most offensive snaps was wide receiver Malik Washington with 53, yet another indication of his value.
-- At running back, practice squad elevation Carlos Washington Jr. got as many offensive snaps at Jaylen Wright, who continues to struggle to find his footing in his third season with the Dolphins. Ollie Gordon II got 43 snaps firmly established as the No. 1 back in the absence of De'Von Achane.
-- Jonah Savaiinaea ended up playing 18 snaps before leaving the game with an ankle injury and being replaced by Jarrett Kingston for the final 48 snaps at right guard.
-- Rookie tight end Seydou Traore got his first offensive snap against the Bengals after being used exclusively on special teams in the first four games — but it was only one.
-- With Jordyn Brooks, JuJu Brents and Michael Taaffe all temporarily leaving the game with injuries, Jacob Rodriguez and Dante Trader Jr. became the only players who played every snap on defense.
-- 2025 first-round pick Kenneth Grant made his return to action but played a very modest 16 defensive snaps, which probably made sense in helping him work his way back into the action. That number better increase once the Dolphins return from their bye, though.
-- The Dolphins opened the game in the nickel and played a good portion of the game with that five-DB alignment, with Chris Johnson Jr. playing 64 of the 65 snaps and Jason Marshall also played 57 snaps.
-- Josh Uche, who's become the most effective edge defender on the team, got the snap count to reflect that, with 45 snaps compared to 36 for Chop Robinson. Practice squad elevation Rodney McGraw played 14 snaps, not far behind Malik Herring.
-- With Brooks leaving the game temporarily, Willie Gay Jr. got extra work at linebacker and finished with 37 snaps, his highest total since the opener against the Las Vegas Raiders when the Dolphins used a lot more three-linebacker looks.
-- With Brents missing some snaps when he was banged up, newcomer Jaylin Simpson got five snaps on defense and had a nice third-down pass breakup against Ja'Marr Chase.
-- Because of the injuries, only four non-specialists saw action only on special teams, down from eight against Minnesota. This time it was Andre Jones Jr., Julius Wood, Marcellus Dial Jr. and Andrew Meyer.
-- Speaking of special teams, Traore again led the way with 21 snaps, followed by 17 for Jones and 15 for McGraw.

title: Four Losers And Four Winners From the Week 5 Dolphins Loss
full_text:
Don't let the 31-24 final score deceive you; this was not a close game between the Miami Dolphins and Cincinnati Bengals. In an important game for Cincy regarding the standings in the AFC North, they took care of business and handed the Fins their fifth straight loss.
At the minimum, if you're looking for player and team progression in the same vain as the Minnesota game, you won't find it here. The offense was stonewalled for three quarters, only finding rhythm when it was too late, and the defense gave up over 300 total yards and four touchdowns.
The Dolphins head into the bye week battered and bruised, figuratively and literally, and worst of all, still searching for answers. Only three teams remain winless in the NFL: Miami, Tennessee, and the Los Angeles Chargers. Based on their performances against the Bengals, it's difficult to predict when they'll finally shower Jeff Hafley with Gatorade.
Yes, Willis doesn't have a star-studded list of weapons to throw to. But Willis flat-out held the offense back, was unable to deal with Cincinnati's commanding front seven, and was more of a liability in the passing game than ever before.
Regardless of how you felt about the comments that Bengals DB Jordan Battle made about Willis's ball-tapping and how it's a tell that he's going to throw the ball, is it purely a coincidence that the DB who caught both interceptions that Willis threw was Battle?
Willis also lost a fumble pretty much by himself near his own goal line and was sacked three times. One of those sacks came on second-and-goal in the third quarter — a case of holding onto the ball for too long, trying to make an impossible play happen instead of throwing the ball away — a consistent mistake he's made this season.
To his credit, he looked decent as a scrambler with 74 yards and a touchdown, but this was by far his worst game of the season purely from a mistake standpoint. His game looks extremely limited, and because the weapons at his disposal are also limited, you get an offensive performance like the Dolphins got against the Bengals — simply not good enough.
Johnson and Miami's secondary had a tough task against Cincinnati since two of their wide receivers, who were questionable — Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins — ended up playing. But Johnson held his own with six total tackles, a low number because he locked down most receivers he was matched up against.
Like the other rookies on defense, Johnson also achieved his first major highlight of the season, a Peanut punch on Chase Brown in the red zone, forcing a fumble that was picked up by Chop Robinson — ignore that Robinson also had the ball punched out, only for JuJu Brents to corral it in the end.
There were only a handful of receptions that Johnson gave up, but nothing major. He may have had a slow start to the season in terms of effectiveness, but he's heating up for the Dolphins at a solid pace.
After being stuffed by the Minnesota defense, Wright needed a bounce-back game to genuinely help out this offense whenever he was on the field, but once again, he was made a non-factor — six carries for 11 yards.
The offensive line has been able (for the most part) to create gaps for Miami's running backs, but Wright's running can be predictable, purely horizontal, and he's been unable to either evade or shake off tacklers in the same way that Ollie Gordon has been able to do.
Both wide receivers Chris Bell and Malik Washington  were both used in the running game for one play each and recorded more rushing yards than Wright (26 & 18). Miami's duo in the backfield was once De'Von Achane and Gordon, and now it's forced to be Gordon and Willis because Wright isn't doing enough to justify remaining the backup running back.
It might not look like much, but Coleman had a breakout game for the Dolphins that was well-needed — three receptions for 30 yards off seven targets, including his first touchdown in the NFL that came in the fourth quarter, beginning a way-too-late rally for Miami that obviously fell short.
Miami's fifth-round pick showcased the ability to create separation even with limited space, headlined by the aforementioned touchdown. He also showcased his athleticism when he dove for a catch at the six-yard line with a minute to go, leading to Willis sneaking into the end zone right after.
Caleb Douglas is still injured and, spoiler alert, Chris Bell had a disappointing game. So, seeing Coleman have the performance he did is reassuring, and maybe Miami's offense could turn to him more often as the season progresses.
The aforementioned "rush" for Bell was an end-around play that he made the most of, assisted by solid blocking from both Kadyn Proctor and Will Kacmarek. As a receiver, Bell was targeted twice but did not record a single reception.
It feels like a combination of the Dolphins not utilizing him as much as they could, along with Bell being unable to create distance between himself and the defensive backs he's matched up against. It's a problem that reared its ugly head against Minnesota and continued into this game.
All in all, it's clear the Dolphins are looking elsewhere in terms of who they want Willis to throw to, and when Douglas is once again available, it wouldn't be shocking to see Bell's already small snap count be erased.
Things got scary for Brooks when he suffered a foot injury in the first half. He would return later on in the game and still come away with eight tackles, tied for the second-most in this game.
Aside from showing the toughness and grit that's to be expected from a veteran like Brooks, he made good on his responsibility to limit tight ends following what TJ Hockenson was able to do for the Vikings. Erick All Jr. was held to 25 yards on three targets. Mike Gesiscki scored a touchdown on Cincinnati's opening drive, but didn't record a single reception the rest of the way.
We have our first coach on one of these lists, and it's been a long time coming for special teams coordinator Chris Tabor. Between the punting, kicking, returning, and especially fielding, this has been a horrific start to the season for the Dolphins, and the blame needs to fall on someone.
Miami, which hasn't had a lead all season, was denied one out of the gate when the Dolphins gave up an 81-yard return on the opening kickoff. Not long after, one of their kickoffs missed the landing zone, which would have placed the ball on the 40-yard line if not for a Cincinnati personal foul that set them back 15 yards.
Riley Patterson cashed in on a 29-yard field goal, but missed an extra point following the final touchdown with a minute to go. It ultimately didn't mean anything because the Dolphins didn't recover the ensuing onside kick, but what if they had? Since he missed the PAT, seven points would have forced overtime instead of winning the game outright.
Bradley Pinion, at the least, had a decent game with a pair of 57- and 59-yard punts, but this was another overall messy performance by the special teams. Miami's offense and defense have enough on their plates to worry about without the special teams putting them in awful situations.
Miami's safety net in the offense, Gordon had another quality game with 88 yards on 18 carries and a touchdown in the first half. Thankfully, his visit to the blue medical tent was brief, and he immediately returned to the game.
The only "negative" you could say about Gordon was that his emotions spilled out on the sidelines, which was caught on video from multiple angles. It occurred following Miami's field goal in the third quarter, despite the offense having a first-and-goal on the 1-yard line.
But honestly, Miami's offense has played and looked so stale up to this point that the outburst from Gordon was genuinely a welcome sign. It shows he cares and wants to see the offense improve more than any other player or even coach for the Dolphins.

title: Five Instant Overreactions to Dolphins-Bengals Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins recorded their fifth straight loss to begin the Jeff Hafley era, as they fell to the Cincinnati Bengals by a score of 31-24. Let’s overreact to this game:
This is, without question, the worst special teams unit I have ever seen. Even their best play, a kickoff that landed the Bengals inside the 5-yard line, wasn’t even a smart kick by Riley Patterson, but rather a very poor one that would have been an out-of-bounds penalty if the returner simply placed one foot on the sideline as he caught it.
The opening kickoff return went 81 yards for the Bengals, setting them up for a quick touchdown. Later in the first half, they attempted a knuckling kick that wound up short of the landing zone, but only placed the Bengals at the 25-yard line because of a personal foul by Cincinnati. Riley Patterson also missed a PAT late.
Somehow, the Bengals found a way to match the Dolphins’ ineptitude multiple times, but it doesn’t excuse the fact that this unit has consistently failed to execute. Blown assignments have drawn the blame of the staff, but it’s worth estimating when this becomes a coaching problem. Either way, this needs to be addressed, because it’s bordering on embarrassing.
The Dolphins’ passing game is broken on every level right now. Their receivers don’t consistently create separation, their play-calling is stale and rarely uses all five eligibles, and Malik Willis just had his worst game of 2026.
The quickest way to fix this would be to simplify things for Willis. Less drawn-out play-action looks, and the understanding from the quarterback that if he doesn’t see anything on the front side, he can use his world-class speed to create something.
Miami has shown legitimate flashes on the ground, and if their passing game can take even a half-step up, they might be able to grab their first win. To achieve that, though, Caleb Douglas needs to come back, Bobby Slowik needs to find rhythm in his play-calling, and Willis’ decision-making needs an overhaul.
Joe Burrow dinked and dunked the Dolphins to death this week, finishing with 23 completions on 32 attempts for 190 yards and four touchdowns. Cincinnati was able to stay ahead of the sticks, primarily by attacking underneath, where they were left with little resistance.
Part of this is simply the Dolphins’ game plan. Their defensive backs play deep to limit explosives and keep possessions to a minimum. However, as their record shows, this may not be conducive to winning games.
It might be time to force the issue. The offense doesn’t have the level of ball control necessary to maximize the few possessions they get, and the defense has, at the very least, shown an ability to create turnovers. A more pressing defensive scheme may actually be more effective as Jeff Hafley searches for his first win.
The loss of De’Von Achane in Week 3 was seen as a death knell to an already struggling run game, but with Ollie Gordon leading the charge, they’ve been explosive over the last two weeks.
In Weeks 4 and 5, Gordon has accumulated 27 carries for 188 yards and two touchdowns. Credit is certainly in order for the offensive line, who have opened up holes consistently, but Gordon’s power and (perhaps more impressively) footwork at 6-2 and 226 pounds has been enough to take advantage of them.
Achane is, obviously, still the No. 1 back on this team when he returns next season, but the potential of spelling him with a skill set that foils his own is exciting. Gordon looks like a gem so far in year two.
As the Dolphins hope to remedy their aforementioned struggling passing game, one key should be third-year receiver Malik Washington, who has really impressed as of late. His start-and-stop ability makes him dangerous in the open field, where he has consistently made the first defender miss. That level of dynamism is seemingly unmatched among Miami’s weaponry.
Washington looks improved in the technical elements of his game. His route-running has looked refined this season, and he’s made a couple nice catches against tight coverage. The chemistry between he and Malik Willis is something the Dolphins should rely on more by getting him in space early and often.

title: Dolphins Week 5 Instant Takeaways: Miserable Day for Malik, Pass Defense
full_text:
A mere look at the final score might suggest some progress for the Miami Dolphins in their Week 5 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, but it actually was the opposite.
The Dolphins did set a new season high with their 24 points, almost doubling their previous high of 13, but the final score of 31-24 didn't do justice to what we saw at Hard Rock Stadium.
The biggest disappointment of all was the play of quarterback Malik Willis, who turned the ball over three times on a day when the margin for error against Joe Burrow and the Bengals.
Willis is in a tough spot with a young wide receiver corps that could be good in time but certainly isn't there yet and with consistent pressure, but it never justified all the miscues and it certainly wasn't the case on this day. And Willis repeated a mistake he had made earlier this season when on a second-and-goal from the 3 he took an unnecessary and ridiculous 8-yard sack when he rolled out of the pocket and just didn't chuck the ball out of bounds for an incompletion before he was taken down.
Pressure or not, regardless of wide receiver play, that's the kind of mistake that Willis has got to stop making.
The Dolphins don't have to make any determination about their quarterback situation until the next offseason, but all the folks calling for the team to spend their first-round pick on that position sure got some good arguments for their case on this day.
-- If we're discussing the wide receiver corps, it was great to see Chris Bell gain 26 yards on an end-around (props to good blocks by Aaron Brewer and Kadyn Proctor), but it's disappointing to not see him be more of a factor in the passing game. Bell still should become a productive NFL wide receiver, but he's not creating a ton of separation at this time.
-- And we've said it before and we'll say it again, Malik Washington easily is the best and most dependable wide receiver at this time, and it's not ideal when he's really like he should be a third wide receiver on a contending team.
-- For his troubles in the passing game, Willis showed again what he can do as a scrambler with 74 yards, including a long of 39. Willis has been reluctant to take off too early so far this season, but for the best results in 2026 maybe that's the way he needs to start operating.
-- Ollie Gordon II had another solid performance with 88 yards on 18 carries, and he's very obviously established himself as the top running back with De'Von Achane gone.
-- The kick coverage units set a bad tone with that long kickoff return allowed on the first play of the game, and this is where maybe the bottom of the roster needs to be churned some more if those players can't get the job done in the kicking game.
-- It didn't matter in the end, but at some point there'll need to be a conversation about Riley Patterson, who just can't be missing extra-point attempts.
-- Bradley Pinion, on the other hand, had a big game punting the ball and his floppy drop of the punt against San Francisco probably has been forgotten by now.
-- By yards alone, the defense did a good job of holding Cincinnati to only 307 total yards, but allowed a 9-for-13 third-down rate was a killer.
-- The pass defense didn't give up the big play, with one exception, but again gave up way too many easy completions underneath.
-- Even on that long touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Ja'Marr Chase, Jason Marshall Jr. had great coverage but Chase made a great catch on the 50-50 ball and was victimized by bad luck as the ball hit Chase's shoulder pad first but bounded softly enough to allow him to still make what became an incredible catch.
-- After being a factor against Minnesota, Chop Robinson again was a complete non-factor, though it's not like Burrow was holding the ball very long. And then there was that bad offside penalty in the fourth quarter.
-- Jacob Rodriguez again piled up the tackle numbers in this game, but the reality is this wasn't a great game for the rookie linebacker. He was beaten in coverage for Cincinnati's first two touchdowns, though he did take a really accurate throw by Burrow on the TD pass to Samaje Perine.
-- So now the Dolphins are 0-5 heading into their bye with the New York Jets next in Week 7, and if it wasn't early obvious, the wins are going to be difficult to come by.

title: Five Dolphins Players Who Have To Deliver in Week 5
full_text:
If the Miami Dolphins take down the Cincinnati Bengals, a lot would need to go their way, including a complete team effort from top to bottom.
The losses that the Dolphins have piled up are slowly improving in terms of the margin of victory for the opponent. They went from an undefeated Minnesota team to a 2-2 Bengals squad that was expected to compete for the AFC North but has had a rough start to the season.
Regardless of which side of the ball the Dolphins are on, there are a few players who need to step up for Miami. Some of them are still looking for a breakout performance, while others already have impressed this season, but Cincinnati will provide some of their most difficult matchups thus far.
After getting removed from the injury report Friday without a status designation, Wright needs to have a breakout game. Ollie Gordon II did well with 100 rushing yards and the team's lone touchdown against the Vikings, but Miami's offense regressed whenever Wright (Who started for this game) took the field, being shut down for 7 yards.
Wright has been thrust into a serious role in the run game and has underperformed. The Dolphins will have their hands full against a stout Cincinnati run defense. Gordon will give everything he has to move the ball, but he can't be the only running back contributing in this game.
So far, Brewer has played well enough to justify his three-year contract extension back in June. He hasn't given up a single sack and has only committed three penalties in 226 snaps. Against Minnesota, he was near-perfect with no QB hits, penalties, and only one pressure.
However, Brewer will be matched up against his toughest assignment so far — nose tackle Dexter Lawrence. Cincinnati acquired Lawrence from the New York Giants ahead of the 2026 NFL draft in exchange for their first-round pick, and he's helped turn their defense into a reliable unit, coordinated by former Miami Hurricanes head coach Al Golden.
Lawrence is having a great start to the season with 10 tackles, a team-leading three sacks, and five tackles for a loss. He and Cincinnati's front seven are doing a great job against the run, allowing just under 100 rushing yards per game (99.5), which doesn't bode well for a Miami offense that'll want to, once again, rely on the run game.
There's no secret when it comes to beating the Bengals since Joe Burrow was drafted in 2020: defenses need to apply pressure on the Pro Bowl quarterback. He's an excellent passer who will make opponents pay if they give him time in the pocket, having thrown for 1,171 yards and seven touchdowns through the air so far this season.
However, he's also been sacked nine times. Both Pittsburgh and Jacksonville applied heavy pressure on Burrow over the course of their contests in the past two weeks, sacking him twice in each game, and the Steelers and Jaguars came out on top.
It just so happens that Miami's pass rush is coming off its most successful game of the season against the Vikings, spearheaded by Sieler who registered two sacks on Kyler Murray. He'll need to bring the momentum of that game to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday.
Usually, Burrow has a plethora of talented wide receivers to throw to, but that might not be the case on Sunday as Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (groin/neck), and Colbie Young (knee) are questionable for this game.
After not having to deal with Justin Jefferson last week, the Dolphins could find themselves facing yet another battered and bruised receiver corps. However, their Achilles' heel against the Vikings was their inability to limit the tight end, TJ Hockenson, who put the offense on his back for 119 yards.
Brooks, who claimed responsibility for Miami's struggles against Hockenson, will need to do a better job maintaining Cincinnati's tight end and former member of the Dolphins, Mike Gesicki. If Chase, Higgins, or Young are out, that could mean an expanded role for Gesicki, who caught Cincinnati's only receiving touchdown of the game against Jacksonville.
Except for their two-score win over Houston, the Bengals have been in close games all season, defeating Tampa Bay by six points but losing to Pittsburgh and Jacksonville by three and five points, respectively.
This is to say that Cincinnati is no stranger to one-score games. The Dolphins could be in a position where they'll need to turn to Patterson to keep this game within reach, or maybe even take the lead. If that were to happen, Patterson better not miss.
Patterson has been perfect when it comes to mid-range kicks between 20 and 40 yards, but missed a 41-yard field goal against Las Vegas, then a 51-yarder against San Francisco. These are distances that are slowly becoming more automatic for the next generation of NFL kickers.
Granted, Patterson has been perfect in his last two games, but hasn't been tested at the aforementioned long-range distances. While almost no major media outlet is expecting a Dolphins upset, there are a fair share of predictions for a one-score win for the Bengals. In a situation like this, the difference between a win or loss could simply come down to a kick.

title: What the Vikings' Week 5 Win Changed About Their Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The Vikings are coming off their most complete game of the season and are now a perfect 5-0 as they head into their Week 6 bye . With the trade deadline less than a month away, the time off will provide the perfect opportunity to examine the needs of the roster.
And as one of the few remaining undefeated teams left, Minnesota will surely be buyers, right?
Despite the unblemished record, there are still plenty of skeptics downplaying the Vikings' perfect start. As of Tuesday afternoon, Minnesota was only tied for the ninth-best Super Bowl odds (+2000)—along with the Bears, Broncos and Patriots. And yet, it's hard to find a team playing better football than the Vikings right now.
Of course, the offense was quite literally the worst in the league early on, and the combined record of the opponents the Vikings have defeated is a lowly 8-17, so there's some fair criticism.
Still, barring another 2016 collapse, the Vikings are well on their way towards a playoff berth and could look to boost the roster via trade over the next few weeks.
After the bye, Minnesota will essentially be at full strength with the likely returns of Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw and T.J. Hockenson. Donovan Jackson is the only offensive starter already gone for the year, but finding a starting-caliber guard is typically easier said than done. Reserve lineman Joe Huber has filled in admirably and, given time, could be a solid replacement.
Beyond that, the Vikings don't seem keen on adding another running back unless it's to give him a week-long stay on the practice squad, and Gavin Bartholomew stepped up at tight end in the absence of Josh Oliver. The only logical move appearing to be gaining steam is dealing wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who has just two catches on the year. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported on Tuesday that he wouldn't be surprised if the buzz increases moving forward.
From @PatMcAfeeShow : In the wake of the Marvin Harrison Jr trade, another WR whose trade market is expected to heat up is #Vikings WR Jauan Jennings. Would a #49ers reunion make sense? pic.twitter.com/DR6mY1OvYb
What was supposed to be the big-ticket free-agent signing (you remember all the Golden State Warriors/Big 3 comparisons), Jennings has instead been a complete afterthought in the Vikings' offense. There are 11 other Vikings with more receiving yards than Jennings after Week 5, and right now he's getting paid a lot of money to just get in some cardio on Sundays.
While moving Jennings for a pick clearly doesn't help the 2026 Vikings, maybe it'll give them the capital to go out and get someone who does.
On defense, the Vikings have been the best unit in the league through five weeks and have very few weaknesses to exploit. One looming issue, however, may be their concerning depth. Minnesota has stayed healthy so far, but if injuries rear their ugly heads, there are a lot of question marks behind the starters.
Eight of the defensive starters have played 80% of the snaps so far (h/t ESPN 's Kevin Seifert), including several untested rookies who haven't needed to step up yet. Caleb Banks, Domonique Orange, Jake Golday and others have played just sparingly, and Minnesota may not be ready to give them the nod just yet.
It's certainly something to watch, and if a key starter goes down, the Vikings may look to add a veteran, especially if they continue their march toward a potential playoff run.
Despite their record suggesting the Vikings should be buyers at the deadline, they will likely sit tight. Injuries haven't ravaged them like certain teams, and general manager Nolan Teasley has seemed very intent on holding onto his 2027 draft picks.
Apologies to the fans hoping for a splash trade, but unless a big injury hits, Jennings might be the only player on the move.

title: The Biggest Decision Kevin O’Connell Got Right vs. Saints (And What It Means Moving Forward)
full_text:
The 5-0 Vikings have certainly been one of the more fascinating teams in the NFL in 2026.
The only other undefeated teams are the 49ers and Chiefs, both widely seen as serious contenders across the league. The Vikings, on the other hand, have raised more questions than answers for some. The squad clearly has a dominant defense and an elite special teams group, but the offense has taken time to find an identity.
Luckily, that seemed to shift against the Saints.
Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell is starting to embrace an offensive identity that often contradicts many of the core principles he had previously set in place, and it may just be the best way to let the offense thrive.
Kyler Murray looked good on Sunday , made even more impressive by the sheer amount of adversity the Vikings’ offense faced due to injuries. The offense took the field without wide receiver Jordan Addison, running back Jordan Mason, left tackle Christian Darrisaw and left guard Donovan Jackson, and they lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion on the team’s first drive. Not exactly ideal.
Luckily, Justin Jefferson was cleared to play after being labeled a game-time decision with an ankle injury.
Despite all of that adversity, the offense had its most complete day so far, and O’Connell deserves credit for trusting his QB to make it happen.
Murray delivered the ball effectively to ten different pass catchers in the afternoon. Unfortunately for an already frustrated Jauan Jennings, he was the only Viking targeted who didn't catch a pass. Murray, though, was precise, effective, and most importantly, played his game.
His 229 yards through the air and 51 on the ground didn’t fit the traditional O’Connell mold of deep shots and passes over the middle, but they led to an impressive 109.6 passer rating and an offense that flashed exciting potential (H/t: Bring Me the Sports ' Will Ragatz).
Lotta green dots for the Vikings' QB1, who understands the power of stacking completions. And this doesn't even show his 50 rushing yards. pic.twitter.com/UKs6mgKkIo
The Vikings’ passing game certainly didn't get off to a hot start this season. They lost Murray early in Week 1 to a concussion, opening the door for a three-TD day on only 133 yards from Carson Wentz after he was given incredible field position by his defense all game.
Murray returned in Week 3 against the Buccaneers but never quite found his footing. The film often looked awkward, with wide receivers’ breaks often coming after Murray’s internal timer had already sent him scrambling.
But Sunday showed the building blocks for something special, and I can’t overstate how impressive that is given the injury woes on that side of the ball. If the team comes out of the bye with a relatively clean bill of health, their Week 7 matchup against the Colts suddenly gives them a chance to put it all together against a defense that allows the fifth-most yards per game before entering a truly challenging November stretch .
This is where champions are forged. pic.twitter.com/ETt56Vk2fU
O’Connell is progressing and learning to lean into his offense's strengths. If he keeps growing, the sky is the limit for this Vikings squad in 2026.

title: Coller: Kyler Murray Showed Vikings His Full Potential in Win vs. Saints (Why That Matters & What's Next)
full_text:
Week 5 of the NFL was defined by madness, crazy finishes and unexpected results. There was a tie, an overtime blocked field goal and a nose tackle-long snapper situation. It was easy to overlook one Vikings player's performance that may impact the remainder of the season.
That would be quarterback Kyler Murray’s 24-for-30 passing day in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday .
Murray produced 224 passing yards and 51 rushing yards, as well as a breathtaking touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson (h/t NFL) and zero turnovers. Pro Football Focus graded him the sixth-best quarterback in Week 5 , and ESPN ’s QBR scored him as having the seventh-best performance.
OH MY JETTAS ✈️ @MINvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9JQWo9ugMo
While it’s easy to overlook Murray’s play because it came against the Saints, who entered having allowed the most points in the NFL and because the Vikings only put up 23 points (thanks to two red zone fumbles), there were things that happened in the game that showed the potential of what Murray can be in head coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense.
One reason to be excited for the Vikings' offensive outlook is Murray's connection with Jefferson.
All summer long, Murray and Jefferson connected in training camp on downfield passes. When the season arrived, Murray got hurt 11 plays into the opening game and then when he came back, Jefferson got hurt on the first drive. In their first game together, Murray found him six times on seven targets for 79 yards.
As a reminder, every quarterback who has ever directed passes in Jefferson’s direction except J.J. McCarthy has had immense success. Here are the passer ratings when targeting Jefferson from 2020 to 2024 (per PFF ):
Murray hasn’t had a connection like that since he played with DeAndre Hopkins early in his career. Maybe you noticed the Cardinals just traded Marvin Harrison Jr. —their supposed “generational” receiver—to the Texans over the weekend.
The other thing Murray has thrived on during his career is finding the tight end. Over the last two weeks, he has comfortably done so. Against the Dolphins, he went 13-for-13 throwing to T.J. Hockenson and when Hockenson got injured early against the Saints, he continued to work the ball to backup TE Gavin Bartholomew, who had five receptions in the game.
It seems Murray and O’Connell are on the same page with quick passing, as Murray completed 11-of-11 throws between zero and nine yards from the line of scrimmage. In previous years, he’s been one of the most accurate QBs in the NFL on short passes, completing 82.8% in 2024. He’s currently the NFL leader at 90% on quick throws.
That’s the sign that it’s working. But the sign that Murray is really getting into a groove is his playmaking confidence outside of the structure of the play.
Murray's scrambling was a throwback to previous years when he was considered one of the most difficult quarterbacks to capture in the NFL.
He converted third downs by either taking advantage of deep coverage or blowing past pass rushers who were trying to track him down. His most impressive play was an instant escape act with star rusher Chase Young in his grill. He spun backward, rolled out and found running back DeeJay Dallas for a third-and-11 conversion. It was a Heisman Murray play.
Combining that type of QB performance with a running game that’s been successful despite missing Jordan Mason for four weeks , the No. 1 defense and No. 1 special teams unit in the NFL could give the Vikings a chance to seriously contend in the NFC, especially with only one other team standing out above the rest thus far (49ers).
As the Vikings go into the difficult part of their schedule after the bye week, when they face the Lions, Bills, 49ers and Packers, they will need one thing that has eluded Murray throughout his career: Consistency.
In 2024, Murray led the Cardinals to a 6-4 record and had a 100.8 passer rating, only for them to win only two games the rest of the season as Murray struggled. In 2021, Arizona opened with seven straight wins before finishing with only 11 and a first-round exit from the playoffs.
The season is still young, so we can’t turn one strong showing into evidence that the Vikings will be holding the Lombardi Trophy at the end of the year. However, we can say that the model for them winning games is clear, and it’s going to take high efficiency, protecting the football and playmaking from Murray.
For the first time vs. New Orleans, Vikings fans saw all of that come together.

title: 3 Most Likely Jauan Jennings Trade Destinations as Vikings Rumors 'Heat Up'
full_text:
It's far from an overreaction to say that Jauan Jennings's brief time with the Minnesota Vikings should be classified as a colossal disappointment .
Brought in to be the No. 3 wide receiver behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, Jennings hasn't come close to looking the part, entering the Vikings' bye week with more games played (four) than catches (two), along with only nine receiving yards and a career-worst 40.2 offensive grade on Pro Football Focus .
For what it's worth, that's the second-worst grade among 179 WRs this season. It's safe to say both Jennings and the Vikings could use a fresh start, which seems to be a growing possibility if the latest buzz is any indication.
Appearing on Tuesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show," NFL insider Ian Rapoport said that he expects discussions around a potential Jennings trade to heat up a little bit over the next, probably, couple of days and weeks ."
From @PatMcAfeeShow : In the wake of the Marvin Harrison Jr trade, another WR whose trade market is expected to heat up is #Vikings WR Jauan Jennings. Would a #49ers reunion make sense? pic.twitter.com/DR6mY1OvYb
Jennings is on a one-year contract, making it easy for the Vikings to hit the reset button if they're looking for a trade. A deal would save the Vikings $5.03 million in cap space while creating just over $4.5 million in dead money, according to Spotrac , which comes off the books once the 2026 season ends.
Despite the slow start to the year, Jennings's name still has value, making him an attractive rental option for any WR-needy teams. With that in mind, here are the three most likely trade destinations for the Vikings' offseason addition.
Sometimes, what's old becomes new again. Like Rapoport pointed out, the 49ers make too much sense as a potential trade destination to ignore.
Drafted 217th overall by the Niners in 2020, Jennings spent his NFL career in the Bay Area before moving to Minnesota . The former Tennessee Volunteer was solid but didn't blow anyone away early on in his San Francisco run. However, that changed in Years 4 and 5. Jennings amassed 1,618 receiving yards and 15 TDs on 132 receptions between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, which is the type of player the Vikings thought they were getting.
Sometimes fresh starters don't work out, though, and a return home might benefit not only Jennings, but the 49ers, too. After all, San Francisco currently has several wideouts—De'Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Ricky Pearsall, and Christian Kirk—on injured reserve, and now Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury . That's without mentioning the Brandon Aiyuk situation .
The 49ers need receiver help, so who better than a familiar face like Jennings? Doing business with a fellow undefeated NFC team might not seem ideal, but if the Niners' desperation helps the Vikings in the long run, there's good reason to do business.
Speaking of undefeated squads, the Chiefs are another team that likely wouldn't mind some WR help.
Entering Week 6, tight end Travis Kelce is the only Kansas City pass-catcher on pace to hit the 1,000-yard mark this season. Even though the Chiefs are undefeated, Patrick Mahomes clearly needs another weapon, especially as top WRs Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy are both averaging career lows in receiving yards per game at 47.5 and 33.3, respectively.
Adding Jennings to the mix would be a huge gain for Mahomes, especially if the current Vikings wideout is motivated by a fresh start. Knowing the Chiefs previously coveted him could also boost Jennings's confidence, as ESPN's Adam Schefter reported in May that the AFC West leaders were interested in signing him before the Vikings won the sweepstakes.
With their WR depth clearly a concern, don't be surprised if the Chiefs are among the first in line to make an offer for Jennings.
Sticking with the AFC, the Dolphins might be Jennings's best path to turning his season around and potentially securing a significant payday in March.
The Dolphins might not have Super Bowl aspirations like the Chiefs or 49ers, but they offer an opportunity to be the big fish in a small pond. Miami's wide receiver situation starts and ends with Malik Washington and rookie WR Caleb Douglas, who hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle injury .
With every other Dolphins pass-catcher averaging 25.4 or fewer receiving yards per game, it's easy to see why a proven veteran like Jennings would be attractive. At the same time, a trip to South Beach could benefit Jennings, who'd easily be in contention for Malik Willis's busiest weapon. Thriving in the role would boost his value heading into free agency, where the Dolphins will have over $110 million to spend —the third-most room in the NFL, according to Spotrac .
On top of that, he'd be reunited with Dolphins offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, who was the 49ers' offensive pass game specialist (2021) and offensive passing game coordinator (2022) during Jennings's first two pro seasons. It's been a while since they worked together, but that doesn't mean they can't rekindle some magic.

title: Vikings Verdict: Judging Super Bowl Hopes, Jauan Jennings  & Other Overreactions to Begin Bye Week
full_text:
The Vikings are undefeated as their bye week arrives , despite taking the path less traveled. They've won ugly, but the Purple and Gold have found a way to pull out a win each time thus far, resulting in first-place status in the NFC North to begin Week 6.
Now, with some time to sit with their thoughts, how will the Vikings proceed moving forward?
Is the Super Bowl actually on the table? Should general manager Nolan Teasley trade his disappointing free agent?
Let's judge some potential Vikings overreactions after the Week 5 win.
At 5-0, it's natural to start to look ahead to the playoffs, but the Vikings are also one of the more unusual undefeated teams in recent memory. Powered by a suffocating defense, an elite special teams unit and an offense that may have started to figure things out, not many NFL teams would want to see Minnesota on the schedule.
Wins all count the same, of course, but the Vikings' previous opponents have a combined record of just 8-17. Meanwhile, the final 12 games feature just four opponents with losing records, putting their unblemished win/loss column to the test.
If the Vikings offense has truly turned a corner, then there's no reason Minnesota shouldn't be in the conversation at the end of the season. The "49" in 49ers may as well stand for the number of injuries they've faced this season, and as another 5-0 squad, they could be a threat to the NFC crown if they can get healthy.
If the Vikings' offense sputters again and the defense slips even slightly, though, this could easily become a .500 team. Still, barring an epic collapse, the Vikings will almost surely make the playoffs, and a one- or two-seed would go a long way towards a potential run.
The Vikings are arguably peaking and now have to sit for the next two weeks thanks to an early bye. While the bye week will help to get some key players back —like Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw and more—an argument could be made that Minnesota would have rather suited up in Week 6 to keep this thing rolling.
Kyler Murray has completed 83% of his last 43 passes and put together his best game as a Viking in Week 5 against the Saints. Getting healthy will be an important step toward the ultimate goal, but for anybody out there who believes in momentum, this bye week couldn't have come at a worse time. Ultimately, it probably won't affect the budding offense too much.
There are 11 other Vikings with more receiving yards than Jauan Jennings this year, and the question on everyone's mind is, " Should the Vikings trade him ?"
A coveted free agent, Jennings has not found a home on the Minnesota offense, notching two catches for nine yards. Head coach Kevin O'Connell has been asked multiple times (h/t VikingzFanPage) about Jennings's lack of production and has quickly pointed out his contributions in the run game.
Fair, I suppose, but he wasn't brought in just to run-block a few snaps a game; the Vikings either need to find some ways to get Jennings involved in the passing game or cut this experiment short. His trade market would surely be robust despite the slow start to 2026, and the Vikings may admit defeat if things don't change ahead of the deadline.
In the Week 5 win, Vikings rookies played just 42 combined offensive and defensive snaps, including 20 from fullback Max Bredeson. Sunday wasn't much different from the rest of the year either, as the rookies have been used sparingly so far in 2026.
The good news, though, is that the Vikings are winning without any significant contributions from their rookie class . So does it matter?
Ideally, getting solid production from at least a few rookies would be some assurance that things are set up for the future. Instead, 2027 might reveal how good (or bad) this class could be. With established starters at many of the positions like linebacker, edge or cornerback, it's not terribly surprising the rookies haven't gotten much of a look.
Not to mention, first-round pick Caleb Banks was always going to be a project .
Still, is there maybe a little too much up in the air after five games?

title: One Offseason Decision Is Already Haunting Vikings as Bye Week Arrives
full_text:
Week 6 is here, which means it's already time for the Vikings to take some time to reflect as their bye arrives. Minnesota is five games into the season now, meaning there's a large enough sample size to dissect this year's offseason decisions, especially those aging like warm milk.
When the Vikings signed former 49ers wide receiver Jauan Jennings to a one-year, $8 million deal in May, it looked like an impactful move that would take the team's passing offense to the next level.
Jennings was a touchdown machine for the 49ers in 2025, finding the end zone nine times on 55 catches in 15 games. In fact, 10.5% of his catches while with the Niners resulted in a TD. Vikings fans loved the idea of having a proven red-zone target to take pressure off Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
Instead, there has been very little return on Minnesota's investment. Jennings has played four of the Vikings' first five games, catching two passes for nine yards on five targets while playing 201 offensive snaps, continuously proving to be the Purple and Gold's worst offseason decision.
So far, Jennings has been outplayed by multiple Vikings receivers below him on the depth chart. Tai Felton, Jeshaun Jones and Myles Price all have more receiving yards than he does and have played significantly fewer snaps. That's without mentioning Jennings is on track for career-worst performances (h/t Pro Football Focus ) when it comes to:
Yards after catch per reception
Passer rating when targeted
Jennings' struggles look even worse given that injuries have also run rampant through the Vikings' locker room.
Addison missed the team's Week 5 game, and Jefferson left Week 3's contest with an ankle injury. Still, Jennings was unable to step up when the team needed him.
Minnesota is already panicking about the situation, activating Jones when he returned from his suspension and signing veteran free-agent wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to try to find more production.
The Vikings aren't done there.
On Monday, the team worked out a few more free-agent wide receivers , according to KPRC 2 Houston's Aaron Wilson. JuJu Smith-Schuster is the most notable name on the list, but D’Wayne Eskridge and Dayton Wade were also in attendance.
It is sad that the Vikings are resorting to free agency since they aren't getting production from Jennings. The investment the team made in him feels like a total misuse of salary cap space, a poor use of offensive snaps and a roster spot that could go to a player who could contribute more.
Minnesota could be more patient with Jennings' offensive struggles if he were making an impact in other ways. However, the 29-year-old wide receiver does not play on special teams and has been a non-factor in the Vikings' struggling offense. If general manager Nolan Teasley wants a fresh start, a trade would create just over $5 million in cap savings while bringing on $4.5 million in dead money, per Spotrac .
For now, the Vikings must feel haunted by the decision to sign Jennings even though it made total sense at the time. There is a chance that he can turn things around after Minnesota's bye week, but unless that happens, Teasley must be wondering how he could have used the salary cap space and the roster spot better during the 2026 NFL season.

title: Vikings' Snap Count vs. Saints: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 5
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings defeated the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season despite injuries piling up for the Purple and Gold and some important mistakes being made on the field.
The 23-13 victory keeps the Vikings undefeated heading into their bye week at a time when the rest should help multiple key players get healthy in time for the next game in two weeks against the Indianapolis Colts.
One key reason that Minnesota was able to keep its winning ways alive was how head coach Kevin O'Connell used the players he had available and how those players were able to contribute to Sunday's contest.
Here are five observations from the Vikings' snap counts against the Saints.
Starting tight end T.J. Hockenson was coming off a huge game against the Miami Dolphins where he caught 13 passes for 119 yards. Sadly, he only played two snaps before having to leave the game with a concussion.
Gavin Bartholomew stepped into his role and played 44 offensive snaps along with eight special teams snaps. He finished second on the team in receptions (5) and receiving yards (33) while earning a 71.3 Pro Football Focus grade for the game.
Typically, it is a great thing if a player is on the field for every possible snap. Even though Josh Metellus was one of only two players who were in the game for all 45 defensive snaps, he struggled mightily against New Orleans.
Metellus had the lowest PFF grade of all Minnesota defenders on Sunday (46.7). The problem is that the Vikings are trying to limit Harrison Smith's snaps but still maximize his efficiency. Meanwhile, Theo Jackson is getting 31 defensive snaps, and Jacob Thomas only got three.
Blake Cashman was the other defensive player to participate in all 45 defensive snaps. He turned that into a team-high nine tackles, one for a loss, and one quarterback hit, on his way to a 79.2 PFF grade for the game.
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores can't afford to take Cashman off the field this season. He is a stabilizing presence in the middle of the defense and deserves to play every possible snap if he is able to.
Jauan Jennings played 49 offensive snaps against the Saints. He was held without a catch and was only targeted once in the game. There is absolutely no chance that giving him that many reps is the most efficient thing for the offense.
He was outplayed by Jeshaun Jones and Tai Felton, both of whom had fewer offensive opportunities. After the bye, it wouldn't be shocking if Jones starts cutting into Jennings' snaps more significantly to get more value out of the routes.
When Hockenson left the game and didn't return, Bartholomew stepped into the receiving role at tight end, and Yurosek became the blocker. However, he showed that he could do a lot more than just block because he caught a pass on Sunday.
Yurosek can block to keep offensive tackle Caleb Tiernan from trying to do what Josh Oliver was doing before his season-ending injury. The fact that he was on the field for 39 offensive snaps and 14 special teams snaps shows how much the coaching staff believes in him.

title: Vikings Stock Report: Who's Rising (and Falling) After Impressive Week 5 Win
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings enter the bye at 5-0 after a dominating showing against the New Orleans Saints, and now have a week to get healthy before taking on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7.
The Vikings' offense has finally started to inch closer to the defense after several weeks of mediocrity, and Minnesota is playing some of the best complementary football in the league. But while some players are on the rise, not everyone is pulling their weight through the perfect start.
So who is seeing their stock soar, and who is seeing their's tank in this week's stock report?
Murray's ascension continued again this week , culminating in his best performance to date with 283 total yards and a score. It's hard to imagine that it was just a few weeks ago that some fans were calling for Carson Wentz to start, but now Murray has this offense rolling. Plus, all it took was the low, low price of four weeks of absolute misery to get there.
He's 36-for-43 since the fourth quarter of the Miami Dolphins game, and the now-functional offense will be getting much healthier after the break, too. Have the Vikings found their quarterback for 2027 and beyond?
It was hard to find many weak spots in the Vikings' dominant win, but after another goose egg from Jennings, it's getting harder and harder to see what his future in Minnesota is. With just two catches on the season despite injuries to Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, Jennings is starting to look like a very expensive WR3 who doesn't add any value on special teams.
Now, that's not to say a trade is imminent, and the Vikings still seem to value his run-blocking. But Jennings is giving other pass catchers, including Odell Beckham Jr., every opportunity to steal his job. Maybe a week off will give the coaches some time to evaluate his role in the offense.
After losing T.J. Hockenson on the second play of the game, Bartholomew stepped up, notching five catches for 33 yards. He was inches shy of reeling in a long touchdown from Murray as well and finished second in receptions and yards, behind only Jefferson.
Bartholomew had some training camp hype, but had to wait his turn behind Hockenson and Josh Oliver. With both out on Sunday, he certainly made the most of his opportunity. While Hockenson will regain his starting status upon his return, Minnesota may look to work Bartholomew in more and more after proving he can handle the load.
Dallas saw just five offensive snaps in a game where Aaron Jones once again carried the load. Dallas' value has primarily been on special teams, but with Jordan Mason set to return after the bye, the Vikings likely won't keep four backs. Keeping a 27-year-old running back who doesn't contribute on offense is a tough sell to Vikings GM Nolan Teasley.
If Demond Claiborne remains a part of the Vikings' future plans, Dallas will surely be the odd man out. If he is released, he'll finish his time with Minnesota with three carries for 10 yards, four catches, and one incredible kick return block.
After a relatively quiet season, Murphy came alive against New Orleans with two interceptions. He was the highest-graded Viking in the win, notching an 86.7 overall grade from Pro Football Focus . With his productive day, Murphy is now tied for the league lead in picks.
The Vikings held Tyler Shough to just 96 passing yards and allowed 85 to Malik Willis the week prior. While Murphy and the secondary have allowed their fair share of big plays, they've remained a steady and redemptive bunch.

title: Harmon's Longship Week 5: Key Takeaways as Vikings Sail South to Defeat Saints for a 5-0 Start
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are docking their ships and returning to shore for a bye-week rest after a decisive 23-13 victory against the struggling New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome. While the scoreboard shows a ten-point game, it never felt that close.
The day's most encouraging moments came from the passing game and quarterback Kyler Murray, who's been fighting desperately to prove he fits in this offense. Here’s how the Vikings got it done in New Orleans and what it means for their pursuit of the ultimate prize.
Sunday’s game proved that Kyler Murray could and should thrive in Minnesota, even with five key offensive starters out with injury. Murray was decisive, patient, and strategic all afternoon. While all-22 footage from his first full game in Tampa Bay showed an internal clock that would send him scrambling before his receivers broke open, yesterday showcased a level of trust and patience in his weapons and line that we had yet to see.
Murray used his legs effectively to gain 51 yards on 10 scrambles, but on multiple plays, a conscious decision to stay in the pocket was evident. Good news: it worked.
Murray ended the best day of his short Viking tenure, completing 24-of-30 for 229 yards and a touchdown through the air. It's even more impressive considering the team lost T.J. Hockenson early after Jordan Addison was ruled out pregame. His gutsy, precise throw to Justin Jefferson over three defenders in the back of the end zone was a jaw-dropper, allowing the Louisiana native receiver to hit 'The Griddy' in front of his hometown crowd (h/t Vikings).
Speechless. @k1 @JJettas2 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/FOHP5Fh7oG
Murray still has room to grow, and head coach Kevin O’Connell still has much to learn about scheming for his specific skill set. But Sunday's passing performance is a reason for optimism, especially since Murray and his weapons have played 18 snaps together this season due to injury, per my count.
Brian Flores and his defense had another stellar day despite totaling only one sack. Saints QB Tyler Shough never caught his breath, as Flores’ unit attacked him all afternoon. At one point near the halfway mark, the Vikings blitzed on an astounding 90.9% of snaps per the FOX broadcast. Minnesota’s defensive backs also had a big day, with Byron Murphy Jr. coming away with two interceptions. Shough, who entered the game with the third-most passing yards in the league, was held to just 96 passing yards and no TDs. The Vikings defense just finds ways to dominate, even when they’re not stacking sacks.
Then there’s Will Reichard, who needs no introduction at this point. The Vikings’ elite kicker went a perfect 3-of-3 on field goals and 2-of-2 on extra points. Even with a positive day from the offense, Reichard’s 53 total points this season are higher than the offense's 50 total points through five weeks (h/t VikingzFanPage). Reichard is also on pace for the second-most points scored by a single player in a season (180). This would fall just six points shy of LaDainian Tomlinson’s 2006 record. His 34 straight field goals dating back to last season are only 10 shy of the NFL record set by Adam Vinatieri in 2016.
#Vikings K Will Reichard has more points (53) than the Vikings offense (50) this season. (Via @JasonHarmonNFL ) pic.twitter.com/Z8HzjBQ63l
The biggest takeaway from yesterday’s game is simple: let Kyler cook. When O’Connell leans into Murray’s skill set and doesn’t try to mold him into Sam Darnold, good things happen. While Murray's passing chart (h/t Will Ragatz) may have given 2024 KOC a jump scare, it's leading to winning football. Avoiding turnovers and dominating time of possession are the best ways to take advantage of the team’s stellar defense, and Murray looks poised to do just that.
If O’Connell can limit the procedural penalties and poorly timed trick-play calls, this offense could do exactly what it needs to for the Vikings to contend… especially once they’re back at full health.
I can’t believe I’m saying this, but thank goodness the Green Bay Packers won yesterday. The Pack’s 31-7 victory over the Tyson Bagent/Case Keenum-led Bears widened Minnesota’s division lead. Detroit, Chicago, and Green Bay are now 3-2, while Minnesota holds a comfortable 5-0 record, including 2-0 in divisional games. The Vikings can build an even larger division lead if they defeat the Lions in Week 8.
The rest of the NFC looks wide open, with San Francisco looking like the Vikings’ biggest threat in the conference. The two teams will meet in Mexico City on November 22 in what could be the game of the year. At this point in the season, I’m feeling confident that the eventual NFC champion will come from the NFC North or West.
I can’t wait for November 22. pic.twitter.com/GsEBzHXm6v
The Vikings now enter the bye week in desperate need of recovery. While I typically dislike an early bye, Minnesota’s list of injuries on offense is too long to be sustainable. O’Connell hopes to have Christian Darrisaw, T.J. Hockenson, Jordan Addison, and Jordan Mason all back as the Vikings host the Colts after the bye , per Will Ragatz.
Listening to Kevin O’Connell, it sounds like Jordan Addison, Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw, and T.J. Hockenson all have a realistic shot to return after the Vikings' bye.
The reinforcements would be crucial for an offense that will face a much harder schedule starting in November. For now, the Vikings rest, and fans can celebrate a hard-fought and often ugly 5-0 start.

title: 3 Studs & 3 Duds From Vikings' Week 5 Win Against the Saints
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings got the job done on the road against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5. With the 23-13 win , the Purple and Gold remain undefeated heading into the team's much-needed bye week.
This was not an easy game for the Vikings. Two turnovers kept the Saints within striking distance for most of the game, but Minnesota's defense and solid special teams performance kept the door closed on any hope for New Orleans to escape with a win.
Needless to say, several great performances from multiple players helped Minnesota stay undefeated on Sunday afternoon. Here are the studs and duds from Minnesota's Week 5 contest against the Saints.
The Vikings had two interceptions against Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, and both of them were hauled in by veteran cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. Minnesota needed those takeaways after losing two fumbles of their own in this game.
Murphy added three tackles, including one for a loss. His awareness and ability to track the ball in the air were major factors in determining Sunday's game, considering Shough was held to under 100 passing yards for the first time this season.
Aaron Jones Sr. had a good day, rushing 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. He also added three receptions for four yards. However, Jones' second-half fumble inside the red zone led to New Orleans' only offensive touchdown of the day.
That said, Jones shouldn't be the only running back carrying the workload. At the same time, DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne didn't have a single carry against the Saints and combined for two catches for 17 yards, while the veteran Jones had to do all the work on the ground.
For a player who was questionable on the injury report, Jefferson looked ready to go against the Saints. The superstar wide receiver was targeted seven times by Kyler Murray and caught six of those for 79 yards and a touchdown.
OH MY JETTAS ✈️ @MINvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9JQWo9ugMo
Seeing Minnesota get into the end zone on Sunday was a thing of beauty, especially with how much the Vikings have struggled offensively lately. Seeing Murray trust Jefferson in a crowd of New Orleans defenders in the back corner of the end zone was both surprising and welcome.
Another week, another dud from Jennings. At this point, it is hard to know what is holding the former 49ers receiver back from contributing in Minnesota. Also, Jennings is being outplayed by Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones, which is not good.
Jennings was the only Vikings player to be targeted by Murray and not catch a pass. He now has two catches on four targets for nine yards this season, which likely has general manager Nolan Teasley wondering why he signed the free-agent pass catcher in the first place.
If the season ended today, kicker Will Reichard would be the team's MVP. He remained perfect this season, connecting on two extra points and three field goals on Sunday, including a great kick from 55 yards out as the clock expired at the end of the first half.
The FOX broadcast said that Reichard has made 57 consecutive kicks, including field goals and extra points. Vikings fans should be extremely happy to hear that, but longtime fans might also feel uneasy hearing that statistic.

title: Could Elijah Ponder, Gabe Jacas be the Patriots Defensive Ends of the Future?
full_text:
One of the offseason needs identified most commonly by analysts for the New England Patriots was their lack of talent and development at edge rusher.
However, through five games this season, the personnel the Patriots are putting out on Sundays have shown that defensive ends may not be as big of a need as people thought.
Elijah Ponder, a second-year undrafted free agent from California Polytechnic, had arguably the most impactful performance on the defensive side of the ball on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. He got to the quarterback, sacking him two separate times and forced a fumble. He was PFF’s highest rated pass rusher from Week 5, notching a 92.2 grade.
It’s not just this small sample size that Ponder’s proven his legitimacy in. His pair of sacks brings his season total to 4.5 on the season, leading the team. He also has a team-high four QB knockdowns and he's tied for fourth on the team with total tackles (though he has the most tackles of all non-defensive backs and non-middle linebackers).
Across Ponder’s 15 games last season, he recorded 4 sacks. His emergence as the Patriots' best backfield havoc reaper will be a part of opponents’ game plan moving forward.
On the other side of the line of scrimmage from Ponder is Dre’Mont Jones. An offseason addition, the Patriots brought in Jones on a three-year, $36.5 million contract. Thus far, Jones’ impact has been minimal, recording just two solo tackles and one sack in the four games he’s appeared in.
Thankfully, another offseason addition for the Patriots has put in the work on the defensive front. The 55th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , Gabe Jacas, has been stellar at defensive edge. Using their second pick, the Patriots picked Jacas out of Illinois and, so far, he has not disappointed.
Jacas has already recorded 1.5 sacks, 17 total tackles, and had an interception in Week 2’s victory against Pittsburgh. In Week 4 against Buffalo, a fifth of Jacas’s pass rushes resulted in quarterback pressures (three of his 14 snaps). He also ranked fifth highest across the league that week in pass rush win rate.
In Sunday's dominant win over the Raiders , Ponder and Jacas combined for nine QB Pressures, according to Pro Football Focus. The two also had a total of eight combined tackles, and each had a 26.1% pass rush win rate.
Of all edge rushers who have been in the league for two seasons or less, Ponder ranks second in the NFL for total pressures with 18 and Jacas is fourth — in just five games, with 14 pressures.
Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas are DUDES pic.twitter.com/Hbj8saXg75
The pairs’ performances have provided relief to a Patriots front office, which has been desperate for elite edge play for years. Ponder and (24) and Jacas (22) may just have what it takes to grow into elite defenders and help the Patriots continue to win games on the defensive side of the ball.

title: Patriots TE Hunter Henry, IJM Host Annual 'Freedom to Play' Ping Pong Tournament
Has Patriots WR Efton Chism III Earned More Playing Time?
full_text:
Behind four Drake Maye passing touchdowns on Sunday, the New England Patriots receiving arsenal proved they were ready to step-up to the challenge of a dwindled personnel group. Of the players asked to compete more than they usually would, none has stood out more than Efton Chism III.
A week ago in Buffalo, where the second-year undrafted free agent was asked to rise to the challenge of replacing Mack Hollins — who went down in the second half with a calf injury — Chism came up with two clutch receptions on the Patriots game-winning drive .
One for a first down, where Chism elevated vertically to haul in Maye’s pass, and the other for the game-winning touchdown on a thrilling 23-yard one-handed grab.
We can't stop thinking about the @EftonChism catch 😌 pic.twitter.com/Mj1gLu1DVU
With the Pats only suiting up four receivers in Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Chism naturally saw the most reps of his career in an NFL game, recording 57 offensive snaps. This was the second highest on the team , trailing only Romeo Doubs.
One of Chism’s more impressive plays came on a catch-and-lateral to TreyVeyon Henderson for a big third-down conversion.
Heads up backwards pass by Efton Chism III to help the Patriots get the 1st down pic.twitter.com/oN70ccHwNV
Chism recorded five receptions and 57 yards during his action-packed day against the Raiders. Both stat lines are the Eastern Washington alum’s NFL best.
On Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel teased the possibility of WR AJ Brown suiting up in Week 6’s game against the New York Jets. Brown, who went down with a high-ankle sprain in the season opener against Seattle, is currently on injured reserve, but eligible to be removed from the list this week.
If Brown does return for the Patriots this week, there is a possibility that Chism reverts back to his previous role in the receiver room, as the fifth or sixth option for Maye. In the first three weeks of the season, Chism only played 26 offensive snaps — which is 22% of his season-total 117 snaps.
However, with Chism’s proven impact on a heavier snap count, there is a likely chance that the 24-year-old earned a useful role among the receivers and will see the field almost as often as he did in the past two weeks.
While Chism’s frame and ability is quite different than that of Brown and Hollins , who are utilized most effectively when lining up as the split receiver, Chism could take the place of Patriots’ fourth-year receiver DeMario “Pop” Douglas.
Douglas recorded a 34-yard touchdown – his first of the season – in Sunday’s 45-17 victory against the Raiders, where he elevated past the defense in a busted coverage into a wide-open end zone. Despite receiving a 53% share of offensive snaps this season, Pop has caught just 13 passes for 147 yards.
The slot receiver played 20 less snaps than his positional counterpart Chism on Sunday, indicating that offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels may have a new favorite slot receiver.
This isn’t a suggestion that the Patriots will do-away with Douglas, who’s an unrestricted free agent in the 2027 offseason. Chism and Douglas are used simultaneously in multiple packages where the offense spreads out and an extra receiver is on the field.
But with Chism’s efficiency thus far, his added usage – even in a healthy receiver room, may lead to less snaps from players like Douglas or second-year receiver, Kyle Williams.
Detailing the impact of the receiver depth, Vrabel said after the game, “They're all ready to go. They all play different positions. That's not easy, you know, to learn three different positions and be able to step in there and block and make plays.”

title: Patriots Lose RB TreVeyon Henderson for Multiple Weeks With Ankle Injury
full_text:
It was announced Tuesday morning by ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson has been diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, following Sunday’s 45-17 victory of the Las Vegas Raiders , and will miss multiple weeks of action.
Henderson, who rushed four times for 22 yards and was the beneficiary of a 16-yard lateral reception from Efton Chism on Sunday, was removed from the game in the second quarter after being rolled up on by Raiders safety Jeremey Chinn during an 11-yard rush down the left sideline.
Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain during Sunday’s win over the Raiders that now is expected to sideline him multiple weeks, per league sources. Henderson will not need surgery, and he is regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return… pic.twitter.com/MKDzQG9PZa
The running back is not expected to have surgery on his right ankle.
Henderson missed Week 1’s action against the Seattle Seahawks with an ankle injury suffered during Patriots training camp. Both ankle injuries sustained this season were to his right ankle.
Henderson was a second-round pick for the Pats in the 2025 draft out of Ohio State. In his rookie season, Henderson was the Patriots’ leading rusher, recording 911 yards and 9 touchdowns. In four games of play (including the two quarters of action in Sunday’s game), Henderson has 163 yards and one score.
Patriots running back depth chart without TreVeyon Henderson: - Rhamondre Stevenson - Corey Kiner - Lan Larison (PS) https://t.co/SXPa9JddWe
Now, the Patriots running back room is shortened to veteran rusher Rhamondre Stevenson and second-year player Corey Kiner, who recorded a fumble on Sunday while stepping in for Henderson. The Patriots practice squad includes Lan Larison, in his second-year with the Patriots after going undrafted in 2025.
The injuries for the Patriots have been a defining factor of their team identity this season, often relying on depth pieces to fill in the role for injured stars. Star wide receiver AJ Brown went down Week 1 against the Seahawks with a high-ankle sprain , and the injuries have continued to accumulate since.
The Patriots already have one running back listed on injured reserve with Myles Montgomery who suffered an undisclosed injury in training camp.
The team has lost 19 players to reserve rosters this season, with 13 actively on the injured reserve. It remains to be seen if Henderson’s injury will land him on the IR – which would mean he’d miss a minimum of four games.
The Patriots also lost starting left tackle Will Campbell on Sunday, who was diagnosed with a knee sprain and may miss several weeks.
With Henderson going down, New England will rely on Stevenson, in his sixth year with the team.
Mike Vrabel said about Stevenson: “We'll need Mondre's ability to create plays out in space and catch the ball," also saying how "it was good to see him fight to get back out there, being limited during the week.”
Stevenson was questionable to play in Sunday’s game with a knee injury , but collected 53 snaps where he rushed for 64 yards and hauled in three passes for 21 yards. Stevenson scored one of the Patriots six touchdowns on a 5-yard carry in the first quarter.

title: Patriots Week 5 Snap Count Analysis: WRs Step Up Into Larger Roles
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots were banged up on both sides of the ball in Week 5. And yet, they were able to muscle their way to a 45-17 blowout of the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday .
"I mean, there's a lot to improve on. There's a lot to work on," Mike Vrabel said postgame. "The penalties are ridiculous, so, you know, we'll have to focus on that and figure out things that we can improve on, which there'll be a lot of."
Here's a look at all three phases of the game, and how many snaps each player got during the Patriots' second-straight win (and third overall win of the season).
OG Alijah Vera-Tucker (75, 100%), OG Ben Brown (75, 100%), QB Drake Maye (75, 100%), C Jared Wilson (75, 100%), OT Morgan Moses (75 100%), WR Romeo Doubs (62, 83%), WR Efton Chism III (57, 76%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (53, 71%), OT Caleb Lomu (49, 65%), TE Hunter Henry (48, 64%), TE Eli Raridon (43, 57%), WR DeMario Douglas (37, 49%), OT Will Campbell (28, 37%), WR Kyle Williams (27, 36%), RB Corey Kiner (15, 20%), TE Tanner Arkin (15, 20%), RB TreVeyon Henderson (12, 16%), TE Cameron Latu (4, 5%)
It was a career day for Efton Chism and Caleb Lomu , who both stepped up with injuries above them on the depth chart. Mack Hollins went down a week ago, opening the door for Chism to play a career-high in snaps. After Will Campbell left the game with a knee injury , the rookie Lomu came in as well (and looked really comfortable at left tackle).
DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams both had upticks in production, and both of them found the end zone as well. They could come back down to earth if A.J. Brown (ankle) comes off of IR next week.

This side of the ball was also depleted, with four cornerbacks out of the game heading into Sunday. That allowed Kindle Vildor to step into a much bigger role in the secondary. He broke up a pass intended for Brock Bowers before punching the ball out of Bowers' hands later in the game.
Because of the scoreboard, some Patriots who might not have gotten a lot of defensive snaps ended up entering the game. Brenden Schooler , coming off of the NFI list and making his season debut, got some snaps at safety, while Elliott Davison got his first snaps as a pro in mop-up duty.
