title: Giants Offense Grades: Winston, Nabers and Likely Rally in 27-27 Tie vs. Washington
full_text:
Jameis Winston threw for 326 yards and three touchdowns in the rain, but it wasn’t enough as the New York Giants escaped from Northwest Stadium with a 27-27 overtime tie against the Washington Commanders.
The Giants’ offense played a tale of two halves, managing just 77 net yards in the first half before the coaches shifted to a more drop-back approach after the break, which produced 240 net yards in the second half of regulation.
The second half also saw some of the Giants’ playmakers who had been nonfactors in the first 30 minutes come alive. Those included tight end Isaiah Likely, who contributed two touchdowns to help the Giants erase a 14-point deficit, and receiver Malik Nabers, who delivered the game-tying score with 1:43 left in the fourth quarter.
The Giants’ ground game remains an enigma, finishing with just 3.7 yards per carry as Washington committed to shutting down the run and forcing Winston to beat the Commanders through the air in sloppy, rainy conditions.
It wasn’t the win the Giants were hoping for, but the tie does increase their lead in the division to 1.5 games, a better outcome than a loss would have been.
Here is how each offensive player graded out against the Commanders, from the quarterbacks through the offensive line.
Winston has been this team’s starting quarterback for three weeks now, and each game has been a “weather” game. His offense has scored 12, 30, and 27 points. He should be 3-0 if not for Cam Skattebo’s backbreaking fumble.
After a slow start, Winston’s arm came alive, as he threw three touchdowns and no interceptions. He also threw for 326 yards on a day better suited for ducks.
After a very sluggish first half, in which the offense lost most every battle at the line of scrimmage, Winston came out on fire in the second half, and he did it without a running game.
Talk about clutch: all three of his touchdown throws came in that second half, the final one with 1:43 left in the fourth quarter to tie the game 27-27.
Admittedly, Winston contributed to the early-game mess with poor pocket awareness that led to the game’s two sacks. After his sack/fumble at the end of the first half, when he should have fallen on the ball instead of trying to pick it up, Winston wasn’t sacked a single time.
In the second half, the Giants seemed more aligned with what the Commanders’ defense was doing, and Winston started getting the ball out of his hands more quickly.
As for the deep ball, New York completed three of 11 attempts in that area. Until the deep ball plays a bigger role on offense, defenses will keep attacking the line of scrimmage and mucking up the running game.
All of McCarthy’s half-dozen snaps were gadget plays, and one drew a facemask penalty on Washington. His two runs went for two yards.
His lone pass was a receiver screen on which he showed off his fast release and strong arm; the completion to Nabers went for 14 yards, but an illegal shift nullified it.
It was interesting how the coaches forced him into the QB rotation so quickly. The coming weeks might be even more interesting, but only if Winston struggles.
It looked like Skattebo was running in place throughout a first half in which he had 12 yards on six carries and nothing through the air.
On the first possession of the second half, he had runs of 7 and 4 yards, his two longest runs of the day to that point. He also threw a couple of positive pass blocks, an area that needed to improve.
He didn’t get a single touch on that big third-quarter drive. In fact, he didn’t come alive until the second overtime series.
His 19-yard run on 3rd-and-2 on a wide toss was a nice change of pace, given how Washington had been packing it in between the tackles all game long.
Runs of 9 and 5 yards set up the offense at the two-minute warning, but on the very next snap, Skattebo allowed the ball to get punched out of his grasp for the backbreaking turnover. It was a great play by the defense, but his third fumble in five games should be setting off alarms in the Giants’ coaching room.
A lack of speed at the position is another big red flag this organization needs to address in the offseason.
Harris looked just as sluggish as the starter early on as the O-line could not sustain its blocks. Harris managed only nine yards on five carries and five yards on one reception in his rotation role.
The second half was a passing man’s paradise, which limited Harris’s playing time, and he was barely utilized throughout the fourth quarter and overtime.
Tracy also did not get much going from scrimmage this week, finishing with six yards on three carries. But his two catches for 25 yards should be a harbinger of things to come.
The Giants need a third-down back, and Tracy should have the job. For the last two weeks, his pass-blocking has been superb.
His fourth-down, 21-yard checkdown scamper was one of the second half’s bigger plays. It remains to be seen whether that will be enough for Tracy to start getting most of his snaps on passing downs.
It’s impressive that Nabers has topped 100 receiving yards the last two weeks, in bad weather no less. And yet people, or more specifically Nabers himself, are saying he doesn’t look like himself yet.
Yes, he’s returning from knee surgery, but he's really picked it up over the last two weeks, with 112 yards on six receptions last week and 121 yards on 11 receptions this week.
He scored a touchdown each week, including a clutch, deep middle route this week that tied the game at 27-27 late in the fourth quarter.
Nabers couldn’t get to one deep ball, and people are still waiting to see more explosiveness. He’s “killing it” in the intermediate areas, with his longest catch a 28-yarder in overtime that set up the offense for the game-winning field goal that never came.
He also had earlier receptions of 14, 16, 18, and 20 yards as he did what most secondaries do these days: keep things in front of them and allow intermediate catches.
The Giants’ WR1 has played a big role in the last two games, and it boggles the mind to think there could be more.
One part of this offense that is crying for attention is the ability this big rookie brings to the field. All he does is catch everything thrown his way, much like Likely catches everything in sight.
Fields didn’t get his first target until early in the third quarter, when he made a defender miss and took it for 13 yards, gaining five after contact and setting up a 3rd-and-2.
On the fourth-quarter game-tying drive, Fields took a 7-yard catch past the marker for a huge first down. These were his only two targets on the day.
His efficiency is off the charts. Since he’s on the field so much for his blocking, you would think the coaches and his quarterback might start looking his way a bit more.
As for his blocking, Fields needs to be more aware of the heavy pressure opposing corners put on the Giants’ running game and get a piece of his man, since those edge defenders are really in attack mode out there.

A third catch came on a gadget play from McCarthy, an actual 5-yard loss, but Mooney was poked in the face on the play and had to leave the game for a handful of plays.
He did drop a pass on a subsequent broken play, with the ball behind him in the wet conditions. Mooney returned after leaving and finished the game.
It felt like Likely caught about 20 balls out there, but his actual numbers were 11 receptions for 94 yards and two scores. After struggling to get in tune with Winston, this week was the first game in which the two looked in sync.
Once again, he didn’t drop a single pass, even though Likely had his fair share of lunging and low pass targets to execute in the pouring rain. He truly does have amazing hands.

title: Four Plays That Defined the Giants’ Wild 27-27 Tie With the Commanders
full_text:
The New York Giants and Washington Commanders played to a 27-27 tie in their first division meeting of the season, a wild game that ended with a result neither side wanted.
The Giants were lucky to be in position to win after Washington took control in the first half and looked like it would keep dominating.
New York staged a major comeback in the final two quarters behind an improved passing performance from Jameis Winston, who completed 33 of 54 pass attempts for 326 yards and three touchdowns to force overtime.
After an extra 10 minutes, neither team made enough plays to leave as the victor. Still, these four plays were the most impactful in leading both the Giants and Commanders to a strange finish.
The last two weeks of the Giants' slate brought plenty of praise for a defense that thwarted two consecutive final opposing drives to seal gritty wins over the Titans and Cardinals.
That same physicality didn't show up when the Commanders took the opening possession of Week 5. Washington came out looking to create chunk plays and found several against the Giants' unprepared unit.
It started with Rachaad White's 27-yard kickoff return, which set the Commanders up at their own 31-yard line. Three plays later, Jayden Daniels connected with tight end Chig Okonkwo for a 23-yard gain to enter New York territory in just over a minute.
On the next play, the Commanders caught the Giants defense sleeping again, scoring on a huge 33-yard run by running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt that finished in the end zone and gave the home team a fast 6-0 advantage, the extra point attempt being no good.
The drive took four plays and 69 yards, putting the Giants in a hole in exactly two minutes. It also marked the second straight week an opponent scored on its first possession against New York (the Cardinals scored an opening touchdown in eight  plays and 58 yards in Week 4).
The score immediately put the heat on Winston and the Giants offense to play catch-up in a game where throwing the ball in the rainy weather wasn't ideal.
The Giants got arguably their best effort from the receiving corps this season, and none of it would have been possible without Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely.
While the duo combined for 22 receptions, 215 yards, and three touchdowns, Likely's stat line (11 catches, 94 yards, 2 TDs) mattered more on the scoreboard. In particular, the tight end's second score nearly didn't happen.
On the Giants' second drive of the third quarter, Likely first found pay dirt on a three-yard connection from Winston, capping the team's longest drive of the game (13 plays, 63 yards). It also answered a 38-yard touchdown scramble by Daniels on the preceding Commanders possession that had grown Washington's lead to 19-6.
The Commanders dealt another blow to the comeback effort when Daniels broke free for a 26-yard keeper that found the end zone, and after Washington converted the two-point try, it was back ahead by two scores.
Once again, it was Likely who wouldn't say die on New York's fourth-quarter attempt to rally. No. 9 put his hands all over the Giants' next possession, catching a 10-yard pass to open the drive, then finishing it with a 16-yard catch-and-run that saw the ball come loose near the goal line.
After an officiating review, Likely had the wherewithal to extend the nose of the football over the plane of the end zone before Rasul Douglas punched it loose, nullifying the turnover and cementing his second touchdown, which pulled the Giants within a 27-20 deficit.
Had the ball really been coughed up, it might have been the lasting gut punch that took the wind out of the Giants' comeback sails.
Instead, Likely notched his third and fourth touchdowns of the year, his second game with multiple scores, and reminded everyone why the Giants made sure the rising star followed John Harbaugh from Baltimore to be a key weapon in their offense.
Though the Giants didn't lose, the tie was never more frustrating than in the final 3:38 of overtime, when they finally had the field position to attempt a game-winning field goal with Dominic Zvada and put the Commanders to bed.
After Zvada's earlier miss, the Giants defense had to come out with heavy pressure to force Daniels into mistakes and stall any movement toward field-goal range for Stevens.
It worked perfectly, as defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson's group got the Commanders offense off the field in four plays and 13 yards behind a forced fumble Washington recovered and a failed fourth-down conversion attempt that drew a delay-of-game penalty when the Giants couldn't be fooled into going offside.
The biggest stop of the afternoon put the ball back in the Giants' hands with a chance to steal the road win and improve to 4-1, but not before Big Blue's offense offered one more turnover to its count of two.
In eight plays and 67 yards, Winston led the Giants offense with two big completions to Nabers for 36 yards. Skattebo handled the rest of the work on the ground, punishing the Commanders' defense with a 19-yard burst followed by two more carries for a total of 14 yards.
With the Giants at the Washington 24-yard line and in Zvada's range, they tried one more carry to set up the next play, but Skattebo lost control of the ball, and the Commanders recovered it to stall the upset.
The crushing fumble wouldn't be the Giants' death knell, as the Commanders would one-up the mistake with an unfathomable case of time mismanagement that ripped away their own shot at a game-winning Stevens kick in the final seconds of the extra period.
For Skattebo and company, it was a play they'll be thinking about beyond Sunday. There had to be some trepidation given Zvada's shaky outing, but there was no better time to trust their young kicker to convert the one kick that would have wiped away the thought of his earlier misses.
Plus, the Giants' ball control has been an issue. Skattebo's mishap was the team's fifth fumble this season and the third they lost, both marks leading the NFL through five games.
One could also wonder what Harbaugh and the coaches were thinking when they elected to push for a few extra yards instead of shutting the door on the Commanders and leaving with a 2-0 record in the NFC East standings.
A tie is not a loss, but with one foolish handoff, the Giants cost themselves a little extra breathing room from their divisional neighbors.
Facing second-and-8 from the 24-yard line, well within field-goal range, the Commanders had no timeouts left and ran a play with no discernible purpose that ended with Daniels getting sacked.
Maybe they were trying to gain a few yards for a closer game-winning field goal. Maybe they wanted to burn time off the clock so that a miss wouldn't leave the Giants time to drive for a field goal attempt of their own.
Or maybe those involved forgot they had no timeouts. Whatever the reason, it was one of the more bizarre endings to a game, and a big reason the contest finished in a draw that increased the Giants' lead in the NFC East to 1.5 games.

title: Jameis Winston Answers Critics With Historic Day in Giants Tie vs. Commanders
full_text:
The adage that says “the backup quarterback is the most popular player on a football roster” is certainly alive and well, at least for the New York Giants .
Such has been the case ever since the Giants acquired J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings for a fifth-round pick.
For many pundits, the arrival of McCarthy, who took five snaps against the Commanders in a package of plays the coaches felt comfortable having him run, meant it was just a matter of time before Jameis Winston’s run as the starter, which has been frustrating at times, would come to an end.
Instead, Winston, who has joked about the “Jameis Winston Experience,” has handled his situation with aplomb and quieted some of those critics calling for McCarthy to take over at quarterback.
The part of the Jameis Winston experience that no one outside of the building sees is that he comes to work, puts in the effort, and is always open to getting better. While his weekly showings are not perfect—whose effort is?—he gives his teammates every chance possible for a win.
A wacky game against the Commanders ended in a 27-27 tie after a major collective brain freeze in overtime, when it appeared Washington forgot it had no timeouts left while driving for the game-winning score. Winston gave the Giants a chance.
The 12-year veteran led the team back from a 14-point deficit, completing 33 of 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns for a passer rating of 96.7, and adding five carries for 27 yards.
It marked the only time since 1950 that a Giant has thrown for at least 300 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for at least 25 yards in the same game.
He also became the first Giants quarterback since Eli Manning on Sept. 24, 2017, to throw three or more touchdowns in the second half.
His passing efficiency, which started slow, improved as the game went on , thanks in part to a coaching adjustment to move away from the no-huddle, control the tempo, and return to the drop-back game.
Winston saved his best performance for the second half, going from 43.8% completion in the first 30 minutes to 75% in the second half, before capping it with a 50% completion rate in overtime.
“I thought he was amazing in the second half,” head coach John Harbaugh said of Winston.
“First half, he wasn’t. He’d be the first to tell you that, but that’s on everybody. I tell the guys, nothing good is all one person. We’re all responsible for all the good, and we’re all responsible for all the bad.”
Winston, who makes no secret of how much he leans into his faith, has surely heard the growing chatter about his current hold on the starting quarterback job and how McCarthy, whose skill set is thought to be closer to Jaxson Dart’s because of his mobility, should be handed the keys to the offense.
But Winston, as he did under pressure against Washington, plays his game.
“I always focus on what my heart desires, and I say this over and over again, I desire to be the New York Football Giants Super Bowl-winning quarterback,” he said.
“I desire to be a great starting quarterback in the NFL. I dreamed of this, and this is who I am, and I know that I’m going to continue to get better and find ways to help this team win football games.”

title: Isaiah Likely Makes Giants History in Wild Tie vs. Commanders
full_text:
New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely has been making sure his on-field production matches every penny the franchise paid him to come over from Baltimore with head coach John Harbaugh during the offseason.
The 6-foot-4 Likely, who traded in Ravens purple for a blue uniform and a three-year, $40 million contract in free agency, has wasted no time making his mark in his Giants tenure.
Harbaugh and the Giants wanted Likely to be a complementary, versatile receiving threat for their initial starting quarterback, Jaxson Dart, and Matt Nagy’s offense. Still, he has gone far beyond that, logging a team-leading 33 receptions on 47 targets for 284 yards and four touchdowns.
The catch total puts him in rare company in Giants lore: he is the first tight end in franchise history to record that many catches through his first five games.
The feat came on the strength of Likely’s breakout effort in the Giants’ roller-coaster 27-27 Week 5 overtime tie against the Washington Commanders, one where the tight end hauled in a career-high 11 catches for 94 yards and two touchdowns to help the team overcome a 14-point second-half deficit.
At the same time, his performance wasn’t enough to counteract other missed opportunities that kept Big Blue from beating its division rival and widening its lead in the NFC East.
“I honestly was shocked,” Likely said about the final result. “I never tied up before in my NFL career, really in any game.”
“I mean, we had the game right there—unfortunate errors. You know, obviously there are plays that we all can have back to really end the game from there. It wasn’t a win, it wasn’t a loss, obviously, but it definitely was a blessing.”
The Giants’ odd blessing of leaving Northwest Stadium with a tie came down to tough conversations and a whole lot of grit.
That started in the team’s much-needed halftime break, when New York trailed the Commanders 12-3 after Dominic Zvada missed a pair of field goals and Jameis Winston fumbled, while the offense managed just 72 passing yards and 26 rushing yards.
Knowing those numbers stemmed purely from a lack of execution, the Giants took advantage of their chance to regroup and made the adjustments that led them back to the fruitful football they missed in the first 30 minutes.
“[We had] great feedback at halftime,” Likely said.
“Player dialogue, coaches’ dialogue, and really just getting behind your brother. Jameis [Winston] had open ears. He understood that the job in the second half was to get us back in the game, and that’s exactly what he did.”
The Giants returned with renewed offensive energy in the second half as Winston connected with Likely for two scores.
The first came on a 13-play drive that featured three late downs, two penalties, and a near interception by Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson that a pass interference penalty wiped out, putting the Giants within three yards of the end zone for a quick strike to cut the deficit to 19-13.
Likely’s biggest moment came when facing what felt like a must-have fourth-down conversion from the Washington 17, No. 9 put the whole team on his shoulders and didn’t settle for the first down, taking it all the way to the end zone.
“It was fourth down, so in my mind I’m thinking, we got to get in the end zone regardless,” Likely said.
“Knowing the situation, knowing the stakes, knowing that when I get the first down, I can be more cautious with the ball in my hands and try to get down if I can if I’m wrapped up, but, in my mind, I was thinking about scoring and try to go up.”
Likely’s second touchdown, which made him the first Giants tight end with nine or more receptions and two or more touchdowns in a single game, was a clear example of why the organization made it a priority to insert him into its offensive huddle and give him the chance to be a No. 1 option, something he couldn’t be behind Mark Andrews in Baltimore.
While his record start was enough to pull the Giants back from defeat in Washington, it didn’t serve as the centerpiece of a win that would have given the franchise its first 4-1 start since the 2022 season and a two-game lead in the division.
Likely and his teammates know they did their job to force a thrilling comeback when they should have been counted out, but they’ll have to wait for another chance to change the script in Week 6, when they welcome the New Orleans Saints to MetLife Stadium.

title: Jets Rookie Report Card: Grading 2026 Draft Picks After First Month of the Season
full_text:
It was not pretty, but the Jets found a way to take down the Browns in a 17-12 season-saving win in the sloppy conditions at MetLife Stadium. Regardless, New York is now 2-3 and in a much better position than it would have been at 1-4 heading into a Week 6 AFC East tilt against the Patriots on Sunday.
Fresh off the hard-fought win in the rain , the Jets put a three-game losing streak behind them and have their eyes set on continuing to make improvements and learn from their previous mistakes going forward. While the discipline and inability to close out each half remain a concern, there is a lot more to feel optimistic about coming off a win this week.
Before the season even got started, there was a lot of hype surrounding the Jets' 2026 draft class. Although injuries or inconsistent play in the early going have provided some mixed results for some, the rookies' talent has been on display, setting the stage for a promising future in Gotham .
With that in mind, let's hand out grades for each of the Jets' eight 2026 draft picks now that it's been over a month since their season opener.
Even though David Bailey led all NFL rookies in pressures during the first month of the season, a lot of fans were concerned about his early returns on the field . That said, he single-handedly took over the Week 5 win over the Browns with three of the team's eight sacks, in addition to seven tackles (five solo), three tackles for loss and four quarterback hits.
Bailey recorded his third sack of the game early in the fourth quarter (h/t NFL) after the defense forced Cleveland's offense into a third-and-30.
THIRD sack of the day for David Bailey @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QTqQqo79NN
The defensive line was easily the best unit on the field for the Jets , which was a huge turnaround from the disappointing play that same group displayed in the games coming in. According to Pro Football Focus , Bailey has the 43rd-ranked overall grade (68.6) and the 10th-most pressures (20) out of 106 qualified edge defenders.
It was a fairly slow start out of the gate for Bailey, but if the Week 5 performance proved anything, it is that he was more than worthy of being selected No. 2 overall and certainly appears to have all the tools to become a star in the league.
Kenyon Sadiq scored his first NFL TD in Week 1 courtesy of the ground game, but his true breakout performance came in Week 3 when he went off for seven catches, 105 yards and his first TD catch. Aside from that, Sadiq has rarely been targeted and has been completely limited in the pass game when the ball has come his way.
Sadiq only had two catches for three yards in the loss to Cleveland and also committed a fumble, so there is definitely some room for improvement . This was also the first game back for Mason Taylor, and it was clear he was going to be a focal point of the tight end group, with 41 snaps to Sadiq's 13.
Granted, the concussion was a setback and limited Sadiq's playing time, but the Jets appear to prefer leaning in Taylor's direction a little more at this stage of the season. Sadiq's raw athletic traits are unmatched and his route separation is elite, but it remains to be seen how much of a factor he will be in this offense when Taylor is on the field.
Omar Cooper Jr.'s NFL career immediately got off to a hot start when he turned a short pass into a 30-yard gain (h/t Glenn Naughton) to set up a TD a few plays later in New York's season-opening win over the Titans. However, that remains his only target and catch of his rookie season after suffering a high ankle sprain during the first quarter of that Week 1 game.
First career catch for @nyjets rookie WR Omar Cooper. Looks like a first round pick if you ask me. pic.twitter.com/NmQRKYSGCK
Cooper has since spent the last four weeks on injured reserve, though the possibility is there for him to play in Sunday's game against the Patriots, depending on the progress he has made in his recovery. The Jets finally figured things out with WR1 Garrett Wilson by looking his way more often and reaping those rewards with seven catches for 104 yards and a TD, but the depth at WR has been an issue, and getting Cooper back sooner rather than later would be a huge benefit.
The grade is not so much a knock on D'Angelo Ponds, but rather due to the lack of playing time he has received as more of a developmental player who is primarily serving a backup role in the secondary. That said, he played a career-high 18 snaps in relief of Jarvis Brownlee Jr. in Week 4 and showcased his run-defense skills when the opportunity presented itself.
It appeared that Ponds was suddenly staring at a bigger role after Brownlee went into concussion protocol following the Week 4 loss to the Bears, but the latter ultimately became a full participant in practice and even recorded his first career sack in Sunday's game, all while Ponds played just two defensive snaps and primarily appeared on special teams.
Darrell Jackson Jr. was expected to be a rotational run-plugger in the middle of head coach Aaron Glenn's defensive schemes. While he only had seven tackles and zero pressures in 85 defensive snaps across the first four games, the fourth-round selection finally broke out and made his impact felt against the Browns.
Jackson had four tackles, one sack, two pressures and two pass deflections in 29 defensive snaps, putting together his best overall game so far in Gang Green. David Onyemata's place on injured reserve has paved the way for Jackson to step up, and the Week 5 performance was the first true sign of what Jackson is capable of.
Veteran Geno Smith has done his part to take care of the ball and manage each game relatively well by completing 72.7% of his passes for 1,084 yards and six TDs. Although he was anything but flashy in the win over the Browns, this is still firmly Smith's job as long as he continues to protect the ball, which could only benefit Cade Klubnik more as the fourth-round pick gets some additional time to learn from Smith and develop under his leadership.
Anez Cooper, the sixth-round pick out of Miami, suffered a right shoulder injury during the preseason finale against the Giants and has been on injured reserve since.
While he is now eligible to return to the roster , it remains to be seen if Cooper will make his season debut or at least be available to play. The offensive line was better against the Browns, but with Dylan Parham dealing with a knee injury and the play up front looking suspect so far, it definitely would not hurt to have an extra body in Cooper to turn to if the opportunity presents itself.
The seventh-round pick suffered a significant bone bruise during training camp before being placed on short-term IR, forcing him to miss at least the first four games of the season. Much like Cooper, it remains to be seen whether VJPayne will be activated back to the 53-man roster soon.
However, this staff is particularly high on Payne's physical traits and special teams potential , which could prove valuable when he does get fully healthy and potential roster holes open up.

title: Jets Ending One Pitiful Trend Is Absolutely Crucial vs. Patriots in Week 6
full_text:
It's Patriots Week, a time when Jets fans gear up for a matchup against Gang Green's biggest rival.
But since 2000, the Jets-Pats rivalry has been as one-sided as it comes. Sure, the Jets have gotten their fair share of licks—a stunning upset in the 2010 divisional round of the playoffs being the top moment—but by and large, this rivalry has gone the Patriots' way for decades.
At 2-3 in Week 6, the Jets have a chance to write a new chapter in this storied rivalry. But as coaches and players have said, they aren't making the game any more meaningful than it already is.
"Every game is important to us; it doesn't matter who you play," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said. "We have a 1-0 mindset every time we go out there. I know it's the Patriots, I know it's a division game, but we want to win this game just like we wanted to win the Cleveland game, and we're going to go out there and prepare to win it."
The Jets may have a central-focused mindset heading into Sunday's contest, but it doesn't take away from one grueling stat they haven't been able to overcome in recent years.
And if the team is going to take the next step in their rebuild, it's a stat that must change on Sunday.
The numbers tell the story. New York is a gruesome 25-65 against AFC East opponents since 2011, including 4-26 against New England during that stretch.
It hasn't gotten much better since Tom Brady left New England either. The Jets are just 2-10 against their rivals since one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time moved on. It highlights the organization's deeper struggles across the division and against their arch nemisis.
Even if Glenn and the Jets aren't focused about what happened last year or over the last 16 years.
The Jets haven't finished over .500 in their division since 2010, the last time they made the playoffs. Many fans are expecting similar struggles when the team travels to Foxborough on Sunday, but there is reason for optimism.
Despite the Patriots coming off a Super Bowl appearance last season and rattling off back-to-back wins against the Bills and Raiders, they are still a team that can be beat. Their defense is a top-five unit, but is league average against the run, and their offense, while potent, can absolutely turn the ball over when you least expect. Drake Maye is currently tied for the league lead in interceptions thrown so far this season (seven).
The Jets still have a long way to go before they can confidently compete for a Super Bowl. The first step to reaching that goal, though, is to win games in the division.
And Glenn's current mindset has Jets players believing their divisional drought may soon come to an end.
Amid the celebration of a Week 5 win over the Browns , one key point rang true throughout Glenn's postgame response to players: Going 1-0 each week, and each day, is how a team like the Jets improves.
And some of the team's biggest stars, including Garrett Wilson, have bought in to that mindset.
According to DraftKings Sportsbook , New England is currently favored by 7.5 points in Sunday's contest . Most people in their right minds would expect the Jets to be unable to compete with the AFC Champions on the road. But what if New York can? What if, instead of a beatdown in Massachusetts, the Jets actually play well enough to win?
Well, that should show that the team is truly heading in the right direction. It would show that the organization, despite falling to 2-4, is capable of playing up to their level of competition.
They may not win on Sunday, but if the Jets put up a quality performance, it could set the franchise up for future success down the road. Heck, a win might catapult the group forward beyond anything fans could have expected this season.
That's what is at stake on Sunday. New York has a chance to show its AFC East problems are over. Correcting a 25-65 mark since 2011 isn't easy, and it doesn't happen in just one game. But Glenn's message of being "1-0 each week" is something the roster and fanbase should get behind.
It might just get the Jets to where they want to go.

title: 5 Jets With Skyrocketing Stocks to Begin Week 6 (David Bailey's Outlook Soars)
full_text:
When you win, it's easy to move forward in the week with rose-colored glasses. For the Jets, their Week 5 win over the Browns not only improved their record to 2-3 , but it also saw plenty of strong performances from key players, stoking optimism for the rest of the season.
From stars like wideout Garrett Wilson to key members of the rookie class, the Jets should be thrilled with what they saw from their core after Sunday's 17-12 win. In fact, five members of Gang Green in particular saw their stock soar after Sunday's victory.
Let's get to the five biggest ones here.
David Bailey has been solid to start his rookie campaign with New York. He hasn't been the transcendent player some Jets fans may have hoped he would be when he was taken with the second overall pick.
Boy, did he look like that on Sunday, though. The Texas Tech product recorded three sacks (h/t NFL), four quarterback hits, and nine pressures. He remains New York's best pass rusher but became one of six rookies since 2000 to record at least five sacks in their first five NFL games.
THIRD sack of the day for David Bailey @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QTqQqo79NN
The best part about Bailey has been his improved run defense. His effort and physicality are there. He's looking the part of an everydown edge rusher.
He's on the cusp of a special rookie season if this continues.
A player who has taken a very positive jump in his second season is former Jets third-round cornerback AZ Thomas. The Florida State product was the seventh-highest-rated player by the Jets on Sunday, according to Pro Football Focus , and has the 11th-highest coverage grade of all corners through five games.
He also hasn't been beaten deep. Thomas has yet to give up a completion beyond 20 yards. The way the Jets have developed him has been a sight to see. He's fourth in the league in pass breakups, and has been close to intercepting multiple passes over the last few weeks.
It seems like the Jets got a really good player here that is only getting better.
It's not hyperbole to say this was the best game Jamien Sherwood has had in two years. The veteran linebacker has struggled mightily in the early season , but was the highest-graded Jets player by PFF against the Browns (83.5). Sherwood recorded four tackles, a quarterback hit, and a pass defended.
If Sherwood can play as he did on Sunday, the rest of the year could change drastically for the Jets' defense. Right now, the linebacker position remains a big question for the organization. Things could change if the team gets his Week 5 form moving forward.
This was the breakout game Jets fans have been waiting for since Braelon Allen was drafted in the fourth round three years ago. 24 carries, 116 yards, and the game-winning touchdown run set the stage for New York's offense to be the catalyst for the unit on Sunday.
For the first time in three years, Allen has rewarded Gang Green for their faith . With Breece Hall due back soon, it's nice for the Jets to recognize and accept that they have a perfectly competent backup behind him.
There is no Jets player who's had more of a consistent start to the season than Dane Belton. The veteran safety has been a revelation for the team through five games, sitting at the seventh-best PFF grade (81.4) among 96 eligible safeties this season. He wasn't targeted in Sunday's win, and he even recorded a sack on a blitz.
Belton, like New York's other safeties, is a Swiss Army knife. The more he plays, the better he is.
And right now he's on an All-Pro trajectory.

title: Faria's Focus: 8 Jets Thoughts After Win vs. Browns (Garrett Wilson, Ongoing Concerns, Optimistic Outlook & More)
full_text:
One day, Jets fans will be able to watch their team at home when the weather is not horrid.
Sunday was not one of those days .
New York used the elements to their advantage, though, in outlasting the AFC North-leading Browns in a 17-12 rock fight . The win bumped the Jets' record to 2-3, with an upcoming Week 6 contest against the Patriots to get ready for.
The end of a three-game losing streak will have plenty of takeaways, so let's go through eight of my top thoughts following New York's latest win over the weekend
Some Jets fans believed that the team was already doomed this season. Others felt there was nothing head coach Aaron Glenn could do to earn another year after a dismal 1-3 start. Most fans would argue a five-point win over the Browns in an ugly contest shouldn't be celebrated.
The jury is still out on Glenn and New York's future, of course. No one knows how the rest of the season should go.
But for a team that won just four of their first 21 games under this current regime, celebrating wins should never be frowned upon. The Jets, for the most part on Sunday, played well. In many ways, the game shouldn't have been as close as it was. New York's defense dominated, and their offense did move the ball down the field consistently. Turnovers and penalties were their big issue.
But there's a fine balance between wanting to see the team be successful and actively rooting for their demise. In the case of the Jets, it's clear that people should celebrate a good win against a team that was in first place in their division at the time rather than get angry over a lost draft pick—especially this early in the year.
TL;DR—it's okay to celebrate a win like this, and don't let anyone tell you it isn't.
That was it. That was the blueprint that showed just how good the Jets' defense could be for the remainder of the season. Glenn called blitz plays on over 50 percent of the snaps faced. In turn, the defense recorded eight sacks and harassed Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson for most of the afternoon.
David Bailey was the big winner, posting a team-high three sacks in a breakout performance from the second overall pick. In many ways, the young star was the best player on the field for the Jets throughout Sunday's contest.
"Just relentless," Glenn said. "The other things that really showed up in the game was (David's) ability to play the run, and I think that's one thing that he's not getting enough credit for, but man, he did a hell of a job when it came to run defense too, so he just had an all-around game as far as affecting the quarterback and playing the run."
It wasn't just Bailey, though. Fourth-round rookie Darrell Jackson Jr. notched his first career sack (h/t Glenn Naughton) and two pass deflections at the line of scrimmage. Throw in quality play from Kingsley Enagbare and Will McDonald IV, and the Jets' defensive line played the best it has all year.
Rookie DT Darrell Jackson having himself a hell of a day.  Two batted passes at the LOS and gets in on a big sack here with Enagbare. pic.twitter.com/W5xxCgLUQT
It also helps that Jamien Sherwood had his best game and was the team's leader in PFF rankings at 83.5 Throw in another elite performance from AZ Thomas, Minkah Fitzpatrick, and Dane Belton and New York's secondary also stood out.
All elite defenses need good pass rushes, though. And the team's performance on Sunday provided the blueprint for how good they could be moving forward.
When it comes to the Jets' offensive game plan, I'll let Glenn's response from Monday tell it all:
"Any time we can get Garrett involved, good things happen," New York's head coach said.
Seven catches, 104 yards and a sick touchdown to get the scoring started. Yep, Wilson remains one of the best receivers in football. As long as he keeps getting the overwhelming share of the targets, New York should stay successful on offense.
What does Glenn do well as head coach? What position group has improved under him?
These are questions that have been asked in recent weeks during New York's three-game losing streak. Yet in Sunday's win over the Browns, it was clear that Glenn's importance to the team was clear .
Defensively, the Jets remain vastly improved from last season. Maybe they aren't good enough to dominate elite offenses like the Bears' or Lions', but even the most ardent critic of Glenn can't deny the improvement in their defense.
The coach's top skill is more than just calling plays, though. In years past, the Jets had a history of keeping their heads down during tough moments. When something bad happened, it would cascade into a mountain of bad things.
So far this season, though, the opposite has happened.
Bad things have happened, and the team has responded. The clearest example came in the closing minutes of the game. Gang Green, down 12-10, watched their quarterback fumble at midfield. In years past, the Jets wouldn't have been able to recover from that. Instead, their special teams made a play, the offense responded, and the team won the game.
That is coaching. It's an example of the team not giving up when things seemed low. And it's a good reminder that while Glenn still has a lot to prove, there are some obvious things to build on.
The Jets should be pleased with this win. They did some things they have struggled to do and found a way at the end to win.
That said, many of the same problems the team has dealt with continues to be an issue.
New York committed 10 penalties on the day for over 100 yards. The Jets' lack of discipline remains a major issue going forward. Their passing offense also seems out of whack at times due to a number of pressures given up. Whether it's starters getting beat along the offensive line or Geno Smith holding onto the ball too long, the Jets need to do a better job of getting the ball out quickly in the passing game.
When healthy, Breece Hall is one of the best running backs in the game. New York's biggest problem has been not finding someone to complement the star runner when he comes off the field. For years, it seemed like the duo of Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis just simply weren't enough.
Allen ran for a career-high 116 yards on 24 carries and the game-winning score from 22 yards out to pace New York's rushing attack. Along the way, he broke several tackles to set the tone for the Jets' offense, earning some praise from his head coach.
It is incredibly important for Allen to continue playing up to this level. It adds a new power dynamic the Jets haven't had - even when Hall is in the game.
Before the season began, it seemed like the Jets had a major question mark at kicker. After five games, that question is no more. Jason Sanders has been excellent since winning the job during camp in a shaky position battle.
Sanders nailed a 54-yard kick in the rain and is 8-for-9 on kicks so far this season. He has missed an extra point, but the former Dolphin appears healthy and is playing very good football.
Even more important, the Jets' punt return unit recovering the muffed punt from the Browns late in the fourth quarter won them the game. New York's special teams unit remains just that: special.
I have been high on Darren Mougey as general manager of the Jets. He seems to understand positional value well and has been very good in the first couple of drafts. The 2025 class has every-down starters in Armand Membou, Mason Taylor and AZ Thomas.
The 2026 class may be even better with Bailey, Sadiq, and Jackson all with breakout games over the first five weeks. New York will need to see more from first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr. when he returns from injured reserve, and more reps for D'Angelo Ponds will be huge for the secondary, but the Jets have six clear starters from the last two draft classes.
It could get up to eight if the aforementioned players are able to produce moving forward.
Getting eight starters in two draft classes is a huge success for any modern GM . For Mougey, his work should be celebrated so far, even with a…

title: Aaron Glenn Is Already a Better Jets Head Coach Than Robert Saleh for One Key Reason
full_text:
In case it wasn't already clear, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is significantly different from his predecessor .
When Robert Saleh was hired by the Jets in 2021, for the better part of three seasons, he spoke about how the job he took was likened to that of an expansion roster. Glenn, meanwhile, never stooped low to criticize his counterpart —instead taking many of the current struggles on the chin through his first 22 games.
That isn't what has separated Glenn from Saleh, though. The biggest difference between the two coaches has come down to the response from the roster.
And it's something that has shown up in each of New York's first five games to begin the 2026 NFL season.
Accountability comes in all shapes and sizes when teams lose. When teams win, though, the true mark of a quality head coach is how they handle the days after.
In the case of Glenn, Sunday's 17-12 win over the Browns put him in the right mindset. Although he was pleased that the Jets got the win, there was a sense of frustration that they didn't play their best.
"Happy that we got us a win, but as you look at that tape, there are a number of things that we have to improve on, which we will actually address this week," Glenn said.
Compare that to Saleh's answer on Sunday. His Titans roster dropped another game, this time falling to 0-5. Instead of circling the wagons, the coach has made it clear: he won't panic. And that is all there is to it.
“ I’ve always felt like that’s a sign of panic where you’ve lost all answers . And right now, I don’t think we’re in a space where we don’t have answers,” Saleh said, per Teresa M. Walker of the Associated Press . “We just got to continue working and try to help our guys get better.”
As a head coach, there's a difference in how Glenn deals with his struggles compared to Saleh. There's also a difference in how the Jets have played under him in Year 2 compared to Glenn's predecessor.
It's true that over five games, the Jets' record under Saleh in his second season was better. The 2022 Jets were 3-2 compared to the current 2-3 mark this season. But the quality of play is different. The 2022 Jets didn't play well in two of their victories—they marched to wins based on last-moment plays.
The 2026 Jets are playing a lot better than the previous group. They have been more competitive in losses and look to be an improving team in wins . The roster is also more focused on its goals than ever before, as made abundantly clear by star receiver Garrett Wilson.
"We have to get over that hump. Go 1-0 this week. Go 1-0 each rep, and that was the mindset that we all talked about before we took the field," Wilson said. "Winning your one-on-one and playing your part in the play and not worrying about the score. That was (Glenn's) message, and all of a sudden, we came in here, and we won. It was spot on."
It's true that Glenn is working with a better roster than Saleh out in Tennessee, but many believed the former Jets coach was done in by organization-wide struggles. In many ways, excuses were made for him throughout his tenure.
With Glenn, there are no excuses. There's just the expectation to win. While there is disappointment that the wins haven't stacked up yet, there's optimism that they will soon .
Therein lies the difference between the past and present Jets head coaches.

title: Jets Rookie and Sophomore Week 6 Power Rankings: Kenyon Sadiq Falls to Lowest Ranking of the Season
full_text:
After dropping the last three games, head coach Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets were in a must-win situation against the Cleveland Browns. Despite sloppy conditions, the team came away victorious, narrowly defeating the Browns 17-13.
There were plenty of positives from the game: Braelon Allen and Garrett Wilson carried the offense with their playmaking, while the Jets’ defense wreaked havoc for Deshaun Watson, sacking him eight times.
Several of the Jets' rookies and sophomores stood out in the win, playing critical roles.
With that said, let’s take a look at where every Jets rookie and second-year player ranks heading into Week 6.
Note: Anez Cooper and V.J. Payne are currently excluded from the list. Both Cooper and Payne are on injured reserve, but are eligible to return after missing the first four games of the season.
A torn ACL in Week 2 ended Arian Smith’s sophomore season prematurely. Still, the former 2025 fourth-round selection didn’t impress on offense or special teams in limited action.
Coming off an underwhelming rookie season, Smith needed to play well to solidify his standing in New York for 2027. But with other receivers getting an opportunity while he’s recovering, it’ll be difficult for the former Georgia Bulldog to earn a role once he returns.
Smith must progress as a receiver if he wants to remain with Gang Green.
Geno Smith hasn’t been bad, nor has he been great either.
Through five games, Smith has completed 72.7% of his passes for 1,084 yards and six touchdowns. The 14-year veteran has been a solid game manager and has kept the ball out of harm's way.
Against the Browns, Smith kept the offense afloat, completing 56.7% of his passes for 182 yards and a touchdown. It wasn’t flashy, but he did enough to get them a win.
As long as Smith keeps New York in games and continues to protect the ball, we won’t be seeing the team turn to Cade Klubnik anytime soon.
While the rookie will remain on the sidelines, he can use this time to learn and develop behind the veteran.
For the third straight week, Kiko Mauigoa was inactive with a quadriceps injury. Even if he were active, the former Miami Hurricane wouldn’t have played on defense, as New York has solely depended on Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood at linebacker.
The second-year player has yet to play a single defensive snap this season, and at this point the only way he does is if either Davis or Sherwood gets hurt. But even that’s not guaranteed, as the Jets could turn to Jaden Keller or Trevin Wallace.
For now, Mauigoa will remain exclusively on special teams.
With Week 5 in the books, Omar Cooper Jr. is officially eligible to come off injured reserve this week. He could return to play in the team’s game against the Patriots, but it all depends on where he is in his recovery.
New York could desperately use the former Indiana Hoosier. Since Adonai Mitchell and he were sidelined, the Jets haven’t gotten much production outside of Garrett Wilson.
The team urgently needs consistent play from one of its pass catchers to ease the pressure off Wilson. Cooper gave us a small glimpse of his playmaking ability in Week 1, turning a short pass into a 30-yard gain to set up a touchdown a few plays later.
Hopefully, New York’s first round choice returns to the field sooner rather than later.
With the Jets adding Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick to the safeties room, along with re-signing Andre Cisco, it was going to be hard for Malachi Moore to see reps on defense.
So far, the second-year safety out of Alabama has played just nine defensive snaps. Despite this, Moore has put his head down and has earned his keep on special teams.
Yet again, Moore recorded another special teams tackle, putting his total at five for the season. He’s been one of Gang Green’s best players on the unit, earning a 71 special teams grade, per Pro Football Focus.
Given how the safeties group has played, Moore will remain out of the rotation. But if someone gets hurt, Moore is deserving of a few snaps.
Last week at this time, it seemed like D’Angelo Ponds would make his first career start against the Browns after Jarvis Brownlee Jr. entered the NFL’s concussion protocol.
However, Brownlee quickly progressed through it and was a full participant in the team’s practice, effectively ending Ponds’ chances of playing any defensive snaps.
The former Indiana Hoosier ended up with just two, primarily playing on the special teams. With the current cornerback group impressing with its performance in coverage, Ponds will remain New York’s top backup.
After missing the last three games with a thumb injury, Mason Taylor returned against Cleveland , posting season highs in receptions (3) and yards (24).
While his numbers weren’t flashy, he finished second on the team in yards and targets with three. With Cooper and Mitchell still sidelined, and Sadiq leaving the game with a concussion, Taylor must raise his game.
After leading New York in receptions last year, he’s had a rough start to Year 2 and needs to become more of a productive player if the team wants to remain competitive.
Two weeks ago, the Jets finally unleashed Kenyon Sadiq. The former Oregon Duck balled out, recording seven receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown.
Since then, however, Sadiq has largely flown under the radar. In the last two games, he’s posted just two catches (seven targets) for three yards and a fumble. With Taylor back in the lineup against the Browns, Sadiq took a step back, playing in just 13 snaps compared to Taylor’s 41.
A concussion limited his usage, but New York clearly prefers Taylor over him. In the first two games, Taylor played 78 snaps, while Sadiq appeared in 55.
Still, it’s early to say whether he’ll play next week against the Patriots, but hopefully Sadiq returns to full health soon.
Darrell Jackson Jr. had remained relatively quiet through the first four games. In 85 defensive snaps, Jackson recorded seven tackles and zero pressures.
With David Onyemata on injured reserve, the Jets hoped that the former Florida State Seminole would step up in his absence. Against Cleveland, Jackson finally emerged.
The 2026 fourth-round selection made his presence felt against the Browns, recording four tackles, a sack, two pressures, and two pass deflections in 29 defensive snaps.
This was Jackson’s best all-around game by far. If he can replicate similar success against New England, it’ll be hard to take away his reps once Onyemata returns.
One of the key matchups heading into this game was Azareye’h Thomas versus Denzel Boston.
Boston quickly emerged as quarterback Deshaun Watson’s favorite target downfield, hauling in 13 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Limiting him and his big-play ability was critical if New York was to win.
Thomas did his part, as Boston didn’t record a catch when lined up against him. For the day, Thomas allowed just two receptions (five targets) for 28 yards, earning a 76.4 coverage grade, per PFF .
Not only has Thomas excelled in coverage, but he’s also played well against the run, earning a 68.7 run-defense grade, ranking 41st among 102 cornerbacks.
With his play so far, the former Florida State Seminole continues to prove he’s among the Jets’ best foundational pieces.
David Bailey has had an up-and-down start to his rookie season.
He was generating pressure in the first two games, recording eight pressures and two sacks. In the last two games, however, Bailey logged just three pressures.
Against the Browns, the former Texas Tech star pass rusher finally had his breakout game.
Bailey dominated Cleveland’s offensive line, registering eight pressures and three sacks, earning an 85.4 coverage grade, per PFF .
He was the best player on the field for the Jets. With New York going up against its division rival next week, Gang Green will need the No. 2 overall pick to be just as impactful to win.
Offensive linemen don’t get the same love as skill players, but they also play a critical role in team success.
This season,…

title: The Biggest Decision Aaron Glenn Got Right Against Browns (And What It Means Moving Forward)
full_text:
There was no doubt coming off three consecutive losses that Sunday's game against the Browns was one the Jets desperately needed to win to stop the bleeding. It was a sloppy affair in rainy conditions, but New York prevailed in a 17-12 season-saving win in a hard-fought game.
Unlike recent weeks when the Jets got off to slow starts and put themselves behind before even getting into the thick of the game, they scored on their opening drive and immediately took control on Sunday. The stagnant offense that has ultimately plagued OC Frank Reich's group was on display again with five consecutive punts afterward, but it was an encouraging win overall that showed this team's resiliency and ability to rise to the occasion when a game is on the line.
While it was clear Reich learned from his recent mistakes and made it a priority to get WR1 Garrett Wilson more involved in the offense with seven receptions (on 11 targets) for 104 yards and a TD, head coach Aaron Glenn put together a masterful game plan defensively following a rough stretch full of disciplinary issues and a failure to perform in four-minute offense.
Those concerns are still palpable after committing 10 penalties for 102 yards and struggling to close out each half on Sunday, but Glenn's focus on overloading the box and creating pressure up front set the tone for the entire game as both teams battled the elements.
It was just one game, but Glenn and his coaching staff put together a solid plan when they needed a win the most. The schedule is only going to get tougher going forward, but a 2-3 record is much better than 1-4 and Glenn's defensive approach had a lot to do with the success the Jets were able to have.
Although the Browns entered the game on a three-game winning streak and in possession of the AFC North lead, there were still some doubts about their run game and whether quarterback Deshaun Watson could continue to play at a high level on a weekly basis.
Throw in the sloppy conditions, and it was a perfect storm for the Jets to tweak their identity defensively and focus more on creating pressure up front instead of relying on sitting back in conservative coverage.
After combining for just three sacks the last two weeks, the Jets went off for eight of them on Sunday, three of which came from rookie David Bailey. His third sack of the game (h/t NFL) took place early in the fourth quarter with the Jets leading 10-6 and the Browns facing a 3rd-and-30 after Jarvis Brownlee Jr.'s first career sack and a delay of game put them well behind the chains.
THIRD sack of the day for David Bailey @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QTqQqo79NN
In addition to the constant pressure and the long-awaited breakout game from Bailey , the Jets made sure to limit Cleveland's run game and force Watson to beat them through the air on a rainy day at MetLife Stadium. That decision proved fruitful as the Browns were held in check to just 96 rush yards and an average of four yards per carry.
That was a huge improvement after giving up 131 rush yards to the Lions and a whopping 232 to the Bears last week. When you combine the lack of success stopping the run on one side with the inability to sustain drives and create a balanced attack offensively, it has not been a good recipe for success in recent weeks for the Jets.
This was also the third time in five games this season that New York has allowed fewer than 200 yards in a game. While they had no answers for the Lions and Bears, the Jets are the first team to accomplish the feat since the 1999 Buccaneers after failing to hold any team under 200 yards all of last season, per ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini (h/t ESPN Research).
This is the 1st time in #Jets history that they held 3 of their first 5 opponents under 200 yards. Happened zero times last season. First team to do it since the 1999 Bucs via ESPN Research
There are still some concerns with Reich's offense getting stagnant and the lack of involvement from the tight ends once again, but Glenn seemed to find a blueprint that can give this team a better chance defensively and get Bailey more involved on each play.
From Bailey, Jowon Briggs, Will McDonald IV and Darrell Jackson Jr. recording sacks up front and Brownlee and safety Dane Belton contributing as well, it was a collective effort that featured a 52% blitz percentage and a 69.2% pressure rate. That prevented Cleveland from establishing any rhythm and forced it into uncomfortable situations early.
As the Jets prepare for their first AFC East competition of the season when they head to Gillette Stadium to face the Patriots on Sunday, Glenn made his seat a little less hot by executing a solid game plan defensively and getting his team back in the win column.
Maybe it had to do with his decision to switch out the Wednesday practice for a walkthrough to make sure his team was fresh for the upcoming stretch, but it still came down to execution and putting a strong effort together on the field.
Even though the Patriots have not had the start to the season they expected at just 3-2, particularly due to the turnover woes from QB Drake Maye, the 2025 MVP runner-up has responded the last two weeks and went off for five TDs in Sunday's win over the Raiders. His elusiveness in the pocket will be something that Glenn and this defense must be prepared for, even if he is tied with Justin Herbert for the most interceptions thrown (seven).
Discipline and ball security remain an issue, but the decision to lean on the pass rush and impose their will up front was key to Glenn and the Jets having success in the rain against the Browns. Sticking with that approach needs to be a bigger priority going forward, especially against someone like Maye who has been turnover-prone this season.

title: Jets Week 5 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Encouraging Win Over Browns
full_text:
There were a lot of concerns for the New York Jets coming into Week 5 as injuries continued to mount in Gotham. That said, they got off to a much quicker start this time around and showed some positive signs in a sloppy 17-12 win over the Browns on a rain-soaked day.
The Jets faced a Browns team coming in that led the AFC North with a 4-1 record and looked much better than in recent years. The Jets humbled them and didn't allow a single touchdown until the fourth quarter. On top of that, New York possessed the ball longer than Cleveland and had better balance on both sides of the ball, unlike the disastrous and historically bad Week 4 loss to the Bears.
While it was easy to overreact to the Jets ' play through the first four games, the three-game losing streak is now behind them after an encouraging outing at MetLife Stadium. With that in mind, let's hand out some grades for each unit ahead of a Week 6 road trip to face the Patriots.
In a game where the elements were not the greatest, Geno Smith was 17-of-30 for 182 yards with one TD and zero interceptions. It was a much better performance than the one he and this offense put together last week, and he even marched the Jets down the field for an opening-drive TD. However, five consecutive punts ensued, and the momentum completely evaporated.
Smith took four sacks in the game and struggled to maintain a consistent aerial attack for New York following the opening drive. He also committed a costly sack-fumble after taking the Jets across midfield, which would've put them in position to answer Cleveland's go-ahead score in the fourth.
It looked like offensive coordinator Frank Reich took it upon himself to get WR Garrett Wilson more involved in the offense on Sunday. One week after recording three catches for 27 yards, Wilson led the team with seven catches (on 11 targets) for 104 yards and a 32-yard score that featured a sick spin move (h/t NFL on CBS).
Garrett Wilson hit the spin move in the open field for a 32-yard TD 🔥 pic.twitter.com/zr5HMfta1b
Wilson's role was even more important as the Jets continue to be plagued by injuries to their WR room. He did his part and elevated the unit when it needed it most. But with Tim Patrick (two catches for 26 yards) and Isaiah Williams (one catch for 16 yards) providing limited contributions, the lack of reliable depth was still on display.
This group has been a mixed bag so far, and it didn't change this week. Mason Taylor returned from a thumb injury on Sunday and came down with three catches for 24 yards. Elsewhere, production was relatively nonexistent. Rookie Kenyon Sadiq recorded two receptions for just three yards, while Jelani Woods received one target.
For Sadiq, who had a career day two weeks ago against the Lions and has looked like a first-round draft steal , it was far from the game he was looking for after committing a fumble inside the 10-yard line and exiting with a concussion. The TE group is even more important until the Jets can get fully healthy at wideout, and Sunday was nowhere near where they need to be.
After an earlier report in the week suggested Breece Hall might not play against the Browns, the Jets were officially without him for Sunday's game as he continues to deal with a right quad injury. While that didn't seem like the best news considering how the Jets struggled to run the ball last week, Braelon Allen went off for 24 carries, 116 yards, and a TD.
Allen's highlight of the game took place in the fourth quarter when he scored the game-winning 22-yard TD late in the fourth quarter (h/t NFL).
Braelon Allen gives the @nyjets the lead! @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HRPQHqjGMd
He averaged 4.8 yards per carry and consistently moved the chains for the Jets, which was something they struggled with one week ago when they went 0-of-7 on third down and could not sustain a drive. Isaiah Davis only received two carries for eight yards, and there was no explosiveness outside of Allen. But his breakout performance is exactly what the Jets needed with Hall on the sidelines.
A lot of credit goes to the Jets' offensive line for opening running lanes for the ground game to explode for 134 yards and a TD, even without Hall behind them. That said, their pass protection left a lot to be desired again, allowing Smith to get sacked four times and frequently pressured from the opening kick.
That shouldn't be a huge surprise, given the Browns were tied for the fifth-most sacks (12) and were sixth in QB pressure percentage (40.4%) coming into Week 5. Still, this offensive line gave up four sacks and has allowed at least three in each of the last four games. Dylan Parham's absence (knee) certainly did not help, but the pass protection must be better moving forward.
This unit went from being arguably the worst in the Week 4 loss to Chicago to the best in Gang Green on Sunday, as it completely had its way in the trenches. For starters, the Jets were much better against the run with only 96 yards. However, their pass rush made all the difference.
In addition to holding Browns QB Deshaun Watson to just 15-of-33 for 155 yards and keeping him out of rhythm, the Jets recorded eight sacks, including three from rookie David Bailey. Jowon Briggs, Darrell Jackson Jr., and Will McDonald IV each had a sack as well. ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini noted after the game that the eight total sacks are "tied for their most in any game in the last 40 seasons."
Jets: 8 sacks (tied for their most in any game in the last 40 seasons, most in a game since 2024 Week 9 vs HOU, 8) #Jets
It was even fitting that McDonald's sack fumble ended the game with just under one minute remaining. The defensive line has struggled to impose its will this season. But Sunday's performance showed what it is capable of and why Bailey, specifically, was selected with the No. 2 pick as someone who could develop into a star in the league .
The LB corps was also instrumental in keeping Cleveland's run game in check, holding Quinshon Judkins to just 3.1 yards per carry. Jamien Sherwood led the way with four total tackles (three solo), one pass defended, and one QB hit, while Demario Davis tacked on four more tackles and a QB hit.
Trevin Wallace was also sharp in coverage and contributed to a strong collective effort from the unit overall. The Browns posed some concerns entering the game on a three-game winning streak, but the Jets held their own and prevented them from establishing any consistency. The LBs were instrumental in that success, especially with their impact plays in the biggest moments.
Aside from one late touchdown pass from Watson to rookie WR Denzel Boston, the secondary was solid in more ways than one. Dane Belton led the whole team with eight tackles (three solo), one sack, one tackle for loss, and one QB hit. Jarvis Brownlee Jr., meanwhile, recorded his first career sack (h/t Jets) just one week after going into concussion protocol.
first career sack for Jarvis Brownlee Jr. 💪 📺: CBS, @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/v1mdZ75lek
Minkah Fitzpatrick, on the other hand, received multiple penalties, one of which was called for unnecessary roughness after colliding with Browns WR KC Concepcion. While those actions rightfully drew scrutiny, the secondary displayed strong coverage and kept the Browns from establishing a rhythm downfield and up front.
Kicker Jason Sanders came to play in the rain, making both of his extra-point attempts and drilling a 54-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter. Punter Austin McNamara was solid again, averaging 42.6 yards per punt and pinning the Browns inside the 20 on three punts. Lastly, Trevin Wallace recovered a botched punt snap from the Browns, which ultimately led to the go-ahead score on the following drive.
The return game was nothing special, but it was still solid. Kene Nwangwu and Williams combined to average 26 yards per kick return. Williams mustered 16.8 yards per punt return and failed to give the Jets a true…

title: Jets Week 5 Awards: 10 Winners After Hard-Fought Win Over Browns
full_text:
The New York Jets could have rolled over after last week's humiliating loss to the Chicago Bears . At 1-3, most fans even questioned whether their head coach would last until the halfway point of the season.
But then Sunday came. New York's roster played inspired, tough football en route to a comeback 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns. Their record is now 2-3.
"Our guys fought," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said. "That was the last thing that we pointed out as far as our prep for the week, just to make sure we have a finish mentality, and it was good to see our guys go out there and finish the game."
As always, we have awards to give out. And on this victory Monday, there's plenty to celebrate.
This was the breakout fans were waiting for. After four games and two sacks, Jets fans were hoping to see a more impactful Bailey as the second-overall pick in the 2026 draft.
Boy, did Bailey ever deliver.
The former Texas Tech product notched three sacks and was easily New York's best player on the field. His impact was felt not just on passing downs, but he was excellent against the run. He's now at five sacks for the season and well on his way to winning Defensive Rookie of the Year.
"I’ve said it all along that his time is going to come," Glenn said. "I have all the confidence in him in the world. He did a good job today. He did a good job."
As good as Bailey is, though, the youngster continues to have his eyes on a greater prize.
"It felt good," Bailey said. "It felt good to know that to do this, to compete against the highest level, and I'm just proud of my d-line. I'm proud of the defense as a whole to come together."
New York's special teams came through on Sunday. First, Jason Sanders hit a 54-yard field goal to start the fourth quarter. Sanders has been quite an asset this season despite a poor training camp.
Then came the pivotal moment. New York fell on a fumbled punt snap, putting the offense in scoring distance. They cashed in on the mistake and came away with the win. It was the kind of game that reminded Jets fans how good their special teams units have been.
A bad snap on the punt and the @nyjets special teams take advantage @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/b0h70NGAn1
"That’s complementary football, and that’s something that I talked to our guys about this morning in our team meeting in here of making sure that we complement each other," Glenn said.
Should New York get that kind of special teams production, it will only help them steal some wins down the stretch.
We'll get to how good Garrett Wilson was in a moment. The biggest surprise from the Jets in Week 5 was their running game, particularly Braelon Allen .
The former fourth-round pick had his first 100-yard (116) game on 24 carries and set the tone with his punishing running style. Allen's performance changed the perception of how the offense operated.
"I thought Braelon played outstanding," Geno Smith said. "I thought the offensive line did a tremendous job at controlling the line of scrimmage up front and really giving us an opportunity to control the clock and run the ball well. It was needed today, and I thought everyone did a great job."
New York's offensive line certainly deserves credit, but it was Allen who bounced off tackles at a high clip.
"My job is easy at the end of the day," Allen said. "Hit the hole hard and don’t get tackled. So, it was a lot of fun."
This was the breakout performance New York was waiting for from him. And it couldn't have come at a better time.
Seven catches, 104 yards, and a dynamic touchdown that gave the Jets an early 7-0 lead.
Yeah, you don't need to look at anything else to show how good Wilson is as a receiver. The veteran wideout was the catalyst for New York's passing offense again and remains the key cog in making sure the group is consistent throughout the game.
3 catches for 70 yards and a TD for @GarrettWilson_V on the @nyjets opening drive. pic.twitter.com/4BQ4YGzdNY
It's no accident that Wilson has been productive in New York's wins this season.
"Everyone that put their effort towards this win," Wilson said. "It's what it's all about, and that's the feeling we're hunting every weekend. It felt good."
He deserves his flowers. Wilson is well on his way to a 100-catch, 1,000-yard, and 10-touchdown season.
If the Jets had lost to the Browns on Sunday, it would have been hard to see where the next few wins would come from. That's what made their victory so important. On paper, the team could theoretically beat both the Dolphins and Raiders on their upcoming schedule.
If an eventual loss to the Patriots is mixed in there (as many expect), the Jets will walk into the second half of the season with a record of 4-4. Far better than they were last season.
Even if their coach has a different mindset.
"We don’t think negatively like that," Glenn said. "We just think each week, we move on, and we have to win the game."
Negative or not, Glenn desperately needed that victory. Now, the team has to build on it.
There's only one word to describe how good the Jets' defensive line was on Sunday:
Eight sacks, a 52% blitz percentage, and a 69.2 pressure rate. We've talked about Bailey and how good he was, but it was a collective effort of dominance brought forth by the Jets' defense.
And Glenn loved every moment of it.
"Each week is different. And I’ve got to do a good job of making sure I create things like that," Glenn said. "We have to continue to do that, and it takes a lot of work to be able to get that done, and the thing is we’ve got guys that can actually rush the passer."
When it comes to Jets home games in which it rains, I'll leave it to wide receiver Tim Patrick to explain.
"It wasn't the best conditions," Patrick said. "I'm learning New Jersey, it only rains on Sundays here."
On Sunday, it appeared the rain actually helped the Jets in this one due to the Browns' mistakes where it mattered most. Still, it must be annoying for players and fans that the weather continues to be poor whenever the Jets are set to play at home.
New York's four-minute offensive drought ended at the end of the game, but it was more due to the Browns making a critical special teams mistake than to the offense moving the ball down the field. Penalties and poor situational awareness continue to hurt this group where it matters most.
This offense has been poor in the final four minutes of the first half. There must be drastic improvement going forward.
With Mason Taylor returning to the field this week, the hope was that his skill set would add a new wrinkle to the team's tight end room. The expectation was that he would pair nicely with first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq.
None of that happened, though. Sadiq caught two passes for three yards, and Taylor saw three receptions for 24 yards. Also, to make matters worse, Sadiq fumbled the ball in the red zone and had to leave the game with a concussion.
It hasn't been the best collective year for New York's tight end room. They'll need it to be better moving forward.
It wasn't Stephens' worst game, but it certainly wasn't his best based on how he's played over the first four games of the season. New York saw Stephens ranked as a top-15 cornerback in the league.
In Cleveland's lone touchdown drive, though, Stephens was called for a pass interference penalty, along with giving up a 29-yard touchdown catch. Stephens will need to shake off this performance because of how well he was doing beforehand.
But at the same time, Sunday was not one of his best.
