title: 5 Studs & 3 Duds in Jets' Season-Saving Win Over Browns in Week 5
full_text:
It wasn't pretty. It wasn't sexy.
But at the end of the day, a win in the NFL counts the same no matter how it was achieved. The New York Jets understand that better than anyone after their 17-12 comeback victory over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.
In a rain-soaked contest in which the Jets tried to end a three-game losing streak, New York outplayed the AFC North-leading Browns before a 29-yard touchdown pass from Deshaun Watson to Denzel Boston gave Cleveland the lead in the final quarter.
After a Jets fumble, the Browns fumbled the snap on a punt, setting up Gang Green's offense to take the lead for good. Now, at 2-3, the Jets will try to build on this win.
And there were plenty of studs that helped them along the way.
When a team drafts a player with one of the top five picks in an NFL Draft, the hope is that they will have a "Welcome to the NFL" moment, a game where he proves exactly why he is a top prospect in the league. After four weeks, Jets fans were getting impatient that second-overall pick David Bailey hadn't had that moment .
Bailey was the best player on the field on Sunday, totaling three sacks, four quarterback hits, and seven pressures. Even better, Bailey made several excellent plays against the run that stymied the Browns' rushing attack.
So far this season, Bailey has recorded five sacks and leads the team in pressures. On Sunday, he proved why the Jets made him the second overall pick.
After missing the last two games, Mason Taylor returned and added another wrinkle to their offense. Many wondered how Taylor's play would mix with first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq.
Overall, though, the tight end position was quite disappointing on Sunday.
Taylor caught just three passes for 24 yards. He laid some strong blocks in the running game, but needs to be more impactful in the passing game. The day wasn't much better for Sadiq either. The rookie made two catches for three yards and lost a fumble in the red zone. In fairness to him, he did get hit hard and had to leave the game with a concussion. But a turnover like that cannot happen.
New York will need more impact plays from this tight end room.
How about the Jets kicker? The weather was atrocious, and Jason Sanders was abysmal all training camp. Yet at the start of the fourth quarter, Sanders nailed a 54-yard field goal in the pouring rain. It was an important field goal, as it put the team within striking distance when the Browns responded with a touchdown.
So far this season, Sanders has been quite good so far this season. He looked like his old All-Pro self.
The drought finally ended, but it's not like the team has seemingly turned the corner with their four-minute offense. The only reason the Jets finally got the job done after going eight straight games without scoring in the final four minutes of the first half and regulation was Cleveland's fumbled punt.
They executed enough to score a touchdown, but they failed to score going into halftime after committing several penalties again, and they couldn't even drain the clock when they got the ball back with the lead in the closing minutes of action. Just because the defense wrapped the game up on its own doesn't excuse the offense.
The group needs to be better when it matters most.
Several young players had great games for the Jets. Chief among them was running back Braelon Allen . He went over 100 yards on 24 carries, including the game-winner from 23 yards out. His best run, though, came when he ran over a Brown and broke it outside for a big gain.
This performance showed how good Allen could be going forward. Getting him to run downhill changes how this running game could look. In fact, this was the best he's looked in his career.
I wouldn't say Stephens had a bad game. However, I'd say he was beaten on the two plays that mattered most at the time. He was called for pass interference on Cleveland's last scoring drive that kept the ball in the Browns' hands.
He also gave up the touchdown in single coverage. If the Browns hadn't fumbled their punt and the Jets hadn't scored, Stephens' play would be highlighted worse than people realize.
For the most part, though, the former Baltimore Raven has been quite good this season. He'll need to be better on Sunday, though.
Garrett Wilson had another dominant game. Ho hum - it must be Sunday.
Wilson's seven-catch, 104-yard day led the way for New York's offense, which included a 32-yard touchdown in which Wilson spun away from a would-be tackler to get into the end zone. He is New York's best offensive weapon and remains the go-to guy this season .
New York's pass rush was exceptional on Sunday. As a collective unit, they recorded eight sacks. Even with how good the group was, though, fourth-round rookie Darrell Jackson Jr. really stood out on his own.
The Florida State product recorded his first career sack on Sunday, but he also had two pass deflections late in the fourth quarter. If he continues to play as he did on Sunday, he will become a consistent player on New York's interior defensive line.
And one of the better late-round picks made in the last few years.
Thomas could have had a game-ending interception on the final drive, but he'll have to settle for a key pass breakup. So far this season, the second-year cornerback has played very well and easily looked like the team's best cornerback on Sunday.
His size and physicality are a perfect fit for the blitz-heavy approach that the Jets want to run with Aaron Glenn. If Thomas continues to perform like he has this season, it will only enhance the team's outlook moving forward.

title: Eagles' Biggest Strength Has Suddenly Become a Major Concern
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — For years, the Eagles’ offensive line has been the foundation of the organization’s sustained success.
That began to erode last season, and the once-dominant group derailed early in the 2026 campaign with injuries continuing to chip away at veteran Pro Bowl selections Landon Dickerson and Cam Jurgens, with the latter having since been traded to Baltimore. Meanwhile, future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson retired and Jurgens’ replacement at center, Drew Kendall, is dealing with a knee injury that cost him Sunday’s loss against Jacksonville in London.
The replacements – Willie Lampkin at left guard, Jake Majors at center and Markel Bell at right tackle – struggled mightily against the Jags.
The period of rapid transition, and the team’s ability to stay competitive in what’s shaping up as a flawed NFC East will hinge in large part on whether the young, lightly experienced group can develop quickly enough to hold the fort.
Moving forward, that trio is likely to remain part of the conversation—either as starters or high-leverage depth—until Dickerson returns, GM Howie Roseman adds reinforcements, or more likely, both.
Lampkin, the 5-foot-11 interior lineman who has drawn praise for his leverage and physicality since training camp, and Majors, the undrafted former Texas center who spent most of last season on the practice squad, almost have to be short-term responses to the attrition.
Bell, the third-round rookie drafted as a potential long-term successor at right tackle, is already in line to hold that spot for the foreseeable future following Johnson’s departure.
The combination represents a stark departure from the veteran-laden lines that fueled recent Eagles success.
Jordan Mailata remains the clear veteran anchor at left tackle but was withered by what he called a “week from hell” in response to Johnson and Jurgens being removed from the locker room on consecutive days. Tyler Steen has provided continuity at right guard, but the other three spots have been an issue, especially in pass protection.
Dickerson is eligible to return as early as this week against the Carolina Panthers, which would allow the Eagles to reinsert an established left guard. However, it may be a leap to expect Dickerson to regain his previous standard. Kendall is also expected to re-enter the mix once healthy.
Until those pieces return and prove durable, however, Lampkin, Majors, and Bell are the primary options available to coach Nick Sirianni and the staff.
The reliance on three players with this kind of minimal combined starting experience creates a very narrow margin for error as the Eagles try to reverse their early-season trajectory.
Roseman has long prioritized offensive line depth and has indicated the team remains focused on competing this year . To do that, additional investment on the offensive line will be needed.

title: Eagles' Snap Counts vs. Jaguars:  Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 5
full_text:
It was a game the Eagles deserved to lose, then suddenly, a game they deserved to win, only to lose in the end on a 57-yard field goal as time expired in a 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London on Sunday. The loss left the Eagles at 2-3, their first time below .500 since Nick Sirianni’s first year as the head coach in 2021.
Here are five observations from the snap counts:
The Eagles’ young offensive linemen got a heavy dose of experience by playing all 62 offensive snaps. They had combined for just 64 in their careers. Bell, of course, is a third-round rookie, but Lampkin and Majors were undrafted, and these were their first career starts. There is still developmental work to be done, and continuity and chemistry to build, but those things take time.
“These are three young players that we have a ton of confidence in,” said OC Sean Mannion. “They're talented. They're getting their first taste of real action. I think they're going to keep getting better. We feel good about the depth of this group while we're kind of weathering the storm through some of these injuries.”
With Dallas Goedert back after missing two games with a knee injury, the Eagles don’t seem invested in getting Ertz many reps. He got seven in London, and he is out of practice squad elevations, so if the Eagles want to keep him, they need to add him to the 53-man roster this week, cut him, or leave him on the practice squad. He needs eight more catches to set the franchise record for career receptions.
The receiver played a career-high 53 snaps. He has made the most of his reps all year, with four touchdowns on just seven catches, making him the first receiver in Eagles history to have four TDs in the first five games since Jeremy Maclin in 2014.
Davis was given a huge raise in the offseason, but his snap count is on the low side. He got just 35 on Sunday. Vic Fangio talked last week about trying to get him more time, but said this week that the defense was in a lot of nickel.
“Not much base, which only two of those guys play, so it kind of becomes three for two with him, [Moro] Ojomo, and Jalen [Carter]," said Fangio. "So those three, and then when you add the other two guys, it's going to spread it out some.”
He spent his whole career as a slot cornerback, but Moore was thrust into a safety role after Michael Carter left with an abdominal injury. Moore played 44 snaps and made five tackles.
“When you consider the lack of background, he's never played safety in his career, gets here after training camp, limited reps with our defense, he's getting some in scout team, I thought he did a pretty damn good job considering the circumstances,” said Fangio.

title: McMullen: Eagles Shouldn’t Bench Jihaad Campbell (Upside Is Too High)
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Vic Fangio spent part of Tuesday doing what defensive coordinators often do when reporters start sniffing around a lineup change: clarifying, downplaying, and perhaps even adding some revisionism to what's going on at the linebacker position in Philadelphia.
Yes, the Eagles planned to get Jeremiah Trotter Jr. on the field for some snaps opposite Zack Baun against the Jaguars in London .
The Eagles’ defensive coordinator confirmed as much at his weekly press briefing on Tuesday. However, Fangio said there was no plan to start Trotter over Campbell—a claim the veteran defensive mind called “an out-and-out lie.”
The new rotation never got off the ground after Trotter was ejected after scuffling with Jacksonville linebacker Bryan Thomas Jr. on the opening kickoff.
Because of circumstances, Campbell started in and finished the 19-17 loss to the Jags, playing 62 of the 72 defensive snaps. His 47.6 overall grade on Pro Football Focus was not impressive , and when asked about the second-year player’s performance by Eagles On SI, Fangio claimed Campbell “played okay.”
That’s not a ringing endorsement coming off the news that Trotter has earned more playing time with a nice performance against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4.
It’s also not a reason to start treating a 22-year-old 2025 first-round pick like a developmental project who’s running out of runway, or at least it shouldn’t be.
Campbell arrived in Philadelphia with the kind of size, speed, and length that make personnel executives take notice (6-foot-3, 235 lbs, and a 4.52-second 40-yard dash). The Alabama product also produced as a rookie when given the chance, posting 80 tackles, an interception, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery while earning All-Rookie recognition and grading out as the No. 15 of 88 LBs ranked by PFF .
This season, the PFF grades are shaky (No. 61 of 72), and coverage has been an issue at times. That’s real. It’s also the normal growing-pain portion of a young linebacker’s career, not a referendum on Campbell's ceiling.
Trotter, a more instinctive but less athletic option, has earned more playing time . Fangio is right about that. When Baun was out against the Rams, the local legacy as the son of the "Axe Man," Jeremiah Trotter Sr., filled in and delivered a 15-tackle day.
Fangio is a stickler for fundamentals and discipline, so it’s no surprise he seems to be gravitating toward the safer option who understands the scheme better.
A series-based rotation that keeps both fresh and gives Fangio a different look could be smart football and good roster management. However, linebacker is typically not a rotational position, so this can’t turn into a soft benching or even a signal that Campbell is on a short leash.
The Eagles moved on from the popular Nakobe Dean in free agency specifically to clear a path for Campbell. They traded up to draft him. They have already seen the traits—range, closing speed, the ability to blitz from different spots—that made him a first-round investment.
Linebackers who combine that athletic profile with the mental processing required in a Fangio defense do not grow on trees. You don’t accelerate that process by taking away snaps and eroding the confidence of a potential difference-maker.
Fangio has been careful not to draw comparisons to previous situations, like veteran Oren Burks holding off Trotter when Dean was injured on the road to Super Bowl LIX.
Campbell is not Dean, but he’s younger and more explosive, while still learning the nuances of Fangio’s complicated scheme.
Young players with Campbell’s upside improve when they play, not when they watch. Competition is healthy; the systematic reduction of a role is how you waste a draft pick.

title: Eagles' Michael Clay Reveals Thoughts on Ill-Fated Kickoff in London
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Leaks were springing up everywhere, and Michael Clay did his best to patch them anyway he could—chewing gum, an index finger, a thumb, personnel changes—yes, the last one.
The Eagles’ special teams coordinator was already without a couple of players on his unit, players who had been ruled out before kickoff against the Jaguars at London’s Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in Week 5. He then lost Jeremiah Trotter, Jr., when he was ejected on the opening kickoff; then Will Shipley and Michael Carter went out with injuries early in the game .
It’s not an excuse. It’s just the reality of the situation. It’s why head coach Nick Sirianni’s decision not to let Jake Elliott kick the ball out of the end zone right after the Eagles took a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left to play was so mystifying.
“You respect anybody that's going out there to jump on the grenade,” Clay said about what it meant to him that Sirianni turned himself into the fall guy. “But it's not just him. He takes a lot of heat, which I respect, but, obviously, I'm the special teams coordinator here, and we didn't get the job done."
Clay was juggling personnel throughout. He was on the sideline just before the ill-fated kickoff that led to the kickoff return that set up the Jags’ walk-off win on a 57-yard field goal by Cam Little.
“You're just trying to move around puzzle pieces,” Clay said. “You try to put personnel in your best spot. I think you saw I moved Kelee (Ringo) from the one to the four to the five, tried to put our best players in certain spots to make some plays. At times it worked out, and in the one spot that it didn't, it burned us, and that's on me as a coach.”
Jonathan Jones played a lot of special teams during his 11-year career, but not so many special teams snaps since 2022. He was on the final kickoff return, which was just his fourth special teams snap of the game. The cornerback played just three snaps in last week’s loss to the Rams.
So, he may have been one of those break-glass-in-case-of-emergency players Clay ran out there for the final kickoff.
Jones made the tackle, but had to chase Ameer Abdullah from behind to make the play. The irony is that if he had taken one second longer to bring Abdullah to the ground, time would have expired and the Eagles would be 3-2, not 2-3.
That’s a tough ask for any player in that situation, however.
“When you're in the heat of the moment, you're in full trail mode (you’re just thinking), ‘Let me get this guy down,’” Clay said. “I don't think anybody's gonna look up at the clock simultaneously then get the guy down who's running full speed ahead. An extra second off at some point in the game—you're not talking about this—but it would have been a perfect storm to happen.
“You know, they played well for 59 minutes, and the last eight seconds we didn't; we didn't do our job in terms of the kickoff coverage. At times, we got too deep in our coverage, didn't get off blocks, didn't make tackles when we needed to, and that's more on myself than anything else.”

title: Eagles Edge Hopes Hinging on Jalyx Hunt 'Miracle' and Jonathan Greenard Return
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – It didn’t look good when Jalyx Hunt’s left leg got bent backward, and he landed on it during the final play of the first half in London on Sunday. It wasn’t.
“It'll be pretty miraculous for Jalyx to play this week,” said defensive coordinator Vic Fangio on Tuesday as the Eagles begin preparation to host the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
It sounds, however, like Hunt could be pushing to make a miracle happen.
“He's gonna be pushing the envelope and making the medical people clear him,” said Fangio. “He's not gonna be one of those guys that's gonna be hesitant to come back.”
Hunt stayed down on the field after the injury, as players and coaches exited through the tunnels at halftime. A cart was brought out to help him, but he chose to be helped off, leaning on two members of the training staff and keeping weight off his injured leg.
Fangio's comment about pushing the envelope to play could be read as a shot at Jonathan Greenard. Listed as questionable heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars, Greenard tried to test his injured ankle before kickoff at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The team’s trainers and Howie Roseman met with Greenard in the end zone, and the outside linebacker looked to be shaking his head back and forth, seemingly indicating he wouldn’t be able to play.
So, he missed yet another game, and he has played in just two of the team’s five games this season.
“Hopefully he'll be ready to go this week, but we gotta see,” said Fangio.
If he can’t, and Hunt doesn’t create a miracle, the Eagles' edge group will be down to Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa. The Eagles also have Mason Reiger and Joshua Weru on the practice squad.
Reiger, who played at Louisville, was signed as an undrafted free agent by the Miami Dolphins after the draft, but was released with an injury. Weru had a nice preseason, but he had never played football until signing with the Eagles via the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Growing up in Kenya, Weru played rugby.
Neither player, however, are Hunt or Greenard.
Hunt has yet to unleash the potential he showed during training camp in August and is looking for his first sack. Still, he is good at providing pressure on a quarterback and setting an edge in the run game.
Greenard was acquired in the offseason to replace Jaelan Phillips, whom the Eagles tried to re-sign in free agency, but he instead chose a better deal with the Panthers. Phillips has sacks in back-to-back games and has played 70 percent of the defensive snaps for Carolina.
“Greenard was gonna take a lot of (Phillips’ playing time and production), and unfortunately, he got hurt in our weight room before training camp started, missed all of camp, missed the first few games,” said Fangio. “Just started practicing and then got the ankle injury. So that was gonna be a big piece of it.”

title: More Bad News On Eagles' Injury Front: Will Shipley Will Miss Time
full_text:
If the Eagles are going to dig out of this three-game losing streak that has left them below .500 for the first time in five years, they are going to have to find a way to do it with running backs who started the season on their practice squad, because Will Shipley is expected to miss a couple of weeks.
ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during Sunday’s loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and could miss multiple weeks.
The injury likely happened on Shipley’s first regular-season touchdown run, a 2-yard burst up the middle behind Willie Lampkin that tied the score at 7-7 in the second quarter of what would become a 19-17 loss to the Jags in London. He was done after just 13 snaps, leaving Dameon Pierce to man the backfield duties alone.
Pierce was added to the 53-man roster on Oct. 7. He has 45 games of experience. In his Eagles debut, he averaged 1.3 yards on 11 carries for 14 yards.
“We've had our eye on him for a very long time, since he came out of college,” said head coach Nick Sirianni, on the same day he and his team flew to England. “When you go through a draft, you only get, what, six, seven, eight picks or whatever it is that year?
“There’re a lot of guys you end up loving that it's like, 'Oh man, he's going to be good for them.' …He brings constant energy to the football team. He's obviously a very talented player and works extremely hard and runs extremely hard. I'm excited for his opportunity.”
The Eagles, who placed Tank Bigsby on injured reserve last week, need to cross their fingers that Saquon Barkley can return for Sunday’s visit from the Carolina Panthers.
Barkley missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury suffered early in the Week 4 loss to the Rams. The running back, who just two years ago ran for more than 2,000 yards and helped the Eagles win a Super Bowl, is averaging 5.1 yards per carry when he’s been able to play, but he’s only played 91 snaps through five weeks.
He’s already had a stinger that sidelined him early against the Titans in Week 2, and now he’s dealing with his latest setback. When he returns, he will find an entirely different offensive line blocking for him, with Lane Johnson retired and Cam Jurgens traded.
Carson Steele was elevated from the practice squad for the game and perhaps he may need to play a bigger role in the short-term.
Steele has fullback experience, so it was somewhat surprising that he didn’t have any offensive role against the Jaguars as a lead blocker, especially with an offensive line that is still trying to build continuity and chemistry. He got 20 snaps on special teams.

title: Eagles Report Card: Grading Every Position Group and Head Coach After Five Games
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles have lost three in a row and, at 2-3, are under .500 for the first time in five years. The grades won’t look pretty on the team’s report card, and perhaps a litany of injuries is the reason.
Still, the offense has been dreadful in the second half. It's averaging 4.6 points, 97.4 total yards, and has 5 three-and-outs. All three stats are last in the NFL.
Here grades for each position and the head coach:
After looking like an MVP in the first two games, leading a game-winning touchdown drive that ended in a touchdown pass with just nine seconds left against the Titans, Jalen Hurts’ play has dropped. He hasn’t taken to Sean Mannion’s overhaul of the offense as quickly as one would have hoped, and he doesn’t always seem to see the entire field. His rebuilt offensive line could be part of that, but his decision-making hasn’t been where it needs to be, and his completion rate is a career-low 57.8 percent.
His ability to pick up yards with his legs has been neutralized, rushing only 23 times – most of that on scrambles from the pocket – 101 yards and one TD.
Still, he gets credit for his eight touchdowns to just three interceptions, as well as the job he did in the first two wins.
Saquon Barkley has been hurt early in two games and missed one already. At 29, can he rebound and still help this team when he gets healthy?
Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, and Will Shipley could be put on IR too, after E SPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during Sunday’s loss to the Jaguars and could miss multiple weeks. That leaves practice squad players Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele to carry the load.
The grade goes up from a ‘C’ because of Darius Cooper , who has four touchdowns on just seven catches. The Eagles haven't had a receiver since Jeremy Maclin in 2014 catch four touchdowns in the first five games of a season.
Tay Wicks has been decent, but the Rams’ Trent McDuffie took him out of the game in a Week 4 loss, and DeVonta Smith has missed two games with an injury. Makai Lemon has done some decent things and should only continue to get better and more involved.
Dallas Goedert picked up where he left off last year, snaring two touchdowns against the Commanders in the opener. Then he got hurt in Week 2 and missed two games. Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins don’t provide much offense, and rookie Eli Stowers is on injured reserve. The Eagles signed Zach Ertz, but an impactful role for the veteran has yet to develop.
Lane Johnson retired, and Cam Jurgens was traded the very next day. The Eagles have had three different starting centers in just five games. Continuity is a big key to successful offensive line play, and there just hasn’t been any yet.
Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter were given big raises, but Davis isn’t having the same impact he did last year. He played 61 percent of the snaps a season ago, but is playing just 46 percent this year.
Carter, on the other hand, has been playing with a broken bone in his wrist, which has hampered him, but his three sacks lead the team, and his five tackles for loss equal the number of TFLs he had last year.
Jalyx Hunt looked like a double-digit sack artist in the making, but he has none. Nolan Smith has two sacks, but he hasn’t shown the play-in, play-out consistency he should have at this point in his career. The big offseason acquisition, Jonathan Greenard, has missed three games with two different injuries and has played just 37 snaps. As for free agents Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa, they haven’t contributed much so far.
Zack Baun continues to play at a high level, though he missed a game due to a concussion, which was the first time he missed a game with an injury since arriving here in 2024. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. was a force in his only start, collecting 15 tackles, and could be taking over the starting job from Jihaad Campbell, last year's first-round pick, who has been up and down.
Quinyon Mitchell notched his first regular-season interception in Week 5, adding to the four he has in the postseason. But neither he nor Cooper DeJean seems to be playing at the level they played at last year, when they both earned All-Pro honors, and Riq Woolen hasn’t had the bounce-back season the Eagles hoped he would have.
One of the team’s biggest question marks entering the season was here. It is more a liability than a question mark at this point. Andrew Mukuba remains inconsistent. Marcus Epps is hurt, but he wasn’t turning heads in the first three games he played before getting banged up. Michael Carter has done some decent things at the position, but the Eagles severely limited here.
The one and only ‘A’ on this report card is well deserved, with Jake Elliott already connecting on both tries beyond 50 yards, Braden Mann looking like an All-Pro, and Rocco Underwood flawless with his long snaps.
When your head coach has to admit to costing the team a game , as Nick Sirianni did after the loss in London, that’s not good. Neither is being 2-3.

title: Nick Sirianni's 'Flower' Speech as Relevant as Ever for Eagles in 2026
full_text:
Another two weeks and it might be time for the speech: “We talkin’ 'bout PRACTICE?”
This one: “It’s really important that the foundation is being built and the roots are going out and the only way the roots are growing, and they get stronger and they grow better is that we all water, we all fertilize so that when it pops out, it really pops out. … keep watering and look at yourself. Are you fertilizing every day? So, when it’s time to pop, it’ll pop.”
That was Nick Sirianni on Oct. 27, 2021. He showed his team a flower during a team meeting and gave that speech. It was his first season as a head coach, and his team had lost four in a row to drop to 2-5. He was on the hot seat. He always seems to be, but back then, seven games in, it was a seat glowing red.
That fiery glow is back. The Eagles have lost three in a row and, at 2-3, are below .500 for the first time since, yep, Sirianni’s first season in town.
My assertion has always been that Sirianni’s strength as a coach is building a culture in the locker room. He does it by insisting on connections between players and coaches, because when adversity strikes, they have only each other to lean on.
Too many think he wins because of the talent given to him. What successful coach doesn’t win with talent general managers give them? The difference is not all of them win the ultimate prize. Sirianni bridges that difference.
In the “water and fertilizer” speech, he talked about always having a different message to give to the team. Fast forward to today, and if they ever need to hear another Sirianni message, it’s right now.
Will this team prove that it is committed to each other? Will they stay together as one and not splinter? It's that kind of week.
“This is where relationships come into play,” said Sirianni on the day after his team lost a heartbreaker, 19-17, in London. “You're constantly communicating with the guys through messages with the team in a team setting but also checking in with guys on as much as you possibly can throughout the week.”
Sirianni was sold to the fan base upon his hire as an offensive-minded coach. That was until he turned playcalling duties over to Shane Steichen after that 2-5 start. That is another Sirianni strength: the ability to make a move when one needs to be made. The way he did not just with Steichen but also when he fired defensive coordinator Sean Desai midway through the 2023 season and replaced him with Matt Patricia.
Steichen worked; Patricia did not. Not all his moves pay off. The point is he isn’t afraid to change things when needed.
His speech on that October day five years ago led to some eye rolls, furrowed brows, quizzical looks, and set the airwaves ablaze: “He’s overmatched.”
Who knew then that the Eagles would become one of the most beautiful flowers fans had probably seen in their lifetimes?
After that speech, they went 7-3 and made the playoffs.
After that speech, the Eagles have done nothing but post double-digit winning seasons, win three NFC East championships, including back-to-back crowns to break a string of 21 consecutive seasons without a repeat winner of the division.
After that speech, they went to two Super Bowls, winning one, and it could have very easily been two if not for some heavy-handed officiating late in the game that virtually ensured the Chiefs the title that year.
“Right now, we are what our record says we are,” said Sirianni. “We're 2-3. We know there's a lot left in the season, and I don't think that there is any panic on any aspect of any player or coach in this building. We've had three-game losing streaks before. Our job is to get up and keep fighting.”

title: McMullen: Eagles’ Second-Half Offense Has Become a Vanishing Act
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - Through five games, the Philadelphia Eagles sit at 2-3 after a third straight setback, a 19-17 gut-wrencher to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London sealed by Cam Little’s 57-yard field goal as time expired.
Nick Sirianni took the blame for the kickoff decision in the waning seconds that allowed the return that set up Little’s heroics, and he also took accountability for losing the game.
However, the bigger and far more persistent problem was the offense’s disappearance after halftime – again.
In the second half of the last three games, the Eagles have produced: three points, 10 three-and-outs, 12 first downs, and a 2-for-20 mark on third down over 18 drives. League-wide, they rank last in  second-half scoring (23 points), total yards (495), three-and-out rate (51.7 percent), and pass yards per attempt (4.0).
Across the first five games, Sean Mannion’s new-look offense has repeatedly built or held first-half leads only to watch drives stall, punts pile up, and opportunities to close games evaporate.
Injuries have not helped—Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith were out in London, the offensive line has been reshuffled due to circumstance and injury, and the run game has been sporadic at best (just 22 yards against the Jaguars).
But the pattern predates the latest absences and echoes issues from last season under Kevin Patullo.
Mannion, who calls plays from the booth in a scheme supposedly influenced by Shanahan-McVay principles, has yet to produce consistent second-half rhythm, third-down efficacy, or explosive plays when the game tightens. It’s been a repetitive offense that has been easily solved by opponents.
Sirianni, speaking Monday, framed the response around collective growth rather than blame when asked about Mannion by Eagles On SI.
“I think that right now, offensively, we all have to be better… players, coaches with myself - all of us have to be better,” the head coach admitted. “We’re not worried about gauging where this person is or where that person is. We’re worried about growth… Obviously it hasn’t been good enough.”
“It’s never just one thing,” Sirianni continued. “… We all have things that we have to get better at… We won’t ever use anything as an excuse… It’s about finding solutions.”
There was an obvious disconnect with Sirianni noting “you have to be different to give yourself an edge” in the NFL, an interesting take as so many teams around the league are playing a similar style of offense, and the Eagles are late to that party.
“You have to take accountability and not look to assign blame, and look yourself in the mirror first,” said Sirianni. “… To do things in the NFL and to win games in the NFL, you have to be different.”
The Eagles offense ranks near the bottom of the league in points and yards per game overall; the under-center and play-action elements have not clicked at the expected rate, and third-down and second-half stalls have become the only real consistency.
Another high-expectations team facing a similar early-season offensive stall has already acted more decisively.
In Denver, Sean Payton reclaimed play-calling duties from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb after just four games. The Broncos were 2-2 and ranked near the bottom of the league in scoring and total yards (around 27th in both) when Payton announced the change after a loss to the 49ers, saying simply, “We’ll make a change offensively. I’ll call the plays.”
Webb remains the coordinator and is involved in game-planning, but Payton is now the voice in Bo Nix’s ear.
Both situations involve a veteran head coach who previously called plays, handing the role to a young, first-time play-caller amid high expectations, only to watch the offense sputter with too many three-and-outs, limited explosiveness, and an inability to sustain drives.
The difference is the timeline and the response: Payton judged four games a sufficient sample and stepped back in; Sirianni continues to emphasize growth, shared accountability, and incremental improvement, with Mannion still calling the plays.
Sirianni also doesn’t want to take play-calling back, but has former Tampa Bay OC Josh Grizzard on staff as the passing game coordinator as a potential contingency option.
Whether the Eagles’ more tempered approach yields the growth Sirianni craves or whether the second-half disappearing act continues and forces a Sean Desai-like bolder adjustment will define the season.
The idea that the Eagles should punt on the campaign is shortsighted given how poor the NFC East is shaping up. Winning the division is an easy path to a sixth straight postseason berth and the kind of sustained success that has been Philadelphia’s seasonal goal since Andy Reid brought the philosophy to the organization in 1999.
Maybe the Super Bowl isn’t realistic this season, but dismissing playoff experience as not good enough for the younger players is specious.
The defense is getting better. The offense, particularly after intermission, has not. As Sirianni put it, the job now is to find solutions. In an industry defined by results, gauging Mannion's job performance is inevitable. If the head coach refuses, someone else will.
The window for growth is narrowing, and Payton's urgency exhibited in Denver may be the template for changing the voice on the headset unless Mannion figures this out.

title: McMullen: Nick Sirianni's 'Accountability' Claim Rings Hollow as Situational Failures Mount
full_text:
To know Nick Sirianni is to understand the Eagles coach’s obsession with situational football.
For that reason, Sunday’s late-game implosion in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars was the exact kind of failure Sirianni cannot afford.
In a matter of moments, Jake Elliott’s 48-yard field goal had the heavily slanted Eagles crowd in a celebratory mood, with the pubs surrounding Tottenham Hotspur Stadium preparing for the onslaught of midnight green.
To those who value results over process, Cam Little’s 57-yard bomb seven seconds later that resulted in a 19-17 Jags win meant the most sensible decision with Jacksonville out of timeouts was instructing Elliott to try for a touchback on the subsequent kickoff after his successful boot, or at least a more controlled “dirty kick” to make things tougher on veteran kick returner Ameer Abdullah.
Instead, Elliott aimed a typical kickoff directly into the landing zone, and Abdullah returned it 53 yards to the Eagles’ 39-yard line.
Had Philadelphia’s kickoff coverage executed none of this, it would not even be thought about, or never mind, discussed. There's a lot to that, though, starting with the fact that one of the Eagles' top coverage players -- Jeremiah Trotter Jr. -- was ejected for scuffling on the opening kickoff that was returned for a touchdown by Jags rookie Josh Cameron before being wiped out by offsetting penalties.
On the final kickoff, after taking the lead and needing to circumvent only eight seconds, Arnold Ebiketie was a little loose with his lane discipline, and Abdullah burst through the gap. Ultimately, fate took over from there when Jonathan Jones caught the speedy running back, but he did it one second too soon.
To the torch and pitchfork crowd, all that was validated was that Sirianni’s miscue was the reason a trip to the United Kingdom felt empty and the coach wasn’t in the mood to put up any kind of fight afterward.
“What hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don’t make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game,” said Sirianni.
He told the locker room the same thing, taking the kind of accountability that will resonate in-house. That’s also the right public stance, even if it does not erase the damage.
As a CEO coach, though, situational football is the area Sirianni has long presented as a strength. He drills it relentlessly beyond the obvious third-down and two-minute spots.
Sirianni talks process until the word almost loses meaning. He wants his teams to take pride in winning by any way that is required. Saturdays are spent going over every possible game-day scenario.
Late-game special teams strategy and clock management sit squarely in that lane, as does Makai Lemon stepping out of bounds instead of forcing Jacksonville to take its third and final timeout, two plays before Elliott stepped on the field to kick his FG.
Had Lemon gone down before crossing the sideline, the Eagles would have bled the clock to three seconds, and Elliott’s kick would have been the game-winner.
Sirianni’s public accountability comes across as empty when he fails to explain the fallout.
“If I followed it, the process, then obviously that turns out to be the wrong decision,” he said. “If I didn’t follow it, then obviously that was the wrong decision.
“Either way, I’m wrong. That’s all I’ll say about that.”
A coach who treats process as the North Star cannot land on “either way, I’m wrong” without the foundation looking cracked.
Owning the result while declining to explain the reasoning leaves the process looking more like a plot twist than a working tool.
That’s not acceptable for a CEO coach.

title: 3 Realistic WR Trade Targets For Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need wide receiver help if they want to make it through the latest rash of injuries plaguing the lineup. Entering Week 6 with a 3-2 record, the Steelers have played well on the offensive side of the ball, even with a shorthanded roster.
The Steelers have a few players on their active roster and practice squad that will likely get the first crack for Week 6. Players like Brandon Smith, Brandon Johnson, Eli Heidenreich and Max Hurleman could all enter the lineup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The other option is to pluck a veteran from another team's practice squad that they feel could plug in and play immediately. Names like K.J. Osborn, Mecole Hardman and Trey Palmer come to mind.
Alternatively, they could try to pull off a low-risk trade. Unlikely to part with the assets required to land a big-name player, the Steelers have been unafraid to add veterans this season. That could again be the case with these three players the Steelers could acquire for very little.
On the eastern side of Pennsylvania, the Philadelphia Eagles are selling off parts. They traded offensive lineman Cam Jurgens shortly after tackle Lane Johnson retired. They already sent AJ Brown out of town before the 2026 season began.
So, what are the Eagles trying get out of Marquise "Hollywood" Brown? The answer is nothing, evidenced by just one game played this season and a whopping two rushes for 12 yards. But last year he posted over 500 yards with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Eagles are set for a fire sale, and all it would take is a seventh or sixth-round pick to get the former 2019 first-round pick in Pittsburgh.
The Jacksonville Jaguars thought they had a gem of a receiver when they took Brian Thomas Jr. in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. That thought was reaffirmed by a 1,200-yard rookie season.
But it's been far less impressive since that first year. He posted just over 700 yards as a sophomore, and he continues to fall out of favor in Jacksonville. Through five games in 2026, he's played less than half of the team's offensive snaps, according to data from Spotrac, and has 105 yards and a single touchdown.
The Jaguars are trying to win with quarterback Trevor Lawrence, and Thomas isn't helping right now. He might help in Pittsburgh, however, where he can play with a different type of quarterback and offensive coach.
How much would Jacksonville need to be convinced? If the Steelers could get him for a day three pick in 2027, then it's a no-brainer. Anything close to the price the Houston Texans paid for Marvin Harrison Jr., and the Steelers have to walk away.
Back in 2024, Jalen Tolbert had the best offensive season of his career. He caught 49 passes for 610 yards and seven touchdowns. Aside from that, he's been a 200-yard receiver over his five seasons in the NFL.
Why that matters for the Steelers is that Mike McCarthy was Tolbert's coach in Dallas that season. Pittsburgh could give Tolbert the chance to shine again under McCarthy. Currently on the 0-5 Miami Dolphins and making $1.4 million in actual cash, the Steelers could land a player their head coach already trusts for virtually nothing.

title: Update: President Donald Trump Cancels Trip to Steelers Game
full_text:
President Donald Trump will not be in attendance for the Pittsburgh Steelers ' next game after deciding to cancel the trip to Tampa Bay.
According to CNN Senior White House Correspondent Kristen Holmes, Trump was expected to be at Raymond James Stadium for the Steelers ' Week 6 bout on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, he has since canceled.
Good news for the many people who hated this news— after we reported it, I am told they pulled down the trip. So… hope you kept your tickets! https://t.co/ZQNpS4EJii
The last time Trump watched Pittsburgh in person was in Week 7 of the 2024 campaign during a Sunday Night Football showdown vs. Aaron Rodgers and the New York Jets.
Trump was the guest of an individual suiteholder for that contest, which marked Russell Wilson's first start for the Steelers in his return from a calf injury.
The organization also honored the 50th anniversary of its Super Bowl IX team that night as Pittsburgh blew out the Jets by a score of 37-15.
The Buccaneers got off to a difficult start this season, losing each of their first four games.
Baker Mayfield, who signed a three-year extension worth $165 million last month, also suffered a dislocated thumb in Week 3 and has remained out ever since.
As a result, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has stepped in as the starting quarterback for the time being. After a rough debut in a Week 4 loss to the Green Bay Packers, however, Daniels helped lead Tampa Bay to an upset victory on Thursday Night Football this past week vs. the Dallas Cowboys.
Mayfield appears to be trending in the right direction, though the signs are still pointing towards Daniels getting the starting nod against Pittsburgh .
While Daniels and the Bucs proved that they can be competitive and come away with wins against quality teams, the Steelers cannot afford to let the opportunity for a win against an inexperienced backup quarterback slip by them.
Sure, Tampa Bay has one of the better defenses in the league and has gotten the run game going thanks to Bucky Irving, but Pittsburgh still by and large has the upper hand as long as Daniels is behind center.
The Steelers' offense showed up in a major way during the team's Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, putting 34 points up on the board, and their defense is still capable of at least holding opposing offenses in check even if the secondary isn't in good shape.
Make no mistake about it, the Buccaneers are a far more formidable squad than their 1-4 record would suggest, but Pittsburgh cannot let them earn the win this week considering their quarterback situation.

title: Steelers Star Must Step Up After WR Injuries
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers put together an impressive offensive showing in their 34-22 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5. For the second time in five games, the Steelers posted 30 points or more, while quarterback Aaron Rodgers has thrown for at least three touchdowns in three consecutive games.
What makes it even more impressive is the Steelers have made improvements on offense despite inconsistent wide receiver play. Thanks to the efforts of Rodgers and running back Jaylen Warren, this group might be finding steady ground.
The one player who cannot be ignored in all of this is tight end Pat Freiermuth. The 27-year-old had a fantastic Week 5 performance, hauling in five receptions for 44 yards and two touchdowns.
It was exactly what the team needed. Amidst a sea of injuries, the Steelers can find safe harbor thanks to the re-emergence of Freiermuth as a top tight end.
It’s long been known that Freiermuth is one of the best athletes at his position. He established that as a rookie in the NFL, but over the years, the offense has failed to prioritize him as they should.
This season, however, it appears that head coach Mike McCarthy is refusing to continue that. In all five games this season, Freiermuth has seen at least four targets. In this most recent contest, he was targeted seven times.
It’s emblematic of one thing - this team prioritizes Freiermuth. Rodgers trusts him as his top tight end, and he continues to go to him in tough situations.
One area the Steelers really focused on Freiermuth in their Week 5 victory was in the red zone. Both of his touchdown receptions came inside the 20-yard line, but it was a specific second quarter play that should give the Steelers confidence moving forward.
On the 1-yard line, the Steelers were expected to come out with jumbo personnel as they tried to power into the end zone. Instead, they came out with an empty set and five receivers out wide.
It was the perfect play call because it put Freiermuth one-on-one with a Colts linebacker, giving him a mismatch at the line of scrimmage.
Freiermuth took advantage. With a quick stutter step, the Steelers tight end created plenty of space for Rodgers to find him, giving the Steelers an early 14-6 lead.
Aaron Rodgers finds Pat Freiermuth for another Steelers TD! #NFL pic.twitter.com/hU254xEhwW
As the Steelers try to build momentum, they keep taking hits. Roman Wilson could miss time after dislocating a finger in Week 5. Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on Injured Reserve, meaning he will be out of action for at least three more weeks.
Despite the hits that keep coming, the Steelers should feel confident in their offensive weaponry. That’s thanks to Pat Freiermuth.

title: Two WRs Steelers Can Poach From Other Teams
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have a wide receiver problem once again. This time, however, injuries are the main culprit to blame.
The Steelers were victorious in Week 5, putting up 34 points in a win over the Indianapolis Colts. The offense has taken strides , putting up more than 30 points in two of the last three weeks. In the process, however, they've lost three wide receivers for multiple weeks. Michael Pittman Jr. is on the Injured Reserve with a foot injury, Roman Wilson has already been ruled out of Week 6 due to a dislocated finger and special teams ace Ben Skowronek left their Week 5 contest with a calf injury.
Even with their practice squad call-ups, the Steelers need another receiver once again. The team could swing a trade before they take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, but the likelier route this organization takes is plucking a player off of a practice squad or from free agency.
These two veterans stand out as the likeliest fits and most immediately available options for the Steelers to add temporarily.
A few seasons ago, K.J. Osborn was a legitimate trade target for the Steelers. Coming off of three straight seasons of at least 500 receiving yards, the former 2020 fifth-round pick was a coveted player around the NFL.
Fast forward to 2026, and he's on the Tennessee Titans practice squad. For the Steelers, that's exactly what they need. Osborn has 66 games of NFL experience, and he could come in and be ready to play as soon as Week 6.
He is not a flashy option, that's for sure. But as a temporary replacement, he is an easy addition.
As an added bonus, where did Osborn have success? His best days came as a member of the Minnesota Vikings, working with current Steelers offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio. That extra connection might be enough to convince the team to take a shot on Osborn.
The Steelers could also look to free agency to add former Kansas City Chiefs, New York Jets and Buffalo Bills receiver Mecole Hardman Jr.
A former Super Bowl winner with the Chiefs, Hardman brings the trait that the Steelers' coaching staff loves: versatility. He has the speed that the team is missing without Wilson on the field. He can play any of the receiver positions. Most importantly, he has experience returning kicks and punts. He's not just a flyer being taken to fill out the bottom of the depth chart, he's someone who can help across multiple situations for the next few weeks.
Plus, he played briefly with Aaron Rodgers as a player with the New York Jets. Rodgers was hurt in the season opener that year and Hardman was later traded away, but the two spent time together previously. If that went well, why not bring him back for a reunion?
Other names to monitor are just as unexciting. Former second-round pick JuJu Smith-Schuster is an option. Odell Beckham Jr. is on the Vikings' practice squad. Other free agent names include Tyreek Hill, KJ Hamler and Josh Reynolds.

title: Steelers Better Hurry for JuJu Smith-Schuster
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers don't have time to waste. They need help at the wide receiver position and have a few outside options that are worth exploring.
One is JuJu Smith-Schuster, but bringing back a former second-round pick isn't something they can wait around for. If they're ready to add some help and have their former wideout on their mind, they need to act fast.
Otherwise, he's going to end up somewhere else.
Smith-Schuster started the week by trying out for the Minnesota Vikings. The 29-year-old hasn't played in 2025, but played all 17 games in 2025, including 12 starts for the Kansas City Chiefs. He recorded 345 yards and a touchdown last season, and is looking to finish the 2026 campaign on a team.
That team could be the Steelers.
The Vikings worked out veteran WR JuJu Smith-Schuster today.
It's hard to say the Steelers shouldn't have interest in Smith-Schuster. Their former second-round pick spent five years in Pittsburgh before starting to bounce around the league. Now, with a desperate need for help at the position due to injuries, he's one of the best options they have to get them through the next few weeks.
With Roman Wilson (hand) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) both missing multiple weeks, and Ben Skowronek (calf) missing Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Pittsburgh's wide receiver room includes DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen.
They'll likely call Brandon Smith up from the practice squad, but they'll still need another option for Aaron Rodgers.
Smith-Schuster isn't their only option. Tyreek Hill, Gabe Davis, Curtis Samuel and others are still available in free agency. They could also look at names like KJ Osborn, Tyler Johnson and others, who currently reside on practice squads across the league.
But if they are interested in Smith-Schuster, they must act fast. And if nothing else, his workout with the Vikings shows that they aren't the only team interested in adding wide receiver talent this late into the season.
Whoever they're after, they shouldn't be waiting. This league is banged up as well, and they don't want to left picking from the final two or three top options available.
This offense is finally starting to find its footing. Aaron Rodgers has groove going and Metcalf, Bernard and the rest of the passing game are starting to click. So, if they're going to make the "right" call at who to add, they need to act fast.
And if it's Smith-Schuster, they may need to act now.

title: Steelers Could Get Rico Dowdle Back at Perfect Time
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle appears to be on the precipice of a return from his toe injury.
While praising Jaylen Warren during his postgame press conference following the Steelers ' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, head coach Mike McCarthy stated that Dowdle was "close" to suiting up in the contest and that he's hopeful he'll make his return in Week 6 vs. the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
“He's the man. He's hauling it right now for us," McCarthy said. "There's a number you like to continue to give him. He's produced. So it's been heavy. It'll be great to get Rico back this week too. I'd love for Rico to practice this week and, hopefully, be up for the game. Yeah, he was close. Having him as a one-two punch was the vision of this offense, but Jaylen's crushing it right now. He's been awesome for us.”
Pittsburgh is in dire straits at the wide receiver position.
Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on the reserve/injured list after aggravating his foot injury last week, meaning he'll need to miss at least another three games. That period will run through the team's Week 9 bye, meaning the earliest he can return is in Week 10 vs. the Cincinnati Bengals.
Meanwhile, Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) both went down in the first half against the Colts and did not play at all in the second half. That left DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Smith, who was elevated from the practice squad, as the only healthy receivers left on the game day roster.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler has reported that Wilson is expected to miss several weeks with his injury, though he is still in the process of gathering information and will seek out a second opinion.
As such, Pittsburgh is lacking depth at receiver and should have a move or two on the horizon to address that situation.
Obviously Dowdle isn't going to help mask the team's issues at the position in a traditional sense, but should he be back on the field against Tampa Bay, he does have the means to make a difference in the passing game.
The Steelers have often relied heavily on their running backs through the air. That was the case last season in Arthur Smith's system, as Kenneth Gainwell had 486 yards on 73 catches while Warren finished with 333 yards over 40 receptions, and the latter has now accumulated 230 receiving yards on 19 catches under Mike McCarthy this year.
Dowdle had posted four receptions for 28 yards in roughly a game-and-a-half before dislocating his toe twice in Week 2 against the Patriots, which has kept him out ever since.
The 28-year-old logged a combined 546 yards and four touchdowns across 78 catches between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns, though, showing that he is capable of making a real impact as a pass catcher out of the backfield and thus could be another key target for Rodgers as Pittsburgh deals with a shortage at receiver for the time being.
Coming into the season, the expectation was that Warren and Dowdle would share the workload at running back with something like a 55/45 or 60/40 split in favor of the former.
That was largely true when Dowdle was healthy, as he had 10 touches in Week 1 vs. the Atlanta Falcons while Warren had 15.
Given how dominant Warren has been since Dowdle went down, however, posting 491 yards from scrimmage in three games while looking like one of the league's top running backs, that type of split is unlikely to materialize moving forward.
Dowdle is a fantastic complementary piece at running back, though he's going to have to take a back seat to Warren.
Instead of a 1A, 1B-type situation, Warren has become the clear top dog for Pittsburgh and is in line to garner somewhere in the ballpark of 70 to 75 percent touches out of the backfield while Dowdle essentially gets the rest.
That could change at some point, but the Steelers simply can't curtail Warren's workload given how well he has played recently.

title: Steelers Make Right Call With Jaylen Warren
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers face a mountain of injuries after their Week 5 victory. Despite emerging with the win, the Steelers lost two key players, at least.
During his weekly press conference, head coach Mike McCarthy shared that wide receivers Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek have already been ruled out for the team’s next contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The Steelers will need to adjust their offensive game plan once again, but the one thing that won’t change is the reliance on running back Jaylen Warren. Asked about how he plans to utilize his backfield once Rico Dowdle returns from injury, McCarthy was clear that Warren is the key piece of the Steelers’ offensive puzzle.
”Jaylen’s our featured player right now. Let’s make sure we all recognize that. He’s hot. He’s playing great football for us,” McCarthy stated . “So it’s important for us as an offense, you know, coaches and players alike, to continue to put him in position to make plays. So, that won’t change.”
Dowdle is expected to return to the field this week after missing the last three games.
McCarthy’s comments are the biggest endorsement of Warren so far, and it comes at a time when he has become undeniable. Even if McCarthy had a different product envisioned for his backfield in the offseason, Warren has forced his hand for the better.
Since Dowdle’s injury, Warren has become the best piece of the offense by a wide margin. He’s received at least 15 carries in three straight contests, and he’s posted rushing yard totals of 127, 93 and 101 yards.
The question that gets asked based off of Warren’s history in the NFL, is, can the Steelers keep using him this frequently? Luckily for the offense, Warren is looking even healthier entering Week 6. McCarthy said that compared to the last two weeks, their lead running back “looks better than the last two Mondays.”
With Warren as the featured back and lead piece on offense, the Steelers have an identity. The offensive line continues to look better, and their reliance on combo blocks and an aggressive demeanor only helps Warren’s game.
If they keep this going, the Steelers are in a good place offensively. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers looks strong over three straight games, and they’ve posted 30 points in back-to-back home games.
It seems like Mike McCarthy is making the right call with Jaylen Warren.

title: Steelers vs. Colts Grades: Offense and Coaching Shine
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers went to war with the Indianapolis Colts. Both organizations were looking for their third victory of the season, but the Steelers left Acrisure Stadium victorious.
The Steelers out together an impressive win over the Colts, defeating them by a final score of 34-22.
It was a winning effort from the Steelers, but how impressive were they in victory? Riding high after their third home win of the season, this is how the Steelers' Week 5 performance grades out
There was tons to like about the offense, which was undoubtedly the best piece of the Steelers in Week 5.
Aaron Rodgers etched his name in Pittsburgh franchise history, joining Terry Bradshaw and Ben Roethlisberger as the only quarterbacks to record three touchdown passes in three consecutive games or more. He finished Week 5 22/31 for 235 yards and three touchdowns.
Even better news exiting the game was the offensive line keeping Rodgers protected. They only allowed one sack in Week 5 and gave Rodgers plenty of time and space in the pocket.
The star of the game, once again, was running back Jaylen Warren. With 15 carries for 101 yards, plus six receptions for 87 yards and an additional score, Warren was an unstoppable force against the Colts. He broke off a 50-yard run for one of his touchdowns, and took a screen pass 87 yards to the house for another.
Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard had the biggest game of his young career as well. Without Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson exiting the game at halftime, Bernard was a frequent target. He finished the game with six receptions for 80 yards on nine targets.
The biggest win of the day for the defense was how they shut down star running back Jonathan Taylor. One of the premier runners in the NFL, the Steelers limited him to less than 50 yards on the ground.
It wasn't a perfect day for the defense, however. They allowed 267 passing yards to quarterback Daniel Jones while only getting him once in the backfield. They also failed to contain tight end Tyler Warren, who posted seven receptions for 83 yards on nine targets.
In the end, the Steelers did enoug defensively to get the victory. But for another week, the defense has had some serious flaws exposed.
Chris Boswell had a bounce back game, hitting both field goals he attempted in Week 5. That included a long of 54 yards and it put the Steelers in front by 12 points in the final moments of the contest.
Punter Cameron Johnson was rock solid in his work as well. He punted three times, posting an average of 52.0 yards per punt.
Even rookie Kaden Wetjen had a good day in the return game. On five kick-off return attempts, he posted 110 yards, good for an average of 22.0 per return.
The Steelers couldn't ask for much more from their special teamsin the win.
You can't be critical of this staff's performance in Week 5. Sure, there were things to clean up, but this was an excellent response to the Week 4 stinker they left.
Head coach Mike McCarthy called a great game offensively, but Patrick Graham moving from the booth to the sideline was a big difference maker. Maybe it was a placebo effect, but the communication was much smoother and well-mannered in Week 5 compared to Week 4.

title: Steelers Need to Sign a WR
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need wide receiver help. Only a day ago, everyone was talking about this team not needing to look at the wide receiver trade market because of their young talent. Today, the group is depleted, and they desperately need help.
With the news that Roman Wilson is set to miss multiple weeks with a finger injury, the Steelers are left with DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard as their starters. Michael Pittman Jr. is on Injured Reserve with a foot injury, and Ben Skowronek also left Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts, dealing with a calf injury.
So, right now, Pittsburgh's room is Metcalf, Bernard and rookie Kaden Wetjen. Wetjen is primarily a returner and hasn't played an offensive snap yet.
The team will likely call up Brandon Smith from the practice squad. Smith didn't record a catch against the Colts but was a training camp standout and a player Aaron Rodgers has shared his faith in multiple times.
"Well, B-Smith hasn't taken a ton of offensive reps. I've been around him for a few years. He was with us in New York, and always enjoyed him being on the fieldand his ability. I think he's a talented guy," Rodgers said after the Colts game.
"But we can play in 12 all day long, and if we need to, we will. But I was really proud of Germ the way he stepped in. There were a couple of plays with B-Smith. Like we had this play we're running inside zone, and we have this short motion to block the safety. Just by the end of the week it was just assumed that motion. I wasn't even calling it.
"I looked over, and I was, like, Oh, B has probably never done this. I was, like, Hey. He didn't know what I was thinking.
"So we were kind of making it up a little bit as we went there, but I'm proud of B-Smith. He's a smart guy and knows his stuff, and he'll be ready to take on a bigger role this week, I’m sure."
The team will likely need to explore their outside options, though. The name everyone will immediately think of is Tyreek Hill, but he's not the only veteran on the market. Two even have ties to the Steelers. And it'll come down to how big of a role the coaching staff is looking to fill with a signing.
If Mike McCarthy wants another starter-level player in the mix, Hill is the name to watch out for. The six-time All-Pro is 32-years-old and looking to play this season after suffering a dislocated knee in 2025. But he claims he's healthy, and if he is, he's easily the biggest name on the market.
If the Steelers are simply looking for a contributor to play behind Metcalf and Bernard , and in the mix with Smith, Skowronek and Wetjen, there are other names.
JuJu Smith-Schuster hasn't played in Pittsburgh since 2021, but spent the first five years of his career wearing the black and gold. The physical receiver is mostly a slot option at this point in his career, but could be a reliable set of hands for short-yardage situations and over the middle passes.
Gabe Davis is recovering from an ACL and may not be ready to play. But at 27 years old, he may be worth making a phone call to to check on his health heading into Week 6.
And then there are others; Ray-Ray McCloud is a player the Steelers' organization knows well. Curtis Samuel is somewhat of a mystery free agent, and maybe the biggest surprise to not be on a roster or practice squad somewhere. Mecole Hardman, Justin Watson, Josh Reynolds and others are still available as well.
It'll come down to Pittsburgh's perference. Whether or not they're looking for a bigger name or a fill-in while they wait for Wilson and Pittman Jr. How long they truly expect both to be out could play a significant role in their decision.
We don't know who yet, but expect someone. The Steelers certainly need another wide receiver before Week 6.

title: Steelers Bringing Back Hard-Hitting LB
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to bring in veteran linebacker Elandon Roberts with the intention of re-signing the 32-year-old, according to Steelers Now's Alan Saunders.
Roberts spent the end of training camp with the Steelers, rejoining the defense and defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, who coached him with the Las Vegas Raiders the year prior. He was the biggest surprise release of the final 53-man roster, being surpassed by Patrick Queen, Payton Wilson, Cole Holcomb and Carson Bruener in the final cuts.
Now, Roberts is set to return to the Steelers, where his presence is needed. Both Queen and Wilson have been under heavy criticism throughout the season for failing to be reliable inside linebacker options. Their struggles have shown the most in run support, which is where Roberts thrives.
It's unknown if Roberts will sign to the active roster or practice squad when he does ink a deal with the Steelers. Chances are, even if he does sign with the practice squad initially, the intention will be to bring him up to the active roster at some point.
Roberts is entering his 11th NFL season, starting 121 games and recording 694 tackles, 14.5 sacks and 60 tackles for loss.
The Steelers defense is trying to figure out their flaws as they approach the midway point of the season, but it's becoming more and more clear that their lack of talent at the inside linebacker room can't be solved without adding to the group. Queen and Wilson have spurts of quality play, but overall, both have struggled more than they've succeeded for the Steelers.
Meanwhile, Cole Holcomb hasn't been a reliable backup and has become more of a special teams contributor than defensive help.
Roberts should be able to come into the Steelers' lineup and help immediately. Whether he joins the starting group or not, his presence in the run game is something Pittsburgh desperately needs. His drive as a starter will also help, and his leadership is also something they can utilize as they try to keep things on track.
How the Steelers create a roster spot for Roberts is up in the air. Bruener is a key special teams contributor and will likely remain in that role for his second season. Holcomb could be a bubble player if the Steelers chose to replace their depth.
If not, Queen and Wilson are the names to watch. And with a starter-level player joining the group, anything is on the table.

title: Week 6 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Seahawks Slide Following Loss to 49ers
full_text:
This weekend was a gut-punch for the Seattle Seahawks as they lost 32-29 against the San Francisco 49ers.
There could be some encouragement for them, considering they had a chance to tie the game late despite multiple turnovers and a lack of an efficient ground game. Unfortunately, Jaxon Smith-Njigba was unable to haul in a pass from Sam Darnold that would have put them in field goal range. As if that wasn't heartbreaking enough, Cooper Kupp was stopped just inches short on fourth-down, ending their bid for a comeback.
Seattle has a quick turnaround with a Thursday Night Football showdown against the Denver Broncos . Before we completely turn our attention to that game, here's a Week 6 NFL Power Rankings roundup, which shows the Seahawks sliding.
Connor Orr dropped Seattle four spots and accuratley says the offense needs Zach Charbonnet back on the field. Without him, their ground game has been a mess and that has a lot to do with their struggles.
"Per friend Sheil Kapadia at The Ringer, this was the worst offensive EPA in a game coached by Mike Macdonald. This is as much a Raheem Morris note as it is a Seattle note, but I don’t think Zach Charbonnet can hit the field soon enough," Orr wrote.
Not a steep drop from ESPN, but the Seahawks are still trending in the wrong direction. Brady Henderson discussed the biggest problem for the Seattle defense this year, which he says is actually the turnovers by their offense.
"The biggest problem for the Seahawks' defense might actually be their offense; the 44 points they've given up off turnovers is tied for most in the NFL," Henderson wrote.
The Athletic also discussed the lack of a ground game in Seattle, although they also believe the return of Jadarian Price could make a difference. They also add that an improved run game would go a long way toward fixing their issues.
"The Seahawks felt the absence of Jadarian Price (chest injury) and Zach Charbonnet (PUP list) Sunday as their running woes continued. They managed just 68 yards on 24 designed rushes (2.83 yards per carry) for their backs. There are a lot of reasons to remain positive about Seattle, but the running game has to improve."
Mo Moton says the Seahawks need to regroup and while he touched on the ground game, his biggest concern is the turnovers. Since Sam Darnold returned in Week 3, Seattle's quarterback has five interceptions, something that can't happen going forward.
"The reigning champions must regroup. The Seattle Seahawks are turning the ball over at an alarming rate—nine giveaways over the last four weeks. Since Sam Darnold returned from injury, he's been part of the problem, throwing five interceptions in his last three outings," Moton wrote.
Nate Davis kept Seattle where they were, which is surprising. That said, he's not worried about a three-point loss when they weren't at their best.
"Too high you say? Sam Darnold threw two more picks on Sunday, their depleted group of running backs fumbled two more times, and even Jaxon Smith-Njigba is dropping a key pass while running wide open and free. Oh, and LB Ernest Jones IV is once again defending Darnold − literally this time. You know the champs are quality. But Sunday's loss feels similar to last year's in L.A., which set off a 12-game winning streak that only ended two weeks ago. Don't be surprised if these 'Hawks take flight soon," Davis wrote.
Davis could be right that the Seahawks are ready to take off, but that's only going to happen if they take better care of the ball and get the run game going.

title: 3 Score Predictions for Seahawks vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are taking on the Denver Broncos for their Week 6 matchup on Thursday Night Football.
In a battle of two contending teams in primetime , anything can happen as the season kicks into another gear. Some members of the Seattle Seahawks On SI staff predicted what the score of the contest would be and explained their reasoning.
Mike Macdonald's club couldn't hang onto the ball last weekend at home against the 49ers. The Seahawks hae committed eight turnovers in their last three games, five of those interceptions by quarterback Sam Darnold.
Seattle's running game has slowed to a crawl, but this week Macdonald's defense stifles a lifeless Denver offense. The 'Hawks settle for six Jason Meyers field goals and escape the Mile High City with a victory.
The Seahawks have been within three points in three of their five matchups, which suggests that this game could end up in either direction. That's exactly what the schedule-makers were hoping for when they scheduled this matchup on primetime for Week 6.
In a battle of former division rivals, the Seahawks and Broncos will renew their rivalry in what should be an incredibly physical, defensive game.
If the contest ends up emerging into a track meet, I like the Seahawks. Their offense has performed better than the Broncos over the course of the season. However, if things remain close, the Broncos should have a better chance to pull this out.
I think the altitude, home atmosphere and traveling on a short week is a tough combination for the Seahawks to try and overcome.
Seattle is coming off a frustrating loss while the Broncos have been up and down this season. They haven't looked like the same team that made it to the AFC Championship Game a year ago, and that's a huge plus for the Seahawks. They sneak out of Denver with a win here, but they will need everyone to improve their play, especially on the ground.
