title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 6 Clash vs. Broncos
full_text:
This Thursday’s clash between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos features two teams with identical records that happen to be chasing a pair of undefeated teams in their respective divisions.
Mike Macdonald’s club comes off a frustrating 32-29 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Sean Payton’s club won ugly at SoFi Stadium, defeating the winless Los Angeles Chargers.
Here are three battles that could go a long way in determining which club gets its fourth victory of the season.
While Seattle’s offensive front crept into Pro Football Focus’ Top 10 last Wednesday, it’s been a rough second year so far for starting left guard Grey Zabel. The 2025 first-round pick from North Dakota State has had his struggles, and is currently PFF’s No. 42 player at the position.
On Thursday night, he figures to have his hands full with defensive end Zach Allen, who currently leads the Broncos with four sacks. He’s Pro Football Focus’ 11th-ranked interior defenders who also ranks 10th in terms of pass rush prowess.
Macdonald’s club has allowed eight sacks in their last two games—five in the loss to the 49ers—this after giving up just three sacks in the club’s first three outings.
Sam Darnold throws another interception! The Seahawks keep handing the ball right back to the 49ers. pic.twitter.com/HN2Yw0cQgX
A year ago, only the Houston Texans allowed fewer total yards per game than the Broncos. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph’s unit also finished second in the league vs. the run. Led by the league’s most productive pass rush, Denver defenders surrendered only 18 scores through the air in 17 regular-season games.
After five weeks of action, Joseph’s unit is just 22nd in the NFL in total defense, while allowing the fourth-most rushing yards per game.
Meanwhile, Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold has been less-than-impressive the past three weeks. He was knocked out early in Week 1 against the Patriots and didn’t play at Arizona. In his last three games, the nine-year pro has thrown seven touchdown passes and been picked off five times.
In five games this season, the Broncos have allowed seven TD tosses and total five interceptions.
Nehemiah Pritchett diving INT! @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pvzpNYvGJF
Macdonald and defensive coordinator Aden Durde have the league’s top-ranked defense in terms of fewest total yards and fewest passing yards per game allowed. The Seahawks also lead the league with 11 takeaways. Seattle defenders have picked off seven passes, with safety Julian Lobe and cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett tied for the club lead with two interceptions. The latter is also second behind Love (5) with four passes defensed.
It’s been a very rough start in 2026 for Broncos’ third-year quarterback Bo Nix, who has nearly as many turnovers (5) as touchdown passes (6) in five outings. He’s also completing just 59.9 percent of his passes and Denver’s offense has scored only nine TDs. Pritchett may indeed add to his pick total—especially is Seattle’s pass rush gets to Nix early and often.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Sheds Further Light On Thursday Night Matchup
full_text:
It’s time for the second injury report of the week, coming at you a couple days early thanks to the Thursday kickoff. Injuries are a significant part of any Thursday game, since the team has much less time to bounce back from their prior bout, and both teams have some concerns. The Denver Broncos are currently the worst off, but we’ll see if that holds into gameday.
Irv Charles (knee) leads the good news this week, as not only did he practice in full today again, he was activated to the roster. He should be playing Thursday at this point. George Holani (ribs, knee) was also getting a full set of reps, so for better or worse he’ll be ready for gameday. Beau Stephens (shoulder) was upgraded to full participation.
Zach Charbonnet (knee) holds in limited participation, and is still assumed to be out this week. Drew Lock (right forearm) remains limited, same for Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) and Leonard Williams (ankle). I’d expect both players to play, although whether they’ll be able to play at the superstar level we’ve come accustomed to is unclear.
Drake Thomas (ankle) was marked as a DNP yet again, which makes his odds of playing on Thursday dip significantly. It’s worth nothing, however, that he did play out the entire second half on Sunday, and this injury report is an estimate since there was no practice today. Chazz Surratt (calf) also remained out, and is almost certainly sitting this week.
The Broncos got some positive news today on the injury front. Brandon Jones (foot) and Ben Powers (biceps) got a second straight day of full practice, so there doesn’t seem to be any real concern there. Sai’vion Jones (shoulder), a backup defensive end who mostly plays on special teams, was limited yesterday and was upgraded to full today, so good news there.
Riley Moss (ribs) was the only limited participant. He looks on track to play, although it’s worth noting he sat against the Chargers on Sunday. As much as he is maligned by Broncos fans, the need for him to take the field this week is desperate, because the team isn’t getting the progress they need from their other top contributors on the back end of their defense.
Overall, however, the Broncos really needed some good news with their defensive backs today, and it did not come. Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), the two best players in that Denver secondary, both were held out of practice again today. Their odds of being available Thursday are very thin at this point. It’s a significant hole to overcome.

title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios for Seahawks vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are kicking Week 6 off with their Thursday Night Football matchup against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High.
The Seahawks are coming off of a loss against the San Francisco 49ers at home, so they are going to be extra focused going into their matchup with a short week incoming. Here's a look at three potential scenarios for the Seahawks as they visit the Broncos:
The Seahawks defense has surrendered 30 or more points in each of their two losses, but 23 or fewer in each of their three wins. The defense will have some struggles with Bo Nix and the Broncos offense on the other sideline, but they have to make sure they return to their identity as a smashmouth, dominant squad.
Perhaps the short week will work in the defense's favor, which is what the Seahawks are striving for. In the two losses they've suffered, the offense has scored 30+ points. The offense hasn't played perfect, but as long as the defense keeps Denver at bay, Seattle should walk away with a win.
The Seahawks have committed nine turnovers in their first five games of the year, which is tied for the fifth-most in the league behind the Chicago Bears, New Orleans Saints, New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers.
Out of those nine turnovers, five of them have come off of Sam Darnold interceptions in the last three games, two of which were one-score losses. That has completely devastated the Seahawks in those contests, and if he hadn't thrown those picks, Seattle could be 5-0.
If the Broncos defense, which already has seven takeaways in five games, can jar the football loose or jump Darnold's passing lanes, it could be a long night for the Seahawks.
The Seahawks have been in four one-score games in five weeks, which suggests that they could be in for another tight one against the Broncos on the road.
The Broncos have struggled in first halves this season, but turn it on after they return from the locker room. They are not a team that one can count out, so the Seahawks have to play four full quarters of football in order to win this one.
I'm expecting the Seahawks to take an early lead, but they don't find the kill shot to take an insurmountable lead. That will keep the door open for the Broncos, who use fourth-quarter heroics and the home crowd to fuel a comeback victory.

title: Seahawks Rookie Report: Top Three Selected Players Now on IR
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks’ 2026 NFL Draft class is looking worse as time progresses. This draft class is facing the unfortunate label that it might be one of the least productive draft classes based on injuries. Their top three drafted players are now on IR and only two rookies are really contributing.
Only two rookies played in the Seahawks’ 32-29 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers . There weren’t performances that could be defined as great, but they could be developed. That’s about the only positive from this rookie class lately. As we learned this past week, this 2026 draft class can get worse.
​There are only two rookies contributing to the Seahawks this past Sunday and only one of them was actually drafted by Seattle. Rookie guard Beau Stephens continued to split reps with veteran Christian Haynes at right guard while starter Anthony Bradford remains on IR. Stephens played 30 reps (47.6%) of the offensive snaps as the Seahawks clearly have a plan for him in the future, even if he hasn’t developed yet. He has had good moments in the loss to the 49ers, but some ugly plays too.
Undrafted rookie cornerback Avery Smith gets back on the field due to some of the injuries among his fellow rookies. After being a healthy scratch in Weeks 3 and 4, Smith participated in 16 special teams snaps, the most he has played this season. His three total tackles, including one for a solo tackle, were good for him to build, but his holding penalty that negated a good return for Rashid Shaheed will be remembered the most.
The Seahawks added a third rookie to their 53-man roster on Oct. 6 with running back Robert Henry Jr. being signed off the Washington Commanders practice squad. He might be as developed or experienced as veterans Emanuel Wilson or George Holani, but surely he can’t be worse .
​There are nine rookies that are on the practice squad as of Tuesday morning. This includes four who were drafted by the Seahawks: cornerback Michael Dansby, defensive tackle Deven Eastern, cornerback Andre Fuller and wide receiver Emmanuel Henderson Jr.
​Guard Evan Beerntsen, edge rusher Aidan Hubbard, running back Dontae McMillan, wide receiver Malick Meiga and defensive tackle Gary Smith III are all undrafted players who could take emergency roster spots if more injuries occur. The Seahawks acquired McMillan after the attempt to sign veteran Joe Mixon fell through .
​The Seahawks now have their top three picks in the draft on IR. Neal was placed on IR before the 49ers game with a hamstring injury. He managed to get on the field for all four games on special teams and one game for defense. Neal will miss at least the games against the Denver Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs and the Chicago Bears.
​Their top-selected rookie running back in Jadarian Price, will be out for at least two more games due to a chest injury. The Seahawks’ run game wasn’t in good shape while he was the number one , but it is certainly a disaster under Wilson and Holani as the main back. It will be a race between Price and veteran Zach Charbonnet to see who saves the offense.
​The final rookie on IR is safety Bud Clark, who suffered a broken ankle in the second preseason game. Clark would have found himself playing in all five games, starting in four of the first games, due to Ty Okada’s injury. The Seahawks likely won’t get him back on the field until he is a 25-year-old second-year player.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Seahawks vs. Broncos in Week 6
full_text:
Five weeks into the 2026 season, both the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos are right where they were a year ago at this time. Both Mike Macdonald’s club and Sean Payton’s squad are off to 3-2 starts this past season. Of course, while the Seahawks went onto to capture their second Lombardi Trophy in Santa Clara, the Broncos were knocked off at home by the New England Patriots in the AFC title game.
This season to date, it’s been somewhat hard to get a gauge on both clubs. The fact is that the Seahawks are already two games behind the first-place San Francisco 49ers, who they fell to on Sunday at Lumen Field, 32-29.
Meanwhile, despite Sunday’s 23-17 victory over the Chargers at SoFi Stadium, Payton’s team trails the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC West.
There was a time where these teams were AFC West rivals (1977-2001). There was also a Super Sunday in which these franchises were combatants—Seattle pummeling Peyton Manning and company at MetLife Stadium in Super Bowl XLVIII, 43-8.
Thursday night will mark the third time in five seasons that the clubs will meet, with the Seahawks winning both games at home in 2022 (17-16) and in ’24 (26-20). As for the last time the teams met in the Mile High City, the Broncos came away with a 27-24 victory in 2018.
What a turn of events before halftime 😱 @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mz5QVBRjhE
In three wins this season, Macdonald’s club has committed a combined two turnovers. In a pair of losses, the ‘Hawks has given up the ball seven times —two of those miscues returned/recovered for scores. Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold has thrown seven TD passes and been picked off five times the last three weeks.
Despite owning a winning record, Payton’s team has been outscored on the season, 111-97. Both of the Broncos’ losses come by double digits, while each of their three wins have been by seven points or less. Keep an eye on the first 30 minutes as Denver have been doubled up in the first half by a 46-23 score.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba is human?? Seahawks turnover on downs on the next play and fall to 3-2. pic.twitter.com/ktRF9VkB0d
For the fourth time this season, Jaxon Smith-Njigba finished a game with 100-plus receiving yards and at least one score. He was targeted eight times and snared five passes for 102 yards and one TD in the loss to the Niners. But it was a catch he didn’t make in the fourth quarter that was the topic of questions.
The Broncos have led the NFL in sacks each of the past two seasons. They amassed 63 quarterback traps in 2024 and a year ago, corralled opposing signal-callers a total of 68 times. This season, they’ve totaled 13 sacks in five games, led by defensive end Zach Allen (4.0) and two-time Pro Bowler Nik Bonitto (3.0).

title: Byron Murphy II Could Decide Whether Seahawks Beat Broncos
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks defensive lineman Byron Murphy II has really come along in his last two weeks of the season.
He has recorded three sacks in the last two games, including a pair in the team's Week 5 loss against the San Francisco 49ers . Murphy has 7.5 sacks over the course of his first 31 games, and he's well on pace to smash that number out of the water this season. Murphy explained how he is improving his pass rush repertoire.
"I feel like it's going pretty good," Murphy said via the team's website.
"Last week, when I got my first sack of the season, I'm like, damn, when you get that first one, they just start coming to you, they start coming in bunches, and I got two yesterday. I feel pretty good just being able to go out there and showcase my pass-rushing ability and for the coaches to believe in me, knowing, 'OK, this guy can rush and we're going to give him opportunities.' Being able to go out there and put my best foot forward is pretty cool."
Murphy will have a tough task against the Broncos' offensive line, which has done a good job keeping quarterback Bo Nix upright this season. After letting him fall to the ground four times in the team's Week 1 opener against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs, Nix has only been sacked twice in the last four games.
The Seahawks already have 14 sacks on the season, putting them in the top 10 among all NFL teams. If Murphy contributes to that number, it makes the team dangerous from the edge and the inside, which makes it so much more difficult for opposing quarterbacks.
The Seahawks have to force the ball out of Nix's hands as soon as possible, and Murphy might be the strongest catalyst towards that.
With Leonard Williams dealing with an ankle injury on a short week, he is up in the air for the team's Week 6 contest against the Broncos. If he is unable to go, Murphy grows in importance for the team's game plan, which is likely going to come down to who wins the battle on the line of scrimmage.

title: What Mike Macdonald Said Should Scare Seahawks vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have their work cut out for them as they take on the AFC West defending champion Denver Broncos in Week 6's edition of Thursday Night Football.
It's one of the tougher games the Seahawks will face this season, as they go on the road at altitude in prime time on a short week against one of the objectively better teams on their schedule. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is aware of how tough the challenge ahead of them is.
"They're a tough team," Macdonald said via the team's website. "They're really talented. Defensively, they pair their personnel well with their scheme. They're aggressive. They do a really good job affecting the quarterback, affecting the ball, and denying the ball.
"Offensively, it's a tried-and-true scheme that Sean's (Payton) done over time. I know he just took over playcalling again, but the quarterback is playing at a very high level. He extends plays. It's complementary football. They're a good football team."
The Seahawks aren't used to facing long odds, but this is one of those moments as they head to Denver. The Broncos are a fundamentally sound team that is better than their 3-2 record suggests. The two losses the Broncos have had so far this season have come against undefeated teams, the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers.
They have found a way to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, and Los Angeles Chargers so far this season, showcasing how they have been battle-tested throughout the year and have proven that they are capable of being one of the best teams in the league.
In some ways, this game could act as a potential Super Bowl preview. Both teams claimed the top seed in their respective conference last season, and Denver was one win away from meeting Seattle in the Super Bowl.
The Week 6 contest against the Broncos may not be as big as the Super Bowl, but it is crucial for Seattle's long-term success . A win on the road in a hostile environment should give the Seahawks a boatload of confidence as they head into a very difficult stretch of their schedule.
Two more primetime games are coming ahead to close out October and start November. How they perform in these next three games could very well determine what kind of positioning the Seahawks are fighting for come the end of the year.

title: How Seahawks Are Preparing for Week 6 vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are just a few days away from going right back out onto the gridiron to take on the Denver Broncos in a crucial Week 6 matchup on Thursday Night Football.
The Seahawks are coming off of a 32-29 loss to their NFC West rival, the San Francisco 49ers, and they have a lot to prove in hopes of not matching their loss total from all of last season. It's been nearly two years since the Seahawks lost consecutive games, so there is a bit of a sense of urgency in the building as they prepare for the Broncos.
"We expect to grow in all three phases," head coach Mike Macdonald said via the team's website. "There's a sense of urgency to grow. Sometimes, you grow best by doubling down on your core competencies and the things you believe in. That's something we want to focus on is making sure that we're all aligned in all of the things, from players to coaches and how we want to play and how we want to execute and what's expected of us.
"We're growing on defense. We're growing on special teams. Our special teams took a jump yesterday. Offense is right there with it, but there's a sense of urgency to get going."
The quick turnaround from their loss against the Niners to preparing for the Broncos is helping the team move on quickly from dwelling too much on the mistakes they made against San Francisco.
"That's the good thing about us this week," linebacker Derick Hall said via the team's website.
"We have a game on Thursday. The guys are process oriented. We're ready to get back to work. Obviously, look at the tape, see where we can grow, see what we can do better, and that's a lot, obviously. Just trying to learn those things and get ready to move forward, toward Thursday because we have a big one in Denver."
The Seahawks now find themselves two games back in the NFC West standings and have some ground to make up. Getting a win against the Broncos will be the first step toward getting back to where they need to be. If they want to establish themselves as Super Bowl contenders once again, they will ensure that they have all their focus on facing off against the Broncos, who are one of the better teams on their schedule.
The key to preparing for a short week is putting the past behind you quickly and moving forward with more purpose. Time is short, so making sure every move toward preparation, mentally and physically, is made with more intent than usual is crucial. There is a larger margin for error, and the Seahawks have to be careful not to fall back into similar mistakes they made in their two losses so far this season.

title: 49ers LT Trent Williams' Latest Performance Shouldn't Be Taken for Granted
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams continues to prove that age is just a number.
At 38, he's still one of the best tackles in the league, but there's even more reason to suggest he's at the top of that list so far this season.
Williams has remained all business since signing a two-year extension this offseason , and that approach has translated to the field, helping the 49ers get off to a 5-0 start through the first five games.
As a unit, the offensive line was incredible through the first four games. Brock Purdy hadn't been sacked, yet he came through and produced incredible performances worthy of an MVP award.
Williams, of course, was one of the bright spots. But in Week 5, against the reigning Super Bowl champions on their home turf, he elevated his game to even greater heights.
He was dominant in pass protection, recording 34 pass-blocking opportunities without allowing a single pressure, sack, or quarterback hit. His practically flawless performance earned him a 100.0 pass-block efficiency rating.
He's at the stage in his career where every dominant performance should serve as a reminder to appreciate what the 49ers have while they still can.
Williams is producing the goods at an elite level - something that's unprecedented for his age. He will not be around forever, so these performances against arguably superior opposition need to be savoured.
Like much of this roster, Mike Evans aside, the only thing missing from Williams' résumé is a Lombardi Trophy. The 49ers are off to a perfect 5-0 start, with Williams playing a significant role in this stretch. If this core is going to win a championship together, this could be its best, and perhaps final, opportunity to get over the line.
Undoubtedly, a place in the Hall of Fame awaits Williams, but winning a Super Bowl would add another remarkable accolade to his legacy. It is the biggest metric of success in this league for a reason. Given his journey and everything he has accomplished, a championship would make an already incredible story that much more special.
It's almost one and a half years more with Williams before he likely retires . So it's important to keep him as healthy as possible, as he will always produce excellent performances.
What the 49ers need is some luck on the injury front, but so far, going 5-0 and 3-0 in the division is about as perfect a start as they could have hoped for in their Super Bowl quest.

title: 3 Reasons the 49ers Will Be Perfectly Fine Without Dre Greenlaw
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will be down one key player on defense in their next game, and it surprisingly won't be due to injury.
Dre Greenlaw will be out of the 49ers' Week 6 contest after t he NFL suspended him for his headbutt on a helmetless Ernest Jones in the win over the Seattle Seahawks.
Being without Greenlaw is a bummer, but the 49ers will actually be perfectly fine without him. Let's dive into the three reasons why they will be.
When Greenlaw was ejected, the 49ers used rookie Jaden Dugger in his stead on base-packages. Dugger did well in this role, so he'll be the first to look at for filling in.
He doesn't get utilized a ton in nickel packages, but I think the 49ers will work him in more there during practice this week. Garrett Wallow would've been an option, but he'll be out with a hamstring injury.
Luke Gifford will be another player they will consider, but I wouldn't call him a "capable" player. Dugger is their best option, and he's more than fine at filling in for Greenlaw.
It's also possible the 49ers look at Tatum Bethune there. He was a healthy scratch against the Seahawks, so we'll see if the 49ers think he can go out there and help.
If the linebackers aren't as capable as the 49ers think, then Raheem Morris will adapt. He's done a tremendous job this season so far, and there's no reason to doubt his ability to mask Greenlaw's absence.
The only thing he can't account for is Greenlaw's energy. That intensity is something he can't help with, but he can move his defense around to account for what Greenlaw was giving them.
It won't be perfect, but he should be able to get the defense to cover up Greenlaw's loss enough, especially since whoever fills in for him will likely be a prime target to be thrown and run at.
Whether the first two points work out or not, at the end of the day, the 49ers will be facing the lowly Washington Commanders. They are insanely mediocre.
Do the 49ers need Greenlaw to beat them? Absolutely not. If they did, they'd have a massive problem on their hands.
Defeating the Commanders should be a lock. They're coming off an embarrassing tie with the New York Giants after Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn's overtime blunder.
The Commanders are in shambles, with their defense as their only decent aspect. San Francisco's defense will be perfectly fine without Greenlaw against a terrible offense.

title: Brock Purdy Reminded Everyone of his Greatest Trait Against Seahawks
full_text:
What an incredible win the San Francisco 49ers got over the Seattle Seahawks . Entering the season, it was by far their toughest matchup on the schedule.
Winning by three points and going down to the wire proved that. The 49ers were significantly better in this game than they were in any of their three contests against Seattle last year.
Brock Purdy was one significant reason for that. He delivered dime after dime to Mike Evans , who dominated Seattle from start to finish.
However, his performance goes beyond his connection with Evans. Just in case anyone forgot, Purdy reminded everyone of his greatest trait against the Seahawks.
It's his mental toughness. That's his elite trait. I've been pointing it out for over three years . The guy has insanely strong mental fortitude. Not even a tank can measure up to it.
Purdy went into a chaotic environment at Lumen Field against the best defense in the NFL, one that has owned him and the 49ers' offense in the last two games, and was nails.
He could've easily folded under the immense pressure. He knew how big-time that game was. It wasn't just about beating a divisional opponent. The 49ers needed to stand up to their nightmare – Seattle's defense.
Purdy didn't let any of the last two matchups with the Seahawks bother him. He went into this game as cool as a cucumber. It's so impressive how he manages to remain unfazed.
But that's been evident since he became the starter in 2022. Whether it was primetime games or the playoffs, he doesn't get timid in important games.
The pressure of the game is one way he proves his mental toughness. Another way is how he responds to physical pressure in a game.
Quarterbacks who start to get sacked, hit, and pressured will likely fold over time. That could've easily happened to Purdy against the Seahawks.
He was pressured on 17 of his 34 dropbacks (50.0%), the third-highest pressure rate he has faced in a game in his career.
If he had started to struggle, no one would've blamed him. But he didn't. Not one bit. He knew what was going to happen to him in this game, despite how amazing his offensive line has been this season.
And while the 49ers' offense couldn't sustain drives for the majority of the game, Purdy helped lead the most important drive of the game, which started in the third quarter while down 26-21.
The 49ers went on a 12-play, 74-yard series that came away with a touchdown. Again, Purdy didn't get discouraged by the weight of the game, the pressure in his face, and the fact that they struggled to move the ball a lot.
Did he play a great game as he did against the Miami Dolphins and the Arizona Cardinals? No. But against the NFL's best defense on the road, he proved more in that game than against Miami and Arizona.
Purdy has raised his game this season. It's tough to deny that, but one thing that's never been debatable is his elite mental toughness, and he reminded everyone of that in the win against the Seahawks.

title: How the 49ers' Week 5 Win Changed Their Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers moved to 5-0 after beating the Seattle Seahawks. Beating the defending Super Bowl Champions in their own house to move into first place in what was deemed the toughest division in the NFL is going to cause the 49ers to get more aggressive with just a few weeks to go until the November 10 trade deadline.
However, the Week 5 win might have changed how the 49ers decide to make moves at the deadline.
Wide receiver shot up to the biggest need, ahead of anything defensive line-related. On one hand, they expect to see Demarcus Robinson, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Deebo Samuel at some point this season. On the other hand, all three are out right now.
Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing are hardly providing any sort of production , and the pass-catching core is starting to center around Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, and George Kittle. They need someone to help take attention away from those three.
Another position that has become more imperative to add is tight end. The good news is that they do not necessarily need a pass-catching tight end. However, with both Kyle Jusczcyk and Jake Tonges out, the team does not have enough versatile threats who can block and catch passes.
Luke Farrell is playing more, but he is not the best blocker, and teams do not respect him as a pass catcher. They only need a slight upgrade from Farrell, but that is something that has to be addressed.
On the defensive line, the interior remains a big need, but an edge rusher might be able to get pushed to the side. Rookie Romello Height and depth piece Keion White held things down for a few weeks. Mykel Williams returned last week, and Nick Bosa might be back this week.
All of a sudden, the edge rusher room could start to look complete.
The interior defensive line is not, though. Osa Odighizuwa is going to set a career-high in snaps early into the season. Gracen Halton is a strong pass rusher, but he is a rookie who is playing a lot. Sebastian Valdez is a practice squad call-up who also runs hot and cold in the run game.
The good news is that they have enough pass-rush juice, and that is what costs draft capital. However, they need to find a run defender soon.

title: Why 49ers DC Raheem Morris is an Upgrade Over Robert Saleh
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' front office made the right decision in appointing Raheem Morris as defensive coordinator this season.
After returning to San Francisco last season, Robert Saleh has since moved on to become the Tennessee Titans' head coach. His contribution to the 49ers was immeasurable in its own right, helping an injury-ridden roster reach the playoffs despite the challenges they faced.
With Morris now in place, the 49ers appear to have made the right choice. Whether or not he was brought in as an upgrade on Saleh, Morris has arguably already proven himself to be one.
Losing Nick Bosa in Week 3 and Fred Warner in Week 6 is a tough blow for any defensive coordinator. Saleh had to contend with those setbacks alongside incessant injuries last season, but the defense's biggest weakness was its inability to consistently generate sacks.
The 49ers recorded just 20 sacks last season, the fewest in the league, which was a disappointing return by any measure. Under Morris, however, they have already shown significant improvement, recording 11 sacks through five games despite injuries on the defensive side of the ball.
Bosa has featured in just two games due to further injury setbacks, while Mykel Williams was limited to a reduced snap count in the most recent outing because that was his first game back from an ACL injury as well. Despite those absences and other defensive injuries, San Francisco has found ways to generate pressure and bring opposing quarterbacks down.
Sure, 11 sacks is some way off the league-leading Detroit Lions' 20, but it represents a considerable improvement on last season's production. More importantly, the 49ers are finding contributions from across the defensive line.
In Week 5 against the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, five sacks were made, all of which came from different players. Jaden Dugger, Sebastian Valdez, Gracen Holton, Keion White and Osa Odighizuwa all recorded one each.
On his influence and the job done so far, Kyle Shanahan stated : "It doesn't surprise me with Raheem. I've just been around him for too long. He's one of the best people and best coaches I've ever been around.
"I tried to bring him here originally when I left Atlanta. They wouldn't let him out. So, it's been a long time coming to get him here. He's done an unbelievable job this year, especially with the injuries, but just overall everything he's mixed up schematically.
"I love the confidence he's given our DBs and the way they've been playing since training camp. He's had a real huge effect on this team and we're very lucky to have him."
The front office needs to try to lock him down for next year. They desperately need continuity at that position.

title: 49ers’ Biggest Hero of 2025 Faces Some Early Questions in 2026
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have enjoyed a perfect 5-0 start to the season despite another year of injuries taking a toll on the roster.
They’ve beaten the Los Angeles Rams on neutral territory in Australia, taken down the Denver Broncos, who reached last season’s AFC Championship Game, and then edged out the very team that ended their season last year and went on to win the Super Bowl, the Seattle Seahawks,
So far, so good, but while these victories over teams that performed better than the 49ers last season should provide confidence, San Francisco is still lacking in certain areas.
The key one is now at a position that was near-perfect in 2025. At kicker, Eddy Piñeiro seems to have dwindled in form quite a bit to start the season. It's not the most worrying thing in the world yet, with the 49ers enjoying a perfect start to the year. But fine margins are huge in this game.
He missed a field goal against Seattle and is so far 2-for-5 on 50+ yard attempts this season. The kick was a complete miss as well. It wasn't even close.
It's far from ideal, especially considering he went 6-for-7 on attempts from 50+ yards last season, with his only miss coming from 65 yards out. He was essentially perfect from all distances last year.
In addition, he's missed two extra points after touchdowns this year. Sure, it's only an extra point, but he missed five all of last season, so it's still something to keep an eye on. No one knows why he's had such a shaky start to the year, which makes it slightly more confusing.
If things don't change soon, the 49ers front office will start to receive scrutiny because they locked him down to a four-year contract in the offseason .
But winning football matches is what they've done and what matters; Piñeiro just has to be ready for those eventual moments when he's needed most - and the Seahawks game was an example of getting them over the line to win 32-29.
There's no reason to put heat on him yet, but in the second half of the year, especially when it's a tough part of the schedule against tricky opponents, the spotlight will be shining brightly on Piñeiro.
For now, it could just be a small bump in the road. That's football. But the 49ers will have to monitor the situation closely.

title: Deebo Samuel Injury Exposes Bigger Problem for 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been able to survive a lot of injuries this season. While Deebo Samuel was a late addition this offseason, the team missing him for the next couple of weeks is really going to test what the offense can do.
As things stand, the 49ers are very top-heavy in their pass-catching corps. The room has 137 total targets. There are four players who make up 107 of those targets. Samuel has 16 receptions for 206 yards this season. Of those, 80 came on a trick play where he did not even make the reception.
So, even as the fourth option, he was not bringing much. Still, he had to be respected as a legitimate option. The offense lost Jake Tonges for the season earlier in the year. Kyle Juszczyk is going to miss the next couple of weeks as well. Even Demarcus Robinson is currently fifth on the team in targets, and he is on the IR.
Without Samuel, the offense is highly reliant on Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, and Mike Evans.
Jacob Cowing has five targets and just one reception. Jordan Watkins has 60 yards on two receptions. Luke Farrell is playing more due to the injuries but is a blocking option who has two receptions for 19 yards.
The 49ers are starting to get too thin in their skill players. McCaffrey, Kittle, and Evans can carry the group, but if all three are being asked to have their best performances throughout the season, the sustainability of this success is not going to last.
Evans has already missed time this year, Kittle is coming back from an injury, and McCaffrey has a few serious injuries on his resume as well.
Because Juszczyk, Robinson, and Samuel will be back at some point, the assumption is the 49ers will not make a drastic move to add a playmaker. Still, it will be tough to get by until then, and the team could end up looking into a trade option as some teams begin to understand they are sellers this year.
The 49ers built up a 5-0 record, and they beat the defending Super Bowl champions. However, that does not guarantee the team is going to win anything in the postseason. They still have to preserve their roster and ensure they can make a run.

title: Dre Greenlaw Suspension Opens Door for 49ers Rookie
full_text:
The suspension of Dre Greenlaw is disappointing for the San Francisco 49ers, but it also opens the door to what the future could look like for the team. Rookie Jaden Dugger has been the 49ers' starting SAM linebacker, but that is a less prominent role.
With Greenlaw out, he is likely going to get his first start at WILL, which means playing the majority of the snaps in Week 6.
Dugger played 55.7% of the 49ers' snaps in their blowout win over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1. He has not played that much since. In Week 2, Dugger played 30.5% of the defensive snaps and then played 37.9% of the snaps in Week 3.
He dipped to just 15 snaps and 22.7% of the snaps overall. This speaks to his role being dependent on the game script. However, he played a career-high 47 snaps and 75% of the snaps with Greenlaw out of the game. This is a much different role.
The 49ers could have kept him as the SAM and played Garrett Wallow more, which is what happened when Greenlaw went down earlier in the year. However, Wallow is going to miss time as well due to an injury. Now that he is going to be out for another game, it gives the rookie a chance to be a full-time starter for the first time.
The former fifth-round pick from Louisiana was known for his versatility in college. He aligned everywhere from the edge to linebacker and safety. The 49ers have been taking advantage of his versatility in his limited role, but this will provide him more of a chance to focus on a specific position.
The question becomes what happens if Dugger plays well. Week 5 was arguably his best game as an NFL player. He embraced the change in role. His athleticism and potential are hard to deny, and if things go right, the plan would be for the 49ers to let Greenlaw go this offseason and have Dugger step into a bigger role. If he can continue to play well to the point where it is not hurting the team, and he is growing into the role he will play next season, does the team really need to go back to Greenlaw? This could be a major opportunity.

title: Realistic or Not Realistic: Who Can the 49ers Add at Wide Receiver?
full_text:
New year, same story in Santa Clara: the 49ers can’t stay healthy.
San Francisco enters Week 6 with a receiver room stretched thin. Only two of the wideouts from the initial 53-man roster, Mike Evans and Jordan Watkins, got through Sunday’s game in Seattle without leaving with an injury. Brandin Cooks is also healthy, but he was signed after Week 2.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan has already said Deebo Samuel will miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury. Jacob Cowing, a player who should already be feeling the heat, left Seattle banged up with an ankle issue.
That leaves the Niners to face the Washington Commanders on Monday night with Evans, Cowing (ankle), Cooks and Watkins. That’s thin help for one of the league’s best passing offenses, so here’s a look at who could come to aid the WR room.
Probability: 1% — Unrealistic
At his peak, Hill was as dynamic as any playmaker in the league. But he’s coming off a season-ending knee injury in 2025 and still has legal trouble hanging over him. San Francisco would likely prefer a player with less noise around him and no rehab to manage. And if Hill is fully healthy, he’s not a practice-squad candidate. He’d command a 53-man roster spot. I think that's where the 49ers would fall out of Tyreek signing race.
Probability: 50% — Realistic
If your first reaction was “who?”, fair enough. Skinner turned heads in the Jets’ 2025 preseason and spent the season on their practice squad, catching one pass for 10 yards and a two-point conversion in the regular season. He’s a 6'5" target who can win downfield, and he ran a 4.52 40-yard dash at his pro day. The concern is Shanahan’s long-standing reluctance to trust young receivers who haven’t mastered the nuances of his offense. Skinner got a workout in late September, but the team signed Dante Pettis instead.
Probability: 0.5% — Unrealistic
If Sunday’s win showed anything, it’s the value of a receiver like Evans, whose huge catch radius means the offense doesn’t have to rely on separation. Brock Purdy knows how to take advantage of that and isn’t shy about letting it fly. Hopkins is on the Georgia Tech coaching staff but has made it clear he isn’t retired. Shanahan loves his veterans, but this is a long shot.
Probability: 60% — Realistic
The 49ers don’t want to give up draft capital for a receiver. They’d rather save it for an edge rusher or an interior defensive lineman. Still, this fit makes too much sense for John Lynch not to at least call Minnesota. Shanahan values veterans, and a player like Jennings would need almost no time to learn the new playbook. He showed clear frustration Sunday, even with the Vikings off to a 5-0 start. He has just two catches for nine yards on the season, far below his production in recent years, which could open the door for a swap of late-round picks.
Probability: 0% — Unrealistic
If Beckham were still a free agent, Shanahan might consider him for the practice squad. But he’s on the Vikings’ practice squad, and I can’t see San Francisco putting him on the 53-man roster. In 2019 the Niners would have jumped at the chance. We’re a long way past that now.
Probability: 0% — Unrealistic
Getting Thomas would cost a second-round pick at minimum, whatever you think of how things have gone in Jacksonville. His draft classmate Marvin Harrison Jr. just went to Houston with a second-rounder as the main return to Arizona. Thomas has done more than Harrison, so that’s the floor for the Jaguars. If the Niners are spending a second, it should go toward a defensive lineman of Vita Vea or DeForest Buckner caliber.
Don’t expect a splash. Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel and De’Zhaun Stribling are all due back this season, and that matters when weighing a move for a player who would count against the 53-man roster.

title: Buccaneers Could Get Wide Receiver Back vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had what they considered to be quite a deep wide receivers corps heading into 2026. Unfortunately, that idea hasn't exactly shown up on the turf through Week 5.
Wideouts Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, both considered to be focal points of the offense, haven't produced relative to expectations. Jalen McMillan, expected to be a valuable weapon for the Bucs, has played just one game so far this season, and he's currently recovering from a knee injury.
Other wideouts, like rookie Ted Hurst and second-year player Tez Johnson, have had to step up in McMillan's place.
But now, the Bucs may be getting back another wide receiver they've been missing all year to help bolster that receiving corps, and he could come back as soon as Sunday when the Buccaneers play the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Bucs wideout David Sills V, who injured himself during training camp with a hamstring injury and was placed on injured reserve, opened his 21-day practice window on Monday. Sills will get his first bit of practice for the first time in a long time on Wednesday as the Bucs prepare for the Steelers.
Sills is a big-bodied wideout who could help Tampa Bay on the outside. He played with Zac Robinson last season with the Atlanta Falcons, so Robinson knows how to use him and the two understand each other's offensive goals quite well.
With McMillan still out, Sills could end up being valuable depth for the Bucs — if Tampa Bay wants to make use of him. Sills has 21 days from Oct. 12 to get back on the field and return to Tampa Bay's active roster. If he does not do so within those 21 days, he remains on IR and must remain there until the end of the season.
As it stands, Tampa Bay's 53-man roster is full. That means that if the Bucs want Sills on the active roster, they'll have to move another player off to make room — that player could go to Tampa Bay's practice squad or get released entirely.
If Sills is able to get back in time for Tampa Bay's game against the Steelers, quarterback Jalon Daniels will have another weapon to work with on offense. If not, he could shoot for the week after against the Carolina Panthers, where starting QB Baker Mayfield will likely be quarterback after he recovers from his thumb injury.
The Bucs play the Steelers on Oct. 18 in Raymond James Stadium.

title: President Donald Trump Reportedly No Longer Attending Buccaneers-Steelers Game
full_text:
EDIT: President Trump reportedly has called his trip to the Buccaneers’ game on Sunday off, per CNN senior White House Correspondent Kristen Holmes. This story was originally written when President Trump was scheduled to attend the game. The original article from the initial report is featured below.
Good news for the many people who hated this news— after we reported it, I am told they pulled down the trip. So… hope you kept your tickets! https://t.co/ZQNpS4EJii
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking to improve to 2-4 on the year when they face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers this upcoming Sunday at Raymond James Stadium. And when they do, they'll reportedly be hosting a high-profile guest.
The President of the United States, Donald Trump, is reportedly planning on attending Tampa Bay's game against Pittsburgh, per CNN senior White House correspondent Kristen Holmes. The game will be played in Tampa, 220 miles away from Trump's Mar-a-Lago home in Palm Beach.
President Trump is expected to attend the Tampa Bay game in Florida Sunday, two sources familiar with the plan tell CNN. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are playing the Steelers.
Trump will attend the game Sunday just one day before he's scheduled to appear in Wichita, Kansas, for a campaign rally ahead of midterm elections.
This game is slated to be the third football game Trump has attended this year, and it will be his first NFL game. Trump previously attended the College Football National Championship game between the Indiana Hoosiers and the Miami Hurricanes in Miami on Jan. 19, and he also attended a game between the Texas Longhorns and the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Sept. 26.
His appearance will mark the first time a sitting United States President has ever attended a Tampa Bay Buccaneers game.
Trump's appearance will certainly increase security around the event, both through traffic on the way there and around the stadium itself, but it could also add a wrinkle that could affect the players and coaches on the field come game day.
Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian told reporters before their game against Tennessee that friends of his on Miami's coaching staff informed him that communications are cut whenever the President moves locations in the stadium.
"Anytime the President changes locations within the stadium, they cut all communication. They cut your headsets in terms of coach to player communication. So you have to plan for that," Sarkisian said . "You get no warning. It just cuts out. You have to be prepared for that."
Trump's own team on social media pushed back at this narrative after his appearance at the game, but either way, it's something to think about for head coach Todd Bowles and his staff.
No, President Trump's departure from the CFP championship in January did not cause headset or comms issues for the teams. @MarcACaputo has the receipts: https://t.co/ZMN0vkpNCS
Bowles and offensive coordinator Zac Robinson are no strangers to that, though. Tampa Bay's communications were not working during the team's first game of the season against the Cincinnati Bengals, and it had to deal with that then, too. There's no guarantee that Trump's appearance will continue to cause those issues, but if it does, the Bucs will likely be prepared.
Tampa Bay faces off against Pittsburgh at 1 p.m. on Oct. 18.

title: Jalon Daniels' Advanced Metrics Trending Upward After First Career Win With Bucs
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers felt dead in the water after starting the season 0-3. And then the unthinkable happened.
They were forced to start an undrafted rookie at quarterback after Baker Mayfield went down with an injury.
Jalon Daniels was thrust into the fire early in his NFL career, but it didn't net him success in his first start. However, he and the team were able to figure out what works best, as he went on to win his second career start against the Dallas Cowboys.
In Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers, in his first start, Daniels was turbulent. He completed 19 passes for 148 yards and a touchdown, but he also threw two interceptions and took three sacks, resulting in a negative passing EPA (expected points added) of -0.194.
EPA, which measures the value of a play based on how much it increases or decreases a team's likelihood of scoring, tells a deeper story about how a player is impacting his team's success.
Daniels was able to flip his impact on the game with a positive EPA against the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, coming away with a positive +0.229 EPA. He completed 76% of his passes for 189 yards, one touchdown, no interceptions and just one sack.
Drastically cutting down on high-risk mistakes and going turnover-free showed his improved decision-making after just one game in a primetime spot.
It wasn't just Daniels who looked sharp against Dallas. It was also the positions that offensive coordinator Zac Robinson was putting him in.
Across both games, Daniels has produced a high completion rate, but an extremely low average depth of target (4.1 yards).
While that didn't necessarily work against the Packers, it did against the Cowboys. It goes to show that Robinson is scheming up high-percentage throws that protect his young quarterback from facing heavy pressure, mitigating negative plays.
This has also allowed Daniels to get the ball out fast to his playmakers to go and make plays, rather than putting all the pressure on himself.
Daniels has also been efficient when using his legs, which will only continue to add another layer to his game as he continues trending upward in the absence of Mayfield.
While Daniels isn't pushing the ball downfield just yet, his trajectory is pointing upward, which likely means Robinson and staff will feel more comfortable opening up the offense for him.
If Daniels can continue the efficient play and growth that we have seen through his first two career starts, the Bucs could be in a good position to steal another game or two while Mayfield works his way back.
No matter what, it's great to see that an undrafted rookie is making the most of the opportunities given to him. The Bucs must make the most of this if they hope to remain in the race for the NFC South, and that might just come down to Daniels continuing to elevate his game over the next week or two.

title: The Most Surprising Group for the Buccaneers During the 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense has actually done pretty well the past couple of weeks in matchups against the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys. The unit helped keep the Bucs in games, and if the offense were better, we would likely be talking about a Bucs team that has a better record than it does right now.
One of the biggest reasons for that is due to a group that started this season as a massive question mark, but has quickly turned into one of the great strengths of the team — the cornerback room.
Let's start off with the player who has likely looked the most impressive — cornerback Jacob Parrish.
Parrish had more pressure placed on him this off-season as he was going to move from inside corner to outside corner due to the lack of depth. So far to this point, Parrish has taken the move in stride and has made multiple plays on the football, including snagging an interception this season.
Zyon McCollum is another player who has really risen to the occasion for the Bucs.
Coming off a very disappointing 2025 season that left many fans wanting the team to move on, McCollum has stepped up against some of the best receivers in the league, CeeDee Lamb and Ja'Marr Chase, and has returned to form as the corner who earned the massive extension with the Buccaneers in the first place.
Finally, we have some surprises in Keionte Scott and Benjamin Morrison. Yes, Scott is a rookie nickel corner for the Buccaneers, but he really has done an excellent job in the short amount of time he's been on the team. He does make mistakes, but overall, it's hard to be too disappointed with how the recent fourth-round rookie has looked for the team.
When Morrison has been able to stay healthy this season, he has shown some great strides in his overall play, especially as a run defender. Yes, he is still struggling with staying healthy, but this is a far cry from the Morrison who looked completely out of place as a rookie last year and should give the Bucs some much-needed depth going forward if he is able to maintain his health.
The future seems bright for this Bucs corner room, and hopefully these players continue to grow and evolve as a strength for this team.

title: Why Baker Mayfield Shouldn’t Start for Buccaneers Against Steelers
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers starting quarterback Baker Mayfield seems to be recovering well from his dislocated thumb suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings.
However, it may not be the wisest of decisions to bring him back this quickly when the Bucs face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers after a long break when they beat the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
After starting the season 0-4 with three of those losses coming with Mayfield at the helm of the offense, the Bucs were finally able to get their first victory with Jalon Daniels commanding the offense.
It wasn't the most spectacular outing for Daniels, but he was able to provide a spark that helped the offense look competent — something they haven't looked like all season.
Daniels performed admirably in his first start, a loss to the Green Bay Packers, but was able to lift the offense against the Cowboys. His charismatic energy, passion, and love for the game seemed to reverberate throughout the rest of the team. That instilled confidence in every player around him.
Everything about the offense seemed to run smoothly, sparking the Bucs to score their second-most points of the season.
Inserting Mayfield at less than 100% against the Steelers would be a disservice given the spark that Daniels has brought to this team.
Mayfield signed a massive extension this past offseason, so bringing him back and putting him in a position to further injure the same injury or worse could put the future of their franchise quarterback in jeopardy.
With the dislocation being on his throwing hand, life will be difficult for Mayfield when it comes to gripping the ball, which will lead to decreased ball security and velocity on his throws.
With further injury and heightened risk of turnover prevalent in rushing Mayfield back against the Steelers in Week 6, it would be smart for the Bucs to continue letting him rehab no matter how much he pushes to return sooner.
The season isn't a complete loss yet, with Tampa Bay still within shouting distance of the NFC South lead.
Taking one step forward after a win, only to take two steps back by playing his injury and rehab wrong, would further put pressure on the front office and coaching staff.

title: Was Mike Evans Right to Leave Buccaneers for 49ers?
full_text:
Some players are franchise legends for their entire career and make their name with just one team. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers know what that's like — linebacker Lavonte David was one of those players, and he retired in 2025 after 14 seasons in red and pewter.
The Bucs also thought wideout Mike Evans was going to be one of those players — and so did he. When Evans re-signed with the Bucs before the start of the 2024 season, he famously declared that he was set to be a "Buc for life." Two years later, he was gone.
Evans decided to spurn the Bucs in free agency and sign with the San Francisco 49ers instead, leaving the team after 12 years of service. There's been plenty of talk about that move ever since it happened, and now that we're five weeks into the season, we're getting a clearer look at where Evans and the Bucs currently stand.
The look? Tampa Bay is 1-4 and staring at oblivion, and Evans and the 49ers are 5-0 and looking toward the Super Bowl.
So, was Evans right in leaving the Buccaneers to chase glory at the end of his career? It sure looks like it right now.
There's no doubt that being a one-franchise player would have meant a lot to Evans. But there are things that matter more, and he's on a better track to achieve those things in San Francisco than he would have been in Tampa Bay.
Evans wants to be a Hall of Famer. To do that, he needs more production, he needs to be in the public eye more often and he needs to be on a team that could potentially win him a ring in the future. There was a time with Tom Brady that the Bucs hit on all three of those requirements, but that time is far gone.
The Bucs are not a Super Bowl-caliber team. They also have multiple wide receivers on their roster to share targets with, so Evans wouldn't have gotten the share he wanted, and with Brady gone and the Bucs middling, Evans likely wouldn't have gotten the exposure required for a Hall of Fame bid.
Even worse? The Buccaneers could be staring at a rebuild next season. If head coach Todd Bowles is fired (and maybe even general manager Jason Licht), the Bucs will be starting from scratch, and Evans could have simply been on his way out regardless. Retiring as a member of the team and continuing to make his case as a Hall of Famer now seems entirely impossible, and that the gamble Evans made here was right.
Whether it was because of what happened at the end of 2025 and the infamous third-and-28 or because he simply wanted a change of scenery, Evans was certainly right to separate from Tampa Bay. And he's proved it already in Week 5 of the regular season.
The Bucs face off against the Steelers in Week 6 to try to move to 2-4 on the year. Evans and the 49ers face off against the Washington Commanders to try and move to 6-0.

title: Week 5 NFC South Update: Are the Buccaneers Still Last in the Division?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their big win in Week 5 out of the way early, beating the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 at AT&T Stadium.
They got to have the rest of the week off and sit back on Sunday while the rest of the league played its Sunday slate. Two other teams in the NFC South played their games, while the Carolina Panthers took the Sunday off too — they were on their bye week, though.
Here's how the Atlanta Falcons and the New Orleans Saints did, and where the Bucs sit in the division — their win changed some things around in the NFC South.
The Panthers technically lead the division because they did not play a game on Sunday, so they still sit at 2-2.
The Atlanta Falcons played a close overtime thriller with the Baltimore Ravens, but they lost 30-23 after a backbreaking Tua Tagovailoa interception late in overtime. As a result, they sit in second with the same amount of wins as Carolina but with an extra loss due to the bye-week discrepancy.
The New Orleans Saints lost their game against the Minnesota Vikings 23-13, which drops them to 1-4 on the year. That game propelled the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to third place in the division, not last, due to New Orleans' NFC South loss against the Falcons and their much poorer point differential.
The craziest thing? With Atlanta's loss on Sunday night, the Bucs are just one game back from the NFC South lead. It would be a surprising turn of events, but if Tampa Bay were to get something going here quickly, the division would still be very much in reach for the Bucs.
That turnaround continues next Sunday. The Bucs face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and they'll try to beat them in Raymond James Stadium to move to 2-4 on the year. A win would be great for Tampa Bay's upward projection, but a loss would plummet them to 1-5 and put most in the organization right back in the hot seat.

title: 3 Buccaneers Players Who Could Be Traded Before Deadline
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may be coming off a win, but things still don't look great for them heading into the rest of the season. The team is 1-4, and if things go poorly, it could be staring at a rebuild next year with a new head coach.
If that's the case, general manager Jason Licht may want to get some new draft capital. Licht almost never trades midseason , but what if he did? And if he needed some draft picks, which Buccaneers players would he be willing to give up? Who would teams want?
We tried to answer all these questions with three potential Bucs players who could be moved before the deadline:
If the Bucs don't play well leading up to the deadline, they'd probably be down to get anything they could from Chris Godwin. Godwin is 30 years old and isn't getting a ton of use in Zac Robinson's scheme, and there are probably a few teams that wouldn't mind his veteran presence and experience at the position — and maybe a few that would utilize him just a bit more.
Godwin is currently playing on a $22 million deal this year after signing a three-year deal for that much on average. But his last deal is a team option, so any team that traded for Godwin could either extend him to the tune of $22 million more or simply let him walk. Godwin could be a rental for any team looking to take themselves over the line, and the Bucs could get a little capital on top.
Gainwell is another player the Bucs haven't been using much. He's only ran the ball 17 times for 44 yards, just 2.6 yards per carry — he's also only caught 11 passes for 54 yards and a touchdown.
RB-needy teams could easily call about Gainwell if needed. The Bucs have Sean Tucker available and Tucker has looked good in his limited snaps, so he could slide right into that RB2 postion (and he's be a lot cheaper). Any team that wants Gainwell would have to take on his two-year, $14 million contract, which he's currently in the first year of.
This one doesn't feel particularly likely, because the Bucs' pass rush hasn't been great. But if Tampa Bay really wants some capital back before what could be a rebuilding year next year, Diaby wouldn't be a bad player to move.
Diaby is on a contract year as it stands and will be a free agent in March. As a result, any team picking him up wouldn't have to worry about taking on a big contract and could instead watch him to see how he plays — if he pays well, they can extend him, and if not, he'd be a quick rental.
Diaby has five solo tackles and a pick without any sacks so far this season. The Bucs probably want to keep him around for now, but it might be wise to simply listen if a team comes calling.

title: Cam Ward Beats David Carr, Tim Couch and Other Busts for Worst Record in First 22 Starts in NFL History
full_text:
After Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans , QB Cam Ward has the fewest wins across 22 starts of any NFL quarterback to begin their career.
In Ward's rookie campaign, he led the Titans to a 3-14 record. The last time Ward guided Tennessee to a win was in December against the Kansas City Chiefs without QB Patrick Mahomes, since the Titans have lost seven straight with Ward at the helm, including a 0-5 start, to begin the 2026 season.
In Sunday's blowout loss to Houston, Titans fans poured boos over the field and held up signs showing their frustrations .
Although football is the ultimate team sport, in recent years, a quarterback's win-loss record has become just as much a position stat as ERA is to pitchers in baseball. Whether or not the blame should fall on the shoulders of the 24-year-old quarterback, the numbers contextualize how medicore Ward's career has been.
Let's take a look at the short list of losing NFL quarterbacks who have started their careers with more wins than Ward.
Former University of Kentucky great, QB Tim Couch, like Ward, was drafted number one in the 1999 NFL Draft to the newly expanded Cleveland Browns.
In 1996, the Browns moved to Baltimore, becoming the Baltimore Ravens. After three years of no football in northern Ohio, the Cleveland Browns were reinstated as an expansion franchise.
Couch made his first career start in Week 2 against the newly rebranded Tennessee Titans; the Browns lost 9-26. Cleveland would only win two games in Couch's rough rookie season, one less than Ward's rookie campaign.
In his sophomore season, Couch led the Browns to a 2-1 start before going on a four-game losing streak. A broken thumb sidelined Couch for missing the remainder of the season.
In 2001, Couch made his 22nd start and lost, going 4-18 in that stretch, earning one more than Ward to begin his career.
Unfortunately, Coach would retire at the age of 26 due to major injuries. He finished his career with the Browns, going 22-37 as a starter, throwing 67 interceptions to 64 touchdowns.
Today, Couch is remembered as the beginning of the Browns' carousel of quarterbacks .
Drafted sixth overall by the Cincinnati Bengals, QB David Klingler was a standout at the University of Houston. The Bengals selected Klingler to be the successor to franchise legend QB Boomer Esaison.
After a rocky start of 4-7, Cincinnati benched Esaison in favor of Klingler. The rookie struggled, losing his first three starts before finally earning his first and only win as a rookie.
The Bengals traded Esaison to the New York Jets, and Klingler was named the full-time starter, but he continued to underperform. In his first 22 starts, he only earned four wins, which is one more win than Ward.
Klingler was benched for good in 1994 after going 0-7 to start the season. Over the next three seasons, Klingler only appeared in five games as a backup.
He finished his career with a 4-20 record, throwing 22 interceptions and 16 touchdowns.
The Houston Texans selected QB David Carr first overall in the 2002 NFL Draft. The Texans were given the first pick because they were an expansion team, bringing football back to Houston since the Oilers left in 1996 for Tennessee.
Similar to Ward, Carr was named the day-one starter as the number one pick. In his NFL debut, Carr steered the newly formed Texans to a 19-10 victory over in-state opponent the Dallas Cowboys.
Carr ended his rookie season with a 4-12 record, earning one more win than Ward despite finishing the season without a touchdown over the final six games. In 2003, Carr made his 22nd start in his sophomore season and lost, finishing with a 6-16 record in that span.
Carr continued to quarterback the Texans for the next several seasons with little success. He made his final start in 2007 as a member of the Carolina Panthers before spending four years as a backup.
In 2012, Carr retired a Super Bowl champion as a backup for Eli Manning. Carr finished his career with a 23-56 record as a starter, throwing 71 interceptions to 65 touchdowns as a pro.
Carr holds an NFL record for the most sacks taken in a single season with 76 , which came in his rookie season.
Coming out of Washington State, QB Ryan Leaf was considered worthy of the first overall pick in the 1998 NFL Draft over Hall of Famer Peyton Manning. Ultimately, the Colts chose Manning, and Leaf was selected second to the San Diego Chargers.
In 1998, Leaf was a Week 1 starter, like Ward. He won his first two starts over the Bills and Titans before getting benched in Week 10 due to a sour performance against the Broncos.
Leaf would appear in one more game in Week 15 as a backup; he finished his rookie season 3-9 as a starter.
Over the next two seasons, Leaf would only make nine more starts before flaming out with the Dallas Cowboys in 2001. Although Leaf was one start shy of 22 career starts, he still earned one more win than Ward.
Across his three seasons as a pro, Leaf went 4-17 as a starter and had a horrendous 14-36 touchdown-to-interception ratio. He was out of the NFL by the age of 25.
Today, Leaf is widely regarded as one of the biggest busts in recent NFL history.

title: Grading Every Titans Position Group After Week 5 Loss vs. Texans
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans produced another lifeless effort on Sunday, falling 26-3 to the Houston Texans in a lopsided battle between two winless teams.
Even the most optimistic Titans fan can’t help but feel dejected after a performance like that . Things started badly, and they only got worse as the game progressed.
This Titans team is simply broken in many ways, and until things get fixed, you’re going to continue seeing the type of poor grades you’re about to sees
QB Cam Ward struggled mightily in this one, completing just 23 of his 36 passes for 170 yards and one interception.
The second-year quarterback continues to be erratic with his ball placement. Ward has a knack for making catches harder than they have to be, which leads to drops or missed opportunities after the catch.
Another area where he continues to struggle is his ability to process what he’s seeing both pre- and post-snap. His inability to diagnose the moving puzzle often gets him in trouble and/or prevents him from hitting the big plays that are there to be made.
All of these issues showed up early and often in what was arguably Ward’s worst outing of the season. But considering the performance of the offensive line (we’ll touch on that later), I’ll at least spare him from the F.
Things got off to a rocky start and never get much better. RB Tyjae Spears fumbled in the first quarter and failed to record a single rushing yard, while RB Tony Pollard averaged less than four yards per carry.
It was a putrid afternoon all around, and the inability to get anything going on the ground was a big reason why.
The receiver group of Carnell Tate, Wan’Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, Calvin Ridley, and Chimere Dike combined for just 137 yards on 13 catches.
There were a couple of big plays left on the table, most notably a couple of missed opportunities to Tate that failed to connect because of poor execution and/or penalties. But aside from that, it was a rather lifeless performance by the entire passing attack.
Where do we even begin with this one?
I would say this was an absolutely atrocious performance by the offensive line, but that would somehow be downplaying how bad it really was. The offensive line allowed a combined 20 pressures, three sacks, and two hits on the day.
LT Dan Moore was the biggest culprit, allowing eight of those pressures for an absurd pressure rate of 19.5 percent.
Watching this play in slow-motion with this music is *chefs kiss* pic.twitter.com/OvC0NYFbzI
It was a long afternoon for the group upfront, and the point total on the scoreboard directly reflects that.
It was another largely irrelevant day for a group that hasn’t contributed much. The group of Gunnar Helm, Daniel Bellinger, and Kylen Granson combined for just five yards.
The latter of whom had the opportunity for a big play early in the game, but he was unable to reel in the pass, and it became another missed opportunity for a team that’s had more than its fair share.
It was a rather mediocre outing for a group that has actually played well for most of the year. The group combined for eight pressures and six run stops. DT Jeffery Simmons led the way with three pressures, while DL Jordan Elliott topped the group with two run stops.
But for the Titans to win, they need their defensive line to be a dominant front, and that just wasn’t the case here.
Cody Barton, Cedric Gray, and Anthony Hill Jr. had a solid game for the most part. The three of them were credited with 17 combined tackles, multiple pressures, and half a sack (Gray).
They also helped play a key role in holding the Texans’ ground game to under three yards per carry.
The Titans’ secondary entered the game very thin on the backend, and it only got worse. S Amani Hooker was ruled out with a concussion, while S Kevin Winston Jr. left early with a quadriceps injury, and their absence was felt throughout the contest.
The Texans’ group of pass catchers combined for 261 yards and one touchdown on 26 catches.

title: Postgame Quotes That Matter From Robert Saleh After Titans' Lifeless Week 5 Loss to Texans
full_text:
Another Sunday means another Tennessee Titans loss. This time, head coach Robert Saleh's group fell to the Houston Texans 26-3 at home, dropping to 0-5 in the 2026 season.
Not much went right for Tennessee against Houston. The offense managed just 187 total yards and didn't find the end zone, while the defense allowed Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud to get too comfortable in the pocket, leading to an efficient outing for the 2023 No. 2 overall pick.
The Titans are arguably the worst team in the NFL and have shown no improvement from last season's 3-14 performance. Saleh spoke to the media after his team's latest embarrassing loss, and it's clear that he is running out of answers.
Though he isn't the sole reason for Sunday's loss to the Texans, quarterback Cam Ward still didn't play very well . The 2025 No. 1 overall pick completed 23 of 36 passes for 170 yards and threw an interception.
After another uninspiring performance from his young signal-caller, Saleh was asked about the possibility of benching Ward for veteran Mitchell Trubisky, and the Titans head coach made it known that Ward is still Tennessee's No. 1 quarterback.
"Cam's our starting quarterback," Saleh said. "We're going to give him every opportunity to be successful this year, and we're going to continue working with him, grinding with him and trying to help him get better."
Ward was also asked why he should remain the Titans' QB1, and the Miami product said he is more than capable of handling the responsibilities of being an NFL starting quarterback.
"I just think my process, what I'm willing to sacrifice every week to get to the player that I want to be," Ward said on remaining as the Titans starting quarterback. "Also the player that the team needs and the organization needs to win games. I love the criticism and everything that comes with the quarterback territory. It's the best position in the world. Stuff goes the right way, you take all the credit. Stuff goes the wrong way, you take all the blame."
He hasn't lived up to expectations so far this year, but it is still too early to bench Ward. Tennessee must give Ward an ample sample size before making a decision on whether he is the answer at the most pivotal position in the sport.
Despite a 0-5 start to his tenure as head coach, Saleh isn't losing any confidence. The defensive-minded coach stated that he will turn the Titans around and bring the franchise back into the sun as a winning organization.
"We are going to flip this thing, and eventually this organization is going to have its day in the sun," Saleh said.
Tennessee has won six games since the start of the 2024 season, and hasn't tallied a victory since Week 16 of the 2025 season. There may not be a franchise in a darker place than the Titans right now, and we'll see whether Saleh can turn the tide and be the coach who brings winning football back to Nashville.
The most impactful quote from Saleh's press conference was his message to his guys about the next 12 games. Saleh said that the final 12 games of the year will decide who will stick around in Tennessee and be a part of the franchise turnaround.
"The next 12 games will determine which of you will be here when we turn this thing around."
The Titans were one of the most active franchises in the league on the player acquisition front this past offseason. So far, none of those additions have paid off and made major contributions. We could see another roster turnover period for Tennessee as soon as next spring.
A road contest against the 2-3 Indianapolis Colts is next for the Titans. A loss would drop Tennessee to 0-6 for the first time since 2009, and could officially kickstart draft talk.
